The standard ACM integration for this architecture is to deploy the ACM certificate to the load balancer, while the instances use their own installed certificates for the HTTPS target connection. Option C correctly separates these roles.

- **B is incorrect** because CloudFront cannot use an Elastic Load Balancing target group object directly as an origin. CloudFront origins are specified by an origin domain name, such as an S3 bucket endpoint, an EC2 instance DNS name, an Elastic Load Balancing load balancer DNS name, or another web server DNS name. AWS lists an Elastic Load Balancing **load balancer** DNS name as a valid origin example, not a target group. See [CloudFront origin domain settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistValuesOrigin.html).

- **D is incorrect** because the option describes installing a certificate on the Network Load Balancer, which implies a TLS listener that terminates TLS at the NLB. AWS documentation explains that a Network Load Balancer TLS listener offloads encryption and decryption to the load balancer. If the requirement were for the targets to decrypt the original TLS traffic without the load balancer decrypting it, the NLB would need a TCP listener on port 443 to pass encrypted traffic through to the targets. That is not what option D specifies. See [Listeners for Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-listeners.html).

Therefore, **option C** is the solution that correctly provides HTTPS from the client to the ALB and HTTPS from the ALB to the EC2 web servers.

zh.question: 一家公司计划在 AWS 上托管一个 Web 应用程序，并希望在一组 Amazon EC2 实例之间对流量进行负载均衡。其中一项安全要求是在客户端和 Web 服务器之间启用端到端传输加密。哪种解决方案可以满足此要求？

options.A: 将 EC2 实例置于 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面。使用 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) 预置 SSL 证书，并将该 SSL 证书与 ALB 关联。导出 SSL 证书并将其安装到每个 EC2 实例上。将 ALB 配置为侦听端口 443，并将流量转发到实例上的端口 443。
options.B: 将 EC2 实例与目标组关联。使用 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) 预置 SSL 证书。创建 Amazon CloudFront 分配并将其配置为使用该 SSL 证书。将 CloudFront 设置为使用目标组作为源服务器。
options.C: 将 EC2 实例置于 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面。使用 AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) 预置 SSL 证书，并将该 SSL 证书与 ALB 关联。预置第三方 SSL 证书并将其安装到每个 EC2 实例上。将 ALB 配置为侦听端口 443，并将流量转发到实例上的端口 443。
options.D: 将 EC2 实例置于 Network Load Balancer (NLB) 后面。预置第三方 SSL 证书并将其安装到 NLB 和每个 EC2 实例上。将 NLB 配置为侦听端口 443，并将流量转发到实例上的端口 443。

zh.explanation:
该公司需要在 Amazon EC2 上运行一个经过负载均衡的 Web 应用程序，并要求在完整请求路径上传输中加密：从客户端到负载均衡器，以及从负载均衡器到 Web 服务器。

**正确答案：C。将 EC2 实例置于 Application Load Balancer 后面，在 ALB 上使用 ACM 证书，在每个 EC2 实例上安装单独的 SSL/TLS 证书，并在两侧都配置 HTTPS。**

Application Load Balancer 可以配置 HTTPS 侦听器以及用于客户端连接的 SSL/TLS 证书。对于后端连接，ALB 目标组同时支持 HTTP 和 HTTPS。当目标组使用 HTTPS 时，AWS 说明负载均衡器会使用安装在目标上的证书与目标建立 TLS 连接。因此，将 ALB 侦听器配置在端口 443，并转发到端口 443 上的 HTTPS 目标组，可以加密流量路径中客户端到 ALB 以及 ALB 到 EC2 的两个部分。请参阅 AWS 文档：[creating an HTTPS listener for an Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/create-https-listener.html) 和 [ALB target group routing configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-target-groups.html)。

在 ALB 上使用 AWS Certificate Manager 也是预期的 AWS 集成方式。ACM 与 Elastic Load Balancing 集成，可在负载均衡器上部署 ACM 证书。对于需要直接安装在 EC2 Web 服务器上的证书，可以在实例上安装单独预置的证书。ACM 文档解释了 ACM 与 Elastic Load Balancing 等服务集成以部署证书，并且 ACM 证书通常不会在支持的导出或集成场景之外直接安装在基于 AWS 的网站或应用程序上。请参阅 [Services integrated with ACM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/acm-services.html)。

**其他选项不正确的原因：**

- **A 不正确**，因为它依赖于导出用于 ALB 的 ACM 证书并将其安装到每个 EC2 实例上。此架构的标准 ACM 集成方式是将 ACM 证书部署到负载均衡器，而实例使用各自安装的证书进行 HTTPS 目标连接。选项 C 正确地区分了这些角色。

- **B 不正确**，因为 CloudFront 不能直接使用 Elastic Load Balancing 目标组对象作为源。CloudFront 源由源域名指定，例如 S3 存储桶端点、EC2 实例 DNS 名称、Elastic Load Balancing 负载均衡器 DNS 名称或其他 Web 服务器 DNS 名称。AWS 将 Elastic Load Balancing **负载均衡器** DNS 名称列为有效源示例，而不是目标组。请参阅 [CloudFront origin domain settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistValuesOrigin.html)。

- **D 不正确**，因为该选项描述了在 Network Load Balancer 上安装证书，这意味着使用在 NLB 处终止 TLS 的 TLS 侦听器。AWS 文档解释说，Network Load Balancer TLS 侦听器会将加密和解密卸载到负载均衡器。如果要求是让目标在负载均衡器不解密的情况下解密原始 TLS 流量，则 NLB 需要在端口 443 上使用 TCP 侦听器，将加密流量透传给目标。但选项 D 并未这样指定。请参阅 [Listeners for Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-listeners.html)。

因此，**选项 C** 是能够正确提供从客户端到 ALB 的 HTTPS 以及从 ALB 到 EC2 Web 服务器的 HTTPS 的解决方案。

en.question: A company wants to migrate its data analytics environment from on premises to AWS. The environment consists of two simple Node.js applications. One of the applications collects sensor data and loads it into a MySQL database. The other application aggregates the data into reports. When the aggregation jobs run, some of the load jobs fail to run correctly. The company must resolve the data loading issue. The company also needs the migration to occur without interruptions or changes for the company’s customers. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Set up an Amazon Aurora MySQL database as a replication target for the on-premises database. Create an Aurora Replica for the Aurora MySQL database, and move the aggregation jobs to run against the Aurora Replica. Set up collection endpoints as AWS Lambda functions behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB), and use Amazon RDS Proxy to write to the Aurora MySQL database. When the databases are synced, disable the replication job and restart the Aurora Replica as the primary instance. Point the collector DNS record to the NLB.
options.B: Set up an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to perform continuous data replication from the on-premises database to Aurora. Move the aggregation jobs to run against the Aurora MySQL database. Set up collection endpoints behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) as Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. When the databases are synced, point the collector DNS record to the ALDisable the AWS DMS sync task after the cutover from on premises to AWS.
options.C: Set up an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to perform continuous data replication from the on-premises database to Aurora. Create an Aurora Replica for the Aurora MySQL database, and move the aggregation jobs to run against the Aurora Replica. Set up collection endpoints as AWS Lambda functions behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB), and use Amazon RDS Proxy to write to the Aurora MySQL database. When the databases are synced, point the collector DNS record to the ALB. Disable the AWS DMS sync task after the cutover from on premises to AWS.
options.D: Set up an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Create an Aurora Replica for the Aurora MySQL database, and move the aggregation jobs to run against the Aurora Replica. Set up collection endpoints as an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to replicate the data to the Aurora MySQL database. When the databases are synced, disable the replication job and restart the Aurora Replica as the primary instance. Point the collector DNS record to the Kinesis data stream.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company is migrating a data analytics environment from on premises to AWS. The current problem is that reporting/aggregation jobs interfere with sensor-data loading into a MySQL database. The solution must both:

1. migrate the database and applications to AWS with minimal/no customer interruption, and
2. separate the read-heavy aggregation workload from the write/load path so that loading failures are resolved.

## Correct answer: C

Option C is the best fit.

- **AWS DMS with continuous replication** is appropriate for migrating the existing on-premises MySQL database to Aurora while keeping the AWS target synchronized until cutover. AWS DMS supports ongoing replication/change data capture (CDC); the documentation describes starting an ongoing replication task and notes CDC native start points for source engines including **MySQL** ([AWS DMS ongoing replication/CDC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Task.CDC.html)). This supports a low-interruption migration pattern: replicate first, cut over DNS after synchronization, then stop the DMS task.
- **Aurora MySQL with an Aurora Replica** resolves the workload contention. Aurora Replicas are read-only reader instances used to scale read operations, while writes are handled by the primary/writer instance. The Aurora documentation states that Aurora Replicas let you issue queries to scale read operations and that the reader endpoint spreads read-only connections across replicas ([Aurora Replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Replication.html)). The reader endpoint is specifically intended for reporting and other read-only operations and reduces overhead on the primary instance ([Aurora reader endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Endpoints.Reader.html)). Moving aggregation jobs to the replica therefore directly addresses the failed load jobs caused by read/write contention.
- **Lambda behind an Application Load Balancer** is valid for the collection endpoint. Application Load Balancers can register Lambda functions as targets and invoke them directly when requests are forwarded to the target group ([ALB Lambda targets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/lambda-functions.html)).
- **RDS Proxy** is a good fit for Lambda/database writes because serverless/event-driven applications often create many short-lived connections. RDS Proxy provides connection pooling and multiplexing, reducing database connection overhead and contention ([RDS Proxy application scalability](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy-best-practices.usage-scenarios.html)).

Together, these choices provide continuous database replication, a low-disruption DNS cutover, scalable HTTP collection endpoints, pooled database connections, and isolation of reporting reads from write/load activity.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Incorrect

This option has several issues:

- It uses an **NLB with Lambda functions**, but Network Load Balancers do **not** support the `lambda` target type. AWS documentation states that NLB target types are `instance`, `ip`, and `alb`, and explicitly says that **Network Load Balancers do not support the `lambda` target type**; Application Load Balancers are the load balancers that support Lambda targets ([NLB target types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-target-groups.html)).
- The option describes setting Aurora MySQL as a replication target but does not clearly use AWS DMS for controlled full-load plus ongoing replication/cutover.
- “Restart the Aurora Replica as the primary instance” is not the right migration/cutover mechanism for this scenario. The goal is to cut over writes from the on-premises collector to the Aurora writer after replication catches up, not to promote a reporting replica as the new primary.

### B. Incorrect

This option uses AWS DMS continuous replication, which is good, and ALB/EC2 for the collector, which could work. However, it **moves the aggregation jobs to the Aurora primary database** instead of to a read replica. That does not resolve the root problem: aggregation/reporting load interfering with sensor-data writes. Aurora documentation recommends using reader endpoints/Aurora Replicas for reporting or read-only operations to reduce overhead on the primary instance ([Aurora reader endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Endpoints.Reader.html)).

### D. Incorrect

This option is not appropriate for the stated migration pattern:

- It does not use AWS DMS for the on-premises MySQL-to-Aurora migration and ongoing synchronization. Kinesis Data Streams and Firehose are not database migration/CDC services for replicating an existing relational MySQL database into Aurora.
- It would require changing the collection interface to a Kinesis data stream, which is a customer/application-facing change, conflicting with the requirement for no customer changes.
- Like option A, it includes an unnecessary “restart/promote replica as primary” style of cutover rather than a standard DMS synchronization followed by application/DNS cutover.

Therefore, **C** is the correct answer.

zh.question: 一家公司希望将其数据分析环境从本地迁移到 AWS。该环境由两个简单的 Node.js 应用程序组成。其中一个应用程序收集传感器数据并将其加载到 MySQL 数据库中。另一个应用程序将数据聚合成报告。当聚合作业运行时，部分加载作业无法正确运行。公司必须解决数据加载问题。公司还需要在不对公司客户造成中断或变更的情况下完成迁移。解决方案架构师应如何满足这些要求？

options.A: 设置一个 Amazon Aurora MySQL 数据库作为本地数据库的复制目标。为该 Aurora MySQL 数据库创建一个 Aurora Replica，并将聚合作业移至 Aurora Replica 上运行。将收集端点设置为位于 Network Load Balancer (NLB) 后面的 AWS Lambda 函数，并使用 Amazon RDS Proxy 写入 Aurora MySQL 数据库。当数据库同步后，禁用复制作业并将 Aurora Replica 重新启动为主实例。将收集器 DNS 记录指向 NLB。
options.B: 设置一个 Amazon Aurora MySQL 数据库。使用 AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) 执行从本地数据库到 Aurora 的持续数据复制。将聚合作业移至 Aurora MySQL 数据库上运行。将收集端点设置为位于 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面的、Auto Scaling 组中的 Amazon EC2 实例。当数据库同步后，将收集器 DNS 记录指向 ALB。在从本地切换到 AWS 后，禁用 AWS DMS 同步任务。
options.C: 设置一个 Amazon Aurora MySQL 数据库。使用 AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) 执行从本地数据库到 Aurora 的持续数据复制。为该 Aurora MySQL 数据库创建一个 Aurora Replica，并将聚合作业移至 Aurora Replica 上运行。将收集端点设置为位于 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面的 AWS Lambda 函数，并使用 Amazon RDS Proxy 写入 Aurora MySQL 数据库。当数据库同步后，将收集器 DNS 记录指向 ALB。在从本地切换到 AWS 后，禁用 AWS DMS 同步任务。
options.D: 设置一个 Amazon Aurora MySQL 数据库。为该 Aurora MySQL 数据库创建一个 Aurora Replica，并将聚合作业移至 Aurora Replica 上运行。将收集端点设置为 Amazon Kinesis data stream。使用 Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose 将数据复制到 Aurora MySQL 数据库。当数据库同步后，禁用复制作业并将 Aurora Replica 重新启动为主实例。将收集器 DNS 记录指向 Kinesis data stream。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该公司正在将数据分析环境从本地迁移到 AWS。当前问题是报告/聚合作业会干扰传感器数据加载到 MySQL 数据库。该解决方案必须同时做到：

1. 以最小/无客户中断的方式将数据库和应用程序迁移到 AWS；并且
2. 将读取密集型聚合工作负载与写入/加载路径分离，以解决加载失败问题。

## 正确答案：C

选项 C 最合适。

- **使用 AWS DMS 进行持续复制** 适合将现有本地 MySQL 数据库迁移到 Aurora，并在切换前保持 AWS 目标端同步。AWS DMS 支持持续复制/change data capture (CDC)；文档描述了启动持续复制任务，并指出包括 **MySQL** 在内的源引擎支持 CDC 原生起点（[AWS DMS ongoing replication/CDC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Task.CDC.html)）。这支持低中断迁移模式：先复制，在同步后切换 DNS，然后停止 DMS 任务。
- **Aurora MySQL 与 Aurora Replica** 可解决工作负载争用。Aurora Replicas 是只读读取器实例，用于扩展读取操作，而写入由主/写入器实例处理。Aurora 文档说明，Aurora Replicas 允许你发出查询以扩展读取操作，并且读取器端点会将只读连接分散到副本上（[Aurora Replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Replication.html)）。读取器端点专门用于报告和其他只读操作，并减少主实例上的开销（[Aurora reader endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Endpoints.Reader.html)）。因此，将聚合作业移至副本直接解决了由读/写争用导致的加载作业失败问题。
- **位于 Application Load Balancer 后面的 Lambda** 可用于收集端点。Application Load Balancers 可以将 Lambda 函数注册为目标，并在请求转发到目标组时直接调用这些函数（[ALB Lambda targets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/lambda-functions.html)）。
- **RDS Proxy** 非常适合 Lambda/数据库写入，因为无服务器/事件驱动型应用程序通常会创建许多短生命周期连接。RDS Proxy 提供连接池和多路复用，减少数据库连接开销和争用（[RDS Proxy application scalability](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy-best-practices.usage-scenarios.html)）。

这些选择结合起来，提供了持续数据库复制、低中断 DNS 切换、可扩展的 HTTP 收集端点、池化数据库连接，以及将报告读取与写入/加载活动隔离。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. 不正确

此选项存在几个问题：

- 它使用 **NLB 与 Lambda 函数**，但 Network Load Balancers 不支持 `lambda` 目标类型。AWS 文档说明，NLB 目标类型为 `instance`、`ip` 和 `alb`，并明确指出 **Network Load Balancers 不支持 `lambda` 目标类型**；Application Load Balancers 才是支持 Lambda 目标的负载均衡器（[NLB target types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-target-groups.html)）。
- 该选项描述将 Aurora MySQL 设置为复制目标，但没有明确使用 AWS DMS 进行受控的全量加载加持续复制/切换。
- “将 Aurora Replica 重新启动为主实例”不是此场景中正确的迁移/切换机制。目标是在复制追上后，将写入从本地收集器切换到 Aurora 写入器，而不是将报告副本提升为新的主实例。

### B. 不正确

此选项使用 AWS DMS 持续复制，这一点是好的，并且用于收集器的 ALB/EC2 也可以工作。但是，它 **将聚合作业移至 Aurora 主数据库**，而不是只读副本。这无法解决根本问题：聚合/报告负载干扰传感器数据写入。Aurora 文档建议对报告或只读操作使用读取器端点/Aurora Replicas，以减少主实例上的开销（[Aurora reader endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Endpoints.Reader.html)）。

### D. 不正确

此选项不适合所述迁移模式：

- 它没有使用 AWS DMS 进行本地 MySQL 到 Aurora 的迁移和持续同步。Kinesis Data Streams 和 Firehose 不是用于将现有关系型 MySQL 数据库复制到 Aurora 的数据库迁移/CDC 服务。
- 它需要将收集接口更改为 Kinesis data stream，这属于面向客户/应用程序的变更，与无客户变更的要求相冲突。
- 与选项 A 一样，它包含不必要的“重新启动/提升副本为主实例”式切换，而不是标准的 DMS 同步后再进行应用程序/DNS 切换。

因此，**C** 是正确答案。

en.question: A health insurance company stores personally identifiable information (PII) in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uses server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) to encrypt the objects. According to a new requirement, all current and future objects in the S3 bucket must be encrypted by keys that the company’s security team manages. The S3 bucket does not have versioning enabled. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to SSE-S3 with a customer managed key. Use the AWS CLI to re-upload all objects in the S3 bucket. Set an S3 bucket policy to deny unencrypted PutObject requests.
options.B: In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). Set an S3 bucket policy to deny unencrypted PutObject requests. Use the AWS CLI to re-upload all objects in the S3 bucket.
options.C: In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). Set an S3 bucket policy to automatically encrypt objects on GetObject and PutObject requests.
options.D: In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to AES-256 with a customer managed key. Attach a policy to deny unencrypted PutObject requests to any entities that access the S3 bucket. Use the AWS CLI to re-upload all objects in the S3 bucket.

en.explanation:
The company currently uses SSE-S3, where Amazon S3 manages the encryption keys. The new requirement is that both existing and future objects must be encrypted with keys under the company security team's control. The practical S3-native way to do that is SSE-KMS using a customer managed AWS KMS key, and existing objects must be rewritten or otherwise have their encryption updated because changing bucket default encryption affects new writes, not already-stored objects.

**Correct answer: B**

Option B is the best match. Amazon S3 documentation states that buckets use SSE-S3 by default, but you can configure buckets to use **server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS)** instead. With SSE-KMS, you can specify a **customer managed key**, and AWS KMS lets you centrally create, manage, rotate, control access to, and audit KMS keys ([Using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingKMSEncryption.html)). This satisfies the requirement for keys managed by the company's security team, assuming the bucket default encryption is configured with the company's customer managed KMS key rather than the AWS managed `aws/s3` key.

For future objects, S3 supports default bucket encryption with SSE-KMS; the S3 default encryption documentation says that if you need more control over keys, such as key rotation and access policy grants, you can choose SSE-KMS ([Setting default server-side encryption behavior for Amazon S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)). S3 bucket policies can also require SSE-KMS for object uploads; the official example denies `PutObject` requests unless the object is encrypted with SSE-KMS, and can require a specific KMS key ARN ([Examples of Amazon S3 bucket policies - Requiring encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies.html)).

For current objects, changing the bucket default encryption is not enough. Existing objects need to be rewritten/copied or otherwise updated. The S3 default encryption documentation describes using Batch Operations, `CopyObject`, or the AWS CLI `copy-object` command to write existing objects back as encrypted objects ([Setting default server-side encryption behavior for Amazon S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)). Re-uploading the objects with the AWS CLI is therefore a valid way to cause the existing objects to be stored under the new SSE-KMS configuration. Because versioning is not enabled, overwriting/re-uploading the same object keys replaces the current objects rather than creating additional versions.

**Why the other options are incorrect**

- **A. Incorrect.** SSE-S3 does not use customer managed keys. SSE-S3 means Amazon S3 managed keys. The documentation explicitly distinguishes SSE-S3 from SSE-KMS and says to use SSE-KMS when you need more control over keys ([Setting default server-side encryption behavior for Amazon S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)). “SSE-S3 with a customer managed key” is not a valid S3 default encryption configuration.

- **C. Incorrect.** This option changes default encryption for future writes but does not handle existing objects. Also, an S3 bucket policy cannot “automatically encrypt objects on GetObject and PutObject requests.” Bucket policies allow or deny requests based on conditions; they do not transform a `GetObject` request into an encryption operation. S3 decrypts encrypted objects when authorized users download them, and encryption of stored objects occurs on writes, copies, or encryption-update operations, not on `GetObject`.

- **D. Incorrect.** “AES-256 with a customer managed key” mixes terms. AES-256 is the encryption algorithm/header value associated with SSE-S3, not a customer managed key option. Customer-managed key control for S3 server-side encryption is provided through AWS KMS customer managed keys with SSE-KMS, not through an “AES-256 customer managed key” bucket setting. S3 documentation says that for more control over keys, use SSE-KMS ([Setting default server-side encryption behavior for Amazon S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)).

Therefore, **B** is the correct choice, with the important interpretation that the SSE-KMS configuration should specify a **customer managed KMS key** controlled by the company's security team.

zh.question: 一家健康保险公司将个人身份信息（PII）存储在一个 Amazon S3 存储桶中。该公司使用采用 S3 托管加密密钥的服务器端加密（SSE-S3）来加密对象。根据一项新要求，S3 存储桶中所有当前和未来的对象都必须由该公司安全团队管理的密钥进行加密。该 S3 存储桶未启用版本控制。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 S3 存储桶属性中，将默认加密更改为使用客户托管密钥的 SSE-S3。使用 AWS CLI 重新上传 S3 存储桶中的所有对象。设置 S3 存储桶策略以拒绝未加密的 PutObject 请求。
options.B: 在 S3 存储桶属性中，将默认加密更改为使用 AWS KMS 托管加密密钥的服务器端加密（SSE-KMS）。设置 S3 存储桶策略以拒绝未加密的 PutObject 请求。使用 AWS CLI 重新上传 S3 存储桶中的所有对象。
options.C: 在 S3 存储桶属性中，将默认加密更改为使用 AWS KMS 托管加密密钥的服务器端加密（SSE-KMS）。设置 S3 存储桶策略，以便在 GetObject 和 PutObject 请求时自动加密对象。
options.D: 在 S3 存储桶属性中，将默认加密更改为使用客户托管密钥的 AES-256。向访问该 S3 存储桶的任何实体附加策略，以拒绝未加密的 PutObject 请求。使用 AWS CLI 重新上传 S3 存储桶中的所有对象。

zh.explanation:
该公司当前使用 SSE-S3，其中 Amazon S3 管理加密密钥。新要求是现有对象和未来对象都必须使用由公司安全团队控制的密钥进行加密。实现这一点的实用 S3 原生方式是使用采用客户托管 AWS KMS 密钥的 SSE-KMS，并且现有对象必须被重新写入，或以其他方式更新其加密，因为更改存储桶默认加密只影响新的写入，不影响已存储的对象。

**正确答案：B**

选项 B 是最匹配的。Amazon S3 文档说明，存储桶默认使用 SSE-S3，但你可以改为将存储桶配置为使用 **AWS KMS keys 的服务器端加密（SSE-KMS）**。使用 SSE-KMS 时，你可以指定一个 **customer managed key**，并且 AWS KMS 允许你集中创建、管理、轮换、控制访问以及审计 KMS 密钥（[Using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingKMSEncryption.html)）。这满足了由公司安全团队管理密钥的要求，前提是存储桶默认加密配置为使用公司的客户托管 KMS 密钥，而不是 AWS 托管的 `aws/s3` 密钥。

对于未来对象，S3 支持使用 SSE-KMS 的默认存储桶加密；S3 默认加密文档说明，如果你需要对密钥进行更多控制，例如密钥轮换和访问策略授权，则可以选择 SSE-KMS（[Setting default server-side encryption behavior for Amazon S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)）。S3 存储桶策略也可以要求对象上传使用 SSE-KMS；官方示例会拒绝未使用 SSE-KMS 加密对象的 `PutObject` 请求，并且可以要求特定的 KMS 密钥 ARN（[Examples of Amazon S3 bucket policies - Requiring encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies.html)）。

对于当前对象，仅更改存储桶默认加密是不够的。现有对象需要被重新写入/复制，或以其他方式更新。S3 默认加密文档描述了使用 Batch Operations、`CopyObject` 或 AWS CLI `copy-object` 命令将现有对象重新写回为加密对象（[Setting default server-side encryption behavior for Amazon S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)）。因此，使用 AWS CLI 重新上传对象是一种有效方式，可以使现有对象按新的 SSE-KMS 配置存储。由于未启用版本控制，使用相同对象键覆盖/重新上传会替换当前对象，而不是创建额外版本。

**为什么其他选项不正确**

- **A. 不正确。** SSE-S3 不使用客户托管密钥。SSE-S3 表示 Amazon S3 托管密钥。文档明确区分了 SSE-S3 和 SSE-KMS，并说明当你需要对密钥进行更多控制时应使用 SSE-KMS（[Setting default server-side encryption behavior for Amazon S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)）。“使用客户托管密钥的 SSE-S3”不是有效的 S3 默认加密配置。

- **C. 不正确。** 此选项更改了未来写入的默认加密，但没有处理现有对象。此外，S3 存储桶策略不能“在 GetObject 和 PutObject 请求时自动加密对象”。存储桶策略根据条件允许或拒绝请求；它们不会将 `GetObject` 请求转换为加密操作。当授权用户下载加密对象时，S3 会解密这些对象；而存储对象的加密发生在写入、复制或加密更新操作时，而不是在 `GetObject` 时。

- **D. 不正确。** “使用客户托管密钥的 AES-256”混淆了术语。AES-256 是与 SSE-S3 关联的加密算法/标头值，不是客户托管密钥选项。S3 服务器端加密的客户托管密钥控制是通过 AWS KMS 客户托管密钥与 SSE-KMS 提供的，而不是通过“AES-256 客户托管密钥”存储桶设置提供的。S3 文档说明，如果要对密钥进行更多控制，请使用 SSE-KMS（[Setting default server-side encryption behavior for Amazon S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)）。

因此，**B** 是正确选择，重要的理解是 SSE-KMS 配置应指定由公司安全团队控制的 **customer managed KMS key**。

en.question: A company is running a web application in the AWS Cloud. The application consists of dynamic content that is created on a set of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group that is configured as a target group for an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company is using an Amazon CloudFront distribution to distribute the application globally. The CloudFront distribution uses the ALB as an origin. The company uses Amazon Route 53 for DNS and has created an A record of www.example.com for the CloudFront distribution. A solutions architect must configure the application so that itis highly available and fault tolerant. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Provision a full, secondary application deployment in a different AWS Region. Update the Route 53 A record to be a failover record. Add both of the CloudFront distributions as values. Create Route 53 health checks.
options.B: Provision an ALB, an Auto Scaling group, and EC2 instances in a different AWS Region. Update the CloudFront distribution, and create a second origin for the new ALCreate an origin group for the two origins. Configure one origin as primary and one origin as secondary.
options.C: Provision an Auto Scaling group and EC2 instances in a different AWS Region. Create a second target for the new Auto Scaling group in the ALB. Set up the failover routing algorithm on the ALB.
options.D: Provision a full, secondary application deployment in a different AWS Region. Create a second CloudFront distribution, and add the new application setup as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator. Add both of the CloudFront distributions as endpoints.

en.explanation:
The application already uses a global CloudFront distribution in front of an ALB-backed Auto Scaling fleet. The question asks for the best highly available and fault-tolerant design for the dynamic origin tier. The key is to add regional redundancy at the **origin** layer and let CloudFront fail over between origins.

**Correct answer: B.**

AWS CloudFront supports **origin failover** for high availability. The official documentation states that you create an **origin group** with two origins, one primary and one secondary; if the primary origin is unavailable or returns configured failure status codes, CloudFront automatically switches to the secondary origin. The setup requires a distribution with at least two origins, then an origin group assigned to a cache behavior ([CloudFront origin failover documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/high_availability_origin_failover.html)).

Therefore, provisioning a second regional origin stack — an ALB, Auto Scaling group, and EC2 instances in another Region — and adding the second ALB as a secondary CloudFront origin directly matches the AWS-supported high availability pattern.

### Why the other options are incorrect

**A. Provision a full secondary deployment and use Route 53 failover between two CloudFront distributions — Incorrect.**  
Route 53 can route a domain name to a CloudFront distribution by using an alias record ([Route 53 CloudFront routing documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-to-cloudfront-distribution.html)). However, this option creates a second CloudFront distribution for the same application domain. For a working HTTPS/custom-domain setup, the secondary CloudFront distribution would also need the same alternate domain name, such as `www.example.com`, but CloudFront does not allow the same alternate domain name to be added to another distribution ([CloudFront alternate domain name restrictions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/CNAMEs.html)). Also, CloudFront is already the global entry point; the more appropriate failover layer here is CloudFront origin failover, not DNS failover between CloudFront distributions.

**C. Add a second target for the new Auto Scaling group in the ALB and use ALB failover routing — Incorrect.**  
This does not add a second ALB and attempts to make a single regional ALB front targets in another Region. ALB is a regional load balancing component, and ALB listener/routing rules do not provide a “failover routing algorithm” for cross-Region application stacks. The option leaves the ALB as a regional dependency and does not match the documented CloudFront origin failover design.

**D. Create a second CloudFront distribution and use AWS Global Accelerator with both distributions as endpoints — Incorrect.**  
AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator endpoints can be Network Load Balancers, Application Load Balancers, EC2 instances, or Elastic IP addresses; CloudFront distributions are not listed as supported endpoints ([AWS Global Accelerator documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/what-is-global-accelerator.html)). This design is also unnecessary because CloudFront is already the global edge distribution layer.

Thus, **B** is the best answer because it adds a second regional origin stack and uses CloudFront origin groups to provide automatic failover from the primary ALB origin to the secondary ALB origin.

zh.question: 一家公司正在 AWS Cloud 中运行一个 Web 应用程序。该应用程序由一组 Amazon EC2 实例上创建的动态内容组成。EC2 实例在一个 Auto Scaling 组中运行，该组被配置为 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 的目标组。该公司正在使用 Amazon CloudFront 分配在全球分发该应用程序。CloudFront 分配使用 ALB 作为源站。该公司使用 Amazon Route 53 进行 DNS，并为 CloudFront 分配创建了 www.example.com 的 A 记录。解决方案架构师必须配置该应用程序，使其具有高可用性和容错能力。哪种解决方案满足这些要求？

options.A: 在不同的 AWS Region 中预置完整的辅助应用程序部署。将 Route 53 A 记录更新为故障转移记录。将两个 CloudFront 分配都添加为值。创建 Route 53 运行状况检查。
options.B: 在不同的 AWS Region 中预置一个 ALB、一个 Auto Scaling 组和 EC2 实例。更新 CloudFront 分配，并为新的 ALB 创建第二个源站。为这两个源站创建一个源站组。将一个源站配置为主源站，将另一个源站配置为辅助源站。
options.C: 在不同的 AWS Region 中预置一个 Auto Scaling 组和 EC2 实例。在 ALB 中为新的 Auto Scaling 组创建第二个目标。设置 ALB 上的故障转移路由算法。
options.D: 在不同的 AWS Region 中预置完整的辅助应用程序部署。创建第二个 CloudFront 分配，并将新的应用程序设置添加为源站。创建一个 AWS Global Accelerator 加速器。将两个 CloudFront 分配都添加为端点。

zh.explanation:
该应用程序已经在 ALB 支持的 Auto Scaling 实例队列前使用了一个全球 CloudFront 分配。问题要求为动态源站层设计最佳的高可用且容错的方案。关键是在 **origin** 层增加区域冗余，并让 CloudFront 在源站之间进行故障转移。

**正确答案：B。**

AWS CloudFront 支持用于高可用性的 **origin failover**。官方文档说明，你可以创建一个包含两个源站的 **origin group**，一个主源站和一个辅助源站；如果主源站不可用或返回已配置的故障状态码，CloudFront 会自动切换到辅助源站。该设置要求分配至少有两个源站，然后将源站组分配给一个缓存行为（[CloudFront origin failover 文档](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/high_availability_origin_failover.html)）。

因此，预置第二个区域源站堆栈——另一个 Region 中的一个 ALB、Auto Scaling 组和 EC2 实例——并将第二个 ALB 添加为辅助 CloudFront 源站，直接符合 AWS 支持的高可用性模式。

### 为什么其他选项不正确

**A. 预置完整的辅助部署，并使用 Route 53 在两个 CloudFront 分配之间进行故障转移 — 不正确。**  
Route 53 可以通过使用别名记录将域名路由到 CloudFront 分配（[Route 53 CloudFront 路由文档](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-to-cloudfront-distribution.html)）。但是，此选项为同一个应用程序域创建了第二个 CloudFront 分配。对于可工作的 HTTPS/自定义域设置，辅助 CloudFront 分配还需要相同的备用域名，例如 `www.example.com`，但 CloudFront 不允许将相同的备用域名添加到另一个分配（[CloudFront 备用域名限制](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/CNAMEs.html)）。此外，CloudFront 已经是全球入口点；这里更合适的故障转移层是 CloudFront origin failover，而不是 CloudFront 分配之间的 DNS 故障转移。

**C. 在 ALB 中为新的 Auto Scaling 组添加第二个目标，并使用 ALB 故障转移路由 — 不正确。**  
这没有添加第二个 ALB，并且试图让单个区域性 ALB 前端指向另一个 Region 中的目标。ALB 是区域性负载均衡组件，ALB 侦听器/路由规则不提供用于跨 Region 应用程序堆栈的“failover routing algorithm”。该选项使 ALB 仍然是一个区域性依赖项，并且不符合已记录的 CloudFront origin failover 设计。

**D. 创建第二个 CloudFront 分配，并使用 AWS Global Accelerator 将两个分配作为端点 — 不正确。**  
AWS Global Accelerator 标准加速器端点可以是 Network Load Balancers、Application Load Balancers、EC2 实例或 Elastic IP 地址；CloudFront 分配未被列为受支持的端点（[AWS Global Accelerator 文档](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/what-is-global-accelerator.html)）。此设计也没有必要，因为 CloudFront 已经是全球边缘分发层。

因此，**B** 是最佳答案，因为它添加了第二个区域源站堆栈，并使用 CloudFront 源站组来提供从主 ALB 源站到辅助 ALB 源站的自动故障转移。

en.question: A company has an organization in AWS Organizations that has a large number of AWS accounts. One of the AWS accounts is designated as a transit account and has a transit gateway that is shared with all of the other AWS accounts. AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections are configured between all of the company’s global offices and the transit account. The company has AWS Config enabled on all of its accounts. The company’s networking team needs to centrally manage a list of internal IP address ranges that belong to the global offices. Developers will reference this list to gain access to their applications securely. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

options.A: Create a JSON file that is hosted in Amazon S3 and that lists all of the internal IP address ranges. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic in each of the accounts that can be invoked when the JSON file is updated. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the SNS topic to update all relevant security group rules with the updated IP address ranges.
options.B: Create a new AWS Config managed rule that contains all of the internal IP address ranges. Use the rule to check the security groups in each of the accounts to ensure compliance with the list of IP address ranges. Configure the rule to automatically remediate any noncompliant security group that is detected.
options.C: In the transit account, create a VPC prefix list with all of the internal IP address ranges. Use AWS Resource Access Manager to share the prefix list with all of the other accounts. Use the shared prefix list to configure security group rules in the other accounts.
options.D: In the transit account, create a security group with all of the internal IP address ranges. Configure the security groups in the other accounts to reference the transit account’s security group by using a nested security group reference of “/sg-1a2b3c4d”.

en.explanation:
The company needs a centrally managed list of internal office CIDR ranges that many accounts can reference in their application security controls, with minimum operational overhead. This is a native fit for a customer-managed VPC prefix list shared by AWS RAM.

**Correct answer: C.**

A customer-managed prefix list is designed to consolidate CIDR blocks and can be used as the source or destination in security group rules: the security group rule documentation lists “the ID of a prefix list” as a valid source/destination component. AWS also documents that a prefix list owner can create and modify prefix list entries centrally. Most importantly for this multi-account Organizations scenario, AWS RAM can share a customer-managed prefix list with specific accounts, an OU, or an entire AWS Organization, and consumers can view the entries and reference the shared prefix list in their AWS resources. This lets the networking team maintain the office IP ranges in the transit/network account, while developers in other accounts reference the same shared prefix list in security group rules. See [Share customer-managed prefix lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/sharing-managed-prefix-lists.html), [Shared prefix list permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/sharing-perms.html), [Work with customer-managed prefix lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/work-with-cust-managed-prefix-lists.html), and [Security group rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-group-rules.html).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

* **A:** Hosting a JSON file in S3 and using SNS/Lambda in every account creates custom automation and per-account operational overhead. It is also more error-prone than using the native reusable prefix list mechanism that security groups can reference directly.
* **B:** AWS Config is for evaluating and remediating compliance, not for providing developers with a reusable centrally managed network object to reference. The option also says to create a new AWS Config *managed* rule, but AWS Config managed rules are AWS-provided predefined rules, not a custom central CIDR list mechanism. Even with remediation, this approach would require custom rule/remediation design and would not meet the requirement as directly as shared prefix lists.
* **D:** A security group reference is not a list of CIDR ranges. Referencing a security group allows traffic from/to the private IPs of resources associated with that referenced security group; it does not import the referenced security group’s CIDR rules. AWS explicitly notes that no rules from the referenced security group are added to the referencing security group. Therefore, creating one security group with the office CIDRs and referencing it from other accounts would not provide the desired centrally managed IP range list semantics.

Therefore, **C** provides the native multi-account, centrally managed, lowest-overhead solution.

zh.question: 一家公司在 AWS Organizations 中有一个组织，其中包含大量 AWS 账户。其中一个 AWS 账户被指定为中转账户，并拥有一个与所有其他 AWS 账户共享的 transit gateway。该公司的所有全球办公室与该中转账户之间都配置了 AWS Site-to-Site VPN 连接。该公司已在所有账户中启用 AWS Config。公司的网络团队需要集中管理一份属于全球办公室的内部 IP 地址范围列表。开发人员将引用此列表，以安全地访问其应用程序。哪种解决方案能以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个托管在 Amazon S3 中的 JSON 文件，其中列出所有内部 IP 地址范围。在每个账户中配置一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题，当 JSON 文件更新时可调用该主题。将 AWS Lambda 函数订阅到 SNS 主题，以使用更新后的 IP 地址范围更新所有相关的安全组规则。
options.B: 创建一个新的 AWS Config 托管规则，其中包含所有内部 IP 地址范围。使用该规则检查每个账户中的安全组，确保其符合该 IP 地址范围列表。配置该规则以自动修复检测到的任何不合规安全组。
options.C: 在中转账户中，创建一个包含所有内部 IP 地址范围的 VPC prefix list。使用 AWS Resource Access Manager 将该 prefix list 共享给所有其他账户。使用共享的 prefix list 配置其他账户中的安全组规则。
options.D: 在中转账户中，创建一个包含所有内部 IP 地址范围的安全组。通过使用“/sg-1a2b3c4d”的嵌套安全组引用，配置其他账户中的安全组以引用中转账户的安全组。

zh.explanation:
该公司需要一个集中管理的内部办公室 CIDR 范围列表，供多个账户在其应用程序安全控制中引用，并且运营开销要最小。这正适合使用由 AWS RAM 共享的客户托管 VPC prefix list。

**正确答案：C。**

客户托管 prefix list 旨在整合 CIDR 块，并可在安全组规则中用作来源或目的地：安全组规则文档将“prefix list 的 ID”列为有效的来源/目的地组成部分。AWS 还说明，prefix list 所有者可以集中创建和修改 prefix list 条目。对于这个多账户 Organizations 场景，最重要的是，AWS RAM 可以将客户托管 prefix list 共享给特定账户、OU 或整个 AWS Organization，使用者可以查看条目并在其 AWS 资源中引用共享的 prefix list。这使网络团队能够在中转/网络账户中维护办公室 IP 范围，而其他账户中的开发人员可以在安全组规则中引用同一个共享的 prefix list。请参阅 [Share customer-managed prefix lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/sharing-managed-prefix-lists.html)、[Shared prefix list permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/sharing-perms.html)、[Work with customer-managed prefix lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/work-with-cust-managed-prefix-lists.html) 和 [Security group rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-group-rules.html)。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

* **A:** 在 S3 中托管 JSON 文件，并在每个账户中使用 SNS/Lambda，会创建自定义自动化和按账户计算的运营开销。与使用安全组可直接引用的原生可重用 prefix list 机制相比，它也更容易出错。
* **B:** AWS Config 用于评估和修复合规性，而不是为开发人员提供一个可重用的、集中管理的网络对象供其引用。该选项还说要创建新的 AWS Config *托管*规则，但 AWS Config 托管规则是 AWS 提供的预定义规则，而不是自定义集中式 CIDR 列表机制。即使有修复，此方法也需要自定义规则/修复设计，并且不如共享 prefix list 那样直接满足要求。
* **D:** 安全组引用不是 CIDR 范围列表。引用安全组允许来自/发往与被引用安全组关联的资源的私有 IP 的流量；它不会导入被引用安全组的 CIDR 规则。AWS 明确指出，被引用安全组中的任何规则都不会添加到引用它的安全组中。因此，创建一个包含办公室 CIDR 的安全组并从其他账户引用它，并不能提供所需的集中管理 IP 范围列表语义。

因此，**C** 提供了原生的多账户、集中管理、最低开销的解决方案。

en.question: A company runs a new application as a static website in Amazon S3. The company has deployed the application to a production AWS account and uses Amazon CloudFront to deliver the website. The website calls an Amazon API Gateway REST API. An AWS Lambda function backs each API method. The company wants to create a CSV report every 2 weeks to show each API Lambda function’s recommended configured memory, recommended cost, and the price difference between current configurations and the recommendations. The company will store the reports in an S3 bucket. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development time?

options.A: Create a Lambda function that extracts metrics data for each API Lambda function from Amazon CloudWatch Logs for the 2-week period. Collate the data into tabular format. Store the data as a .csv file in an S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to schedule the Lambda function to run every 2 weeks.
options.B: Opt in to AWS Compute Optimizer. Create a Lambda function that calls the ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations operation. Export the .csv file to an S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to schedule the Lambda function to run every 2 weeks.
options.C: Opt in to AWS Compute Optimizer. Set up enhanced infrastructure metrics. Within the Compute Optimizer console, schedule a job to export the Lambda recommendations to a .csv file. Store the file in an S3 bucket every 2 weeks.
options.D: Purchase the AWS Business Support plan for the production account. Opt in to AWS Compute Optimizer for AWS Trusted Advisor checks. In the Trusted Advisor console, schedule a job to export the cost optimization checks to a .csv file. Store the file in an S3 bucket every 2 weeks.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The requirement is to produce, every 2 weeks, a CSV report for the Lambda functions behind the API Gateway methods. The report must include recommended configured memory, recommended cost, and the price/cost difference or savings compared with the current Lambda configuration, and the file must be stored in S3. The solution should require the **least development time**.

## Correct answer: B

**B. Opt in to AWS Compute Optimizer. Create a Lambda function that calls the `ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations` operation. Export the `.csv` file to an S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to schedule the Lambda function to run every 2 weeks.**

This is the best fit because AWS Compute Optimizer natively supports Lambda function recommendations. AWS states that Compute Optimizer generates recommendations for several resource types, including **AWS Lambda functions**, and that you must opt in before Compute Optimizer analyzes resources ([What is AWS Compute Optimizer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/what-is-compute-optimizer.html)).

The specific API operation named in option B is designed for exactly this use case: `ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations` **exports optimization recommendations for AWS Lambda functions** and exports them as a **CSV file** plus JSON metadata to an existing **Amazon S3 bucket** ([ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/APIReference/API_ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations.html)). The API supports fields such as:

- `CurrentConfigurationMemorySize`
- `CurrentCostTotal` / `CurrentCostAverage`
- `RecommendationOptionsConfigurationMemorySize`
- `RecommendationOptionsCostLow` / `RecommendationOptionsCostHigh`
- `RecommendationOptionsSavingsOpportunityPercentage`
- `RecommendationOptionsEstimatedMonthlySavingsValue`

These fields align directly with the requested recommended configured memory, recommended cost, and cost/price difference information ([Exported files](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/exported-files.html)). Compute Optimizer also documents Lambda estimated monthly savings and savings opportunity as the difference between current and recommended Lambda memory specifications ([Viewing Lambda function recommendations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/view-lambda-recommendations.html)).

Finally, EventBridge scheduled rules can run on a rate expression such as days-based intervals; a biweekly schedule can be implemented as `rate(14 days)` because rate expressions support positive values with units including `days` ([EventBridge rate expressions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-scheduled-rule-pattern.html)). This means only a small Lambda wrapper around a native export API is needed, minimizing custom report-generation logic.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Custom CloudWatch Logs extraction and CSV generation

This would require manually extracting and interpreting Lambda metrics from CloudWatch Logs, calculating memory recommendations and costs, formatting a report, and writing CSV output. That is significantly more custom development than using Compute Optimizer’s built-in Lambda recommendations and CSV export API. It also does not directly provide the same recommendation model that Compute Optimizer provides for Lambda functions.

### C. Compute Optimizer console scheduled export with enhanced infrastructure metrics

This option is not the best answer for two reasons:

1. **Enhanced infrastructure metrics are not needed for Lambda recommendations.** AWS documents enhanced infrastructure metrics as a paid feature that applies to **Amazon EC2 instances, instances in EC2 Auto Scaling groups, and Amazon RDS DB instances**, not Lambda functions ([Enhanced infrastructure metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/enhanced-infrastructure-metrics.html)).
2. The documented Compute Optimizer console export procedure creates an export job to S3, but the requirement is an automated export every 2 weeks. The native API plus EventBridge schedule in option B directly addresses that automation requirement ([Exporting your recommendations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/exporting-your-recommendations.html)).

### D. AWS Business Support + Trusted Advisor

Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks are not the right mechanism for detailed Lambda memory-size recommendations and exported fields such as recommended configured memory, recommended cost ranges, and estimated monthly savings. Compute Optimizer is the AWS service that directly supports Lambda function rightsizing recommendations and exportable Lambda-specific recommendation fields. Purchasing Business Support is unnecessary and does not reduce development effort for this specific report compared with directly using Compute Optimizer’s export API.

## Conclusion

Option **B** uses the AWS-native recommendation engine for Lambda functions, exports the required recommendation and cost fields directly to CSV in S3, and uses EventBridge for the required two-week schedule. It satisfies the requirements with the least custom development.

zh.question: 一家公司将一个新应用作为静态网站运行在 Amazon S3 中。公司已将该应用部署到一个生产 AWS 账户，并使用 Amazon CloudFront 交付该网站。该网站调用一个 Amazon API Gateway REST API。每个 API 方法都由一个 AWS Lambda 函数提供支持。公司希望每 2 周创建一份 CSV 报告，显示每个 API Lambda 函数的建议配置内存、建议成本，以及当前配置与建议之间的价格差异。公司将把报告存储在一个 S3 桶中。哪种解决方案能以最少的开发时间满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Lambda 函数，从 Amazon CloudWatch Logs 中提取每个 API Lambda 函数在 2 周期间的指标数据。将数据整理为表格格式。将数据作为 .csv 文件存储在 S3 桶中。创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，计划该 Lambda 函数每 2 周运行一次。
options.B: 选择加入 AWS Compute Optimizer。创建一个 Lambda 函数来调用 ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations 操作。将 .csv 文件导出到 S3 桶。创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，计划该 Lambda 函数每 2 周运行一次。
options.C: 选择加入 AWS Compute Optimizer。设置 enhanced infrastructure metrics。在 Compute Optimizer 控制台中，计划一个作业以将 Lambda 建议导出为 .csv 文件。每 2 周将该文件存储到 S3 桶中。
options.D: 为生产账户购买 AWS Business Support 计划。为 AWS Trusted Advisor 检查选择加入 AWS Compute Optimizer。在 Trusted Advisor 控制台中，计划一个作业以将成本优化检查导出为 .csv 文件。每 2 周将该文件存储到 S3 桶中。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

要求是每 2 周为 API Gateway 方法背后的 Lambda 函数生成一份 CSV 报告。报告必须包括建议配置内存、建议成本，以及与当前 Lambda 配置相比的价格/成本差异或节省金额，并且文件必须存储在 S3 中。解决方案应需要**最少的开发时间**。

## 正确答案：B

**B. 选择加入 AWS Compute Optimizer。创建一个 Lambda 函数来调用 `ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations` 操作。将 `.csv` 文件导出到 S3 桶。创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，计划该 Lambda 函数每 2 周运行一次。**

这是最合适的选择，因为 AWS Compute Optimizer 原生支持 Lambda 函数建议。AWS 表示，Compute Optimizer 会为多种资源类型生成建议，包括 **AWS Lambda 函数**，并且在 Compute Optimizer 分析资源之前必须先选择加入（[What is AWS Compute Optimizer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/what-is-compute-optimizer.html)）。

选项 B 中提到的特定 API 操作正是为此用例而设计的：`ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations` **导出 AWS Lambda 函数的优化建议**，并将其作为 **CSV 文件**以及 JSON 元数据导出到现有的 **Amazon S3 桶**（[ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/APIReference/API_ExportLambdaFunctionRecommendations.html)）。该 API 支持如下字段：

- `CurrentConfigurationMemorySize`
- `CurrentCostTotal` / `CurrentCostAverage`
- `RecommendationOptionsConfigurationMemorySize`
- `RecommendationOptionsCostLow` / `RecommendationOptionsCostHigh`
- `RecommendationOptionsSavingsOpportunityPercentage`
- `RecommendationOptionsEstimatedMonthlySavingsValue`

这些字段直接对应所请求的建议配置内存、建议成本以及成本/价格差异信息（[Exported files](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/exported-files.html)）。Compute Optimizer 还说明，Lambda 预估每月节省金额和节省机会表示当前 Lambda 内存规格与建议内存规格之间的差异（[Viewing Lambda function recommendations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/view-lambda-recommendations.html)）。

最后，EventBridge 计划规则可以基于 rate 表达式（例如按天的间隔）运行；每两周一次的计划可以实现为 `rate(14 days)`，因为 rate 表达式支持正值以及包括 `days` 在内的单位（[EventBridge rate expressions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-scheduled-rule-pattern.html)）。这意味着只需要围绕原生导出 API 编写一个很小的 Lambda 包装器，从而最大限度减少自定义报告生成逻辑。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. 自定义 CloudWatch Logs 提取和 CSV 生成

这需要手动从 CloudWatch Logs 中提取并解释 Lambda 指标，计算内存建议和成本，格式化报告，并写入 CSV 输出。与使用 Compute Optimizer 的内置 Lambda 建议和 CSV 导出 API 相比，这需要显著更多的自定义开发。它也不能直接提供 Compute Optimizer 为 Lambda 函数提供的同一套建议模型。

### C. Compute Optimizer 控制台计划导出并使用 enhanced infrastructure metrics

此选项不是最佳答案，原因有两个：

1. **Lambda 建议不需要 enhanced infrastructure metrics。** AWS 将 enhanced infrastructure metrics 说明为一项付费功能，适用于 **Amazon EC2 实例、EC2 Auto Scaling groups 中的实例以及 Amazon RDS DB 实例**，而不适用于 Lambda 函数（[Enhanced infrastructure metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/enhanced-infrastructure-metrics.html)）。
2. 文档中的 Compute Optimizer 控制台导出过程会创建一个到 S3 的导出作业，但要求是每 2 周自动导出一次。选项 B 中的原生 API 加 EventBridge 计划直接满足了该自动化要求（[Exporting your recommendations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/compute-optimizer/latest/ug/exporting-your-recommendations.html)）。

### D. AWS Business Support + Trusted Advisor

Trusted Advisor 成本优化检查并不是用于提供详细 Lambda 内存大小建议和导出字段（例如建议配置内存、建议成本范围以及预估每月节省金额）的正确机制。Compute Optimizer 才是直接支持 Lambda 函数 right-sizing 建议以及可导出的 Lambda 专属建议字段的 AWS 服务。购买 Business Support 并非必要，而且与直接使用 Compute Optimizer 的导出 API 相比，并不会减少此特定报告的开发工作量。

## 结论

选项 **B** 使用 AWS 原生的 Lambda 函数建议引擎，将所需的建议和成本字段直接导出为 S3 中的 CSV，并使用 EventBridge 实现所需的两周计划。它以最少的自定义开发满足要求。

en.question: A company’s factory and automation applications are running in a single VPC. More than 20 applications run on a combination of Amazon EC2, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), and Amazon RDS. The company has software engineers spread across three teams. One of the three teams owns each application, and each time is responsible for the cost and performance of all of its applications. Team resources have tags that represent their application and team. The teams use IAM access for daily activities. The company needs to determine which costs on the monthly AWS bill are attributable to each application or team. The company also must be able to create reports to compare costs from the last 12 months and to help forecast costs for the next 12 months. A solutions architect must recommend an AWS Billing and Cost Management solution that provides these cost reports. Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.A: Activate the user-define cost allocation tags that represent the application and the team.
options.B: Activate the AWS generated cost allocation tags that represent the application and the team.
options.C: Create a cost category for each application in Billing and Cost Management.
options.D: Activate IAM access to Billing and Cost Management.
options.E: Create a cost budget.
options.F: Enable Cost Explorer.

en.explanation:
The company needs a cost allocation and reporting solution that can attribute monthly AWS charges to each application and team, compare historical costs for the last 12 months, and forecast costs for the next 12 months. The correct choices are **A, C, and F**.

**A. Activate the user-defined cost allocation tags that represent the application and the team — Correct.**  
The application and team tags are tags that the company created and applied to its resources. AWS identifies these as **user-defined** tags, and they must be activated as cost allocation tags before they can appear in Cost Explorer or cost allocation reports. AWS also notes that tags can represent business categories such as application names or owners, and that tagging resources with an application name can help track the total cost of that application. Therefore, the company should activate the application and team tags as user-defined cost allocation tags. See [Organizing and tracking costs using AWS cost allocation tags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/cost-alloc-tags.html).

**C. Create a cost category for each application in Billing and Cost Management — Correct.**  
AWS Cost Categories help map AWS costs to an organization’s internal business structures. Cost categories can group costs into meaningful categories, such as teams or applications, and they appear in Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, AWS Cost and Usage Reports, and Cost Anomaly Detection. In Cost Explorer, a cost category appears as an additional billing dimension that can be used to filter or group costs. Creating cost categories for applications provides a structured way to allocate and report costs by application and team. See [Organizing costs using AWS Cost Categories](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/manage-cost-categories.html).

**F. Enable Cost Explorer — Correct.**  
AWS Cost Explorer is the AWS Billing and Cost Management tool for viewing and analyzing cost and usage. It supports cost and usage reports, filtering and grouping, historical analysis, and forecasting. Cost Explorer can display up to the last 13 months of cost data and forecast costs for the next 18 months, which satisfies the requirement to compare the last 12 months and forecast the next 12 months. See [Analyzing your costs and usage with AWS Cost Explorer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-what-is.html).

The other options are not correct:

**B. Activate the AWS generated cost allocation tags that represent the application and the team — Incorrect.**  
AWS-generated tags are defined, created, and applied by AWS. The scenario describes tags that represent the company’s own applications and teams, which are user-defined business tags. AWS-generated tags do not inherently represent the company’s application ownership or team structure.

**D. Activate IAM access to Billing and Cost Management — Incorrect.**  
Activating IAM access allows IAM users and roles to access the Billing and Cost Management console when they also have appropriate permissions. This is an access-control step, not the cost allocation and reporting mechanism requested by the question. The reporting requirements are met by activating the relevant cost allocation tags, defining Cost Categories, and using Cost Explorer. See [Overview of managing access permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/control-access-billing.html).

**E. Create a cost budget — Incorrect.**  
AWS Budgets is useful for setting cost or usage thresholds and receiving alerts, but the requirement is to generate reports that attribute monthly costs, compare the previous 12 months, and forecast the next 12 months. Cost Explorer, combined with cost allocation tags and Cost Categories, directly addresses those reporting and forecasting needs.

zh.question: 一家公司的工厂和自动化应用程序运行在单个 VPC 中。超过 20 个应用程序运行在 Amazon EC2、Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 和 Amazon RDS 的组合之上。该公司的软件工程师分布在三个团队中。每个应用程序都由这三个团队中的一个团队负责，并且每个团队负责其所有应用程序的成本和性能。团队资源带有表示其应用程序和团队的标签。这些团队使用 IAM 访问权限进行日常活动。公司需要确定每月 AWS 账单上的哪些成本可归属于每个应用程序或团队。公司还必须能够创建报告，以比较过去 12 个月的成本，并帮助预测未来 12 个月的成本。解决方案架构师必须推荐一种可提供这些成本报告的 AWS Billing and Cost Management 解决方案。哪组操作组合可以满足这些要求？（选择三项。）

options.A: 激活表示应用程序和团队的用户定义成本分配标签。
options.B: 激活表示应用程序和团队的 AWS 生成的成本分配标签。
options.C: 在 Billing and Cost Management 中为每个应用程序创建一个成本类别。
options.D: 激活对 Billing and Cost Management 的 IAM 访问权限。
options.E: 创建成本预算。
options.F: 启用 Cost Explorer。

zh.explanation:
公司需要一种成本分配和报告解决方案，能够将每月 AWS 费用归因到每个应用程序和团队，比较过去 12 个月的历史成本，并预测未来 12 个月的成本。正确选项是 **A、C 和 F**。

**A. 激活表示应用程序和团队的用户定义成本分配标签 — 正确。**  
应用程序和团队标签是公司创建并应用到其资源上的标签。AWS 将这些标签识别为 **用户定义** 标签，并且必须先将其激活为成本分配标签，它们才能显示在 Cost Explorer 或成本分配报告中。AWS 还指出，标签可以表示业务类别，例如应用程序名称或所有者；使用应用程序名称标记资源可以帮助跟踪该应用程序的总成本。因此，公司应将应用程序和团队标签激活为用户定义成本分配标签。请参阅 [Organizing and tracking costs using AWS cost allocation tags](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/cost-alloc-tags.html)。

**C. 在 Billing and Cost Management 中为每个应用程序创建一个成本类别 — 正确。**  
AWS Cost Categories 可帮助将 AWS 成本映射到组织的内部业务结构。成本类别可以将成本分组为有意义的类别，例如团队或应用程序，并会显示在 Cost Explorer、AWS Budgets、AWS Cost and Usage Reports 和 Cost Anomaly Detection 中。在 Cost Explorer 中，成本类别会作为额外的账单维度出现，可用于筛选或分组成本。为应用程序创建成本类别提供了一种结构化方式，用于按应用程序和团队分配与报告成本。请参阅 [Organizing costs using AWS Cost Categories](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/manage-cost-categories.html)。

**F. 启用 Cost Explorer — 正确。**  
AWS Cost Explorer 是 AWS Billing and Cost Management 中用于查看和分析成本与用量的工具。它支持成本和用量报告、筛选和分组、历史分析以及预测。Cost Explorer 最多可以显示过去 13 个月的成本数据，并预测未来 18 个月的成本，这满足了比较过去 12 个月并预测未来 12 个月的要求。请参阅 [Analyzing your costs and usage with AWS Cost Explorer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-what-is.html)。

其他选项不正确：

**B. 激活表示应用程序和团队的 AWS 生成的成本分配标签 — 不正确。**  
AWS 生成的标签由 AWS 定义、创建并应用。该场景描述的是表示公司自身应用程序和团队的标签，它们属于用户定义的业务标签。AWS 生成的标签并不天然表示公司的应用程序所有权或团队结构。

**D. 激活对 Billing and Cost Management 的 IAM 访问权限 — 不正确。**  
激活 IAM 访问权限允许 IAM 用户和角色在同时拥有适当权限时访问 Billing and Cost Management 控制台。这是一个访问控制步骤，而不是题目要求的成本分配和报告机制。通过激活相关成本分配标签、定义 Cost Categories 并使用 Cost Explorer，即可满足报告要求。请参阅 [Overview of managing access permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/control-access-billing.html)。

**E. 创建成本预算 — 不正确。**  
AWS Budgets 对于设置成本或用量阈值并接收提醒很有用，但要求是生成报告，用于归因每月成本、比较过去 12 个月并预测未来 12 个月。Cost Explorer 结合成本分配标签和 Cost Categories，可以直接满足这些报告和预测需求。

en.question: An AWS customer has a web application that runs on premises. The web application fetches data from a third-party API that is behind a firewall. The third party accepts only one public CIDR block in each client’s allow list. The customer wants to migrate their web application to the AWS Cloud. The application will be hosted on a set of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in a VPC. The ALB is located in public subnets. The EC2 instances are located in private subnets. NAT gateways provide internet access to the private subnets. How should a solutions architect ensure that the web application can continue to call the third-party API after the migration?

options.A: Associate a block of customer-owned public IP addresses to the VPC. Enable public IP addressing for public subnets in the VPC.
options.B: Register a block of customer-owned public IP addresses in the AWS account. Create Elastic IP addresses from the address block and assign them to the NAT gateways in the VPC.
options.C: Create Elastic IP addresses from the block of customer-owned IP addresses. Assign the static Elastic IP addresses to the ALB.
options.D: Register a block of customer-owned public IP addresses in the AWS account. Set up AWS Global Accelerator to use Elastic IP addresses from the address block. Set the ALB as the accelerator endpoint.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The application servers will run on EC2 instances in **private subnets**. Those instances reach the internet through **public NAT gateways**. The third-party API firewall allows only the customer's existing public CIDR block, so after migration the source public IPs seen by the third party must still come from that customer-owned range.

## Correct answer: B

**B. Register a block of customer-owned public IP addresses in the AWS account. Create Elastic IP addresses from the address block and assign them to the NAT gateways in the VPC.**

This is the correct design because outbound internet calls from instances in private subnets go through the NAT gateways. AWS documentation states that a NAT gateway lets instances in a private subnet connect to services outside the VPC, and for a **public NAT gateway**, the internet gateway maps the NAT gateway's private IPv4 address to the **Elastic IP address associated with the NAT gateway**. Therefore, the third-party API will see the NAT gateway Elastic IPs as the source addresses for outbound calls ([NAT gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html)).

AWS also documents that, after bringing a customer-owned IPv4 range to AWS, the range appears as an address pool and you can create Elastic IP addresses from that pool for AWS resources. Specifically, BYOIP Elastic IPs can be used with **NAT gateways** ([Use your BYOIP address range in Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/byoip-working-with.html)). Thus, registering the customer's public CIDR block and allocating EIPs from that pool to the NAT gateways preserves an allow-listable public source range for the private EC2 instances' outbound API traffic.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Associate customer-owned public IPs to the VPC and enable public IP addressing for public subnets

This does not solve the problem. The application EC2 instances are in **private subnets**, not public subnets, and their outbound internet access is through NAT gateways. Enabling public IP addressing on public subnets would not make the private instances' outbound traffic use the customer-owned CIDR. The relevant source public IP for the third-party API is the NAT gateway EIP, not public subnet auto-assigned addresses.

### C. Create customer-owned Elastic IPs and assign the static Elastic IPs to the ALB

This is wrong for two reasons. First, the third-party API calls are **outbound** from the private EC2 instances, not inbound through the ALB. The ALB's public-facing address is used by clients reaching the web application, not by the application servers when they initiate outbound connections to the API. Second, Elastic Load Balancing documentation indicates that clients resolve a load balancer DNS name to load balancer node IPs; optional Elastic IP association is described for **Network Load Balancers**, not Application Load Balancers ([How Elastic Load Balancing works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html)).

### D. Register customer-owned public IPs and use AWS Global Accelerator with the ALB as endpoint

Global Accelerator in front of the ALB would affect **inbound** client traffic to the ALB, not the source IP used by EC2 instances making outbound calls to the third-party API. The outbound path from private instances still uses the NAT gateways. Therefore, this does not ensure that the third-party firewall sees the customer-owned CIDR as the source for API requests.

## Conclusion

The source public addresses for outbound internet traffic from private EC2 instances are the NAT gateway Elastic IP addresses. To continue using the customer's third-party allow-listed CIDR, bring/register the customer-owned IP block in AWS, allocate Elastic IPs from that BYOIP pool, and associate those EIPs with the public NAT gateways. **Answer B is correct.**

zh.question: 一位 AWS 客户有一个在本地运行的 Web 应用程序。该 Web 应用程序从位于防火墙后面的第三方 API 获取数据。该第三方在每个客户端的允许列表中只接受一个公有 CIDR 块。客户希望将其 Web 应用程序迁移到 AWS Cloud。该应用程序将托管在 VPC 中位于 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面的一组 Amazon EC2 实例上。ALB 位于公有子网中。EC2 实例位于私有子网中。NAT gateways 为私有子网提供互联网访问。解决方案架构师应如何确保 Web 应用程序在迁移后可以继续调用第三方 API？

options.A: 将一块客户自有的公有 IP 地址关联到 VPC。为 VPC 中的公有子网启用公有 IP 寻址。
options.B: 在 AWS 账户中注册一块客户自有的公有 IP 地址。基于该地址块创建 Elastic IP 地址，并将其分配给 VPC 中的 NAT gateways。
options.C: 基于客户自有 IP 地址块创建 Elastic IP 地址。将静态 Elastic IP 地址分配给 ALB。
options.D: 在 AWS 账户中注册一块客户自有的公有 IP 地址。设置 AWS Global Accelerator 以使用该地址块中的 Elastic IP 地址。将 ALB 设置为加速器端点。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

应用程序服务器将在 **私有子网** 中的 EC2 实例上运行。这些实例通过 **public NAT gateways** 访问互联网。第三方 API 防火墙只允许客户现有的公有 CIDR 块，因此迁移后第三方看到的源公有 IP 仍必须来自该客户自有范围。

## 正确答案：B

**B. 在 AWS 账户中注册一块客户自有的公有 IP 地址。基于该地址块创建 Elastic IP 地址，并将其分配给 VPC 中的 NAT gateways。**

这是正确的设计，因为来自私有子网中实例的出站互联网调用会通过 NAT gateways。AWS 文档说明，NAT gateway 允许私有子网中的实例连接到 VPC 外部的服务；对于 **public NAT gateway**，internet gateway 会将 NAT gateway 的私有 IPv4 地址映射到 **与 NAT gateway 关联的 Elastic IP address**。因此，第三方 API 会看到 NAT gateway 的 Elastic IP 作为出站调用的源地址（[NAT gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html)）。

AWS 还在文档中说明，在将客户自有 IPv4 范围带入 AWS 后，该范围会显示为一个地址池，你可以从该池中为 AWS 资源创建 Elastic IP 地址。具体来说，BYOIP Elastic IPs 可用于 **NAT gateways**（[Use your BYOIP address range in Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/byoip-working-with.html)）。因此，注册客户的公有 CIDR 块，并从该池中分配 EIP 给 NAT gateways，可以为私有 EC2 实例的出站 API 流量保留一个可加入允许列表的公有源地址范围。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. 将客户自有公有 IP 关联到 VPC，并为公有子网启用公有 IP 寻址

这不能解决问题。应用程序 EC2 实例位于 **私有子网**，而不是公有子网，并且它们的出站互联网访问通过 NAT gateways。为公有子网启用公有 IP 寻址不会让私有实例的出站流量使用客户自有 CIDR。第三方 API 关注的相关源公有 IP 是 NAT gateway EIP，而不是公有子网自动分配的地址。

### C. 创建客户自有 Elastic IP，并将静态 Elastic IP 分配给 ALB

这有两个原因是错误的。首先，第三方 API 调用是来自私有 EC2 实例的 **出站** 调用，而不是通过 ALB 的入站调用。ALB 的面向公有网络地址用于客户端访问 Web 应用程序，而不是应用程序服务器发起到 API 的出站连接时使用。其次，Elastic Load Balancing 文档表明，客户端会将负载均衡器 DNS 名称解析为负载均衡器节点 IP；可选的 Elastic IP 关联是针对 **Network Load Balancers** 描述的，而不是 Application Load Balancers（[How Elastic Load Balancing works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html)）。

### D. 注册客户自有公有 IP，并使用 AWS Global Accelerator，将 ALB 作为端点

在 ALB 前面使用 Global Accelerator 会影响到达 ALB 的 **入站** 客户端流量，而不会影响 EC2 实例向第三方 API 发起出站调用时使用的源 IP。来自私有实例的出站路径仍然使用 NAT gateways。因此，这无法确保第三方防火墙看到客户自有 CIDR 作为 API 请求的源。

## 结论

来自私有 EC2 实例的出站互联网流量的源公有地址是 NAT gateway Elastic IP 地址。要继续使用客户已加入第三方允许列表的 CIDR，请在 AWS 中带入/注册客户自有 IP 块，从该 BYOIP 池中分配 Elastic IP，并将这些 EIP 与 public NAT gateways 关联。**答案 B 是正确的。**

options.A: Add s3:CreateBucket with “Allow” effect to the SCP.
options.B: Remove the account from the OU, and attach the SCP directly to account 1111-1111-1111.
options.C: Instruct the developers to add Amazon S3 permissions to their IAM entities.
options.D: Remove the SCP from account 1111-1111-1111.

en.explanation:
The question is testing the difference between an AWS Organizations service control policy (SCP) and IAM permissions inside a member account. The attached SCP allows all actions except `cloudtrail:*`. Therefore, `s3:CreateBucket` is within the maximum permissions allowed by the SCP. However, that does **not** mean the developers automatically have permission to create S3 buckets.

**Correct answer: C. Instruct the developers to add Amazon S3 permissions to their IAM entities.**

AWS documentation states that an SCP **never grants permissions**. SCPs define the **maximum available permissions** for IAM users and roles in member accounts. The same documentation also states that users and roles must still be granted permissions through appropriate IAM permission policies, and that a user without IAM permission policies has no access even if the applicable SCPs allow all services and actions ([AWS Organizations SCP effects on permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)).

In this scenario, the SCP does not deny S3. It explicitly denies only CloudTrail actions. If the developers cannot create S3 buckets, the likely missing piece is an IAM identity-based policy, group policy, role policy, or other applicable permission that allows `s3:CreateBucket`.

### Why the other options are incorrect

- **A. Add `s3:CreateBucket` with “Allow” effect to the SCP.**  
  Incorrect. The SCP already has `"Action": "*"` with `"Effect": "Allow"`, so `s3:CreateBucket` is already allowed by the SCP guardrail. Also, adding an Allow to an SCP would still not grant the developers the permission; IAM permissions are still required.

- **B. Remove the account from the OU, and attach the SCP directly to account 1111-1111-1111.**  
  Incorrect. Moving the same SCP from the OU level to the account level does not solve the problem. The SCP would still not grant permissions. The issue is not where the SCP is attached; the issue is that the developers need IAM permissions for S3.

- **D. Remove the SCP from account 1111-1111-1111.**  
  Incorrect. The current SCP is not blocking S3 bucket creation because it denies only CloudTrail actions. Removing the SCP would unnecessarily remove the intended CloudTrail guardrail and would not address missing IAM permissions in a controlled way.

Therefore, the administrator should ensure that the developers' IAM users, groups, or roles have an appropriate policy that allows Amazon S3 bucket creation.

options.A: 向 SCP 添加 s3:CreateBucket，并将效果设为“Allow”。
options.B: 将该账户从 OU 中移除，并将 SCP 直接附加到账户 1111-1111-1111。
options.C: 指示开发人员向其 IAM 实体添加 Amazon S3 权限。

zh.explanation:
本题考查 AWS Organizations 服务控制策略（SCP）与成员账户内部 IAM 权限之间的区别。附加的 SCP 允许除 `cloudtrail:*` 之外的所有操作。因此，`s3:CreateBucket` 位于 SCP 允许的最大权限范围内。但是，这**并不**意味着开发人员会自动拥有创建 S3 存储桶的权限。

**正确答案：C. 指示开发人员向其 IAM 实体添加 Amazon S3 权限。**

AWS 文档说明，SCP **永远不会授予权限**。SCP 定义成员账户中 IAM 用户和角色的**最大可用权限**。同一文档还说明，仍必须通过适当的 IAM 权限策略向用户和角色授予权限，并且即使适用的 SCP 允许所有服务和操作，没有 IAM 权限策略的用户也没有访问权限（[AWS Organizations SCP 对权限的影响](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)）。

在此场景中，SCP 并未拒绝 S3。它只显式拒绝 CloudTrail 操作。如果开发人员无法创建 S3 存储桶，缺失的部分很可能是允许 `s3:CreateBucket` 的 IAM 基于身份的策略、组策略、角色策略或其他适用权限。

### 为什么其他选项不正确

- **A. 向 SCP 添加 `s3:CreateBucket`，并将效果设为“Allow”。**  
  不正确。该 SCP 已经包含 `"Action": "*"` 和 `"Effect": "Allow"`，因此 `s3:CreateBucket` 已经被 SCP 护栏允许。此外，向 SCP 添加 Allow 仍然不会向开发人员授予该权限；仍然需要 IAM 权限。

- **B. 将该账户从 OU 中移除，并将 SCP 直接附加到账户 1111-1111-1111。**  
  不正确。将同一个 SCP 从 OU 级别移动到账户级别并不能解决问题。SCP 仍然不会授予权限。问题不在于 SCP 附加在哪里；问题在于开发人员需要 S3 的 IAM 权限。

- **D. 从账户 1111-1111-1111 中移除 SCP。**  
  不正确。当前 SCP 并未阻止 S3 存储桶创建，因为它只拒绝 CloudTrail 操作。移除 SCP 会不必要地移除预期的 CloudTrail 护栏，并且无法以受控方式解决缺失 IAM 权限的问题。

因此，管理员应确保开发人员的 IAM 用户、组或角色具有允许创建 Amazon S3 存储桶的适当策略。

en.question: A company has a monolithic application that is critical to the company’s business. The company hosts the application on an Amazon EC2 instance that runs Amazon Linux 2. The company’s application team receives a directive from the legal department to back up the data from the instance’s encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume to an Amazon S3 bucket. The application team does not have the administrative SSH key pair for the instance. The application must continue to serve the users. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Attach a role to the instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Use the AWS Systems Manager Session Manager option to gain access to the instance and run commands to copy data into Amazon S3.
options.B: Create an image of the instance with the reboot option turned on. Launch a new EC2 instance from the image. Attach a role to the new instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Run a command to copy data into Amazon S3.
options.C: Take a snapshot of the EBS volume by using Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM). Copy the data to Amazon S3.
options.D: Create an image of the instance. Launch a new EC2 instance from the image. Attach a role to the new instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Run a command to copy data into Amazon S3.

en.explanation:
The company must copy data from the encrypted EBS volume of a running Amazon Linux 2 EC2 instance into an S3 bucket, but the team does not have the SSH key pair and the application must remain available.

**Correct answer: A. Attach a role to the instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to access the instance and run commands to copy data into Amazon S3.**

Session Manager is designed for this situation because it provides interactive shell or CLI access to managed EC2 instances without opening inbound ports, maintaining bastion hosts, or managing SSH keys. Access is controlled through IAM policies, so the lack of the administrative SSH key pair does not prevent authorized access through Systems Manager ([AWS Systems Manager Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager.html)).

An IAM role can be attached to an EC2 instance during or after launch, including when the instance is running. Therefore, the team can attach or update an instance profile that grants the required S3 write permissions, along with the permissions required for Systems Manager managed-instance access, without stopping the application ([Attach an IAM role to an instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/attach-iam-role.html)). After starting a Session Manager session, the team can run commands such as `aws s3 cp` or `aws s3 sync` from the instance to copy the mounted file-system data to the required S3 bucket while the application continues serving users.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. Create an image of the instance with the reboot option turned on.** This violates the availability requirement. The EC2 `CreateImage` API explains that when `NoReboot` is `false`, the instance is rebooted before the image is created so buffered data is written to the volumes. Option B explicitly uses the reboot option, which can interrupt the critical application ([CreateImage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_CreateImage.html)).

- **C. Take a snapshot of the EBS volume by using Amazon DLM. Copy the data to Amazon S3.** EBS snapshots are backups of EBS volumes, and they are stored in Amazon S3, but AWS stores them in S3 buckets that customers cannot access directly. The snapshots cannot be accessed through the Amazon S3 console or S3 API, so this does not create a file-level backup in the company’s S3 bucket as required ([Amazon EBS snapshots](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-snapshots.html)).

- **D. Create an image of the instance. Launch a new EC2 instance from the image.** This is also not the best fit because creating an AMI reboots the source instance by default unless `NoReboot` is explicitly set to `true`. The default for `NoReboot` is `false`, so the source instance is rebooted before image creation, which can disrupt the running application ([CreateImage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_CreateImage.html)). It is also unnecessarily indirect compared with copying the data directly from the existing running instance through Session Manager.

Therefore, **option A** is the only solution that satisfies all requirements: no SSH key pair is needed, the instance can continue running, the encrypted EBS volume’s mounted data can be accessed from the operating system, and the data can be copied into the company’s S3 bucket.

zh.question: 一家公司有一个对其业务至关重要的单体应用程序。该公司将该应用程序托管在一台运行 Amazon Linux 2 的 Amazon EC2 实例上。公司的应用团队收到法务部门的指示，要求将该实例的加密 Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) 卷中的数据备份到 Amazon S3 存储桶。应用团队没有该实例的管理员 SSH 密钥对。应用程序必须继续为用户提供服务。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 为该实例附加一个具有写入 Amazon S3 权限的角色。使用 AWS Systems Manager Session Manager 选项访问该实例，并运行命令将数据复制到 Amazon S3。
options.B: 在启用重启选项的情况下创建该实例的映像。从该映像启动新的 EC2 实例。为新实例附加一个具有写入 Amazon S3 权限的角色。运行命令将数据复制到 Amazon S3。
options.C: 使用 Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) 创建 EBS 卷的快照。将数据复制到 Amazon S3。
options.D: 创建该实例的映像。从该映像启动新的 EC2 实例。为新实例附加一个具有写入 Amazon S3 权限的角色。运行命令将数据复制到 Amazon S3。

zh.explanation:
公司必须将一台正在运行 Amazon Linux 2 的 EC2 实例的加密 EBS 卷中的数据复制到 S3 存储桶，但团队没有 SSH 密钥对，并且应用程序必须保持可用。

**正确答案：A. 为该实例附加一个具有写入 Amazon S3 权限的角色。使用 AWS Systems Manager Session Manager 访问该实例，并运行命令将数据复制到 Amazon S3。**

Session Manager 专为这种情况而设计，因为它可以在不打开入站端口、不维护堡垒主机或不管理 SSH 密钥的情况下，为托管 EC2 实例提供交互式 shell 或 CLI 访问。访问由 IAM 策略控制，因此缺少管理员 SSH 密钥对并不会阻止通过 Systems Manager 进行授权访问（[AWS Systems Manager Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager.html)）。

IAM 角色可以在 EC2 实例启动期间或启动之后附加到该实例，包括实例正在运行时。因此，团队可以附加或更新一个实例配置文件，授予所需的 S3 写入权限，以及 Systems Manager 托管实例访问所需的权限，而无需停止应用程序（[Attach an IAM role to an instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/attach-iam-role.html)）。启动 Session Manager 会话后，团队可以从实例运行 `aws s3 cp` 或 `aws s3 sync` 等命令，将挂载的文件系统数据复制到所需的 S3 存储桶，同时应用程序继续为用户提供服务。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **B. 在启用重启选项的情况下创建该实例的映像。** 这违反了可用性要求。EC2 `CreateImage` API 说明，当 `NoReboot` 为 `false` 时，实例会在创建映像之前重启，以便将缓冲的数据写入卷。选项 B 明确使用重启选项，这可能会中断关键应用程序（[CreateImage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_CreateImage.html)）。

- **C. 使用 Amazon DLM 创建 EBS 卷的快照。将数据复制到 Amazon S3。** EBS 快照是 EBS 卷的备份，并且它们存储在 Amazon S3 中，但 AWS 将它们存储在客户无法直接访问的 S3 存储桶中。这些快照无法通过 Amazon S3 控制台或 S3 API 访问，因此这不会按要求在公司的 S3 存储桶中创建文件级备份（[Amazon EBS snapshots](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-snapshots.html)）。

- **D. 创建该实例的映像。从该映像启动新的 EC2 实例。** 这也不是最佳选择，因为除非将 `NoReboot` 明确设置为 `true`，否则创建 AMI 默认会重启源实例。`NoReboot` 的默认值是 `false`，因此源实例会在创建映像之前重启，这可能会中断正在运行的应用程序（[CreateImage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_CreateImage.html)）。与通过 Session Manager 直接从现有运行实例复制数据相比，这种方法也不必要地间接。

因此，**选项 A** 是唯一满足所有要求的解决方案：不需要 SSH 密钥对，实例可以继续运行，可以从操作系统访问加密 EBS 卷中已挂载的数据，并且可以将数据复制到公司的 S3 存储桶。

en.question: A solutions architect needs to copy data from an Amazon S3 bucket m an AWS account to a new S3 bucket in a new AWS account. The solutions architect must implement a solution that uses the AWS CLI. Which combination of steps will successfully copy the data? (Choose three.)

options.A: Create a bucket policy to allow the source bucket to list its contents and to put objects and set object ACLs in the destination bucket. Attach the bucket policy to the destination bucket.
options.B: Create a bucket policy to allow a user in the destination account to list the source bucket’s contents and read the source bucket’s objects. Attach the bucket policy to the source bucket.
options.C: Create an IAM policy in the source account. Configure the policy to allow a user in the source account to list contents and get objects in the source bucket, and to list contents, put objects, and set object ACLs in the destination bucket. Attach the policy to the user.
