en.question: A financial services company in North America plans to release a new online web application to its customers on AWS. The company will launch the application in the us-east-1 Region on Amazon EC2 instances. The application must be highly available and must dynamically scale to meet user traffic. The company also wants to implement a disaster recovery environment for the application in the us-west-1 Region by using active-passive failover. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a VPC in us-east-1 and a VPC in us-west-1. Configure VPC peering. In the us-east-1 VPC, create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across multiple Availability Zones in both VPCs. Create an Auto Scaling group that deploys the EC2 instances across the multiple Availability Zones in both VPCs. Place the Auto Scaling group behind the ALB.
options.B: Create a VPC in us-east-1 and a VPC in us-west-1. In the us-east-1 VPC, create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across multiple Availability Zones in that VPC. Create an Auto Scaling group that deploys the EC2 instances across the multiple Availability Zones in the us-east-1 VPC. Place the Auto Scaling group behind the ALSet up the same configuration in the us-west-1 VPC. Create an Amazon Route 53 hosted zone. Create separate records for each ALEnable health checks to ensure high availability between Regions.
options.C: Create a VPC in us-east-1 and a VPC in us-west-1. In the us-east-1 VPC, create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across multiple Availability Zones in that VPCreate an Auto Scaling group that deploys the EC2 instances across the multiple Availability Zones in the us-east-1 VPPlace the Auto Scaling group behind the ALB. Set up the same configuration in the us-west-1 VPCreate an Amazon Route 53 hosted zone. Create separate records for each ALB. Enable health checks and configure a failover routing policy for each record.
options.D: Create a VPC in us-east-1 and a VPC in us-west-1. Configure VPC peering. In the us-east-1 VPC, create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across multiple Availability Zones in both VPCs. Create an Auto Scaling group that deploys the EC2 instances across the multiple Availability Zones in both VPCs. Place the Auto Scaling group behind the ALB. Create an Amazon Route 53 hosted zone. Create a record for the ALB.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company needs a web application in **us-east-1** that is highly available and dynamically scalable, plus a **disaster recovery environment in us-west-1** using **active-passive failover**.

## Correct answer: C

Option C is correct because it builds a complete regional stack in both Regions and uses Route 53 DNS failover to make **us-east-1 the active primary** and **us-west-1 the passive standby**.

The design has three required parts:

1. **High availability within each Region**: An ALB spans multiple Availability Zones, and AWS recommends enabling multiple AZs for load balancers. For Application Load Balancers, enabling at least two AZs is required, and this allows the load balancer to continue routing to healthy targets if one AZ fails ([Elastic Load Balancing documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html)).
2. **Dynamic scaling**: The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group behind the ALB. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can span an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones in the Region and attach a load balancer to distribute incoming traffic across those AZs ([EC2 Auto Scaling documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-add-az-console.html)). Auto Scaling groups can also be attached to target groups used by Application Load Balancers ([EC2 Auto Scaling documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/attach-load-balancer-asg.html)).
3. **Active-passive DR across Regions**: Route 53 failover routing is specifically designed for this pattern. In an active-passive configuration, Route 53 returns the healthy primary resource while it is available, and returns the healthy secondary resource when the primary becomes unhealthy. For one primary and one secondary resource, Route 53 uses records with the **Failover** routing policy ([Route 53 documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html)).

Therefore, creating an ALB and Auto Scaling group in **us-east-1**, creating the same stack in **us-west-1**, and configuring Route 53 health checks with failover routing records for the ALBs meets all requirements.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Incorrect

This option attempts to create a single ALB and Auto Scaling group that extend across multiple Availability Zones in both VPCs/Regions. That is not the right architecture for multi-Region DR. Auto Scaling groups are configured across Availability Zones **within the Region** they operate in, not as one group spanning two Regions ([EC2 Auto Scaling documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-add-az-console.html)). It also lacks Route 53 active-passive failover routing.

### B. Incorrect

This option correctly creates separate stacks in both Regions, but it only says to create records and enable health checks. It does **not** specify a Route 53 **failover routing policy** with primary and secondary records. Health checks alone do not define active-passive DNS behavior. Route 53 active-passive failover requires failover records so that Route 53 returns the primary record when healthy and the secondary record when the primary is unhealthy ([Route 53 documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html)).

### D. Incorrect

This option has the same cross-Region single-stack problem as option A and also creates only one Route 53 record for the ALB. It does not create separate primary and secondary records and does not configure failover routing. Therefore, it cannot implement active-passive disaster recovery between us-east-1 and us-west-1.

## Conclusion

**C** is the only option that provides:

- Multi-AZ ALB and Auto Scaling for high availability and dynamic scaling in each Region
- A separate standby deployment in us-west-1
- Route 53 health-based **active-passive failover** between the primary and secondary ALBs

zh.question: 一家位于北美的金融服务公司计划在 AWS 上向其客户发布一个新的在线 Web 应用程序。该公司将在 us-east-1 区域的 Amazon EC2 实例上启动该应用程序。该应用程序必须具备高可用性，并且必须能够动态扩展以满足用户流量需求。该公司还希望通过主动-被动故障转移，在 us-west-1 区域为该应用程序实施灾难恢复环境。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 us-east-1 中创建一个 VPC，并在 us-west-1 中创建一个 VPC。配置 VPC 对等连接。在 us-east-1 VPC 中，创建一个跨两个 VPC 中多个可用区的 Application Load Balancer (ALB)。创建一个 Auto Scaling 组，将 EC2 实例部署到两个 VPC 中的多个可用区。将该 Auto Scaling 组放置在 ALB 后面。
options.B: 在 us-east-1 中创建一个 VPC，并在 us-west-1 中创建一个 VPC。在 us-east-1 VPC 中，创建一个跨该 VPC 中多个可用区的 Application Load Balancer (ALB)。创建一个 Auto Scaling 组，将 EC2 实例部署到 us-east-1 VPC 中的多个可用区。将该 Auto Scaling 组放置在 ALB 后面。在 us-west-1 VPC 中设置相同的配置。创建一个 Amazon Route 53 托管区域。为每个 ALB 创建单独的记录。启用运行状况检查，以确保区域之间的高可用性。
options.C: 在 us-east-1 中创建一个 VPC，并在 us-west-1 中创建一个 VPC。在 us-east-1 VPC 中，创建一个跨该 VPC 中多个可用区的 Application Load Balancer (ALB)。创建一个 Auto Scaling 组，将 EC2 实例部署到 us-east-1 VPC 中的多个可用区。将该 Auto Scaling 组放置在 ALB 后面。在 us-west-1 VPC 中设置相同的配置。创建一个 Amazon Route 53 托管区域。为每个 ALB 创建单独的记录。启用运行状况检查，并为每条记录配置故障转移路由策略。
options.D: 在 us-east-1 中创建一个 VPC，并在 us-west-1 中创建一个 VPC。配置 VPC 对等连接。在 us-east-1 VPC 中，创建一个跨两个 VPC 中多个可用区的 Application Load Balancer (ALB)。创建一个 Auto Scaling 组，将 EC2 实例部署到两个 VPC 中的多个可用区。将该 Auto Scaling 组放置在 ALB 后面。创建一个 Amazon Route 53 托管区域。为该 ALB 创建一条记录。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该公司需要在 **us-east-1** 中运行一个具备高可用性且可动态扩展的 Web 应用程序，并且还需要使用 **主动-被动故障转移** 在 **us-west-1** 中建立一个 **灾难恢复环境**。

## 正确答案：C

选项 C 正确，因为它在两个区域中都构建了完整的区域级堆栈，并使用 Route 53 DNS 故障转移，使 **us-east-1 成为活动主站点**，**us-west-1 成为被动备用站点**。

该设计包含三个必需部分：

1. **每个区域内的高可用性**：ALB 跨多个可用区，AWS 建议为负载均衡器启用多个 AZ。对于 Application Load Balancers，必须至少启用两个 AZ，这样如果一个 AZ 发生故障，负载均衡器仍可继续将流量路由到运行状况良好的目标（[Elastic Load Balancing documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html)）。
2. **动态扩展**：EC2 实例位于 ALB 后面的 Auto Scaling 组中。Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling 可以让一个 Auto Scaling 组跨该区域中的多个可用区，并附加一个负载均衡器，以在这些 AZ 之间分发传入流量（[EC2 Auto Scaling documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-add-az-console.html)）。Auto Scaling 组也可以附加到 Application Load Balancers 使用的目标组（[EC2 Auto Scaling documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/attach-load-balancer-asg.html)）。
3. **跨区域主动-被动 DR**：Route 53 故障转移路由专为这种模式而设计。在主动-被动配置中，当主资源可用时，Route 53 返回运行状况良好的主资源；当主资源运行状况不佳时，则返回运行状况良好的辅助资源。对于一个主资源和一个辅助资源，Route 53 使用带有 **Failover** 路由策略的记录（[Route 53 documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html)）。

因此，在 **us-east-1** 中创建 ALB 和 Auto Scaling 组，在 **us-west-1** 中创建相同的堆栈，并为 ALB 配置 Route 53 运行状况检查和故障转移路由记录，可以满足所有要求。

## 其他选项为什么不正确

### A. 不正确

此选项尝试创建一个跨两个 VPC/区域中多个可用区的单一 ALB 和 Auto Scaling 组。这并不是适用于多区域 DR 的正确架构。Auto Scaling 组是在其运行所在区域**内**跨可用区进行配置的，而不是作为一个跨两个区域的组（[EC2 Auto Scaling documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-add-az-console.html)）。它还缺少 Route 53 主动-被动故障转移路由。

### B. 不正确

此选项正确地在两个区域中创建了单独的堆栈，但它只说明创建记录并启用运行状况检查。它**没有**指定带有主记录和辅助记录的 Route 53 **故障转移路由策略**。仅有运行状况检查并不能定义主动-被动 DNS 行为。Route 53 主动-被动故障转移需要故障转移记录，以便 Route 53 在主记录运行状况良好时返回主记录，并在主记录运行状况不佳时返回辅助记录（[Route 53 documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html)）。

### D. 不正确

此选项与选项 A 有相同的跨区域单一堆栈问题，并且只为 ALB 创建了一条 Route 53 记录。它没有创建单独的主记录和辅助记录，也没有配置故障转移路由。因此，它无法在 us-east-1 和 us-west-1 之间实现主动-被动灾难恢复。

## 结论

**C** 是唯一同时提供以下能力的选项：

- 在每个区域中使用 Multi-AZ ALB 和 Auto Scaling 实现高可用性和动态扩展
- 在 us-west-1 中部署单独的备用环境
- 在主 ALB 和辅助 ALB 之间基于 Route 53 运行状况的 **主动-被动故障转移**

en.question: A company has an environment that has a single AWS account. A solutions architect is reviewing the environment to recommend what the company could improve specifically in terms of access to the AWS Management Console. The company’s IT support workers currently access the console for administrative tasks, authenticating with named IAM users that have been mapped to their job role. The IT support workers no longer want to maintain both their Active Directory and IAM user accounts. They want to be able to access the console by using their existing Active Directory credentials. The solutions architect is using AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to implement this functionality. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on the IAM Identity Center feature in Organizations. Create and configure a directory in AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) with a two-way trust to the company’s on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and set the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory as the identity source. Create permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory.
options.B: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on the IAM Identity Center feature in Organizations. Create and configure an AD Connector to connect to the company’s on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and select the AD Connector as the identity source. Create permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the company’s Active Directory.
options.C: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on all features for the organization. Create and configure a directory in AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) with a two-way trust to the company’s on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and select the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory as the identity source. Create permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory.
options.D: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on all features for the organization. Create and configure an AD Connector to connect to the company’s on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and set the AD Connector as the identity source. Create permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the company’s Active Directory.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The company wants AWS Management Console access for IT support staff by using their existing on-premises Active Directory credentials, instead of maintaining separate named IAM users. The proposed service is AWS IAM Identity Center, and the question asks for the **most cost-effective** implementation.

## Correct answer: D

Option D is the best answer because it combines the required IAM Identity Center / AWS Organizations setup with the lower-cost way to use an existing on-premises Active Directory:

* AWS documentation says that AWS Organizations is recommended for IAM Identity Center, and that if IAM Identity Center is added to an organization, **all AWS Organizations features must be enabled**. The IAM Identity Center prerequisites state: “If you've already set up AWS Organizations and are going to add IAM Identity Center to your organization, make sure that all AWS Organizations features are enabled” ([IAM Identity Center prerequisites and considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/identity-center-prerequisites.html)). The IAM Identity Center and Organizations page repeats that all Organizations features should be enabled when adding IAM Identity Center to an organization ([IAM Identity Center and AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/identity-center-and-orgs.html)).
* IAM Identity Center can use Active Directory as an identity source. The documentation says you must have an existing **AD Connector** or AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory in AWS Directory Service, and that you can connect a self-managed Active Directory to IAM Identity Center ([Using Active Directory as an identity source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/gs-ad.html)).
* AD Connector is the more cost-effective fit when the company already has Active Directory and simply wants to authenticate users against it. AWS describes AD Connector as “a directory gateway” that redirects directory requests to on-premises Microsoft Active Directory without caching information in the cloud. It also allows end users and administrators to use existing corporate credentials and manage AWS resources through IAM role-based access to the AWS Management Console ([AD Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/directory_ad_connector.html)).

Therefore, creating an organization with all features enabled, configuring AD Connector to the existing on-premises AD, setting it as the IAM Identity Center identity source, and assigning permission sets to AD groups meets the requirements at the lowest cost among the choices.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A

Option A uses AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a two-way trust to the existing on-premises Active Directory. This can work technically, but it is not the most cost-effective choice for a single-account environment that already has an on-premises AD. It introduces a managed Microsoft AD directory in AWS instead of using AD Connector as a gateway to the existing directory.

### B

Option B correctly uses AD Connector, which is the cost-effective directory connectivity choice. However, it does not state that **all AWS Organizations features** are enabled. The AWS IAM Identity Center documentation specifically says that when adding IAM Identity Center to AWS Organizations, all Organizations features should be enabled. Because option D includes that requirement and still uses AD Connector, D is more complete.

### C

Option C correctly enables all AWS Organizations features, but it uses AWS Managed Microsoft AD with a two-way trust. Like option A, this adds an AWS managed directory where AD Connector would be sufficient to use the existing on-premises AD credentials. Therefore, it is not the most cost-effective solution.

zh.question: 一家公司拥有一个仅包含单个 AWS 账户的环境。解决方案架构师正在审查该环境，以建议公司可以在哪些方面进行改进，尤其是关于 AWS Management Console 的访问。公司的 IT 支持人员目前使用已映射到其工作角色的命名 IAM 用户进行身份验证，从而访问控制台执行管理任务。IT 支持人员不再希望同时维护其 Active Directory 和 IAM 用户账户。他们希望能够使用现有的 Active Directory 凭证访问控制台。解决方案架构师正在使用 AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) 来实现此功能。哪种解决方案能够以最具成本效益的方式满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 AWS Organizations 中创建一个组织。在 Organizations 中开启 IAM Identity Center 功能。创建并配置 AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) 中的目录，并与公司的本地 Active Directory 建立双向信任。配置 IAM Identity Center，并将 AWS Managed Microsoft AD 目录设置为身份源。创建权限集，并将其映射到 AWS Managed Microsoft AD 目录中的现有组。
options.B: 在 AWS Organizations 中创建一个组织。在 Organizations 中开启 IAM Identity Center 功能。创建并配置 AD Connector，以连接到公司的本地 Active Directory。配置 IAM Identity Center，并选择 AD Connector 作为身份源。创建权限集，并将其映射到公司 Active Directory 中的现有组。
options.C: 在 AWS Organizations 中创建一个组织。为该组织开启所有功能。创建并配置 AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) 中的目录，并与公司的本地 Active Directory 建立双向信任。配置 IAM Identity Center，并选择 AWS Managed Microsoft AD 目录作为身份源。创建权限集，并将其映射到 AWS Managed Microsoft AD 目录中的现有组。
options.D: 在 AWS Organizations 中创建一个组织。为该组织开启所有功能。创建并配置 AD Connector，以连接到公司的本地 Active Directory。配置 IAM Identity Center，并将 AD Connector 设置为身份源。创建权限集，并将其映射到公司 Active Directory 中的现有组。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

该公司希望 IT 支持人员使用其现有的本地 Active Directory 凭证访问 AWS Management Console，而不是维护单独的命名 IAM 用户。拟使用的服务是 AWS IAM Identity Center，题目要求选择**最具成本效益**的实现方式。

## 正确答案：D

选项 D 是最佳答案，因为它将所需的 IAM Identity Center / AWS Organizations 设置与使用现有本地 Active Directory 的较低成本方式结合起来：

* AWS 文档说明，建议将 AWS Organizations 用于 IAM Identity Center；并且如果将 IAM Identity Center 添加到组织中，**必须启用所有 AWS Organizations 功能**。IAM Identity Center 先决条件中说明：“If you've already set up AWS Organizations and are going to add IAM Identity Center to your organization, make sure that all AWS Organizations features are enabled”（[IAM Identity Center prerequisites and considerations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/identity-center-prerequisites.html)）。IAM Identity Center 和 Organizations 页面也重申，在向组织添加 IAM Identity Center 时，应启用所有 Organizations 功能（[IAM Identity Center and AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/identity-center-and-orgs.html)）。
* IAM Identity Center 可以使用 Active Directory 作为身份源。文档说明，您必须在 AWS Directory Service 中已有 **AD Connector** 或 AWS Managed Microsoft AD 目录，并且可以将自管理 Active Directory 连接到 IAM Identity Center（[Using Active Directory as an identity source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/gs-ad.html)）。
* 当公司已有 Active Directory，并且只是希望根据该目录对用户进行身份验证时，AD Connector 是更具成本效益的选择。AWS 将 AD Connector 描述为“a directory gateway”，它会将目录请求重定向到本地 Microsoft Active Directory，而不会在云中缓存信息。它还允许最终用户和管理员使用现有公司凭证，并通过基于 IAM 角色的 AWS Management Console 访问来管理 AWS 资源（[AD Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/directory_ad_connector.html)）。

因此，创建启用了所有功能的组织，配置连接到现有本地 AD 的 AD Connector，将其设置为 IAM Identity Center 身份源，并将权限集分配给 AD 组，可以在各选项中以最低成本满足要求。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A

选项 A 使用 AWS Managed Microsoft AD，并与现有本地 Active Directory 建立双向信任。这在技术上可行，但对于已经拥有本地 AD 的单账户环境而言，并不是最具成本效益的选择。它引入了 AWS 中的托管 Microsoft AD 目录，而不是使用 AD Connector 作为通往现有目录的网关。

### B

选项 B 正确使用了 AD Connector，这是具备成本效益的目录连接方式。但是，它没有说明已启用**所有 AWS Organizations 功能**。AWS IAM Identity Center 文档明确说明，当将 IAM Identity Center 添加到 AWS Organizations 时，应启用所有 Organizations 功能。由于选项 D 包含该要求，并且仍然使用 AD Connector，因此 D 更完整。

### C

选项 C 正确启用了所有 AWS Organizations 功能，但它使用 AWS Managed Microsoft AD 并建立双向信任。与选项 A 一样，这会添加一个 AWS 托管目录，而使用 AD Connector 就足以使用现有本地 AD 凭证。因此，它不是最具成本效益的解决方案。

en.question: A video streaming company recently launched a mobile app for video sharing. The app uploads various files to an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The files range in size from 1 GB to 10 GB. Users who access the app from Australia have experienced uploads that take long periods of time. Sometimes the files fail to completely upload for these users. A solutions architect must improve the app’s performance for these uploads. Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the S3 bucket. Configure the app to use the Transfer Acceleration endpoint for uploads.
options.B: Configure an S3 bucket in each Region to receive the uploads. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy the files to the distribution S3 bucket.
options.C: Set up Amazon Route 53 with latency-based routing to route the uploads to the nearest S3 bucket Region.
options.D: Configure the app to break the video files into chunks. Use a multipart upload to transfer files to Amazon S3.
options.E: Modify the app to add random prefixes to the files before uploading.

en.explanation:
## Scenario

The application uploads large video files (1–10 GB) from users in Australia to a centralized Amazon S3 bucket in `us-east-1`. The problem is long-distance upload latency and unreliable completion for large objects. The best solutions must improve upload speed and resiliency for large S3 uploads without changing the target architecture unnecessarily.

## Correct answers: A and D

### A. Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the S3 bucket. Configure the app to use the Transfer Acceleration endpoint for uploads.

This is correct. Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration is designed for fast transfers over long geographic distances. AWS states that Transfer Acceleration is useful when customers upload to a centralized bucket from all over the world, when transferring gigabytes to terabytes across continents, or when clients cannot use all available internet bandwidth when uploading to S3. The documentation also says that clients must use the `bucket-name.s3-accelerate.amazonaws.com` endpoint after Transfer Acceleration is enabled. This directly matches Australian users uploading multi-GB files to a centralized bucket in `us-east-1`.

AWS also describes Transfer Acceleration as using globally distributed CloudFront edge locations to accelerate data transport over geographical distances. See [Configuring fast, secure file transfers using Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/transfer-acceleration.html) and [Best practices design patterns: optimizing Amazon S3 performance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance.html).

### D. Configure the app to break the video files into chunks. Use a multipart upload to transfer files to Amazon S3.

This is correct. Multipart upload is a best practice for large objects. AWS states that multipart upload lets a client upload an object as independent parts, in any order, and if one part fails, only that part needs to be retransmitted. AWS also lists improved throughput through parallel uploads and quick recovery from network issues as key advantages. This directly addresses both symptoms: slow uploads and incomplete uploads.

For 1–10 GB files, multipart upload is strongly applicable. AWS recommends considering multipart upload when object size reaches 100 MB, and the multipart limits support objects far larger than this use case. See [Uploading and copying objects using multipart upload in Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html) and [Amazon S3 multipart upload limits](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/qfacts.html).

## Incorrect options

### B. Configure an S3 bucket in each Region to receive the uploads. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy the files to the distribution S3 bucket.

This is not one of the best answers. Regional buckets could reduce the distance for initial ingestion, but this option alone does not address the reliability and efficiency of uploading 1–10 GB files over the internet. It also introduces multi-Region bucket management and replication complexity. The question specifically involves improving upload performance to an S3 bucket in `us-east-1`; S3 Transfer Acceleration is the AWS feature designed for this centralized-bucket, long-distance upload pattern.

### C. Set up Amazon Route 53 with latency-based routing to route the uploads to the nearest S3 bucket Region.

This is not correct by itself. Route 53 latency-based routing can route DNS traffic to a lower-latency endpoint, but the scenario has a single S3 bucket in `us-east-1`. Routing users to a nearest Region would require additional regional upload endpoints or buckets and still would not solve large-object upload resiliency. It also does not replace multipart upload or S3 Transfer Acceleration for large uploads to a centralized S3 bucket.

### E. Modify the app to add random prefixes to the files before uploading.

This is not correct for the described problem. Randomizing prefixes can be relevant to distributing very high S3 request rates across prefixes, but the issue here is not S3 prefix hot-spotting or request-rate throttling. The problem is long-distance, multi-GB uploads that are slow or fail before completion. AWS S3 performance guidance emphasizes Transfer Acceleration for fast data transport over long distances and multipart upload for large-object throughput and resiliency; random prefixes do not directly address the Australia-to-`us-east-1` large upload failure pattern.

## Conclusion

The two solutions that directly address the requirements are:

- **A — S3 Transfer Acceleration** for faster long-distance uploads to the centralized S3 bucket.
- **D — Multipart upload** for parallelism, improved throughput, and recovery from partial network failures during large uploads.

zh.question: 一家视频流媒体公司最近推出了一款用于视频分享的移动应用。该应用将各种文件上传到 us-east-1 区域中的一个 Amazon S3 存储桶。文件大小从 1 GB 到 10 GB 不等。从澳大利亚访问该应用的用户遇到上传耗时很长的问题。有时这些用户的文件无法完整上传。解决方案架构师必须提升该应用在这些上传场景下的性能。哪些解决方案可以满足这些要求？（选择两项。）

options.A: 在 S3 存储桶上启用 S3 Transfer Acceleration。配置应用使用 Transfer Acceleration 端点进行上传。
options.B: 在每个区域配置一个 S3 存储桶来接收上传。使用 S3 Cross-Region Replication 将文件复制到分发 S3 存储桶。
options.C: 设置 Amazon Route 53，并使用基于延迟的路由将上传路由到最近的 S3 存储桶区域。
options.D: 配置应用将视频文件拆分成块。使用 multipart upload 将文件传输到 Amazon S3。
options.E: 修改应用，在上传前为文件添加随机前缀。

zh.explanation:
## 场景

该应用将来自澳大利亚用户的大型视频文件（1–10 GB）上传到位于 `us-east-1` 的集中式 Amazon S3 存储桶。问题是长距离上传延迟以及大型对象无法可靠完成上传。最佳解决方案必须在不必要地改变目标架构的情况下，提升大型 S3 上传的速度和弹性。

## 正确答案：A 和 D

### A. 在 S3 存储桶上启用 S3 Transfer Acceleration。配置应用使用 Transfer Acceleration 端点进行上传。

这是正确的。Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration 专为跨长地理距离的快速传输而设计。AWS 表示，当客户从世界各地上传到集中式存储桶、跨大洲传输数 GB 到数 TB 的数据，或客户端在上传到 S3 时无法使用所有可用互联网带宽时，Transfer Acceleration 很有用。文档还说明，在启用 Transfer Acceleration 后，客户端必须使用 `bucket-name.s3-accelerate.amazonaws.com` 端点。这与澳大利亚用户将多 GB 文件上传到 `us-east-1` 中的集中式存储桶的场景直接匹配。

AWS 还将 Transfer Acceleration 描述为使用全球分布的 CloudFront 边缘站点来加速跨地理距离的数据传输。请参阅 [Configuring fast, secure file transfers using Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/transfer-acceleration.html) 和 [Best practices design patterns: optimizing Amazon S3 performance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance.html)。

### D. 配置应用将视频文件拆分成块。使用 multipart upload 将文件传输到 Amazon S3。

这是正确的。Multipart upload 是大型对象的最佳实践。AWS 表示，multipart upload 允许客户端将对象作为独立部分上传，可以按任意顺序上传；如果某个部分失败，只需要重新传输该部分。AWS 还将通过并行上传提升吞吐量以及从网络问题中快速恢复列为关键优势。这直接解决了两个症状：上传缓慢和上传不完整。

对于 1–10 GB 文件，multipart upload 非常适用。AWS 建议在对象大小达到 100 MB 时考虑 multipart upload，并且 multipart 限制支持远大于此用例的对象。请参阅 [Uploading and copying objects using multipart upload in Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html) 和 [Amazon S3 multipart upload limits](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/qfacts.html)。

## 错误选项

### B. 在每个区域配置一个 S3 存储桶来接收上传。使用 S3 Cross-Region Replication 将文件复制到分发 S3 存储桶。

这不是最佳答案之一。区域存储桶可以缩短初始摄取的距离，但该选项本身并未解决通过互联网上传 1–10 GB 文件的可靠性和效率问题。它还会引入多区域存储桶管理和复制复杂性。题目明确涉及提升到 `us-east-1` 中某个 S3 存储桶的上传性能；S3 Transfer Acceleration 是 AWS 为这种集中式存储桶、长距离上传模式设计的功能。

### C. 设置 Amazon Route 53，并使用基于延迟的路由将上传路由到最近的 S3 存储桶区域。

该选项本身不正确。Route 53 基于延迟的路由可以将 DNS 流量路由到延迟较低的端点，但场景中只有一个位于 `us-east-1` 的 S3 存储桶。将用户路由到最近的区域需要额外的区域上传端点或存储桶，并且仍然无法解决大型对象上传的弹性问题。对于上传到集中式 S3 存储桶的大型文件，它也不能替代 multipart upload 或 S3 Transfer Acceleration。

### E. 修改应用，在上传前为文件添加随机前缀。

这不适用于所描述的问题。随机化前缀可能与在多个前缀之间分散极高 S3 请求率有关，但这里的问题不是 S3 前缀热点或请求速率节流。问题是长距离、多 GB 上传速度慢或在完成前失败。AWS S3 性能指南强调使用 Transfer Acceleration 在长距离上快速传输数据，并使用 multipart upload 提升大型对象的吞吐量和弹性；随机前缀并不能直接解决澳大利亚到 `us-east-1` 的大型上传失败模式。

## 结论

直接满足要求的两个解决方案是：

- **A — S3 Transfer Acceleration**：用于更快地将数据长距离上传到集中式 S3 存储桶。
- **D — Multipart upload**：用于在大型上传期间实现并行性、提升吞吐量，并从部分网络故障中恢复。

en.question: An application is using an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance in the us-east-1 Region. After a failover test, the application lost the connections to the database and could not re-establish the connections. After a restart of the application, the application re-established the connections. A solutions architect must implement a solution so that the application can re-establish connections to the database without requiring a restart. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v1 DB instance. Migrate the RDS DB instance to the Aurora Serverless v1 DB instance. Update the connection settings in the application to point to the Aurora reader endpoint.
options.B: Create an RDS proxy. Configure the existing RDS endpoint as a target. Update the connection settings in the application to point to the RDS proxy endpoint.
options.C: Create a two-node Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. Migrate the RDS DB instance to the Aurora DB cluster. Create an RDS proxy. Configure the existing RDS endpoint as a target. Update the connection settings in the application to point to the RDS proxy endpoint.
options.D: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Export the database to Amazon S3 by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Configure Amazon Athena to use the S3 bucket as a data store. Install the latest Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) driver for the application. Update the connection settings in the application to point to the Athena endpoint

en.explanation:
### What the question is asking

The application uses an **Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance**. During a failover, the database endpoint eventually points to the new primary/standby promotion, but existing client connections are interrupted. The problem is that the application cannot recover those database connections until the application process is restarted. The requirement is to allow the application to re-establish database connectivity after failover **without an application restart**.

### Correct answer: B

**B. Create an RDS proxy. Configure the existing RDS endpoint as a target. Update the connection settings in the application to point to the RDS proxy endpoint.**

Amazon RDS Proxy is designed for this situation. AWS states that RDS Proxy lets applications pool and share database connections and **makes applications more resilient to database failures by automatically connecting to a standby DB instance while preserving application connections**. It can be enabled for most supported applications with no code changes, and the application connects to the proxy endpoint instead of directly to the DB endpoint. See [Amazon RDS Proxy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.html).

This directly addresses the symptom in the question: after a Multi-AZ failover, the application should continue using the proxy endpoint and not require a full application restart to recover database connectivity.

Also, RDS Multi-AZ DB instance failover itself is expected behavior: AWS automatically switches to the standby replica in another Availability Zone, and failover typically takes 60–120 seconds. See [Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.Failover.html). RDS Proxy improves the application's resilience during this database-side failover event.

### Why the other options are incorrect

**A. Create an Aurora MySQL Serverless v1 DB instance and point the application to the Aurora reader endpoint.**

This does not solve the stated problem. The issue is application connection recovery after database failover, not the need to change database engines. In addition, a **reader endpoint** is for read traffic and would not be appropriate for a general application that needs to write to the database.

**C. Create an Aurora MySQL DB cluster, migrate the database, then create an RDS proxy.**

RDS Proxy is the relevant component, but migrating from RDS for MySQL to Aurora is unnecessary to meet the requirement. The existing RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance can use RDS Proxy directly. This option adds migration complexity and risk without being required.

**D. Export the database to Amazon S3 with DMS, query with Athena, and use an ODBC driver.**

This changes the architecture from an operational MySQL database to an S3/Athena analytics-style query model. It does not provide a transactional MySQL-compatible endpoint for the application and does not address automatic connection recovery after RDS Multi-AZ failover.

### Conclusion

The best solution is to place **Amazon RDS Proxy** between the application and the RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance and update the application to connect to the **RDS Proxy endpoint**.

**Answer: B**

zh.question: 某应用程序正在 us-east-1 区域中使用一个 Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ 数据库实例。在一次故障转移测试后，该应用程序丢失了与数据库的连接，并且无法重新建立连接。重启应用程序后，应用程序重新建立了连接。解决方案架构师必须实施一种解决方案，使应用程序无需重启即可重新建立与数据库的连接。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v1 数据库实例。将 RDS 数据库实例迁移到 Aurora Serverless v1 数据库实例。更新应用程序中的连接设置，使其指向 Aurora reader endpoint。
options.B: 创建一个 RDS proxy。将现有 RDS endpoint 配置为目标。更新应用程序中的连接设置，使其指向 RDS proxy endpoint。
options.C: 创建一个双节点 Amazon Aurora MySQL 数据库集群。将 RDS 数据库实例迁移到 Aurora 数据库集群。创建一个 RDS proxy。将现有 RDS endpoint 配置为目标。更新应用程序中的连接设置，使其指向 RDS proxy endpoint。
options.D: 创建一个 Amazon S3 bucket。使用 AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) 将数据库导出到 Amazon S3。配置 Amazon Athena 使用该 S3 bucket 作为数据存储。为应用程序安装最新的 Open Database Connectivity (ODBC) 驱动程序。更新应用程序中的连接设置，使其指向 Athena endpoint

zh.explanation:
### 题目在问什么

该应用程序使用一个 **Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ 数据库实例**。在故障转移期间，数据库 endpoint 最终会指向新的主实例/提升后的备用实例，但现有客户端连接会被中断。问题在于，应用程序在进程重启之前无法恢复这些数据库连接。要求是在故障转移后允许应用程序重新建立数据库连接，且**无需重启应用程序**。

### 正确答案：B

**B. 创建一个 RDS proxy。将现有 RDS endpoint 配置为目标。更新应用程序中的连接设置，使其指向 RDS proxy endpoint。**

Amazon RDS Proxy 正是为这种情况而设计的。AWS 表示，RDS Proxy 允许应用程序池化并共享数据库连接，并且**通过在保留应用程序连接的同时自动连接到 standby DB instance，使应用程序对数据库故障更具弹性**。对于大多数受支持的应用程序，它可以在无需更改代码的情况下启用，并且应用程序连接到 proxy endpoint，而不是直接连接到 DB endpoint。参见 [Amazon RDS Proxy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/rds-proxy.html)。

这直接解决了题目中的症状：在 Multi-AZ 故障转移后，应用程序应继续使用 proxy endpoint，而无需完整重启应用程序来恢复数据库连接。

此外，RDS Multi-AZ 数据库实例故障转移本身是预期行为：AWS 会自动切换到另一个 Availability Zone 中的备用副本，故障转移通常需要 60–120 秒。参见 [Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.Failover.html)。RDS Proxy 可在此数据库端故障转移事件期间提高应用程序的弹性。

### 为什么其他选项不正确

**A. 创建一个 Aurora MySQL Serverless v1 数据库实例，并将应用程序指向 Aurora reader endpoint。**

这不能解决所述问题。问题是数据库故障转移后的应用程序连接恢复，而不是需要更改数据库引擎。此外，**reader endpoint** 用于读取流量，不适用于需要写入数据库的一般应用程序。

**C. 创建一个 Aurora MySQL 数据库集群，迁移数据库，然后创建 RDS proxy。**

RDS Proxy 是相关组件，但为了满足要求，不需要从 RDS for MySQL 迁移到 Aurora。现有的 RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ 数据库实例可以直接使用 RDS Proxy。此选项增加了迁移复杂性和风险，而并非必需。

**D. 使用 DMS 将数据库导出到 Amazon S3，通过 Athena 查询，并使用 ODBC 驱动程序。**

这会将架构从运营型 MySQL 数据库改为 S3/Athena 分析式查询模型。它不会为应用程序提供事务型 MySQL 兼容 endpoint，也无法解决 RDS Multi-AZ 故障转移后的自动连接恢复问题。

### 结论

最佳解决方案是在应用程序与 RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ 数据库实例之间放置 **Amazon RDS Proxy**，并更新应用程序以连接到 **RDS Proxy endpoint**。

**答案：B**

en.question: A company is building a solution in the AWS Cloud. Thousands or devices will connect to the solution and send data. Each device needs to be able to send and receive data in real time over the MQTT protocol. Each device must authenticate by using a unique X.509 certificate. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Set up AWS IoT Core. For each device, create a corresponding Amazon MQ queue and provision a certificate. Connect each device to Amazon MQ.
options.B: Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and configure it with an AWS Lambda authorizer. Run an MQTT broker on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Set the Auto Scaling group as the target for the NLConnect each device to the NLB.
options.C: Set up AWS IoT Core. For each device, create a corresponding AWS IoT thing and provision a certificate. Connect each device to AWS IoT Core.
options.D: Set up an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API and a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Create integration between API Gateway and the NLB. Configure a mutual TLS certificate authorizer on the HTTP API. Run an MQTT broker on an Amazon EC2 instance that the NLB targets. Connect each device to the NLB.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company has **thousands of devices** that must communicate **bidirectionally in real time** using **MQTT**, and each device must authenticate with a **unique X.509 certificate**. The key design criterion is **least operational overhead**.

## Correct answer: C

**C. Set up AWS IoT Core. For each device, create a corresponding AWS IoT thing and provision a certificate. Connect each device to AWS IoT Core.**

AWS IoT Core is the purpose-built managed AWS service for this requirement. The AWS documentation states that AWS IoT Core supports **MQTT** and **MQTT over WSS**, and that the AWS IoT Core message broker supports devices and clients that use MQTT to publish and subscribe to messages ([What is AWS IoT?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-iot.html)). AWS also documents that devices connect through AWS IoT Core, send and receive messages using account-specific device endpoints, and that the AWS IoT Device SDKs support device communication using MQTT and WSS ([Connect devices to AWS IoT](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-connect-devices.html)).

For authentication, AWS IoT device connections use **X.509 client certificates**. The same AWS documentation states that device connections to AWS IoT use X.509 client certificates and AWS Signature Version 4 for authentication ([Connect devices to AWS IoT](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-connect-devices.html)). AWS IoT also supports associating device certificates with IoT things: AWS documentation explains that a certificate authenticates a device with AWS IoT so that it can connect, and attaching the certificate to a thing resource establishes the relationship between the device and the thing resource ([Attach a thing or policy to a client certificate](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/attach-to-cert.html)).

Because AWS IoT Core provides the managed message broker, device endpoints, MQTT support, certificate-based authentication, thing registry, policies, and fleet/device management capabilities, it avoids the operational burden of running and scaling custom MQTT brokers or creating per-device queues. Therefore, option C best meets all requirements with the least operational overhead.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. AWS IoT Core plus one Amazon MQ queue per device

This option incorrectly adds **Amazon MQ queues for each device** and says to connect each device to Amazon MQ. Amazon MQ is a managed message broker service, but it is not the purpose-built IoT device connectivity layer in AWS. Creating and managing a queue per device for thousands of devices would add unnecessary operational overhead and does not use the native AWS IoT Core device registry, IoT thing model, and certificate-to-thing association. AWS IoT Core already provides the MQTT message broker for device publish/subscribe communication, so Amazon MQ is unnecessary.

### B. NLB, Lambda authorizer, and self-managed MQTT broker on EC2

This option requires operating an MQTT broker fleet on EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer, including scaling, patching, broker configuration, high availability, certificate/authentication integration, monitoring, and capacity management. That is significantly more operational overhead than using AWS IoT Core, which is already a managed device connectivity and MQTT broker service.

### D. API Gateway HTTP API, NLB, mutual TLS, and MQTT broker on EC2

This option is also overly complex and mismatched. API Gateway HTTP APIs and mutual TLS can help authenticate HTTP clients, but the requirement is real-time MQTT communication. The option still requires running an MQTT broker on EC2 and managing the NLB and integration path. It does not provide the managed IoT device registry, thing/certificate relationship, IoT policies, or native managed MQTT broker capabilities of AWS IoT Core.

## Conclusion

Use **AWS IoT Core with IoT things and unique X.509 certificates** for each device. It natively supports MQTT communication and certificate-based device authentication with the lowest operational overhead.

**Answer: C**

zh.question: 一家公司正在 AWS Cloud 中构建一个解决方案。数千台设备将连接到该解决方案并发送数据。每台设备都需要能够通过 MQTT 协议实时发送和接收数据。每台设备都必须使用唯一的 X.509 证书进行身份验证。哪种解决方案能够以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 设置 AWS IoT Core。为每台设备创建一个对应的 Amazon MQ 队列并预置证书。将每台设备连接到 Amazon MQ。
options.B: 创建 Network Load Balancer (NLB)，并使用 AWS Lambda 授权方对其进行配置。在 Auto Scaling 组中的 Amazon EC2 实例上运行 MQTT 代理。将该 Auto Scaling 组设置为 NLConnect each device to the NLB 的目标。
options.C: 设置 AWS IoT Core。为每台设备创建一个对应的 AWS IoT thing 并预置证书。将每台设备连接到 AWS IoT Core。
options.D: 设置 Amazon API Gateway HTTP API 和 Network Load Balancer (NLB)。在 API Gateway 和 NLB 之间创建集成。在 HTTP API 上配置 mutual TLS 证书授权方。在 NLB 所指向的 Amazon EC2 实例上运行 MQTT 代理。将每台设备连接到 NLB。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该公司有**数千台设备**，这些设备必须使用 **MQTT** 进行**实时双向**通信，并且每台设备都必须使用**唯一的 X.509 证书**进行身份验证。关键设计标准是**最少运营开销**。

## 正确答案：C

**C. 设置 AWS IoT Core。为每台设备创建一个对应的 AWS IoT thing 并预置证书。将每台设备连接到 AWS IoT Core。**

AWS IoT Core 是专为此需求构建的 AWS 托管服务。AWS 文档指出，AWS IoT Core 支持 **MQTT** 和 **MQTT over WSS**，并且 AWS IoT Core 消息代理支持使用 MQTT 发布和订阅消息的设备和客户端（[什么是 AWS IoT？](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-iot.html)）。AWS 还记录了设备通过 AWS IoT Core 连接，使用账户特定的设备端点发送和接收消息，并且 AWS IoT Device SDKs 支持使用 MQTT 和 WSS 进行设备通信（[将设备连接到 AWS IoT](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-connect-devices.html)）。

对于身份验证，AWS IoT 设备连接使用 **X.509 客户端证书**。同一 AWS 文档指出，设备连接到 AWS IoT 时使用 X.509 客户端证书和 AWS Signature Version 4 进行身份验证（[将设备连接到 AWS IoT](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-connect-devices.html)）。AWS IoT 还支持将设备证书与 IoT things 关联：AWS 文档解释说，证书用于向 AWS IoT 验证设备身份，使其能够连接；将证书附加到 thing 资源会建立设备与 thing 资源之间的关系（[将 thing 或策略附加到客户端证书](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/attach-to-cert.html)）。

由于 AWS IoT Core 提供托管消息代理、设备端点、MQTT 支持、基于证书的身份验证、thing 注册表、策略以及机群/设备管理功能，因此它避免了运行和扩展自定义 MQTT 代理或为每台设备创建队列所带来的运营负担。因此，选项 C 最能以最少的运营开销满足所有要求。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. AWS IoT Core 加上每台设备一个 Amazon MQ 队列

此选项错误地为**每台设备**添加了 **Amazon MQ 队列**，并要求将每台设备连接到 Amazon MQ。Amazon MQ 是一项托管消息代理服务，但它不是 AWS 中专为 IoT 设备连接而构建的连接层。为数千台设备创建和管理每台设备一个队列会增加不必要的运营开销，并且没有使用原生 AWS IoT Core 设备注册表、IoT thing 模型以及证书到 thing 的关联。AWS IoT Core 已经为设备发布/订阅通信提供了 MQTT 消息代理，因此 Amazon MQ 是不必要的。

### B. NLB、Lambda 授权方以及 EC2 上的自托管 MQTT 代理

此选项需要在 Network Load Balancer 后面的 EC2 实例上运营 MQTT 代理机群，包括扩展、修补、代理配置、高可用性、证书/身份验证集成、监控和容量管理。这比使用 AWS IoT Core 具有显著更多的运营开销，因为 AWS IoT Core 已经是一项托管的设备连接和 MQTT 代理服务。

### D. API Gateway HTTP API、NLB、mutual TLS 以及 EC2 上的 MQTT 代理

此选项也过于复杂且不匹配。API Gateway HTTP API 和 mutual TLS 可以帮助对 HTTP 客户端进行身份验证，但要求是实时 MQTT 通信。该选项仍然需要在 EC2 上运行 MQTT 代理，并管理 NLB 和集成路径。它不提供 AWS IoT Core 所具备的托管 IoT 设备注册表、thing/证书关系、IoT 策略或原生托管 MQTT 代理功能。

## 结论

为每台设备使用带有 IoT things 和唯一 X.509 证书的 **AWS IoT Core**。它原生支持 MQTT 通信和基于证书的设备身份验证，并具有最低的运营开销。

**答案：C**

en.question: A company is running several workloads in a single AWS account. A new company policy states that engineers can provision only approved resources and that engineers must use AWS CloudFormation to provision these resources. A solutions architect needs to create a solution to enforce the new restriction on the IAM role that the engineers use for access. What should the solutions architect do to create the solution?

options.A: Upload AWS CloudFormation templates that contain approved resources to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the IAM policy for the engineers’ IAM role to only allow access to Amazon S3 and AWS CloudFormation. Use AWS CloudFormation templates to provision resources.
options.B: Update the IAM policy for the engineers’ IAM role with permissions to only allow provisioning of approved resources and AWS CloudFormation. Use AWS CloudFormation templates to create stacks with approved resources.
options.C: Update the IAM policy for the engineers’ IAM role with permissions to only allow AWS CloudFormation actions. Create a new IAM policy with permission to provision approved resources, and assign the policy to a new IAM service role. Assign the IAM service role to AWS CloudFormation during stack creation.
options.D: Provision resources in AWS CloudFormation stacks. Update the IAM policy for the engineers’ IAM role to only allow access to their own AWS CloudFormation stack.

en.explanation:
The company wants to enforce two controls on the engineers' access role: engineers must provision infrastructure **only through AWS CloudFormation**, and CloudFormation must be able to create **only approved resources**.

**Correct answer: C.**

AWS CloudFormation can use a **service role** to perform stack operations. The AWS documentation states that a service role allows CloudFormation to make calls to stack resources on behalf of the user, and that if a service role is specified, CloudFormation uses that role's credentials instead of the user's credentials. It also notes that a service role can be used to explicitly specify the actions CloudFormation can perform, which might differ from what the user can do ([CloudFormation service role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-iam-servicerole.html)).

Therefore, the correct enforcement model is:

1. Give the engineers' IAM role permission to perform only the required CloudFormation stack actions, rather than direct permissions to create EC2, S3, IAM, or other resources.
2. Create a separate IAM service role for CloudFormation with permissions limited to provisioning the approved resources.
3. Configure CloudFormation stacks to use that service role.

This separates the engineers' permissions from CloudFormation's provisioning permissions. Engineers cannot directly provision resources outside CloudFormation, and CloudFormation can provision only what the service role allows. In a real implementation, the engineers' role would also need tightly scoped `iam:PassRole` permission for the specific CloudFormation service role, because AWS documentation states that users must have permission to pass the service role when specifying it for a stack ([CloudFormation service role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-iam-servicerole.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. Incorrect.** Storing approved templates in S3 and allowing access to S3 and CloudFormation does not fully enforce that engineers can provision only approved resources. Unless the IAM policy strictly requires specific template URLs or resource types, engineers could create or modify templates that include unapproved resources. AWS does provide condition keys such as `cloudformation:TemplateUrl` and `cloudformation:ResourceTypes` to restrict stack creation, but simply uploading templates to S3 and allowing S3/CloudFormation access is not sufficient enforcement ([Example IAM identity-based policies for CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/security_iam_id-based-policy-examples.html)).

- **B. Incorrect.** Giving the engineers' IAM role permissions to provision approved resources plus CloudFormation means the engineers could potentially provision those approved resources directly through the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, SDKs, or APIs, bypassing CloudFormation. This violates the requirement that engineers **must use CloudFormation**.

- **D. Incorrect.** Restricting engineers to their own CloudFormation stacks controls which stacks they can access, but it does not by itself ensure that the stacks contain only approved resource types. It also does not define a separate least-privilege service role for CloudFormation to enforce approved provisioning permissions.

Thus, option **C** is the best answer because it uses IAM and a CloudFormation service role to enforce both requirements: engineers use CloudFormation, and CloudFormation provisions only approved resources.

zh.question: 一家公司在单个 AWS 账户中运行多个工作负载。一项新的公司政策规定，工程师只能预置已批准的资源，并且工程师必须使用 AWS CloudFormation 来预置这些资源。解决方案架构师需要创建一个解决方案，以对工程师用于访问的 IAM 角色强制执行这一新限制。解决方案架构师应该如何创建该解决方案？

options.A: 将包含已批准资源的 AWS CloudFormation 模板上传到 Amazon S3 存储桶。更新工程师 IAM 角色的 IAM policy，使其仅允许访问 Amazon S3 和 AWS CloudFormation。使用 AWS CloudFormation 模板预置资源。
options.B: 更新工程师 IAM 角色的 IAM policy，授予仅允许预置已批准资源和使用 AWS CloudFormation 的权限。使用 AWS CloudFormation 模板创建包含已批准资源的堆栈。
options.C: 更新工程师 IAM 角色的 IAM policy，授予仅允许 AWS CloudFormation 操作的权限。创建一个新的 IAM policy，授予预置已批准资源的权限，并将该 policy 分配给一个新的 IAM service role。在创建堆栈期间将该 IAM service role 分配给 AWS CloudFormation。
options.D: 在 AWS CloudFormation 堆栈中预置资源。更新工程师 IAM 角色的 IAM policy，使其仅允许访问他们自己的 AWS CloudFormation 堆栈。

zh.explanation:
该公司希望对工程师的访问角色强制执行两项控制：工程师必须**只能通过 AWS CloudFormation**预置基础设施，并且 CloudFormation 必须能够**只创建已批准的资源**。

**正确答案：C。**

AWS CloudFormation 可以使用 **service role** 来执行堆栈操作。AWS 文档说明，service role 允许 CloudFormation 代表用户调用堆栈资源；如果指定了 service role，CloudFormation 会使用该角色的凭证，而不是用户的凭证。文档还指出，可以使用 service role 显式指定 CloudFormation 可以执行的操作，这些操作可能不同于用户可以执行的操作（[CloudFormation service role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-iam-servicerole.html)）。

因此，正确的强制执行模型是：

1. 仅授予工程师的 IAM 角色执行所需 CloudFormation 堆栈操作的权限，而不是授予其直接创建 EC2、S3、IAM 或其他资源的权限。
2. 为 CloudFormation 创建一个单独的 IAM service role，其权限限制为预置已批准的资源。
3. 配置 CloudFormation 堆栈以使用该 service role。

这将工程师的权限与 CloudFormation 的预置权限分离。工程师无法在 CloudFormation 之外直接预置资源，而 CloudFormation 只能预置 service role 允许的资源。在实际实施中，工程师的角色还需要针对特定 CloudFormation service role 的严格限定的 `iam:PassRole` 权限，因为 AWS 文档指出，用户在为堆栈指定 service role 时必须拥有传递该 service role 的权限（[CloudFormation service role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-iam-servicerole.html)）。

**其他选项错误的原因：**

- **A. 错误。** 将已批准的模板存储在 S3 中并允许访问 S3 和 CloudFormation，不能完全强制确保工程师只能预置已批准的资源。除非 IAM policy 严格要求特定的模板 URL 或资源类型，否则工程师可能会创建或修改包含未批准资源的模板。AWS 确实提供了诸如 `cloudformation:TemplateUrl` 和 `cloudformation:ResourceTypes` 之类的条件键来限制堆栈创建，但仅仅将模板上传到 S3 并允许访问 S3/CloudFormation，并不足以实现强制执行（[Example IAM identity-based policies for CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/security_iam_id-based-policy-examples.html)）。

- **B. 错误。** 授予工程师的 IAM 角色预置已批准资源以及 CloudFormation 的权限，意味着工程师可能会通过 AWS Management Console、AWS CLI、SDK 或 API 直接预置这些已批准资源，从而绕过 CloudFormation。这违反了工程师**必须使用 CloudFormation**的要求。

- **D. 错误。** 将工程师限制为只能访问他们自己的 CloudFormation 堆栈，可以控制他们能访问哪些堆栈，但它本身并不能确保堆栈只包含已批准的资源类型。它也没有定义单独的最小权限 CloudFormation service role 来强制执行已批准的预置权限。

因此，选项 **C** 是最佳答案，因为它使用 IAM 和 CloudFormation service role 来强制执行两个要求：工程师使用 CloudFormation，并且 CloudFormation 只预置已批准的资源。

en.question: A solutions architect is designing the data storage and retrieval architecture for a new application that a company will be launching soon. The application is designed to ingest millions of small records per minute from devices all around the world. Each record is less than 4 KB in size and needs to be stored in a durable location where it can be retrieved with low latency. The data is ephemeral and the company is required to store the data for 120 days only, after which the data can be deleted. The solutions architect calculates that, during the course of a year, the storage requirements would be about 10-15 TB. Which storage strategy is the MOST cost-effective and meets the design requirements?

options.A: Design the application to store each incoming record as a single .csv file in an Amazon S3 bucket to allow for indexed retrieval. Configure a lifecycle policy to delete data older than 120 days.
options.B: Design the application to store each incoming record in an Amazon DynamoDB table properly configured for the scale. Configure the DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL) feature to delete records older than 120 days.
options.C: Design the application to store each incoming record in a single table in an Amazon RDS MySQL database. Run a nightly cron job that runs a query to delete any records older than 120 days.
options.D: Design the application to batch incoming records before writing them to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the metadata for the object to contain the list of records in the batch and use the Amazon S3 metadata search feature to retrieve the data. Configure a lifecycle policy to delete the data after 120 days.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The workload ingests **millions of small records per minute** from globally distributed devices. Each record is **less than 4 KB**, must be stored durably, must be retrievable with **low latency**, and must be retained for **only 120 days**. The key architectural requirements are high write scale, low-latency item retrieval, and automatic expiration of ephemeral data.

## Correct answer: B

**B. Design the application to store each incoming record in an Amazon DynamoDB table properly configured for the scale. Configure the DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL) feature to delete records older than 120 days.**

DynamoDB is the best fit among the listed choices because it is a managed NoSQL database designed for high-scale operational workloads and low-latency key-value/document access. AWS describes DynamoDB as a fully managed, serverless NoSQL database with **single-digit millisecond performance at any scale**, and notes that it scales to support tables of virtually any size while maintaining consistent performance and high availability ([DynamoDB introduction](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html)).

The 120-day retention requirement is also directly addressed by DynamoDB TTL. AWS states that DynamoDB TTL is a **cost-effective method for deleting items that are no longer relevant**, using a per-item expiration timestamp, and that DynamoDB automatically deletes expired items without consuming write throughput in the source Region ([DynamoDB TTL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/TTL.html)).

Although DynamoDB may not be the cheapest raw storage service compared with S3, the question requires the **most cost-effective solution that meets all design requirements**, including low-latency individual record retrieval and very high-scale ingestion. Among the provided options, DynamoDB is the service purpose-built for that access pattern.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Store each record as a single `.csv` file in S3

S3 is durable and supports lifecycle expiration, but storing **millions of tiny objects per minute** as individual files is not the best design for low-latency indexed record retrieval. S3 is object storage, not a low-latency indexed record database. AWS documents that S3 can achieve small object latencies of roughly **100–200 milliseconds**, and recommends CloudFront or ElastiCache if single-digit millisecond latency is required ([S3 performance optimization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance.html)).

Also, S3 object metadata is not an indexed database structure for retrieving arbitrary records inside millions of small objects. This approach would create high request volume and operational/query complexity compared with DynamoDB.

### C. Store each record in a single RDS MySQL table and delete nightly

Amazon RDS MySQL is a relational database. It can be appropriate for transactional relational workloads, but this scenario describes a massive-scale key-value/time-series-like ingestion pattern with millions of small records per minute and simple retention-based expiry. DynamoDB is specifically designed to avoid the scaling and operational complexity of relational databases for such high-scale operational workloads, while providing consistent low-latency access ([DynamoDB introduction](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html)).

A nightly cron job to delete old rows also adds operational overhead and can create large delete workloads, locking/contention, or performance impact. DynamoDB TTL is a native feature for this exact retention requirement.

### D. Batch records into S3 and use object metadata to retrieve records

Batching records into S3 can reduce PUT request cost and may be attractive for archival or analytics workloads. However, this option does not satisfy the stated low-latency individual retrieval requirement as well as DynamoDB. S3 small object access latency is documented at roughly **100–200 milliseconds**, whereas DynamoDB is documented for **single-digit millisecond performance** ([S3 performance optimization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance.html), [DynamoDB introduction](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html)).

The option is also flawed because it proposes storing the list of records in S3 object metadata and using that metadata for retrieval. S3 user-defined metadata is limited: the `PUT` request header is limited to 8 KB, and user-defined metadata is limited to **2 KB** ([S3 user-defined metadata](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingMetadata.html)). That is not a viable index for batches containing many records.

## Conclusion

DynamoDB with TTL is the best answer because it directly supports high-scale ingestion of small records, low-latency item retrieval, and automatic expiration after 120 days. Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

zh.question: 一名解决方案架构师正在为一家公司即将发布的新应用程序设计数据存储和检索架构。该应用程序旨在从世界各地的设备每分钟摄取数百万条小记录。每条记录的大小小于 4 KB，需要存储在一个持久的位置，并且能够以低延迟检索。该数据是临时性的，公司只需将数据存储 120 天，之后即可删除。解决方案架构师计算得出，在一年期间，存储需求约为 10-15 TB。哪种存储策略最具成本效益，并且满足设计要求？

options.A: 将应用程序设计为把每条传入记录作为单个 .csv 文件存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中，以便进行索引检索。配置生命周期策略以删除超过 120 天的数据。
options.B: 将应用程序设计为把每条传入记录存储在针对该规模进行了适当配置的 Amazon DynamoDB 表中。配置 DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL) 功能以删除超过 120 天的记录。
options.C: 将应用程序设计为把每条传入记录存储在 Amazon RDS MySQL 数据库中的单个表内。运行每晚的 cron 作业，执行查询以删除任何超过 120 天的记录。
options.D: 将应用程序设计为在写入 Amazon S3 存储桶之前对传入记录进行批处理。更新对象的元数据，使其包含批次中的记录列表，并使用 Amazon S3 元数据搜索功能检索数据。配置生命周期策略以在 120 天后删除数据。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

该工作负载从全球分布的设备每分钟摄取**数百万条小记录**。每条记录**小于 4 KB**，必须持久存储，必须能够以**低延迟**检索，并且只需保留 **120 天**。关键架构要求是高写入规模、低延迟项检索，以及临时数据的自动过期。

## 正确答案：B

**B. 将应用程序设计为把每条传入记录存储在针对该规模进行了适当配置的 Amazon DynamoDB 表中。配置 DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL) 功能以删除超过 120 天的记录。**

在列出的选项中，DynamoDB 最适合，因为它是一种托管 NoSQL 数据库，专为大规模运行型工作负载和低延迟键值/文档访问而设计。AWS 将 DynamoDB 描述为一种完全托管的无服务器 NoSQL 数据库，在任何规模下都具有**个位数毫秒级性能**，并指出它可以扩展以支持几乎任意大小的表，同时保持一致的性能和高可用性（[DynamoDB 简介](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html)）。

120 天保留要求也可以由 DynamoDB TTL 直接满足。AWS 表示，DynamoDB TTL 是一种**用于删除不再相关的项目的经济高效方法**，它使用每个项目的过期时间戳，并且 DynamoDB 会自动删除过期项目，而不会消耗源区域中的写入吞吐量（[DynamoDB TTL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/TTL.html)）。

尽管与 S3 相比，DynamoDB 可能不是最便宜的原始存储服务，但题目要求的是**满足所有设计要求的最具成本效益的解决方案**，其中包括低延迟的单条记录检索和超大规模摄取。在给定选项中，DynamoDB 是为这种访问模式专门构建的服务。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. 将每条记录作为单个 `.csv` 文件存储在 S3 中

S3 具备持久性并支持生命周期过期，但将**每分钟数百万个微小对象**作为单独文件存储，并不是低延迟索引记录检索的最佳设计。S3 是对象存储，而不是低延迟索引记录数据库。AWS 文档说明，S3 可以实现约 **100–200 毫秒**的小对象延迟，并建议如果需要个位数毫秒级延迟，则使用 CloudFront 或 ElastiCache（[S3 性能优化](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance.html)）。

此外，S3 对象元数据并不是用于在数百万个小对象中检索任意记录的索引数据库结构。与 DynamoDB 相比，这种方法会产生高请求量以及运维/查询复杂性。

### C. 将每条记录存储在单个 RDS MySQL 表中，并每晚删除

Amazon RDS MySQL 是关系数据库。它可以适用于事务型关系工作负载，但此场景描述的是一种大规模键值/类时间序列摄取模式：每分钟数百万条小记录，以及简单的基于保留期的过期。DynamoDB 专门用于避免关系数据库在这种大规模运行型工作负载中的扩展和运维复杂性，同时提供一致的低延迟访问（[DynamoDB 简介](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html)）。

每晚使用 cron 作业删除旧行也会增加运维开销，并可能产生大量删除工作负载、锁定/争用或性能影响。DynamoDB TTL 是针对这一保留要求的原生功能。

### D. 将记录批处理到 S3 中，并使用对象元数据检索记录

将记录批量写入 S3 可以降低 PUT 请求成本，并且可能适合归档或分析工作负载。但是，与 DynamoDB 相比，此选项无法同样好地满足所述低延迟单条记录检索要求。S3 小对象访问延迟记录约为 **100–200 毫秒**，而 DynamoDB 的文档性能为**个位数毫秒级**（[S3 性能优化](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance.html)，[DynamoDB 简介](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html)）。

该选项还存在缺陷，因为它建议将记录列表存储在 S3 对象元数据中，并使用该元数据进行检索。S3 用户定义元数据是有限的：`PUT` 请求标头限制为 8 KB，用户定义元数据限制为 **2 KB**（[S3 用户定义元数据](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingMetadata.html)）。对于包含许多记录的批次来说，这不是可行的索引。

## 结论

DynamoDB 与 TTL 结合是最佳答案，因为它直接支持小记录的大规模摄取、低延迟项检索，以及 120 天后的自动过期。因此，正确答案是 **B**。

en.question: A retail company is hosting an ecommerce website on AWS across multiple AWS Regions. The company wants the website to be operational at all times for online purchases. The website stores data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Which solution will provide the HIGHEST availability for the database?

options.A: Configure automated backups on Amazon RDS. In the case of disruption, promote an automated backup to be a standalone DB instance. Direct database traffic to the promoted DB instance. Create a replacement read replica that has the promoted DB instance as its source.
options.B: Configure global tables and read replicas on Amazon RDS. Activate the cross-Region scope. In the case of disruption, use AWS Lambda to copy the read replicas from one Region to another Region.
options.C: Configure global tables and automated backups on Amazon RDS. In the case of disruption, use AWS Lambda to copy the read replicas from one Region to another Region.
options.D: Configure read replicas on Amazon RDS. In the case of disruption, promote a cross-Region and read replica to be a standalone DB instance. Direct database traffic to the promoted DB instance. Create a replacement read replica that has the promoted DB instance as its source.

en.explanation:
The scenario is an ecommerce site deployed across multiple AWS Regions with a database on **Amazon RDS for MySQL**. The question asks which listed option provides the highest database availability / disaster recovery capability among the choices.

**Correct answer: D. Configure read replicas on Amazon RDS, promote a cross-Region read replica during disruption, redirect traffic, and create a replacement read replica.**

Amazon RDS read replicas support cross-Region deployments. AWS documentation states that read replicas can be used for **implementing disaster recovery**, and that you can **promote a read replica to a standalone instance as a disaster recovery solution if the primary DB instance fails**. The promotion workflow in the documentation matches option D: promote the read replica, direct database traffic to the promoted DB instance, and create a replacement read replica with the promoted DB instance as its source. RDS uses asynchronous replication for read replicas, so this is not zero-data-loss HA, but among the given options it provides the fastest and most available cross-Region recovery pattern for RDS for MySQL. See [Working with DB instance read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html) and [Promoting a read replica to be a standalone DB instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Promote.html).

### Why the other options are incorrect

**A. Automated backups and promote an automated backup** — Incorrect. Automated backups are for restore/PITR, not something you “promote” like a read replica. AWS documentation says point-in-time restore **creates a new DB instance** without modifying the source DB instance. Restoring from backup is generally slower than failing over by promoting an already-running read replica, and it is not the highest-availability option here. See [Restoring a DB instance to a specified time for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIT.html).

**B. Global tables and read replicas on Amazon RDS** — Incorrect. “Global tables” is a **DynamoDB** multi-Region feature, not an Amazon RDS for MySQL feature. DynamoDB global tables automatically replicate DynamoDB table data across Regions, but this does not apply to RDS for MySQL. See [DynamoDB global tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html).

**C. Global tables and automated backups on Amazon RDS** — Incorrect for the same reason as B: global tables are for DynamoDB, not RDS for MySQL. Additionally, automated backups are a restore mechanism, not an HA failover mechanism.

Therefore, **D** is the best answer among the provided choices.

zh.question: 一家零售公司在 AWS 的多个 AWS 区域中托管一个电子商务网站。该公司希望网站始终能够用于在线购买。该网站将数据存储在一个 Amazon RDS for MySQL 数据库实例中。哪种解决方案将为数据库提供最高可用性？

options.A: 在 Amazon RDS 上配置自动备份。发生中断时，将自动备份提升为独立数据库实例。将数据库流量引导到提升后的数据库实例。创建一个替代只读副本，并将提升后的数据库实例作为其源。
options.B: 在 Amazon RDS 上配置全局表和只读副本。激活跨区域范围。发生中断时，使用 AWS Lambda 将只读副本从一个区域复制到另一个区域。
options.C: 在 Amazon RDS 上配置全局表和自动备份。发生中断时，使用 AWS Lambda 将只读副本从一个区域复制到另一个区域。
options.D: 在 Amazon RDS 上配置只读副本。发生中断时，将跨区域只读副本提升为独立数据库实例。将数据库流量引导到提升后的数据库实例。创建一个替代只读副本，并将提升后的数据库实例作为其源。

zh.explanation:
该场景是一个部署在多个 AWS 区域中的电子商务网站，数据库运行在 **Amazon RDS for MySQL** 上。题目询问在给出的选项中，哪一个可以为数据库提供最高的可用性/灾难恢复能力。

**正确答案：D. 在 Amazon RDS 上配置只读副本，在中断期间提升跨区域只读副本，重定向流量，并创建替代只读副本。**

Amazon RDS 只读副本支持跨区域部署。AWS 文档说明，只读副本可用于**实施灾难恢复**，并且如果主数据库实例发生故障，你可以**将只读副本提升为独立实例，作为灾难恢复解决方案**。文档中的提升流程与选项 D 一致：提升只读副本，将数据库流量引导到提升后的数据库实例，并创建一个以提升后的数据库实例为源的替代只读副本。RDS 对只读副本使用异步复制，因此这不是零数据丢失的 HA，但在给定选项中，它为 RDS for MySQL 提供了最快且可用性最高的跨区域恢复模式。请参阅 [Working with DB instance read replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html) 和 [Promoting a read replica to be a standalone DB instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Promote.html)。

### 为什么其他选项不正确

**A. Automated backups and promote an automated backup** — 不正确。自动备份用于还原/PITR，并不是像只读副本那样可以“提升”的对象。AWS 文档说明，时间点还原会**创建新的数据库实例**，而不会修改源数据库实例。从备份还原通常比提升一个已在运行的只读副本进行故障转移更慢，因此它不是这里最高可用性的选项。请参阅 [Restoring a DB instance to a specified time for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIT.html)。

**B. Global tables and read replicas on Amazon RDS** — 不正确。“Global tables”是 **DynamoDB** 的多区域功能，不是 Amazon RDS for MySQL 的功能。DynamoDB global tables 会跨区域自动复制 DynamoDB 表数据，但这不适用于 RDS for MySQL。请参阅 [DynamoDB global tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html)。

**C. Global tables and automated backups on Amazon RDS** — 不正确，原因与 B 相同：global tables 用于 DynamoDB，而不是 RDS for MySQL。此外，自动备份是一种还原机制，而不是 HA 故障转移机制。

因此，在提供的选项中，**D** 是最佳答案。

en.question: Example Corp. has an on-premises data center and a VPC named VPC A in the Example Corp. AWS account. The on-premises network connects to VPC A through an AWS Site-To-Site VPN. The on-premises servers can properly access VPC A. Example Corp. just acquired AnyCompany, which has a VPC named VPC B. There is no IP address overlap among these networks. Example Corp. has peered VPC A and VPC B. Example Corp. wants to connect from its on-premise servers to VPC B. Example Corp. has properly set up the network ACL and security groups. Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?

options.A: Create a transit gateway. Attach the Site-to-Site VPN, VPC A, and VPC B to the transit gateway. Update the transit gateway route tables for all networks to add IP range routes for all other networks.
options.B: Create a transit gateway. Create a Site-to-Site VPN connection between the on-premises network and VPC B, and connect the VPN connection to the transit gateway. Add a route to direct traffic to the peered VPCs, and add an authorization rule to give clients access to the VPCs A and B.
options.C: Update the route tables for the Site-to-Site VPN and both VPCs for all three networks. Configure BGP propagation for all three networks. Wait for up to 5 minutes for BGP propagation to finish.
options.D: Modify the Site-to-Site VPN’s virtual private gateway definition to include VPC A and VPC B. Split the two routers of the virtual private getaway between the two VPCs.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

Example Corp currently has on-premises connectivity only to **VPC A** through an AWS Site-to-Site VPN. VPC A is peered with **VPC B**, and there is no CIDR overlap. The requirement is for on-premises servers to access VPC B with the **least operational effort**.

The important limitation is that VPC peering is not a transit mechanism. AWS states that VPC peering does **not** support transitive peering, and specifically for edge-to-edge routing: if VPC A has a VPN connection to a corporate network, resources in VPC B **can't use the VPN connection** to communicate with that corporate network ([VPC peering basics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/vpc-peering-basics.html)). Therefore, simply relying on the existing VPN into VPC A plus the VPC peering connection to VPC B will not work.

## Correct answer: A

**A. Create a transit gateway. Attach the Site-to-Site VPN, VPC A, and VPC B to the transit gateway. Update the transit gateway route tables for all networks to add IP range routes for all other networks.**

This is the correct solution. AWS Transit Gateway acts as a Regional virtual router for traffic between VPCs and on-premises networks ([How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html)). AWS documentation also states that a transit gateway can be used to interconnect multiple VPCs and on-premises networks and can be the AWS-side VPN endpoint for Site-to-Site VPN ([What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html)).

Transit Gateway supports attaching **one or more VPCs** and **one or more VPN connections** ([How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html)). By attaching VPC A, VPC B, and the Site-to-Site VPN to the same transit gateway and configuring the transit gateway route tables, the on-premises network and both VPCs can route to each other through a central managed hub. This avoids building separate VPNs or unsupported peering transit paths, and it is the lowest-operational-effort scalable design.

## Incorrect options

### B. Create a transit gateway, create a Site-to-Site VPN connection between on-premises and VPC B, connect the VPN connection to the transit gateway, add routes and an authorization rule

This option is internally confused and not the least-effort design. A Site-to-Site VPN is established to an AWS-side **target gateway**, such as a virtual private gateway or transit gateway. AWS defines Transit Gateway as a transit hub that can interconnect VPCs and on-premises networks and act as the VPN endpoint ([What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html)). The correct design is to connect the VPN to the transit gateway and attach the VPCs to that gateway, not to create a VPN “between on-premises and VPC B” and then somehow use that VPN through a transit gateway.

Also, “authorization rule” terminology is associated with AWS Client VPN access control, not AWS Site-to-Site VPN routing. This option adds unnecessary complexity and does not describe the clean Transit Gateway hub-and-spoke design.

### C. Update route tables for the Site-to-Site VPN and both VPCs, configure BGP propagation for all three networks

This does not meet the requirement because VPC peering does not allow the on-premises VPN attached to VPC A to be used transitively by VPC B. AWS explicitly states that if VPC A has a VPN connection to a corporate network, resources in VPC B cannot use that VPN connection to communicate with the corporate network ([VPC peering basics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/vpc-peering-basics.html)).

Updating route tables or waiting for BGP propagation cannot overcome this architectural limitation. VPC peering is a direct one-to-one connection, not a transit router.

### D. Modify the Site-to-Site VPN virtual private gateway definition to include VPC A and VPC B, and split the virtual private gateway routers between the two VPCs

This is not a valid AWS architecture. AWS documentation defines a **virtual private gateway** as the VPN endpoint on the AWS side of a Site-to-Site VPN connection that can be attached to a **single VPC** ([What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html)). You cannot attach one virtual private gateway to multiple VPCs or split its routers between VPCs.

## Conclusion

Because VPC peering does not support transitive/edge-to-edge routing from VPC B through VPC A’s VPN, the least-operational-effort solution is to use **AWS Transit Gateway** as the central routing hub and attach the Site-to-Site VPN, VPC A, and VPC B.

**Answer: A**

zh.question: Example Corp. 拥有一个本地数据中心，以及位于 Example Corp. AWS 账户中的一个名为 VPC A 的 VPC。本地网络通过 AWS Site-To-Site VPN 连接到 VPC A。本地服务器可以正常访问 VPC A。Example Corp. 刚刚收购了 AnyCompany，后者有一个名为 VPC B 的 VPC。这些网络之间没有 IP 地址重叠。Example Corp. 已将 VPC A 和 VPC B 建立对等连接。Example Corp. 希望从其本地服务器连接到 VPC B。Example Corp. 已正确设置网络 ACL 和安全组。哪种解决方案能够以最少的运维工作量满足此要求？

options.A: 创建一个 transit gateway。将 Site-to-Site VPN、VPC A 和 VPC B 挂载到该 transit gateway。更新所有网络的 transit gateway 路由表，为所有其他网络添加 IP 范围路由。
options.B: 创建一个 transit gateway。在本地网络和 VPC B 之间创建 Site-to-Site VPN 连接，并将该 VPN 连接连接到 transit gateway。添加一条路由以将流量定向到已对等连接的 VPC，并添加一条授权规则以授予客户端访问 VPC A 和 VPC B 的权限。
options.C: 更新 Site-to-Site VPN 和两个 VPC 的路由表，以覆盖全部三个网络。为全部三个网络配置 BGP 传播。等待最多 5 分钟，直到 BGP 传播完成。
options.D: 修改 Site-to-Site VPN 的 virtual private gateway 定义，使其包含 VPC A 和 VPC B。将 virtual private getaway 的两个路由器拆分到这两个 VPC 之间。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

Example Corp 目前仅通过 AWS Site-to-Site VPN 与 **VPC A** 建立了本地连接。VPC A 与 **VPC B** 建立了对等连接，并且没有 CIDR 重叠。要求是让本地服务器以**最少的运维工作量**访问 VPC B。

重要限制是，VPC peering 不是一种传输机制。AWS 声明 VPC peering **不**支持传递式对等连接，尤其是对于 edge-to-edge routing：如果 VPC A 有到公司网络的 VPN 连接，那么 VPC B 中的资源**不能使用该 VPN 连接**与该公司网络通信（[VPC peering basics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/vpc-peering-basics.html)）。因此，仅依赖现有进入 VPC A 的 VPN 加上到 VPC B 的 VPC peering connection 是行不通的。

## 正确答案：A

**A. 创建一个 transit gateway。将 Site-to-Site VPN、VPC A 和 VPC B 挂载到该 transit gateway。更新所有网络的 transit gateway 路由表，为所有其他网络添加 IP 范围路由。**

这是正确的解决方案。AWS Transit Gateway 充当用于 VPC 与本地网络之间流量的区域虚拟路由器（[How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html)）。AWS 文档还说明，transit gateway 可用于互连多个 VPC 和本地网络，并且可以作为 Site-to-Site VPN 的 AWS 侧 VPN 端点（[What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html)）。

Transit Gateway 支持挂载**一个或多个 VPC**以及**一个或多个 VPN 连接**（[How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html)）。通过将 VPC A、VPC B 和 Site-to-Site VPN 挂载到同一个 transit gateway，并配置 transit gateway 路由表，本地网络和两个 VPC 可以通过一个集中管理的枢纽彼此路由。这避免了构建单独的 VPN 或不受支持的对等传递路径，并且是运维工作量最低的可扩展设计。

## 错误选项

### B. 创建 transit gateway，在本地和 VPC B 之间创建 Site-to-Site VPN 连接，将该 VPN 连接连接到 transit gateway，添加路由和授权规则

该选项内部逻辑混乱，并且不是工作量最少的设计。Site-to-Site VPN 是连接到 AWS 侧**目标网关**的，例如 virtual private gateway 或 transit gateway。AWS 将 Transit Gateway 定义为可以互连 VPC 和本地网络、并充当 VPN 端点的传输枢纽（[What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html)）。正确设计是将 VPN 连接到 transit gateway，并将 VPC 挂载到该网关，而不是创建一个“本地和 VPC B 之间”的 VPN，然后以某种方式通过 transit gateway 使用该 VPN。

此外，“authorization rule”术语与 AWS Client VPN 访问控制相关，而不是 AWS Site-to-Site VPN 路由。此选项增加了不必要的复杂性，并且没有描述清晰的 Transit Gateway hub-and-spoke 设计。

### C. 更新 Site-to-Site VPN 和两个 VPC 的路由表，为全部三个网络配置 BGP 传播

这不满足要求，因为 VPC peering 不允许 VPC B 传递式地使用挂载到 VPC A 的本地 VPN。AWS 明确说明，如果 VPC A 有到公司网络的 VPN 连接，VPC B 中的资源不能使用该 VPN 连接与公司网络通信（[VPC peering basics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/vpc-peering-basics.html)）。

更新路由表或等待 BGP 传播无法克服这一架构限制。VPC peering 是直接的一对一连接，而不是传输路由器。

### D. 修改 Site-to-Site VPN virtual private gateway 定义以包含 VPC A 和 VPC B，并将 virtual private gateway 路由器拆分到两个 VPC 之间

这不是有效的 AWS 架构。AWS 文档将 **virtual private gateway** 定义为 Site-to-Site VPN 连接在 AWS 侧的 VPN 端点，可挂载到**单个 VPC**（[What is AWS Site-to-Site VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/VPC_VPN.html)）。你不能将一个 virtual private gateway 挂载到多个 VPC，也不能将其路由器拆分到多个 VPC 之间。

## 结论

由于 VPC peering 不支持从 VPC B 通过 VPC A 的 VPN 进行传递式/edge-to-edge routing，因此运维工作量最少的解决方案是使用 **AWS Transit Gateway** 作为中央路由枢纽，并挂载 Site-to-Site VPN、VPC A 和 VPC B。

**答案：A**

en.question: A company recently completed the migration from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud by using a replatforming strategy. One of the migrated servers is running a legacy Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) service that a critical application relies upon. The application sends outbound email messages to the company’s customers. The legacy SMTP server does not support TLS encryption and uses TCP port 25. The application can use SMTP only. The company decides to use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) and to decommission the legacy SMTP server. The company has created and validated the SES domain. The company has lifted the SES limits. What should the company do to modify the application to send email messages from Amazon SES?

options.A: Configure the application to connect to Amazon SES by using TLS Wrapper. Create an IAM role that has ses:SendEmail and ses:SendRawEmail permissions. Attach the IAM role to an Amazon EC2 instance.
options.B: Configure the application to connect to Amazon SES by using STARTTLS. Obtain Amazon SES SMTP credentials. Use the credentials to authenticate with Amazon SES.
options.C: Configure the application to use the SES API to send email messages. Create an IAM role that has ses:SendEmail and ses:SendRawEmail permissions. Use the IAM role as a service role for Amazon SES.
options.D: Configure the application to use AWS SDKs to send email messages. Create an IAM user for Amazon SES. Generate API access keys. Use the access keys to authenticate with Amazon SES.

en.explanation:
The application can send email **only by using SMTP**, so the migration target must be the Amazon SES **SMTP interface**, not the SES API or AWS SDKs. Amazon SES SMTP connections also require TLS encryption, and SES supports two TLS connection mechanisms: **STARTTLS** and **TLS Wrapper**. For STARTTLS, the SMTP client connects to the SES SMTP endpoint on **port 25, 587, or 2587**, then upgrades the connection to TLS. TLS Wrapper uses different ports, **465 or 2465**. Amazon SES SMTP also requires an SMTP user name and password; these SMTP credentials are distinct from normal AWS access keys.

**Correct answer: B. Configure the application to connect to Amazon SES by using STARTTLS. Obtain Amazon SES SMTP credentials. Use the credentials to authenticate with Amazon SES.**

This matches the requirements precisely:

* The application remains SMTP-based, which is supported by Amazon SES through the SMTP interface.
