The company has a local Linux server that hosts an API that provides local feedback to the workers. How should the company deploy the ML model to meet these requirements?

options.A: Set up an Amazon Kinesis video stream from each IP camera to AWS. Use Amazon EC2 instances to take still images of the streams. Upload the images to an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy a SageMaker endpoint with the ML model. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to call the inference endpoint when new images are uploaded. Configure the Lambda function to call the local API when a defect is detected.
options.B: Deploy AWS IoT Greengrass on the local server. Deploy the ML model to the Greengrass server. Create a Greengrass component to take still images from the cameras and run inference. Configure the component to call the local API when a defect is detected.
options.C: Order an AWS Snowball device. Deploy a SageMaker endpoint the ML model and an Amazon EC2 instance on the Snowball device. Take still images from the cameras. Run inference from the EC2 instance. Configure the instance to call the local API when a defect is detected.
options.D: Deploy Amazon Monitron devices on each IP camera. Deploy an Amazon Monitron Gateway on premises. Deploy the ML model to the Amazon Monitron devices. Use Amazon Monitron health state alarms to call the local API from an AWS Lambda function when a defect is detected.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company has already trained an Amazon SageMaker model to detect defects from still images captured by IP cameras. The key design requirement is **local, on-premises inference and local feedback even when internet connectivity is unavailable**. The local Linux server also hosts the feedback API, so the best solution should run the image-capture, inference, and API-calling logic on premises.

## Correct answer: B

**B. Deploy AWS IoT Greengrass on the local server. Deploy the ML model to the Greengrass server. Create a Greengrass component to take still images from the cameras and run inference. Configure the component to call the local API when a defect is detected.**

AWS IoT Greengrass is designed for this exact edge-computing pattern. The AWS documentation states that Greengrass lets devices **act locally on generated data**, **run predictions based on machine learning models**, **react autonomously to local events**, and communicate with other devices on the **local network**. It also supports packaging and running software as components, Lambda functions, containers, native processes, or custom runtimes ([AWS IoT Greengrass overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/greengrass/v2/developerguide/what-is-iot-greengrass.html)).

For ML inference specifically, AWS IoT Greengrass supports deploying ML workloads to Greengrass core devices. The documentation describes model components, runtime components, and inference components, and explains that custom components can contain the model, runtime, and inference code. It also states that Greengrass supports custom-trained models stored in Amazon S3 and SageMaker AI edge packaging jobs for SageMaker Neo-compiled models ([Perform machine learning inference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/greengrass/v2/developerguide/perform-machine-learning-inference.html)).

Therefore, deploying Greengrass on the local Linux server, deploying the trained model as a Greengrass ML/model component, and creating a component that captures still images, performs inference, and calls the local feedback API satisfies all requirements, including operation during internet outages after the edge deployment is in place.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Kinesis Video Streams, S3, SageMaker endpoint, Lambda, and local API

This design sends camera streams and images to AWS, stores images in S3, invokes a cloud-hosted SageMaker endpoint, and uses Lambda to call back to the local API. It depends on internet connectivity for video upload, S3 upload, SageMaker endpoint invocation, and Lambda execution. If the factory internet connection is down, the solution cannot provide timely local feedback. This violates the core requirement.

### C. Snowball device with SageMaker endpoint and EC2

AWS Snowball Edge can provide edge computing capabilities such as local storage and EC2-compatible instances, as described in the Snowball Edge documentation ([What is Snowball Edge?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/whatisedge.html)). However, the option proposes deploying a **SageMaker endpoint** on the Snowball device. A SageMaker real-time endpoint is a managed SageMaker hosting capability in AWS, not the appropriate mechanism for deploying a trained model onto a local factory Linux server. This option is also unnecessarily heavy and does not use the existing local server. Greengrass is the AWS edge service intended for deploying components and ML inference logic to local devices.

### D. Amazon Monitron devices and Monitron Gateway

Amazon Monitron is not a general-purpose computer vision or custom SageMaker model deployment service. The documentation describes Monitron sensors as capturing **vibration and temperature data** from machines, and gateways as sending that data to the AWS Cloud ([Amazon Monitron components](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Monitron/latest/user-guide/monitron-components.html)). The scenario requires inference from **IP camera still images** using an already trained SageMaker image defect model, and local feedback during connectivity loss. Monitron is for equipment condition monitoring, not deploying a custom image-recognition model to IP cameras or a local server.

## Conclusion

The only option that provides local image capture, local ML inference, and local API integration while continuing to operate during internet outages is **B: AWS IoT Greengrass on the local server with a Greengrass ML inference component**.

zh.question: 一家制造公司正在为其工厂构建一套检测解决方案。该公司在每条装配线的末端都有 IP 摄像头。该公司已使用 Amazon SageMaker 训练了一个机器学习（ML）模型，用于从静态图像中识别常见缺陷。公司希望在检测到缺陷时向工厂工人提供本地反馈。即使工厂的互联网连接中断，公司也必须能够提供此反馈。公司有一台本地 Linux 服务器，该服务器托管一个 API，用于向工人提供本地反馈。公司应如何部署该 ML 模型以满足这些要求？

options.A: 为每个 IP 摄像头设置一个从摄像头到 AWS 的 Amazon Kinesis 视频流。使用 Amazon EC2 实例从这些流中截取静态图像。将图像上传到 Amazon S3 存储桶。使用该 ML 模型部署 SageMaker 端点。当新图像上传时，调用 AWS Lambda 函数来调用推理端点。配置 Lambda 函数在检测到缺陷时调用本地 API。
options.B: 在本地服务器上部署 AWS IoT Greengrass。将 ML 模型部署到 Greengrass 服务器。创建一个 Greengrass 组件，用于从摄像头截取静态图像并运行推理。配置该组件在检测到缺陷时调用本地 API。
options.C: 订购一台 AWS Snowball 设备。在 Snowball 设备上部署包含该 ML 模型的 SageMaker 端点和一个 Amazon EC2 实例。从摄像头截取静态图像。从 EC2 实例运行推理。配置该实例在检测到缺陷时调用本地 API。
options.D: 在每个 IP 摄像头上部署 Amazon Monitron 设备。在本地部署 Amazon Monitron Gateway。将 ML 模型部署到 Amazon Monitron 设备。使用 Amazon Monitron 运行状况警报，在检测到缺陷时通过 AWS Lambda 函数调用本地 API。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该公司已经训练了一个 Amazon SageMaker 模型，用于检测 IP 摄像头捕获的静态图像中的缺陷。关键设计要求是 **本地、本地部署推理，并且即使互联网连接不可用也能提供本地反馈**。本地 Linux 服务器也托管反馈 API，因此最佳解决方案应在本地运行图像捕获、推理和 API 调用逻辑。

## 正确答案：B

**B. 在本地服务器上部署 AWS IoT Greengrass。将 ML 模型部署到 Greengrass 服务器。创建一个 Greengrass 组件，用于从摄像头截取静态图像并运行推理。配置该组件在检测到缺陷时调用本地 API。**

AWS IoT Greengrass 正是为这种边缘计算模式而设计的。AWS 文档指出，Greengrass 使设备能够**对生成的数据进行本地操作**、**基于机器学习模型运行预测**、**自主响应本地事件**，并与**本地网络**上的其他设备通信。它还支持将软件打包并作为组件、Lambda 函数、容器、本机进程或自定义运行时运行（[AWS IoT Greengrass 概述](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/greengrass/v2/developerguide/what-is-iot-greengrass.html)）。

对于 ML 推理，AWS IoT Greengrass 支持将 ML 工作负载部署到 Greengrass 核心设备。文档描述了模型组件、运行时组件和推理组件，并解释了自定义组件可以包含模型、运行时和推理代码。文档还指出，Greengrass 支持存储在 Amazon S3 中的自定义训练模型，以及用于 SageMaker Neo 编译模型的 SageMaker AI 边缘打包作业（[执行机器学习推理](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/greengrass/v2/developerguide/perform-machine-learning-inference.html)）。

因此，在本地 Linux 服务器上部署 Greengrass，将训练好的模型作为 Greengrass ML/模型组件部署，并创建一个组件来捕获静态图像、执行推理并调用本地反馈 API，即可满足所有要求，包括在边缘部署完成后在互联网中断期间继续运行。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. Kinesis Video Streams、S3、SageMaker 端点、Lambda 和本地 API

此设计将摄像头流和图像发送到 AWS，将图像存储在 S3 中，调用云托管的 SageMaker 端点，并使用 Lambda 回调本地 API。它依赖互联网连接来上传视频、上传到 S3、调用 SageMaker 端点以及执行 Lambda。如果工厂互联网连接中断，该解决方案无法提供及时的本地反馈。这违反了核心要求。

### C. 带有 SageMaker 端点和 EC2 的 Snowball 设备

AWS Snowball Edge 可以提供边缘计算能力，例如本地存储和兼容 EC2 的实例，Snowball Edge 文档对此有所说明（[什么是 Snowball Edge？](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/whatisedge.html)）。但是，该选项建议在 Snowball 设备上部署 **SageMaker 端点**。SageMaker 实时端点是 AWS 中的托管 SageMaker 托管能力，并不是将训练好的模型部署到本地工厂 Linux 服务器上的适当机制。此选项也不必要地笨重，并且没有使用现有的本地服务器。Greengrass 才是用于将组件和 ML 推理逻辑部署到本地设备的 AWS 边缘服务。

### D. Amazon Monitron 设备和 Monitron Gateway

Amazon Monitron 不是通用的计算机视觉或自定义 SageMaker 模型部署服务。文档将 Monitron 传感器描述为从机器捕获**振动和温度数据**，将网关描述为把这些数据发送到 AWS Cloud（[Amazon Monitron 组件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Monitron/latest/user-guide/monitron-components.html)）。该场景要求使用已训练的 SageMaker 图像缺陷模型，对 **IP 摄像头静态图像**进行推理，并在连接丢失期间提供本地反馈。Monitron 用于设备状态监控，而不是将自定义图像识别模型部署到 IP 摄像头或本地服务器。

## 结论

唯一能够提供本地图像捕获、本地 ML 推理和本地 API 集成，并在互联网中断期间继续运行的选项是 **B：在本地服务器上部署 AWS IoT Greengrass，并使用 Greengrass ML 推理组件**。

en.question: A solutions architect must create a business case for migration of a company's on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The solutions architect will use a configuration management database (CMDB) export of all the company's servers to create the case. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use AWS Well-Architected Tool to import the CMDB data to perform an analysis and generate recommendations.
options.B: Use Migration Evaluator to perform an analysis. Use the data import template to upload the data from the CMDB export.
options.C: Implement resource matching rules. Use the CMDB export and the AWS Price List Bulk API to query CMDB data against AWS services in bulk.
options.D: Use AWS Application Discovery Service to import the CMDB data to perform an analysis.

en.explanation:
The question asks for the most cost-effective way to create a migration **business case** for moving an on-premises data center to AWS, using an existing CMDB export of servers.

**Correct answer: B. Use Migration Evaluator to perform an analysis. Use the data import template to upload the data from the CMDB export.**

AWS Prescriptive Guidance describes **Migration Evaluator** as a business case analysis tool for cloud planning and migration. Its product overview explicitly includes the ability to provide a business case for AWS planning and migration decisions, and its pricing model is **no charge**. The same page lists **data import** support for uploading IT asset data from sources such as a **CMDB extract**, vCenter extract, SolarWinds, Hyper-V, or SCCM, and describes TCO coverage for AWS and on-premises costs over 1-year and 3-year periods. This directly matches the requirement to use a CMDB export to create a cost-effective migration business case. See [Migration Evaluator - AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-tools/business-case-migration-evaluator.html).

### Why the other options are incorrect

**A. Use AWS Well-Architected Tool to import the CMDB data to perform an analysis and generate recommendations.**  
The AWS Well-Architected Tool is used to review AWS workloads against best practices and identify risks such as high-risk issues and medium-risk issues based on workload review answers. It is not designed to import CMDB server inventory and generate a migration TCO/business case. See [Workloads - AWS Well-Architected Tool](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/userguide/workloads.html).

**C. Implement resource matching rules. Use the CMDB export and the AWS Price List Bulk API to query CMDB data against AWS services in bulk.**  
The AWS Price List Bulk API is for consuming and downloading AWS product and pricing information in bulk. It does not provide migration assessment logic, rightsizing analysis, license analysis, or a ready business case. Building custom resource matching and pricing logic would be more complex and less cost-effective than using Migration Evaluator, which already provides these capabilities at no charge. See [Getting price list files using the AWS Price List Bulk API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/using-the-aws-price-list-bulk-api.html).

**D. Use AWS Application Discovery Service to import the CMDB data to perform an analysis.**  
AWS discovery tools and Migration Hub import can bring on-premises server and application information into Migration Hub, including server specifications and utilization data. However, this option is focused on discovery and migration tracking/planning, not on producing the specific business-case/TCO analysis requested. AWS documentation separately identifies **Migration Evaluator** as the migration assessment service that helps create a directional business case for AWS cloud planning and migration. See [Discover on-premises resources using AWS Migration Hub discovery tools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/latest/ug/gs-new-user-discovery.html).

Therefore, **Migration Evaluator with the data import template** is the best and most cost-effective fit.

zh.question: 解决方案架构师必须为将公司的本地数据中心迁移到 AWS Cloud 创建业务案例。该解决方案架构师将使用包含公司所有服务器的配置管理数据库（CMDB）导出来创建该案例。哪种解决方案能够以最低成本满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 AWS Well-Architected Tool 导入 CMDB 数据，以执行分析并生成建议。
options.B: 使用 Migration Evaluator 执行分析。使用数据导入模板上传来自 CMDB 导出的数据。
options.C: 实施资源匹配规则。使用 CMDB 导出和 AWS Price List Bulk API 批量查询 CMDB 数据与 AWS 服务的匹配情况。
options.D: 使用 AWS Application Discovery Service 导入 CMDB 数据以执行分析。

zh.explanation:
该问题要求使用现有的服务器 CMDB 导出，为将本地数据中心迁移到 AWS 创建迁移**业务案例**，并且要求成本效益最高。

**正确答案：B. 使用 Migration Evaluator 执行分析。使用数据导入模板上传来自 CMDB 导出的数据。**

AWS Prescriptive Guidance 将 **Migration Evaluator** 描述为用于云规划和迁移的业务案例分析工具。其产品概述明确包含为 AWS 规划和迁移决策提供业务案例的能力，并且其定价模式是**不收费**。同一页面列出了**数据导入**支持，可从 **CMDB extract**、vCenter extract、SolarWinds、Hyper-V 或 SCCM 等来源上传 IT 资产数据，并描述了针对 1 年和 3 年周期的 AWS 与本地成本的 TCO 覆盖范围。这直接匹配了使用 CMDB 导出来创建成本效益高的迁移业务案例的要求。请参阅 [Migration Evaluator - AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-tools/business-case-migration-evaluator.html)。

### 为什么其他选项不正确

**A. 使用 AWS Well-Architected Tool 导入 CMDB 数据，以执行分析并生成建议。**  
AWS Well-Architected Tool 用于根据最佳实践审查 AWS 工作负载，并基于工作负载审查答案识别风险，例如高风险问题和中等风险问题。它并非设计用于导入 CMDB 服务器清单并生成迁移 TCO/业务案例。请参阅 [Workloads - AWS Well-Architected Tool](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/userguide/workloads.html)。

**C. 实施资源匹配规则。使用 CMDB 导出和 AWS Price List Bulk API 批量查询 CMDB 数据与 AWS 服务的匹配情况。**  
AWS Price List Bulk API 用于批量使用和下载 AWS 产品与定价信息。它不提供迁移评估逻辑、合适规格调整分析、许可证分析或现成的业务案例。构建自定义资源匹配和定价逻辑会比使用 Migration Evaluator 更复杂且成本效益更低，而 Migration Evaluator 已经免费提供这些能力。请参阅 [Getting price list files using the AWS Price List Bulk API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/using-the-aws-price-list-bulk-api.html)。

**D. 使用 AWS Application Discovery Service 导入 CMDB 数据以执行分析。**  
AWS 发现工具和 Migration Hub 导入可以将本地服务器和应用程序信息导入 Migration Hub，包括服务器规格和利用率数据。但是，该选项侧重于发现以及迁移跟踪/规划，而不是生成题目要求的特定业务案例/TCO 分析。AWS 文档单独将 **Migration Evaluator** 标识为迁移评估服务，可帮助为 AWS Cloud 规划和迁移创建方向性业务案例。请参阅 [Discover on-premises resources using AWS Migration Hub discovery tools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/latest/ug/gs-new-user-discovery.html)。

因此，**带有数据导入模板的 Migration Evaluator** 是最佳且最具成本效益的选择。

en.question: A company has a website that runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The ALB is associated with an AWS WAF web ACL. The website often encounters attacks in the application layer. The attacks produce sudden and significant increases in traffic on the application server. The access logs show that each attack originates from different IP addresses. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to mitigate these attacks. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors server access. Set a threshold based on access by IP address. Configure an alarm action that adds the IP address to the web ACL’s deny list.
options.B: Deploy AWS Shield Advanced in addition to AWS WAF. Add the ALB as a protected resource.
options.C: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors user IP addresses. Set a threshold based on access by IP address. Configure the alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function to add a deny rule in the application server’s subnet route table for any IP addresses that activate the alarm.
options.D: Inspect access logs to find a pattern of IP addresses that launched the attacks. Use an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to deny traffic from the countries that host those IP addresses.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The website is behind an ALB and already has an AWS WAF web ACL. The attacks are at the application layer and cause sudden, significant traffic spikes from many different IP addresses. That pattern is consistent with an application-layer DDoS/HTTP flood style attack. The question asks for mitigation with the **least operational overhead**.

## Correct answer: B

**B. Deploy AWS Shield Advanced in addition to AWS WAF. Add the ALB as a protected resource.**

AWS Shield is specifically designed for DDoS protection, including **application layer (layer 7)** attacks. AWS documentation states that Shield Standard and Shield Advanced provide protections against DDoS attacks at layers 3, 4, and **7**, and describes application-layer attacks as web request floods that deny service by flooding an application with valid requests ([How AWS Shield and Shield Advanced work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-overview.html)).

Shield Advanced can protect **Application Load Balancers** when they are explicitly added as protected resources. The AWS documentation lists Application Load Balancers among the ELB load balancers that Shield Advanced protects and notes that protections must be explicitly configured ([List of AWS resources that AWS Shield Advanced protects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-advanced-summary-protected-resources.html)).

This is also the best fit for least operational overhead because Shield Advanced can integrate with AWS WAF for application-layer DDoS mitigation. AWS documentation states that Shield Advanced can be configured to automatically mitigate layer 7 attacks by counting or blocking attack web requests, and that it manages mitigation rules in the resource's associated web ACL. It also compares current traffic patterns against historical baselines and can create and deploy custom AWS WAF rules to respond to detected DDoS attacks ([Automating application layer DDoS mitigation with Shield Advanced](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-automatic-app-layer-response.html)).

Therefore, deploying Shield Advanced and adding the ALB as a protected resource is the most managed and operationally efficient solution.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. CloudWatch alarm that adds IPs to the WAF deny list

This approach requires building and maintaining custom detection and response automation. It is also poorly suited to the described attack because each attack originates from different IP addresses. Blocking individual IPs after they cross a threshold can lag behind the attack, risks blocking legitimate clients, and creates ongoing operational tuning. Shield Advanced provides managed application-layer DDoS detection and mitigation through WAF, which is lower overhead.

### C. CloudWatch alarm and Lambda to add deny rules to the subnet route table

This is not an appropriate way to block individual malicious client IP addresses. VPC route tables are for routing traffic to targets, not for maintaining a deny list of source IP addresses. This option also requires custom Lambda automation and would not be as operationally simple or effective as Shield Advanced with WAF.

### D. Inspect logs and use Route 53 geolocation routing to deny countries

This is manual, coarse-grained, and high overhead. The attacks originate from different IP addresses, and there is no assurance that they come from a stable or identifiable set of countries. Blocking whole countries can also deny legitimate users and does not provide dynamic application-layer DDoS mitigation.

## Conclusion

The correct answer is **B** because Shield Advanced supports application-layer DDoS protection, can protect ALBs, and can work with AWS WAF to automate mitigation with the least operational overhead.

zh.question: 一家公司有一个网站，运行在 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面的 Amazon EC2 实例上。这些实例位于一个 Auto Scaling 组中。该 ALB 关联了一个 AWS WAF web ACL。该网站经常遭遇应用层攻击。这些攻击会导致应用服务器上的流量突然且显著增加。访问日志显示，每次攻击都来自不同的 IP 地址。解决方案架构师需要实施一种解决方案来缓解这些攻击。哪种解决方案能以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个监控服务器访问情况的 Amazon CloudWatch 警报。根据按 IP 地址统计的访问量设置阈值。配置一个警报操作，将该 IP 地址添加到 web ACL 的拒绝列表中。
options.B: 除 AWS WAF 外，部署 AWS Shield Advanced。将 ALB 添加为受保护资源。
options.C: 创建一个监控用户 IP 地址的 Amazon CloudWatch 警报。根据按 IP 地址统计的访问量设置阈值。配置该警报调用一个 AWS Lambda 函数，为任何触发该警报的 IP 地址在应用服务器的子网路由表中添加一条拒绝规则。
options.D: 检查访问日志，找出发起攻击的 IP 地址模式。使用 Amazon Route 53 地理位置路由策略，拒绝来自托管这些 IP 地址的国家/地区的流量。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该网站位于 ALB 后面，并且已经有一个 AWS WAF web ACL。攻击发生在应用层，并导致来自许多不同 IP 地址的流量突然显著激增。这种模式与应用层 DDoS/HTTP 洪泛式攻击一致。题目要求以**最少运营开销**进行缓解。

## 正确答案：B

**B. 除 AWS WAF 外，部署 AWS Shield Advanced。将 ALB 添加为受保护资源。**

AWS Shield 专门用于 DDoS 防护，包括**应用层（第 7 层）**攻击。AWS 文档说明，Shield Standard 和 Shield Advanced 针对第 3、4 和 **7** 层的 DDoS 攻击提供防护，并将应用层攻击描述为 Web 请求洪泛，即通过大量有效请求淹没应用程序来造成服务拒绝（[How AWS Shield and Shield Advanced work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-overview.html)）。

当 Application Load Balancers 被明确添加为受保护资源时，Shield Advanced 可以保护它们。AWS 文档在 Shield Advanced 可保护的 ELB 负载均衡器中列出了 Application Load Balancers，并说明必须显式配置防护（[List of AWS resources that AWS Shield Advanced protects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-advanced-summary-protected-resources.html)）。

这也是最符合最少运营开销要求的选择，因为 Shield Advanced 可以与 AWS WAF 集成，用于应用层 DDoS 缓解。AWS 文档说明，可以将 Shield Advanced 配置为通过计数或阻止攻击性 Web 请求来自动缓解第 7 层攻击，并且它会在资源关联的 web ACL 中管理缓解规则。它还会将当前流量模式与历史基线进行比较，并可以创建和部署自定义 AWS WAF 规则以响应检测到的 DDoS 攻击（[Automating application layer DDoS mitigation with Shield Advanced](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-automatic-app-layer-response.html)）。

因此，部署 Shield Advanced 并将 ALB 添加为受保护资源，是最托管化且运营效率最高的解决方案。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. 添加 IP 到 WAF 拒绝列表的 CloudWatch 警报

这种方法需要构建和维护自定义检测与响应自动化。它也不太适合题述攻击，因为每次攻击都来自不同的 IP 地址。在单个 IP 超过阈值后再阻止它们，可能滞后于攻击，存在阻止合法客户端的风险，并会带来持续的运营调优。Shield Advanced 通过 WAF 提供托管式应用层 DDoS 检测和缓解，运营开销更低。

### C. CloudWatch 警报和 Lambda，用于向子网路由表添加拒绝规则

这不是阻止单个恶意客户端 IP 地址的适当方式。VPC 路由表用于将流量路由到目标，而不是维护源 IP 地址拒绝列表。此选项还需要自定义 Lambda 自动化，并且不如结合 WAF 的 Shield Advanced 在运营上简单或有效。

### D. 检查日志并使用 Route 53 地理位置路由拒绝国家/地区

这是手动的、粗粒度的，并且运营开销很高。攻击来自不同 IP 地址，无法保证它们来自一组稳定或可识别的国家/地区。阻止整个国家/地区也可能拒绝合法用户，并且不能提供动态的应用层 DDoS 缓解。

## 结论

正确答案是 **B**，因为 Shield Advanced 支持应用层 DDoS 防护，可以保护 ALB，并且可以与 AWS WAF 配合，以最少的运营开销自动缓解攻击。

en.question: A company has a critical application in which the data tier is deployed in a single AWS Region. The data tier uses an Amazon DynamoDB table and an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. The current Aurora MySQL engine version supports a global database. The application tier is already deployed in two Regions. Company policy states that critical applications must have application tier components and data tier components deployed across two Regions. The RTO and RPO must be no more than a few minutes each. A solutions architect must recommend a solution to make the data tier compliant with company policy. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Add another Region to the Aurora MySQL DB cluster
options.B: Add another Region to each table in the Aurora MySQL DB cluster
options.C: Set up scheduled cross-Region backups for the DynamoDB table and the Aurora MySQL DB cluster
options.D: Convert the existing DynamoDB table to a global table by adding another Region to its configuration
options.E: Use Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller to automate database backup and recovery to the secondary Region

en.explanation:
The application tier is already deployed in two AWS Regions. The gap is the **data tier**: an existing DynamoDB table and an Aurora MySQL DB cluster are currently in one Region, but policy requires both data-tier components to be deployed across two Regions with RTO/RPO of only a few minutes. That points to managed cross-Region replication services, not backup/restore.

Correct answers: **A and D**.

- **A. Add another Region to the Aurora MySQL DB cluster — Correct.** The question explicitly states that the current Aurora MySQL version supports an Aurora global database. Amazon Aurora Global Database is designed to span multiple AWS Regions: one primary Region and up to 10 secondary Regions. AWS documentation states that Aurora replicates data to secondary Regions using dedicated infrastructure with latency typically under a second, and that secondary clusters help provide lower RTO and lower RPO than traditional replication solutions ([Using Amazon Aurora Global Database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html)). Adding a secondary Region to the Aurora global database makes the Aurora data tier multi-Region and supports the required recovery objectives.

- **D. Convert the existing DynamoDB table to a global table by adding another Region to its configuration — Correct.** DynamoDB global tables are a fully managed, multi-Region, multi-active database feature. AWS documentation says global tables automatically replicate DynamoDB table data across AWS Regions and are intended for business continuity and high availability through multi-Region deployment. The documentation also notes that applications can achieve high resilience with low or zero RPO by shifting traffic to a different Region if processing is interrupted ([DynamoDB global tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html)). This meets the DynamoDB portion of the requirement.

Incorrect options:

- **B. Add another Region to each table in the Aurora MySQL DB cluster — Incorrect.** Aurora MySQL tables are not individually configured with AWS Regions. Cross-Region deployment for Aurora is done at the DB cluster/global database level, by adding a secondary Aurora DB cluster/Region to an Aurora global database, not by adding Regions to individual MySQL tables.

- **C. Set up scheduled cross-Region backups for the DynamoDB table and the Aurora MySQL DB cluster — Incorrect.** Scheduled backups are a backup-and-restore DR pattern. AWS describes backup and restore as an approach that can mitigate regional disasters, but it requires restoring data and redeploying infrastructure in the recovery Region, which can increase recovery time ([Disaster recovery options in the cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html)). For RTO/RPO of only a few minutes and an explicit requirement that data-tier components be deployed across two Regions, real-time or near-real-time replication via DynamoDB global tables and Aurora Global Database is the appropriate design.

- **E. Use Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller to automate database backup and recovery to the secondary Region — Incorrect.** Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) supports multi-Region recovery orchestration and DNS traffic failover through Region switch and routing controls, and readiness checks for failover preparedness. It does not convert DynamoDB or Aurora into replicated multi-Region databases, nor is it a database backup/restore service ([ARC multi-Region recovery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/r53recovery/latest/dg/what-is-route53-recovery.html)). ARC could help orchestrate application failover, but it does not satisfy the data-tier replication requirement by itself.

zh.question: 一家公司有一个关键应用程序，其数据层部署在单个 AWS 区域中。数据层使用一个 Amazon DynamoDB 表和一个 Amazon Aurora MySQL 数据库集群。当前 Aurora MySQL 引擎版本支持全局数据库。应用程序层已经部署在两个区域中。公司策略规定，关键应用程序必须将应用程序层组件和数据层组件部署在两个区域中。RTO 和 RPO 都必须不超过几分钟。解决方案架构师必须推荐一种解决方案，使数据层符合公司策略。哪两项步骤组合可以满足这些要求？（选择两项。）

options.A: 向 Aurora MySQL 数据库集群添加另一个区域
options.B: 向 Aurora MySQL 数据库集群中的每个表添加另一个区域
options.C: 为 DynamoDB 表和 Aurora MySQL 数据库集群设置计划的跨区域备份
options.D: 通过在配置中添加另一个区域，将现有 DynamoDB 表转换为全局表
options.E: 使用 Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller 自动执行到辅助区域的数据库备份和恢复

zh.explanation:
应用程序层已经部署在两个 AWS 区域中。缺口在于**数据层**：现有的 DynamoDB 表和 Aurora MySQL 数据库集群目前位于一个区域中，但策略要求两个数据层组件都部署在两个区域中，并且 RTO/RPO 仅为几分钟。这指向托管的跨区域复制服务，而不是备份/还原。

正确答案：**A 和 D**。

- **A. 向 Aurora MySQL 数据库集群添加另一个区域 — 正确。** 题目明确说明当前 Aurora MySQL 版本支持 Aurora global database。Amazon Aurora Global Database 旨在跨多个 AWS 区域：一个主区域和最多 10 个辅助区域。AWS 文档指出，Aurora 使用专用基础设施将数据复制到辅助区域，延迟通常低于一秒，并且辅助集群有助于提供比传统复制解决方案更低的 RTO 和更低的 RPO（[Using Amazon Aurora Global Database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database.html)）。向 Aurora global database 添加辅助区域，可使 Aurora 数据层实现多区域部署，并支持所需的恢复目标。

- **D. 通过在配置中添加另一个区域，将现有 DynamoDB 表转换为全局表 — 正确。** DynamoDB global tables 是一种完全托管的多区域、多活数据库功能。AWS 文档指出，global tables 会自动在 AWS 区域之间复制 DynamoDB 表数据，旨在通过多区域部署实现业务连续性和高可用性。文档还指出，如果处理被中断，应用程序可以通过将流量切换到另一个区域来实现高弹性以及低 RPO 或零 RPO（[DynamoDB global tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html)）。这满足了要求中 DynamoDB 部分的需求。

错误选项：

- **B. 向 Aurora MySQL 数据库集群中的每个表添加另一个区域 — 错误。** Aurora MySQL 表不能单独配置 AWS 区域。Aurora 的跨区域部署是在数据库集群/全局数据库级别完成的，即向 Aurora global database 添加辅助 Aurora 数据库集群/区域，而不是向单个 MySQL 表添加区域。

- **C. 为 DynamoDB 表和 Aurora MySQL 数据库集群设置计划的跨区域备份 — 错误。** 计划备份是一种备份和还原 DR 模式。AWS 将备份和还原描述为一种可以缓解区域性灾难的方法，但它需要在恢复区域中还原数据并重新部署基础设施，这可能会增加恢复时间（[Disaster recovery options in the cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws/disaster-recovery-options-in-the-cloud.html)）。对于仅几分钟的 RTO/RPO，以及要求数据层组件显式部署在两个区域中的要求，通过 DynamoDB global tables 和 Aurora Global Database 实现实时或近实时复制才是合适的设计。

- **E. 使用 Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller 自动执行到辅助区域的数据库备份和恢复 — 错误。** Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) 通过区域切换和路由控制支持多区域恢复编排和 DNS 流量故障转移，并通过就绪检查支持故障转移准备情况。它不会将 DynamoDB 或 Aurora 转换为复制型多区域数据库，也不是数据库备份/还原服务（[ARC multi-Region recovery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/r53recovery/latest/dg/what-is-route53-recovery.html)）。ARC 可以帮助编排应用程序故障转移，但其本身无法满足数据层复制要求。

en.question: A telecommunications company is running an application on AWS. The company has set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the company's on-premises data center and AWS. The company deployed the application on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones behind an internal Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company's clients connect from the on-premises network by using HTTPS. The TLS terminates in the ALB. The company has multiple target groups and uses path-based routing to forward requests based on the URL path. The company is planning to deploy an on-premises firewall appliance with an allow list that is based on IP address. A solutions architect must develop a solution to allow traffic flow to AWS from the on-premises network so that the clients can continue to access the application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure the existing ALB to use static IP addresses. Assign IP addresses in multiple Availability Zones to the ALB. Add the ALB IP addresses to the firewall appliance.
options.B: Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Associate the NLB with one static IP addresses in multiple Availability Zones. Create an ALB-type target group for the NLB and add the existing ALAdd the NLB IP addresses to the firewall appliance. Update the clients to connect to the NLB.
options.C: Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Associate the LNB with one static IP addresses in multiple Availability Zones. Add the existing target groups to the NLB. Update the clients to connect to the NLB. Delete the ALB Add the NLB IP addresses to the firewall appliance.
options.D: Create a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB). Assign static IP addresses to the GWLB in multiple Availability Zones. Create an ALB-type target group for the GWLB and add the existing ALB. Add the GWLB IP addresses to the firewall appliance. Update the clients to connect to the GWLB.

en.explanation:
The application currently depends on an **internal Application Load Balancer** for HTTPS termination and path-based routing to multiple target groups. The new on-premises firewall requires an IP-address allow list, so the AWS endpoint that clients connect to must provide stable IP addresses while preserving the existing ALB layer-7 routing behavior.

**Correct answer: B**

Create an **internal Network Load Balancer** in front of the existing ALB, assign static IPs to the NLB in the enabled Availability Zones, create a target group of type `alb`, register the existing ALB as the target, and allow-list the NLB IP addresses on the on-premises firewall.

AWS explicitly documents this pattern: you can create a target group with target type **Application Load Balancer** and register an ALB as the target of an NLB. The NLB listener must be TCP, and AWS notes that with this configuration, **HTTPS listeners on the ALB can still terminate TLS traffic**. AWS also states that when creating the NLB, you can use static IP addresses for each Availability Zone, which is useful when adding specific IP addresses to firewall allow lists ([Use an Application Load Balancer as a target of a Network Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/application-load-balancer-target.html)).

This preserves the ALB's application-layer functionality. ALB listener rules can route requests based on conditions including `path-pattern`, and ALB evaluates listener rules to select the target group ([Listener rules for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/listener-rules.html)). Therefore, the NLB provides stable network-level IPs for the firewall, while the ALB continues HTTPS termination and path-based routing.

### Why the other options are incorrect

**A. Configure the existing ALB to use static IP addresses**  
This is not a valid ALB configuration. ALBs are layer-7 load balancers that use AWS-managed load balancer nodes and DNS-based access. The supported documented pattern for static IP allow-listing while retaining ALB features is to place an NLB in front of the ALB. NLBs, not ALBs, provide static IP behavior per enabled Availability Zone; AWS documents that NLB nodes use static IP addresses and can optionally use one Elastic IP per subnet for internet-facing NLBs ([Network Load Balancer overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/introduction.html)).

**C. Replace the ALB by adding the existing target groups directly to an NLB**  
This would lose the ALB's layer-7 capabilities. An NLB operates at layer 4, while an ALB operates at layer 7 and evaluates listener rules to route based on application content such as URL path ([Application Load Balancer overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.html)). The question explicitly requires continued HTTPS termination at the ALB and path-based routing to multiple target groups. NLB target groups are not a replacement for ALB listener rules and path-based routing.

**D. Use a Gateway Load Balancer with an ALB-type target group**  
Gateway Load Balancer is designed for distributing traffic to virtual appliances, using GENEVE on port 6081. Its target group target types are `instance` and `ip`, not `alb` ([Target groups for Gateway Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/target-groups.html)). It is not the correct service to provide a static frontend for HTTPS clients while preserving ALB path-based routing.

Therefore, **B** is the only option that provides stable allow-listable IP addresses and keeps the existing ALB capabilities.

zh.question: 一家电信公司正在 AWS 上运行一个应用程序。该公司已在公司的本地数据中心与 AWS 之间建立了 AWS Direct Connect 连接。该公司将应用程序部署在多个可用区中的 Amazon EC2 实例上，这些实例位于一个内部 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面。公司的客户端使用 HTTPS 从本地网络进行连接。TLS 在 ALB 中终止。该公司有多个目标组，并使用基于路径的路由根据 URL 路径转发请求。该公司计划部署一个本地防火墙设备，其允许列表基于 IP 地址。解决方案架构师必须制定一个解决方案，允许流量从本地网络流向 AWS，以便客户端能够继续访问该应用程序。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 配置现有 ALB 使用静态 IP 地址。将多个可用区中的 IP 地址分配给 ALB。将 ALB IP 地址添加到防火墙设备。
options.B: 创建一个 Network Load Balancer (NLB)。将 NLB 与多个可用区中的一个静态 IP 地址关联。为 NLB 创建一个 ALB 类型的目标组，并添加现有 ALB。将 NLB IP 地址添加到防火墙设备。更新客户端以连接到 NLB。
options.C: 创建一个 Network Load Balancer (NLB)。将 LNB 与多个可用区中的一个静态 IP 地址关联。将现有目标组添加到 NLB。更新客户端以连接到 NLB。删除 ALB。将 NLB IP 地址添加到防火墙设备。
options.D: 创建一个 Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)。在多个可用区中为 GWLB 分配静态 IP 地址。为 GWLB 创建一个 ALB 类型的目标组，并添加现有 ALB。将 GWLB IP 地址添加到防火墙设备。更新客户端以连接到 GWLB。

zh.explanation:
该应用程序目前依赖一个 **内部 Application Load Balancer** 来进行 HTTPS 终止，并基于路径路由到多个目标组。新的本地防火墙需要基于 IP 地址的允许列表，因此客户端连接到的 AWS 端点必须提供稳定的 IP 地址，同时保留现有 ALB 的第 7 层路由行为。

**正确答案：B**

在现有 ALB 前面创建一个 **内部 Network Load Balancer**，在启用的可用区中为 NLB 分配静态 IP，为其创建一个类型为 `alb` 的目标组，将现有 ALB 注册为目标，并在本地防火墙上将 NLB IP 地址加入允许列表。

AWS 明确记录了这种模式：你可以创建目标类型为 **Application Load Balancer** 的目标组，并将 ALB 注册为 NLB 的目标。NLB 侦听器必须是 TCP，并且 AWS 指出，在此配置下，**ALB 上的 HTTPS 侦听器仍然可以终止 TLS 流量**。AWS 还说明，在创建 NLB 时，可以为每个可用区使用静态 IP 地址，这在向防火墙允许列表添加特定 IP 地址时非常有用（[Use an Application Load Balancer as a target of a Network Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/application-load-balancer-target.html)）。

这保留了 ALB 的应用层功能。ALB 侦听器规则可以根据包括 `path-pattern` 在内的条件路由请求，并且 ALB 会评估侦听器规则以选择目标组（[Listener rules for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/listener-rules.html)）。因此，NLB 为防火墙提供稳定的网络层 IP，而 ALB 继续进行 HTTPS 终止和基于路径的路由。

### 为什么其他选项不正确

**A. 配置现有 ALB 使用静态 IP 地址**  
这不是有效的 ALB 配置。ALB 是第 7 层负载均衡器，使用 AWS 托管的负载均衡器节点和基于 DNS 的访问。在保留 ALB 功能的同时进行静态 IP 允许列表配置，受支持且有文档说明的模式是在 ALB 前面放置一个 NLB。提供每个已启用可用区静态 IP 行为的是 NLB，而不是 ALB；AWS 文档说明 NLB 节点使用静态 IP 地址，并且对于面向互联网的 NLB，可以选择每个子网使用一个 Elastic IP（[Network Load Balancer overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/introduction.html)）。

**C. 通过将现有目标组直接添加到 NLB 来替换 ALB**  
这会失去 ALB 的第 7 层能力。NLB 在第 4 层运行，而 ALB 在第 7 层运行，并评估侦听器规则以根据应用内容（例如 URL 路径）进行路由（[Application Load Balancer overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.html)）。题目明确要求继续在 ALB 上终止 HTTPS，并基于路径路由到多个目标组。NLB 目标组不能替代 ALB 侦听器规则和基于路径的路由。

**D. 使用带有 ALB 类型目标组的 Gateway Load Balancer**  
Gateway Load Balancer 旨在将流量分发到虚拟设备，并在端口 6081 上使用 GENEVE。其目标组目标类型是 `instance` 和 `ip`，而不是 `alb`（[Target groups for Gateway Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/target-groups.html)）。它不是为 HTTPS 客户端提供静态前端并同时保留 ALB 基于路径路由的正确服务。

因此，**B** 是唯一既能提供稳定且可加入允许列表的 IP 地址，又能保留现有 ALB 功能的选项。

en.question: A company runs an application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances that are in private subnets behind an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB is the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. An AWS WAF web ACL that contains various AWS managed rules is associated with the CloudFront distribution. The company needs a solution that will prevent internet traffic from directly accessing the ALB. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create a new web ACL that contains the same rules that the existing web ACL contains. Associate the new web ACL with the ALB.
options.B: Associate the existing web ACL with the ALB.
options.C: Add a security group rule to the ALB to allow traffic from the AWS managed prefix list for CloudFront only.
options.D: Add a security group rule to the ALB to allow only the various CloudFront IP address ranges.

en.explanation:
The application instances are already in private subnets, but the internet-facing ALB is publicly reachable. Because CloudFront is intended to be the only public entry point, the question asks how to prevent direct internet clients from reaching the ALB with the least operational overhead.

**Correct answer: C. Add a security group rule to the ALB to allow traffic from the AWS managed prefix list for CloudFront only.**

AWS documents that the CloudFront managed prefix list contains the IP address ranges of all CloudFront globally distributed **origin-facing servers**. If an AWS-hosted origin is protected by a VPC security group, you can use this managed prefix list to allow inbound traffic to the origin only from CloudFront origin-facing servers, thereby preventing non-CloudFront traffic from reaching the origin. AWS also states that CloudFront maintains the prefix list so it stays up to date, and that you do not need to maintain IP ranges yourself ([CloudFront: Use the CloudFront managed prefix list](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/LocationsOfEdgeServers.html)). An internet-facing ALB has a security group, so restricting the ALB security group inbound rule to `com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing` is the lowest-operational-overhead way to allow CloudFront-to-origin traffic while blocking direct internet access.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. Create a new web ACL with the same rules and associate it with the ALB.**  
  This would apply WAF inspection at the ALB as well as CloudFront, but it does **not** inherently prevent direct access to the ALB. Direct requests could still reach the ALB and be evaluated by WAF. It also duplicates rule management, increasing operational overhead.

- **B. Associate the existing web ACL with the ALB.**  
  This does not meet the requirement because associating WAF with the ALB does not make the ALB reachable only from CloudFront. Also, in practice, a web ACL associated with a CloudFront distribution is a global/CloudFront-scoped WAF resource, while ALB associations use regional scope, so the same web ACL is not the appropriate mechanism for both resources.

- **D. Add a security group rule to the ALB to allow only the various CloudFront IP address ranges.**  
  This could work functionally, but it has higher operational overhead. CloudFront IP ranges can change, and maintaining them manually requires updates. AWS specifically recommends the CloudFront managed prefix list because AWS keeps it current and customers do not need to maintain the IP range list themselves ([CloudFront: Use the CloudFront managed prefix list](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/LocationsOfEdgeServers.html)).

Therefore, **C** is the best answer.

zh.question: 一家公司在一组位于私有子网中的 Amazon EC2 实例上运行一个应用程序，这些实例位于一个面向互联网的 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面。该 ALB 是一个 Amazon CloudFront 分配的源站。一个包含各种 AWS 托管规则的 AWS WAF Web ACL 与该 CloudFront 分配相关联。该公司需要一种解决方案，防止互联网流量直接访问 ALB。哪种解决方案能够以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个新的 Web ACL，其中包含现有 Web ACL 所包含的相同规则。将新的 Web ACL 与 ALB 关联。
options.B: 将现有 Web ACL 与 ALB 关联。
options.C: 向 ALB 添加安全组规则，仅允许来自 CloudFront 的 AWS 托管前缀列表的流量。
options.D: 向 ALB 添加安全组规则，仅允许各种 CloudFront IP 地址范围。

zh.explanation:
应用程序实例已经位于私有子网中，但面向互联网的 ALB 仍可被公网访问。由于 CloudFront 旨在作为唯一的公共入口点，本题询问如何以最少的运营开销防止直接的互联网客户端访问 ALB。

**正确答案：C。向 ALB 添加安全组规则，仅允许来自 CloudFront 的 AWS 托管前缀列表的流量。**

AWS 文档说明，CloudFront 托管前缀列表包含所有 CloudFront 全球分布式**面向源站的服务器**的 IP 地址范围。如果 AWS 托管的源站受 VPC 安全组保护，你可以使用此托管前缀列表，仅允许来自 CloudFront 面向源站的服务器的入站流量到达源站，从而防止非 CloudFront 流量到达源站。AWS 还说明 CloudFront 会维护该前缀列表，使其保持最新，并且你无需自行维护 IP 范围（[CloudFront：使用 CloudFront 托管前缀列表](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/LocationsOfEdgeServers.html)）。面向互联网的 ALB 具有安全组，因此将 ALB 安全组入站规则限制为 `com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing`，是在阻止直接互联网访问的同时允许 CloudFront 到源站流量的最低运营开销方式。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A。创建一个包含相同规则的新 Web ACL，并将其与 ALB 关联。**  
  这会在 ALB 以及 CloudFront 上应用 WAF 检查，但它本身并不会阻止对 ALB 的直接访问。直接请求仍然可以到达 ALB 并由 WAF 评估。这也会重复规则管理，增加运营开销。

- **B。将现有 Web ACL 与 ALB 关联。**  
  这不符合要求，因为将 WAF 与 ALB 关联并不会让 ALB 只能从 CloudFront 访问。此外，在实践中，与 CloudFront 分配关联的 Web ACL 是全局/CloudFront 范围的 WAF 资源，而 ALB 关联使用区域范围，因此同一个 Web ACL 不是同时用于这两类资源的合适机制。

- **D。向 ALB 添加安全组规则，仅允许各种 CloudFront IP 地址范围。**  
  这在功能上可以实现，但运营开销更高。CloudFront IP 范围可能会变化，手动维护这些范围需要更新。AWS 特别推荐 CloudFront 托管前缀列表，因为 AWS 会保持其最新，客户无需自行维护 IP 范围列表（[CloudFront：使用 CloudFront 托管前缀列表](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/LocationsOfEdgeServers.html)）。

因此，**C** 是最佳答案。

en.question: A company is running an application that uses an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster as a caching layer. A recent security audit revealed that the company has configured encryption at rest for ElastiCache. However, the company did not configure ElastiCache to use encryption in transit. Additionally, users can access the cache without authentication. A solutions architect must make changes to require user authentication and to ensure that the company is using end-to-end encryption. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an AUTH token. Store the token in AWS System Manager Parameter Store, as an encrypted parameter. Create a new cluster with AUTH, and configure encryption in transit. Update the application to retrieve the AUTH token from Parameter Store when necessary and to use the AUTH token for authentication.
options.B: Create an AUTH token. Store the token in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the existing cluster to use the AUTH token, and configure encryption in transit. Update the application to retrieve the AUTH token from Secrets Manager when necessary and to use the AUTH token for authentication.
options.C: Create an SSL certificate. Store the certificate in AWS Secrets Manager. Create a new cluster, and configure encryption in transit. Update the application to retrieve the SSL certificate from Secrets Manager when necessary and to use the certificate for authentication.
options.D: Create an SSL certificate. Store the certificate in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, as an encrypted advanced parameter. Update the existing cluster to configure encryption in transit. Update the application to retrieve the SSL certificate from Parameter Store when necessary and to use the certificate for authentication.

en.explanation:
The scenario asks how to add **client authentication** and **end-to-end encryption** to an existing Amazon ElastiCache for Redis caching layer that already has encryption at rest but lacks TLS in transit and authentication.

**Correct answer: B.**

ElastiCache for Redis OSS/Valkey supports TLS in transit for client-to-node and node-to-node traffic. The AWS documentation states that in-transit encryption provides encrypted client connections, encrypted server connections, server authentication, and client authentication through Redis OSS/Valkey AUTH. It also states that modifying the in-transit encryption setting on an existing node-based cluster is supported for replication groups running Redis OSS version 7 and later, and Valkey 7.2 and later ([ElastiCache in-transit encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/in-transit-encryption.html)).

For enabling TLS on an existing cluster, AWS documents a two-step migration: first set transit encryption mode to `preferred` so both encrypted and unencrypted clients can connect, then after clients are migrated, set the mode to `required` so only encrypted connections are allowed ([Enabling in-transit encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/in-transit-encryption-enable.html)).

For authentication, ElastiCache AUTH tokens are the relevant mechanism. AWS states that AUTH can be enabled only for encryption-in-transit-enabled Redis OSS/Valkey clusters, and that an existing cluster can be modified with `ModifyReplicationGroup` using an `--auth-token` and an `--auth-token-update-strategy` such as `ROTATE`, followed by `SET` to make the token required ([Authenticating with the Valkey and Redis OSS AUTH command](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/auth.html)). Storing the AUTH token in AWS Secrets Manager is appropriate because Secrets Manager is designed to manage, retrieve, and rotate application credentials, API keys, and other secrets, and applications can retrieve secrets dynamically at runtime ([What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)).

Therefore, creating an AUTH token, storing it in Secrets Manager, modifying the existing cluster to enable TLS and use AUTH, and updating the application to retrieve and use the token satisfies both requirements.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A:** This uses an AUTH token and TLS, but it creates a new cluster. Current ElastiCache documentation supports enabling in-transit encryption on an existing Redis OSS 7+ replication group and enabling AUTH on an existing TLS-enabled cluster. Creating a new cluster is unnecessary and introduces migration/cutover work. Also, Secrets Manager is the better purpose-built service for managing application secrets and rotation.
- **C:** Redis OSS/ElastiCache client authentication is not implemented by creating and storing an SSL certificate for the application to use. The documentation specifically identifies AUTH as the client authentication mechanism and also notes that ElastiCache does not support mutual TLS. TLS provides encrypted transport and server authentication, not certificate-based client authentication in this context.
- **D:** This has the same certificate-based authentication problem as option C. An SSL certificate stored in Parameter Store does not configure Redis AUTH, and ElastiCache does not use customer-provided client SSL certificates for Redis client authentication.

zh.question: 一家公司正在运行一个应用程序，该应用程序使用 Amazon ElastiCache for Redis 集群作为缓存层。最近的一次安全审计发现，该公司已为 ElastiCache 配置了静态加密。但是，该公司没有将 ElastiCache 配置为使用传输中加密。此外，用户可以在不进行身份验证的情况下访问缓存。解决方案架构师必须进行更改，以要求用户身份验证，并确保公司使用端到端加密。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 AUTH 令牌。将该令牌作为加密参数存储在 AWS System Manager Parameter Store 中。创建一个启用 AUTH 的新集群，并配置传输中加密。更新应用程序，使其在需要时从 Parameter Store 检索 AUTH 令牌，并使用该 AUTH 令牌进行身份验证。
options.B: 创建一个 AUTH 令牌。将该令牌存储在 AWS Secrets Manager 中。配置现有集群以使用该 AUTH 令牌，并配置传输中加密。更新应用程序，使其在需要时从 Secrets Manager 检索 AUTH 令牌，并使用该 AUTH 令牌进行身份验证。
options.C: 创建一个 SSL 证书。将该证书存储在 AWS Secrets Manager 中。创建一个新集群，并配置传输中加密。更新应用程序，使其在需要时从 Secrets Manager 检索 SSL 证书，并使用该证书进行身份验证。
options.D: 创建一个 SSL 证书。将该证书作为加密的高级参数存储在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中。更新现有集群以配置传输中加密。更新应用程序，使其在需要时从 Parameter Store 检索 SSL 证书，并使用该证书进行身份验证。

zh.explanation:
该场景询问如何向现有的 Amazon ElastiCache for Redis 缓存层添加**客户端身份验证**和**端到端加密**；该缓存层已经具有静态加密，但缺少传输中的 TLS 和身份验证。

**正确答案：B。**

ElastiCache for Redis OSS/Valkey 支持对客户端到节点以及节点到节点的流量进行传输中 TLS 加密。AWS 文档说明，传输中加密可提供加密的客户端连接、加密的服务器连接、服务器身份验证，以及通过 Redis OSS/Valkey AUTH 实现的客户端身份验证。文档还说明，对于运行 Redis OSS 版本 7 及更高版本和 Valkey 7.2 及更高版本的复制组，支持在现有基于节点的集群上修改传输中加密设置（[ElastiCache in-transit encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/in-transit-encryption.html)）。

对于在现有集群上启用 TLS，AWS 记录了一个两步迁移过程：首先将传输加密模式设置为 `preferred`，以便加密和未加密的客户端都可以连接；然后在客户端迁移完成后，将模式设置为 `required`，以便只允许加密连接（[Enabling in-transit encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/in-transit-encryption-enable.html)）。

对于身份验证，ElastiCache AUTH 令牌是相关机制。AWS 说明，AUTH 只能为启用了传输中加密的 Redis OSS/Valkey 集群启用，并且可以使用 `ModifyReplicationGroup` 通过 `--auth-token` 和 `--auth-token-update-strategy`（例如 `ROTATE`）修改现有集群，然后使用 `SET` 使令牌成为必需（[Authenticating with the Valkey and Redis OSS AUTH command](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/auth.html)）。将 AUTH 令牌存储在 AWS Secrets Manager 中是合适的，因为 Secrets Manager 旨在管理、检索和轮换应用程序凭证、API 密钥及其他机密，应用程序可以在运行时动态检索机密（[What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)）。

因此，创建 AUTH 令牌，将其存储在 Secrets Manager 中，修改现有集群以启用 TLS 并使用 AUTH，并更新应用程序以检索和使用该令牌，可以满足这两个要求。

**其他选项为什么不正确：**

- **A:** 该选项使用 AUTH 令牌和 TLS，但它创建了一个新集群。当前 ElastiCache 文档支持在现有 Redis OSS 7+ 复制组上启用传输中加密，并在现有启用 TLS 的集群上启用 AUTH。创建新集群是不必要的，并会引入迁移/切换工作。此外，Secrets Manager 是更适合用于管理应用程序机密和轮换的专用服务。
- **C:** Redis OSS/ElastiCache 客户端身份验证不是通过创建并存储供应用程序使用的 SSL 证书来实现的。文档明确指出 AUTH 是客户端身份验证机制，并且还说明 ElastiCache 不支持 mutual TLS。TLS 在此上下文中提供加密传输和服务器身份验证，而不是基于证书的客户端身份验证。
- **D:** 该选项与选项 C 存在相同的基于证书的身份验证问题。存储在 Parameter Store 中的 SSL 证书不会配置 Redis AUTH，ElastiCache 也不会使用客户提供的客户端 SSL 证书进行 Redis 客户端身份验证。

en.question: A company is running a compute workload by using Amazon EC2 Spot Instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. The launch template uses two placement groups and a single instance type. Recently, a monitoring system reported Auto Scaling instance launch failures that correlated with longer wait times for system users. The company needs to improve the overall reliability of the workload. Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.A: Replace the launch template with a launch configuration to use an Auto Scaling group that uses attribute-based instance type selection.
options.B: Create a new launch template version that uses attribute-based instance type selection. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the new launch template version.
options.C: Update the launch template Auto Scaling group to increase the number of placement groups.
options.D: Update the launch template to use a larger instance type.

en.explanation:
The workload uses **EC2 Spot Instances in an Auto Scaling group**, but the current launch template is highly constrained: it specifies **one instance type** and uses placement groups. The reported launch failures and user wait times indicate that Auto Scaling cannot always find matching Spot capacity. The requirement is to improve reliability by increasing the likelihood that Auto Scaling can successfully launch replacement or scale-out instances.

**Correct answer: B. Create a new launch template version that uses attribute-based instance type selection. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the new launch template version.**

AWS documentation for Auto Scaling launch failures says that when there is no matching Spot capacity, a recommended solution is to follow the best practice of using **a diverse set of instance types** so the group is not reliant on one specific instance type ([Troubleshoot EC2 instance launch failures](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ts-as-instancelaunchfailure.html)). Attribute-based instance type selection directly supports this by allowing you to specify required attributes such as vCPU count, memory, storage, and burstable performance instead of hard-coding a single instance type. When the Auto Scaling group needs to launch an instance, it searches for matching instance types that are available in the Availability Zone, and the allocation strategy determines which matching type to launch ([Create mixed instances group using attribute-based instance type selection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/create-mixed-instances-group-attribute-based-instance-type-selection.html)).

Creating a **new launch template version** and updating the Auto Scaling group to use it is also the correct operational approach. AWS states that if you associate a new launch template or launch configuration with an Auto Scaling group, all new instances use the updated configuration, while existing instances continue running until replaced or refreshed ([Update an Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/update-auto-scaling-group.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. Replace the launch template with a launch configuration to use attribute-based instance type selection.**  
  This is not the right direction. The documented prerequisite for attribute-based instance type selection is to create/use a **launch template**, not a launch configuration ([attribute-based instance type selection prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/create-mixed-instances-group-attribute-based-instance-type-selection.html)). Launch configurations are the older mechanism and do not solve the need to broaden Spot capacity choices through modern mixed instance/attribute-based selection.

- **C. Update the launch template Auto Scaling group to increase the number of placement groups.**  
  The launch failures are caused by constrained capacity matching, especially with Spot. Increasing the number of placement groups does not address the AWS-recommended fix of diversifying instance types. Placement constraints can make capacity harder to obtain; the documented remedy for insufficient capacity is to use more Availability Zones and a diverse set of instance types, not more placement groups ([Troubleshoot EC2 instance launch failures](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ts-as-instancelaunchfailure.html)).

- **D. Update the launch template to use a larger instance type.**  
  This still relies on a **single instance type**, and a larger instance type may be even harder to obtain as Spot capacity. It does not provide the flexibility AWS recommends for Spot reliability. Attribute-based instance type selection provides a pool of compatible instance types instead of a single fixed type.

Therefore, **B** is the best solution because it increases Spot capacity flexibility and follows AWS guidance for reducing launch failures caused by insufficient matching Spot capacity.

zh.question: 一家公司正在使用 Auto Scaling 组中的 Amazon EC2 Spot Instances 运行计算工作负载。启动模板使用两个置放群组和单一实例类型。最近，监控系统报告了 Auto Scaling 实例启动失败，并且这些失败与系统用户等待时间变长相关。该公司需要提高工作负载的整体可靠性。哪种解决方案可以满足此要求？

options.A: 将启动模板替换为启动配置，以使用采用基于属性的实例类型选择的 Auto Scaling 组。
options.B: 创建一个新的启动模板版本，使用基于属性的实例类型选择。配置 Auto Scaling 组使用新的启动模板版本。
options.C: 更新启动模板 Auto Scaling 组，以增加置放群组的数量。
options.D: 更新启动模板以使用更大的实例类型。

zh.explanation:
该工作负载使用 **Auto Scaling 组中的 EC2 Spot Instances**，但当前启动模板受到高度限制：它指定了 **一个实例类型**，并使用置放群组。报告的启动失败和用户等待时间表明，Auto Scaling 并不总是能找到匹配的 Spot 容量。要求是通过提高 Auto Scaling 成功启动替换实例或横向扩展实例的可能性来提高可靠性。

**正确答案：B. 创建一个新的启动模板版本，使用基于属性的实例类型选择。配置 Auto Scaling 组使用新的启动模板版本。**

关于 Auto Scaling 启动失败，AWS 文档指出，当没有匹配的 Spot 容量时，建议的解决方案是遵循使用 **一组多样化实例类型** 的最佳实践，使该组不依赖某个特定实例类型（[排查 EC2 实例启动失败](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ts-as-instancelaunchfailure.html)）。基于属性的实例类型选择直接支持这一点，它允许你指定所需属性，例如 vCPU 数量、内存、存储和突发性能，而不是硬编码单一实例类型。当 Auto Scaling 组需要启动实例时，它会搜索在可用区中可用的匹配实例类型，并由分配策略决定启动哪种匹配类型（[使用基于属性的实例类型选择创建混合实例组](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/create-mixed-instances-group-attribute-based-instance-type-selection.html)）。

创建 **新的启动模板版本** 并更新 Auto Scaling 组以使用它，也是正确的运维方法。AWS 表示，如果将新的启动模板或启动配置与 Auto Scaling 组关联，则所有新实例都使用更新后的配置，而现有实例会继续运行，直到被替换或刷新（[更新 Auto Scaling 组](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/update-auto-scaling-group.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A. 将启动模板替换为启动配置，以使用采用基于属性的实例类型选择的 Auto Scaling 组。**  
  这不是正确方向。基于属性的实例类型选择的文档化先决条件是创建/使用 **启动模板**，而不是启动配置（[基于属性的实例类型选择先决条件](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/create-mixed-instances-group-attribute-based-instance-type-selection.html)）。启动配置是较旧的机制，无法通过现代混合实例/基于属性的选择来满足扩大 Spot 容量选择范围的需求。

- **C. 更新启动模板 Auto Scaling 组，以增加置放群组的数量。**  
  启动失败是由容量匹配受限导致的，尤其是在 Spot 场景中。增加置放群组数量并不能解决 AWS 推荐的实例类型多样化修复方案。置放约束可能会使容量更难获得；对于容量不足，文档化的补救措施是使用更多可用区和一组多样化的实例类型，而不是更多置放群组（[排查 EC2 实例启动失败](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ts-as-instancelaunchfailure.html)）。

- **D. 更新启动模板以使用更大的实例类型。**  
  这仍然依赖 **单一实例类型**，而且更大的实例类型作为 Spot 容量可能更难获得。它没有提供 AWS 为 Spot 可靠性所建议的灵活性。基于属性的实例类型选择提供的是一组兼容实例类型，而不是单一固定类型。

因此，**B** 是最佳解决方案，因为它提高了 Spot 容量灵活性，并遵循 AWS 关于减少由匹配 Spot 容量不足导致的启动失败的指导。

en.question: A company is migrating a document processing workload to AWS. The company has updated many applications to natively use the Amazon S3 API to store, retrieve, and modify documents that a processing server generates at a rate of approximately 5 documents every second. After the document processing is finished, customers can download the documents directly from Amazon S3. During the migration, the company discovered that it could not immediately update the processing server that generates many documents to support the S3 API. The server runs on Linux and requires fast local access to the files that the server generates and modifies. When the server finishes processing, the files must be available to the public for download within 30 minutes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?

options.A: Migrate the application to an AWS Lambda function. Use the AWS SDK for Java to generate, modify, and access the files that the company stores directly in Amazon S3.
options.B: Set up an Amazon S3 File Gateway and configure a file share that is linked to the document store. Mount the file share on an Amazon EC2 instance by using NFS. When changes occur in Amazon S3, initiate a RefreshCache API call to update the S3 File Gateway.
options.C: Configure Amazon FSx for Lustre with an import and export policy. Link the new file system to an S3 bucket. Install the Lustre client and mount the document store to an Amazon EC2 instance by using NFS.
options.D: Configure AWS DataSync to connect to an Amazon EC2 instance. Configure a task to synchronize the generated files to and from Amazon S3.

en.explanation:
The workload has a legacy Linux processing server that still expects a local file interface, needs low-latency local access while it creates/modifies files, and the completed files must end up in Amazon S3 for public download within 30 minutes. The least-effort pattern is to provide the server with a file share that is backed by S3 rather than rewriting the server.

**Correct answer: B. Set up an Amazon S3 File Gateway and mount it with NFS.**

Amazon S3 File Gateway is designed for this exact bridge: it provides a file interface into Amazon S3 and lets applications store and retrieve S3 objects by using standard file protocols such as **NFS** and SMB. AWS describes it as giving access to S3 objects as files or file share mount points, with low-latency access through transparent local caching, and notes that the gateway can also be deployed as an AMI in Amazon EC2 ([AWS Storage Gateway: What is Amazon S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html)). AWS also documents deploying an S3 File Gateway on an EC2 host ([Deploy a customized Amazon EC2 host for S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/ec2-gateway-file.html)).

The `RefreshCache` detail in option B is consistent with File Gateway cache behavior for changes made directly in S3 outside the gateway workflow. AWS states that the gateway maintains a cached inventory for NFS/SMB clients and that refreshing the S3 bucket object cache updates that inventory to reflect S3-side changes. AWS also documents automated and manual refresh methods, including a common fixed rate of 30 minutes for a scheduled refresh workflow ([Refreshing Amazon S3 bucket object cache](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/refresh-cache.html)). For files written through the gateway, the gateway transfers data to S3; for objects changed directly in S3 by other applications, a cache refresh keeps the mounted file share’s inventory current.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

* **A. Migrate the application to Lambda and use the SDK.** This requires rewriting or replatforming the processing server to use AWS SDK/S3 APIs. The scenario explicitly says the company cannot immediately update the processing server to support the S3 API and needs fast local file access. Therefore, this is not the least-effort migration path.

* **C. Configure FSx for Lustre and mount by using NFS.** FSx for Lustre can be linked to S3 and is useful for high-performance compute workflows, but the option is technically wrong because FSx for Lustre is mounted with the Lustre client and the Lustre mount type, not NFS. AWS’s getting started guide instructs users to install the Lustre client and mount with `sudo mount -t lustre ...`, not an NFS mount ([Getting started with Amazon FSx for Lustre](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/getting-started.html)). Also, FSx for Lustre is generally a heavier-weight HPC-oriented file system than needed for a simple legacy file-to-S3 bridge.

* **D. Configure AWS DataSync to synchronize files to and from S3.** DataSync is useful for migrations and periodic transfers, but it does not provide the server with a low-latency local file interface backed by S3. In addition, scheduled DataSync tasks have a minimum interval of 1 hour; AWS explicitly states that you cannot schedule a task faster than 1 hour ([Scheduling when your AWS DataSync task runs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/task-scheduling.html)). That does not satisfy the requirement that completed files be available in S3 within 30 minutes with minimal effort.

Therefore, **B** is the best answer.

zh.question: 一家公司正在将文档处理工作负载迁移到 AWS。该公司已经更新了许多应用程序，使其能够原生使用 Amazon S3 API 来存储、检索和修改处理服务器生成的文档，该服务器大约每秒生成 5 个文档。文档处理完成后，客户可以直接从 Amazon S3 下载这些文档。在迁移期间，公司发现无法立即更新生成许多文档的处理服务器以支持 S3 API。该服务器运行在 Linux 上，并且需要对其生成和修改的文件进行快速本地访问。当服务器完成处理后，文件必须在 30 分钟内可供公众下载。哪种解决方案能够以最少的工作量满足这些要求？

options.A: 将应用程序迁移到 AWS Lambda 函数。使用 AWS SDK for Java 生成、修改和访问公司直接存储在 Amazon S3 中的文件。
options.B: 设置 Amazon S3 File Gateway，并配置一个链接到文档存储的文件共享。使用 NFS 将该文件共享挂载到 Amazon EC2 实例上。当 Amazon S3 中发生更改时，发起 RefreshCache API 调用以更新 S3 File Gateway。
options.C: 配置带有导入和导出策略的 Amazon FSx for Lustre。将新的文件系统链接到 S3 存储桶。安装 Lustre 客户端，并使用 NFS 将文档存储挂载到 Amazon EC2 实例。
options.D: 配置 AWS DataSync 以连接到 Amazon EC2 实例。配置一个任务，将生成的文件与 Amazon S3 进行双向同步。

zh.explanation:
该工作负载有一台旧版 Linux 处理服务器，仍然需要文件本地接口，在创建/修改文件时需要低延迟的本地访问，并且完成的文件必须最终进入 Amazon S3，以便公众下载。最少工作量的模式是为服务器提供一个由 S3 支持的文件共享，而不是重写服务器。

**正确答案：B。设置 Amazon S3 File Gateway，并使用 NFS 挂载它。**

Amazon S3 File Gateway 正是为这种桥接场景设计的：它为 Amazon S3 提供文件接口，并允许应用程序使用 **NFS** 和 SMB 等标准文件协议来存储和检索 S3 对象。AWS 将其描述为能够以文件或文件共享挂载点的形式访问 S3 对象，并通过透明的本地缓存提供低延迟访问；同时指出该网关也可以作为 AMI 部署在 Amazon EC2 中（[AWS Storage Gateway: What is Amazon S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html)）。AWS 还记录了在 EC2 主机上部署 S3 File Gateway 的方法（[Deploy a customized Amazon EC2 host for S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/ec2-gateway-file.html)）。

选项 B 中的 `RefreshCache` 细节与 File Gateway 对通过网关工作流之外直接在 S3 中进行的更改的缓存行为一致。AWS 表示，网关会为 NFS/SMB 客户端维护缓存清单，刷新 S3 bucket 对象缓存会更新该清单，以反映 S3 端的更改。AWS 还记录了自动和手动刷新方法，包括计划刷新工作流常用的固定 30 分钟频率（[Refreshing Amazon S3 bucket object cache](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/refresh-cache.html)）。对于通过网关写入的文件，网关会将数据传输到 S3；对于由其他应用程序直接在 S3 中更改的对象，缓存刷新会使已挂载文件共享的清单保持最新。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

* **A. 将应用程序迁移到 Lambda 并使用 SDK。** 这需要重写处理服务器或将其重新平台化以使用 AWS SDK/S3 API。场景明确说明公司无法立即更新处理服务器以支持 S3 API，并且需要快速本地文件访问。因此，这不是工作量最少的迁移路径。

* **C. 配置 FSx for Lustre 并使用 NFS 挂载。** FSx for Lustre 可以链接到 S3，并且适用于高性能计算工作负载，但该选项在技术上是错误的，因为 FSx for Lustre 是使用 Lustre 客户端和 Lustre 挂载类型进行挂载，而不是 NFS。AWS 的入门指南指示用户安装 Lustre 客户端，并使用 `sudo mount -t lustre ...` 挂载，而不是 NFS 挂载（[Getting started with Amazon FSx for Lustre](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/getting-started.html)）。此外，FSx for Lustre 通常是面向 HPC 的较重量级文件系统，对于简单的旧版文件到 S3 桥接来说并不必要。

* **D. 配置 AWS DataSync 以将文件与 S3 同步。** DataSync 对迁移和周期性传输很有用，但它不会为服务器提供由 S3 支持的低延迟本地文件接口。此外，计划的 DataSync 任务最小间隔为 1 小时；AWS 明确表示无法将任务计划为快于 1 小时运行一次（[Scheduling when your AWS DataSync task runs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/task-scheduling.html)）。这无法在最少工作量下满足完成的文件必须在 30 分钟内可用于 S3 的要求。

因此，**B** 是最佳答案。

en.question: A delivery company is running a serverless solution in the AWS Cloud. The solution manages user data, delivery information, and past purchase details. The solution consists of several microservices. The central user service stores sensitive data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Several of the other microservices store a copy of parts of the sensitive data in different storage services. The company needs the ability to delete user information upon request. As soon as the central user service deletes a user, every other microservice must also delete its copy of the data immediately. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Activate DynamoDB Streams on the DynamoDB table. Create an AWS Lambda trigger for the DynamoDB stream that will post events about user deletion in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure each microservice to poll the queue and delete the user from the DynamoDB table.
options.B: Set up DynamoDB event notifications on the DynamoDB table. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target for the DynamoDB event notification. Configure each microservice to subscribe to the SNS topic and to delete the user from the DynamoDB table.
options.C: Configure the central user service to post an event on a custom Amazon EventBridge event bus when the company deletes a user. Create an EventBridge rule for each microservice to match the user deletion event pattern and invoke logic in the microservice to delete the user from the DynamoDB table.
options.D: Configure the central user service to post a message on an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue when the company deletes a user. Configure each microservice to create an event filter on the SQS queue and to delete the user from the DynamoDB table.

en.explanation:
The company needs a serverless event-driven fan-out design: when the central user service deletes a user, every microservice that has stored a copy of that user data must be notified and run its own deletion logic.

**Correct answer: C. Configure the central user service to post an event on a custom Amazon EventBridge event bus when the company deletes a user. Create an EventBridge rule for each microservice to match the user deletion event pattern and invoke logic in the microservice to delete the user data.**

Amazon EventBridge is the best fit because an EventBridge event bus is designed to route events from sources to **zero or more targets**. AWS describes an event bus as a router that receives events and delivers them to targets, and custom event buses can be created for application events. EventBridge rules can match incoming events by event pattern and send matching events to targets for processing. This lets the central user service publish a single user-deletion event, while each microservice has an independent rule and target path that invokes that service’s deletion workflow. See the EventBridge documentation for [event buses and rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-what-is-how-it-works-concepts.html).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A is incorrect.** DynamoDB Streams can capture item-level changes, including deletes, in near real time; DynamoDB writes stream records when an application creates, updates, or deletes items in a table. However, this option sends the deletion event to a single SQS queue that all microservices poll. A single SQS queue is a task distribution/competing-consumer pattern, not a broadcast mechanism that guarantees every microservice receives the same deletion event. The SQS standard queue documentation lists allocating tasks to multiple worker nodes as a standard use case, which is different from fan-out to every service. See [DynamoDB Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html) and [Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html).

- **B is incorrect.** The option refers to DynamoDB event notifications directly targeting an SNS topic. DynamoDB’s documented change data capture mechanism is DynamoDB Streams, which captures item-level modifications such as creates, updates, and deletes. The option is not the appropriate DynamoDB eventing model for this requirement.

- **D is incorrect.** Posting one message to one SQS queue does not ensure that every microservice receives and processes the same deletion event. Multiple consumers of a single SQS queue are used to distribute work among consumers. In addition, creating an “event filter” on an SQS queue is not the correct model for routing one deletion event to multiple independent microservices.

Therefore, **C** is the correct solution because EventBridge provides the required custom event bus and rule-based fan-out pattern for notifying each microservice to delete its copy of the user data.

zh.question: 一家配送公司正在 AWS 云中运行一个无服务器解决方案。该解决方案管理用户数据、配送信息和历史购买详情。该解决方案由多个微服务组成。中央用户服务将敏感数据存储在 Amazon DynamoDB 表中。其他几个微服务会在不同的存储服务中存储部分敏感数据的副本。公司需要能够按请求删除用户信息。一旦中央用户服务删除某个用户，其他每个微服务也必须立即删除其数据副本。哪种解决方案将满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 DynamoDB 表上启用 DynamoDB Streams。为 DynamoDB 流创建一个 AWS Lambda 触发器，该触发器会将有关用户删除的事件发布到 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列中。配置每个微服务轮询该队列，并从 DynamoDB 表中删除该用户。
options.B: 在 DynamoDB 表上设置 DynamoDB 事件通知。创建一个 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题作为 DynamoDB 事件通知的目标。配置每个微服务订阅该 SNS 主题，并从 DynamoDB 表中删除该用户。
options.C: 配置中央用户服务在公司删除用户时，在自定义 Amazon EventBridge 事件总线上发布一个事件。为每个微服务创建一个 EventBridge 规则，以匹配用户删除事件模式，并调用微服务中的逻辑从 DynamoDB 表中删除该用户。
options.D: 配置中央用户服务在公司删除用户时，向 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列发布一条消息。配置每个微服务在该 SQS 队列上创建事件筛选器，并从 DynamoDB 表中删除该用户。

zh.explanation:
公司需要一种无服务器、事件驱动的扇出设计：当中央用户服务删除一个用户时，所有存储了该用户数据副本的微服务都必须收到通知，并运行自己的删除逻辑。

**正确答案：C。配置中央用户服务在公司删除用户时，在自定义 Amazon EventBridge 事件总线上发布一个事件。为每个微服务创建一个 EventBridge 规则，以匹配用户删除事件模式，并调用微服务中的逻辑来删除用户数据。**

Amazon EventBridge 是最佳选择，因为 EventBridge 事件总线旨在将事件从源路由到 **零个或多个目标**。AWS 将事件总线描述为一个路由器，它接收事件并将事件传送到目标，并且可以为应用程序事件创建自定义事件总线。EventBridge 规则可以按事件模式匹配传入事件，并将匹配的事件发送到目标进行处理。这样，中央用户服务可以发布一个用户删除事件，而每个微服务都有独立的规则和目标路径，用于调用该服务的删除工作流。请参阅 EventBridge 文档中的 [event buses and rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-what-is-how-it-works-concepts.html)。

**其他选项不正确的原因：**

- **A 不正确。** DynamoDB Streams 可以近实时捕获项目级更改，包括删除；当应用程序在表中创建、更新或删除项目时，DynamoDB 会写入流记录。但是，该选项将删除事件发送到所有微服务都轮询的单个 SQS 队列。单个 SQS 队列是一种任务分发/竞争消费者模式，而不是保证每个微服务都收到相同删除事件的广播机制。SQS 标准队列文档将向多个工作节点分配任务列为标准用例，这不同于向每个服务扇出。请参阅 [DynamoDB Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html) 和 [Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html)。

- **B 不正确。** 该选项提到 DynamoDB event notifications 直接以 SNS 主题为目标。DynamoDB 有文档记录的变更数据捕获机制是 DynamoDB Streams，它捕获项目级修改，例如创建、更新和删除。该选项并不是满足此要求的适当 DynamoDB 事件模型。

- **D 不正确。** 向一个 SQS 队列发布一条消息并不能确保每个微服务都收到并处理相同的删除事件。单个 SQS 队列的多个消费者用于在消费者之间分配工作。此外，在 SQS 队列上创建“event filter”并不是将一个删除事件路由到多个独立微服务的正确模型。

因此，**C** 是正确的解决方案，因为 EventBridge 提供了所需的自定义事件总线和基于规则的扇出模式，用于通知每个微服务删除其用户数据副本。

en.question: A company is running a web application in a VPC. The web application runs on a group of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB is using AWS WAF. An external customer needs to connect to the web application. The company must provide IP addresses to all external customers. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Assign an Elastic IP address to the NLB.
options.B: Allocate an Elastic IP address. Assign the Elastic IP address to the ALProvide the Elastic IP address to the customer.
options.C: Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator. Specify the ALB as the accelerator's endpoint. Provide the accelerator's IP addresses to the customer.
options.D: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the ALB as the origin. Ping the distribution's DNS name to determine the distribution's public IP address. Provide the IP address to the customer.

en.explanation:
The application is already running behind an **Application Load Balancer (ALB)** and is using **AWS WAF**. The new requirement is to give external customers fixed IP addresses to connect to or allowlist, while keeping operational overhead low.

**Correct answer: C. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator, specify the ALB as the endpoint, and provide the accelerator IP addresses.**

AWS Global Accelerator is designed for this exact pattern. The documentation states that Global Accelerator provides static IP addresses associated with an accelerator, and for IPv4 it provides **two static IPv4 addresses**. It also states that standard accelerator endpoints can include **Application Load Balancers**. Therefore, placing Global Accelerator in front of the existing ALB provides stable public IP addresses without replacing the load balancer or redesigning the application path ([What is AWS Global Accelerator?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/what-is-global-accelerator.html)). The ALB integration documentation also describes Global Accelerator as directing traffic to **static IP addresses that serve as fixed endpoints** for the load balancer ([Integrations for your Application Load Balancer - AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-integrations.html)).

This also preserves the current ALB-based architecture and AWS WAF usage. AWS WAF can protect regional resources including **Application Load Balancers**, and the existing ALB can continue to use its web ACL ([Resources that you can protect with AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/how-aws-waf-works-resources.html)).

### Why the other options are incorrect

**A. Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Assign an Elastic IP address to the NLB.**  
An internet-facing NLB can use Elastic IP addresses per Availability Zone, so this can provide static IPs ([Update the Availability Zones for your Network Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/availability-zones.html)). However, this option requires replacing the ALB, which is more operationally disruptive and may lose ALB Layer 7 features. More importantly, the existing application uses AWS WAF, and AWS WAF regional resource support includes Application Load Balancer but not Network Load Balancer ([Resources that you can protect with AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/how-aws-waf-works-resources.html)). This is not the least-overhead solution.

**B. Allocate an Elastic IP address and assign it to the ALB.**  
This is not a supported approach for an Application Load Balancer. ALBs are configured by enabling Availability Zones and selecting subnets; the ALB subnet configuration does not provide the NLB-style Elastic IP mapping option ([Update the Availability Zones for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-subnets.html)). Elastic IP assignment for static load balancer IPs is documented for internet-facing Network Load Balancers, not ALBs ([Update the Availability Zones for your Network Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/availability-zones.html)).

**D. Configure CloudFront and provide the IP address obtained by pinging the distribution DNS name.**  
CloudFront is not a reliable way to provide a small, fixed set of static IP addresses by pinging a distribution DNS name. CloudFront uses globally distributed edge infrastructure and AWS maintains CloudFront IP ranges through a managed prefix list, which is kept up to date because the set of CloudFront origin-facing IP ranges changes over time ([Locations and IP address ranges of CloudFront edge servers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/LocationsOfEdgeServers.html)). Pinging a CloudFront DNS name does not produce a durable customer allowlist target and would create operational overhead.

Therefore, **C** provides the required fixed public IP addresses while retaining the existing ALB and AWS WAF configuration with the least operational overhead.
