Since the contact center has dozens of contact flows and claimed numbers, waiting to create those resources during an outage increases RTO compared with having flows already present.

- **C is wrong** because it delays creation of **hundreds of users** until failover. Users/agents are required for the contact center to operate. AWS explicitly notes that when shifting telephony traffic, agents/sign-ins must also be shifted so they can handle calls in the other Region. Creating hundreds of users during failover is likely to produce a longer RTO than automating the smaller remaining phone-number step in option D.

References: [Create a replica of your existing Amazon Connect instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/create-replica-connect-instance.html), [UpdateTrafficDistribution API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateTrafficDistribution.html), [AWS::Connect::PhoneNumber](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-connect-phonenumber.html), [Monitoring Route 53 health checks using CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/monitoring-health-checks.html).

zh.question: 一家公司正在使用 Amazon Connect 构建呼叫中心。该公司的运营团队正在跨 AWS 区域定义灾难恢复（DR）策略。该联络中心有数十个联系流、数百名用户以及数十个已认领的电话号码。哪种解决方案将以最低的 RTO 提供 DR？

options.A: 创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来检查 Amazon Connect 实例的可用性，并在不可用时向运营团队发送通知。创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，每 5 分钟调用一次该 Lambda 函数。收到通知后，指示运营团队使用 AWS Management Console 在第二个区域中预置新的 Amazon Connect 实例。使用 AWS CloudFormation 模板部署联系流、用户和已认领的电话号码。
options.B: 在第二个区域中预置一个包含所有现有用户的新 Amazon Connect 实例。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来检查 Amazon Connect 实例的可用性。创建一个 Amazon EventBridge 规则，每 5 分钟调用一次该 Lambda 函数。发生问题时，将该 Lambda 函数配置为部署一个 AWS CloudFormation 模板，在第二个区域中预置联系流和已认领的号码。
options.C: 在第二个区域中预置一个包含所有现有联系流和已认领电话号码的新 Amazon Connect 实例。为 Amazon Connect 实例的 URL 创建 Amazon Route 53 运行状况检查。为失败的运行状况检查创建 Amazon CloudWatch 警报。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来部署一个 AWS CloudFormation 模板，以预置所有用户。将该警报配置为调用该 Lambda 函数。
options.D: 在第二个区域中预置一个包含所有现有用户和联系流的新 Amazon Connect 实例。为 Amazon Connect 实例的 URL 创建 Amazon Route 53 运行状况检查。为失败的运行状况检查创建 Amazon CloudWatch 警报。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来部署一个 AWS CloudFormation 模板，以预置已认领的电话号码。将该警报配置为调用该 Lambda 函数。

zh.explanation:
该场景询问的是 Amazon Connect 灾难恢复设计，需要在环境中已有许多已配置资源（数十个流、数百名用户以及数十个已认领电话号码）的情况下实现 **最低 RTO**。为了实现低 RTO，DR 区域应在中断发生前准备好联络中心中最大且依赖关系最重的部分，而故障转移操作应只自动化剩余的可恢复步骤。

**正确答案：D。**

选项 D 会在辅助 Amazon Connect 实例中预先预置现有的 **用户** 和 **联系流**。这很重要，因为用户/座席和流是座席登录并处理呼叫所必需的。关于 Amazon Connect 跨区域弹性的 AWS 文档强调，当电话流量被转移时，座席/登录也必须被转移或可用；否则，呼叫可能会到达另一个区域却没有可用座席接听。Amazon Connect Global Resiliency 文档还将 **流** 和 **用户** 列为副本实例中会镜像的资源，这表明它们是应存在于两个区域以实现弹性运营的核心资源。最后，CloudFormation 支持 `AWS::Connect::PhoneNumber`，它“将电话号码认领到指定的 Connect 实例或流量分配组”，因此在故障转移期间自动预置已认领电话号码是一个有效的剩余恢复步骤。Route 53 运行状况检查可以使用 CloudWatch 警报进行监控，并且 Route 53 文档说明，当运行状况检查指标表明端点不正常时，警报会进入 `ALARM` 状态，这可用作故障转移触发器。

因此，在列出的选项中，**D 提供最低 RTO**，因为辅助区域已准备好高基数且对运营至关重要的资源——用户和流——剩余任务也已自动化。

### 为什么其他选项不正确

- **A 错误**，因为它要等到故障发生后，才由运营团队手动在另一个区域中预置新的 Amazon Connect 实例，然后部署用户、流和电话号码。人工干预加上完整环境预置会导致最高的 RTO。

- **B 错误**，因为仅预先预置了用户。联系流和电话号码只有在故障发生后才会部署。由于该联络中心有数十个联系流和已认领号码，在中断期间才创建这些资源会增加 RTO，而不是像已准备好流那样降低 RTO。

- **C 错误**，因为它将 **数百名用户** 的创建延迟到故障转移时。用户/座席是联络中心运行所必需的。AWS 明确指出，在转移电话流量时，座席/登录也必须被转移，以便他们能够在另一个区域处理呼叫。在故障转移期间创建数百名用户，很可能比选项 D 中自动化较小规模的剩余电话号码步骤产生更长的 RTO。

参考资料：[Create a replica of your existing Amazon Connect instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/create-replica-connect-instance.html), [UpdateTrafficDistribution API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateTrafficDistribution.html), [AWS::Connect::PhoneNumber](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-connect-phonenumber.html), [Monitoring Route 53 health checks using CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/monitoring-health-checks.html).

en.question: A company runs an application on AWS. The company curates data from several different sources. The company uses proprietary algorithms to perform data transformations and aggregations. After the company performs ETL processes, the company stores the results in Amazon Redshift tables. The company sells this data to other companies. The company downloads the data as files from the Amazon Redshift tables and transmits the files to several data customers by using FTP. The number of data customers has grown significantly. Management of the data customers has become difficult. The company will use AWS Data Exchange to create a data product that the company can use to share data with customers. The company wants to confirm the identities of the customers before the company shares data. The customers also need access to the most recent data when the company publishes the data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Data Exchange for APIs to share data with customers. Configure subscription verification. In the AWS account of the company that produces the data, create an Amazon API Gateway Data API service integration with Amazon Redshift. Require the data customers to subscribe to the data product.
options.B: In the AWS account of the company that produces the data, create an AWS Data Exchange datashare by connecting AWS Data Exchange to the Redshift cluster. Configure subscription verification. Require the data customers to subscribe to the data product.
options.C: Download the data from the Amazon Redshift tables to an Amazon S3 bucket periodically. Use AWS Data Exchange for S3 to share data with customers. Configure subscription verification. Require the data customers to subscribe to the data product.
options.D: Publish the Amazon Redshift data to an Open Data on AWS Data Exchange. Require the customers to subscribe to the data product in AWS Data Exchange. In the AWS account of the company that produces the data, attach IAM resource-based policies to the Amazon Redshift tables to allow access only to verified AWS accounts.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The company currently stores the monetized ETL output in Amazon Redshift tables and distributes files by FTP. It wants to move to AWS Data Exchange, verify customer identity before access, and let subscribers access the most recent published data with the least operational overhead.

## Correct answer: B

**B. Create an AWS Data Exchange datashare by connecting AWS Data Exchange to the Redshift cluster, enable subscription verification, and require customers to subscribe.**

This is the best fit because AWS Data Exchange supports **Amazon Redshift datashares**. AWS documentation states that producers can create AWS Data Exchange datashares that connect to Amazon Redshift databases, and that approved providers can add these datashares to AWS Data Exchange products. When a customer subscribes, AWS Data Exchange **automatically adds the customer as a data consumer** and removes access when the subscription ends. Consumers can then query the shared data in Amazon Redshift directly, without extracting, transforming, or loading the data ([AWS Data Exchange datashares - Amazon Redshift](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/adx_datashare_overview.html)).

This also addresses freshness and operational overhead. The Redshift documentation says subscribers can query **granular, up-to-date data in Amazon Redshift without the need to extract, transform, and load the data** ([AWS Data Exchange datashares - Amazon Redshift](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/adx_datashare_overview.html)). The AWS Data Exchange subscriber documentation similarly explains that an Amazon Redshift data set contains datashares that provide read-only access to tables, views, schemas, and UDFs, and that after the subscription starts, subscribers can query the data in Amazon Redshift without ETL ([Subscribing to and accessing an AWS Data Exchange product containing Amazon Redshift data sets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/data-exchange/latest/userguide/subscribing-to-Redshift-product.html)).

The identity-confirmation requirement is met by **subscription verification**. AWS documentation states that, for public AWS Data Exchange products, subscribers submit additional information about their identity and intended use case, and the provider reviews that information before approving the subscription ([Subscription verification for subscribers in AWS Data Exchange](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/data-exchange/latest/userguide/subscription-verification-sub.html)). Providers can enable subscription verification for their products ([Creating an offer for AWS Data Exchange products](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/data-exchange/latest/userguide/prepare-offers.html)).

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. AWS Data Exchange for APIs with API Gateway integration to Redshift

This could expose data through an API, but it requires designing, building, securing, and operating an API Gateway/API integration path to Redshift. That adds application/API management overhead and does not use the native Redshift datashare capability. Since the data already resides in Redshift and AWS Data Exchange datashares allow subscribers to query Redshift data directly, this is not the least-operational-overhead solution.

### C. Export Redshift data periodically to S3 and use AWS Data Exchange for S3

This is workable for file-based distribution, but it keeps a batch export process similar to the current FTP-oriented pattern. The company would need to schedule and manage exports from Redshift to S3 and publish updated data. It also introduces lag between Redshift updates and S3 publication. By contrast, Redshift datashares let subscribers query up-to-date Redshift data directly without extraction or ETL, making option B lower overhead.

### D. Publish as Open Data and use IAM resource-based policies on Redshift tables

This does not meet the requirements. Open Data is not appropriate for selling proprietary data to verified customers only. In addition, the proposed access-control model is not how AWS Data Exchange Redshift datashare subscriptions are managed. AWS Data Exchange datashares manage subscriber entitlement by adding and removing subscribed customers as consumers of the datashare; it is not a matter of attaching resource-based IAM policies directly to individual Redshift tables.

## Conclusion

Option **B** is correct because it uses the native AWS Data Exchange + Amazon Redshift datashare integration, supports subscriber identity verification, automatically manages subscriber access, and allows customers to query current Redshift data without periodic exports or custom APIs.

zh.question: 一家公司在 AWS 上运行一个应用程序。该公司从多个不同来源整理数据。公司使用专有算法执行数据转换和聚合。公司执行 ETL 流程后，将结果存储在 Amazon Redshift 表中。公司将这些数据出售给其他公司。公司从 Amazon Redshift 表中将数据下载为文件，并使用 FTP 将这些文件传输给多个数据客户。数据客户数量显著增长。管理这些数据客户变得困难。公司将使用 AWS Data Exchange 创建一个数据产品，用于与客户共享数据。公司希望在共享数据之前确认客户的身份。客户还需要在公司发布数据时访问最新数据。哪种解决方案能够以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 AWS Data Exchange for APIs 与客户共享数据。配置订阅验证。在生产数据的公司的 AWS 账户中，创建 Amazon API Gateway Data API service 与 Amazon Redshift 的集成。要求数据客户订阅该数据产品。
options.B: 在生产数据的公司的 AWS 账户中，通过将 AWS Data Exchange 连接到 Redshift 集群来创建 AWS Data Exchange datashare。配置订阅验证。要求数据客户订阅该数据产品。
options.C: 定期将 Amazon Redshift 表中的数据下载到 Amazon S3 桶。使用 AWS Data Exchange for S3 与客户共享数据。配置订阅验证。要求数据客户订阅该数据产品。
options.D: 将 Amazon Redshift 数据发布到 Open Data on AWS Data Exchange。要求客户在 AWS Data Exchange 中订阅该数据产品。在生产数据的公司的 AWS 账户中，将 IAM 基于资源的策略附加到 Amazon Redshift 表，以仅允许已验证的 AWS 账户访问。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该公司目前将货币化的 ETL 输出存储在 Amazon Redshift 表中，并通过 FTP 分发文件。公司希望迁移到 AWS Data Exchange，在允许访问之前验证客户身份，并让订阅者以最少的运营开销访问最新发布的数据。

## 正确答案：B

**B. 通过将 AWS Data Exchange 连接到 Redshift 集群来创建 AWS Data Exchange datashare，启用订阅验证，并要求客户订阅。**

这是最合适的选择，因为 AWS Data Exchange 支持 **Amazon Redshift datashares**。AWS 文档指出，生产者可以创建连接到 Amazon Redshift 数据库的 AWS Data Exchange datashares，并且获批准的提供商可以将这些 datashares 添加到 AWS Data Exchange 产品中。当客户订阅时，AWS Data Exchange 会**自动将客户添加为数据使用者**，并在订阅结束时移除访问权限。然后，使用者可以直接在 Amazon Redshift 中查询共享数据，而无需提取、转换或加载数据（[AWS Data Exchange datashares - Amazon Redshift](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/adx_datashare_overview.html)）。

这也满足了数据新鲜度和运营开销方面的要求。Redshift 文档表示，订阅者可以在 Amazon Redshift 中查询**细粒度的最新数据，而无需提取、转换和加载数据**（[AWS Data Exchange datashares - Amazon Redshift](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/adx_datashare_overview.html)）。AWS Data Exchange 订阅者文档同样解释说，Amazon Redshift 数据集包含 datashares，这些 datashares 提供对表、视图、架构和 UDF 的只读访问权限，并且在订阅开始后，订阅者可以在 Amazon Redshift 中查询数据，而无需 ETL（[订阅和访问包含 Amazon Redshift 数据集的 AWS Data Exchange 产品](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/data-exchange/latest/userguide/subscribing-to-Redshift-product.html)）。

身份确认要求通过**订阅验证**来满足。AWS 文档指出，对于公开的 AWS Data Exchange 产品，订阅者会提交有关其身份和预期使用场景的附加信息，提供商会在批准订阅之前审核这些信息（[AWS Data Exchange 中订阅者的订阅验证](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/data-exchange/latest/userguide/subscription-verification-sub.html)）。提供商可以为其产品启用订阅验证（[为 AWS Data Exchange 产品创建报价](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/data-exchange/latest/userguide/prepare-offers.html)）。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A. AWS Data Exchange for APIs 与 API Gateway 到 Redshift 的集成

这可以通过 API 暴露数据，但需要设计、构建、保护并运营通往 Redshift 的 API Gateway/API 集成路径。这会增加应用程序/API 管理开销，并且没有使用原生 Redshift datashare 功能。由于数据已经驻留在 Redshift 中，而 AWS Data Exchange datashares 允许订阅者直接查询 Redshift 数据，因此这不是运营开销最低的解决方案。

### C. 定期将 Redshift 数据导出到 S3 并使用 AWS Data Exchange for S3

这对于基于文件的分发是可行的，但它保留了类似当前 FTP 模式的批量导出流程。公司需要安排和管理从 Redshift 到 S3 的导出，并发布更新后的数据。它还会在 Redshift 更新和 S3 发布之间引入延迟。相比之下，Redshift datashares 允许订阅者直接查询最新的 Redshift 数据，而无需提取或 ETL，因此选项 B 的开销更低。

### D. 发布为 Open Data，并在 Redshift 表上使用 IAM 基于资源的策略

这不满足要求。Open Data 不适合仅向已验证客户出售专有数据。此外，所提出的访问控制模型并不是 AWS Data Exchange Redshift datashare 订阅的管理方式。AWS Data Exchange datashares 通过将已订阅客户添加为 datashare 的使用者以及移除这些客户来管理订阅者授权；这不是直接将基于资源的 IAM 策略附加到各个 Redshift 表的问题。

## 结论

选项 **B** 正确，因为它使用原生 AWS Data Exchange + Amazon Redshift datashare 集成，支持订阅者身份验证，自动管理订阅者访问权限，并允许客户查询当前 Redshift 数据，而无需定期导出或自定义 API。

en.question: A solutions architect is designing a solution to process events. The solution must have the ability to scale in and out based on the number of events that the solution receives. If a processing error occurs, the event must move into a separate queue for review. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Send event details to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure an AWS Lambda function as a subscriber to the SNS topic to process the events. Add an on-failure destination to the function. Set an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as the target.
options.B: Publish events to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. Configure the Auto Scaling group to scale in and out based on the ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric of the queue. Configure the application to write failed messages to a dead-letter queue.
options.C: Write events to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure a DynamoDB stream for the table. Configure the stream to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to process the events.
options.D: Publish events to an Amazon EventBndge event bus. Create and run an application on an Amazon EC2 instance with an Auto Scaling group that is behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Set the ALB as the event bus target. Configure the event bus to retry events. Write messages to a dead-letter queue if the application cannot process the messages.

en.explanation:
The solution needs a durable event-processing queue, a processing tier that can scale in and out as the queue load changes, and a separate queue for messages that cannot be processed successfully.

**Correct answer: B. Publish events to an Amazon SQS queue, process them with an EC2 Auto Scaling group, scale based on queue metrics, and send failed messages to a dead-letter queue.**

Amazon SQS is the right service to buffer the events. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can then run a fleet of worker instances that polls the queue and processes messages. AWS documents this exact pattern: you can scale an Auto Scaling group in response to changes in system load in an Amazon SQS queue, with EC2 instances processing messages from that queue. AWS also describes calculating queue backlog per instance from SQS message count and Auto Scaling group capacity for scaling decisions ([Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html)).

For error handling, Amazon SQS supports dead-letter queues. A source queue can target a DLQ for messages that are not processed successfully, and the DLQ lets you isolate and review unconsumed messages to determine why processing failed ([Using dead-letter queues in Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-dead-letter-queues.html)). This directly satisfies the requirement to move failed events into a separate queue for review.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. SNS topic with Lambda subscriber and Lambda on-failure destination:** This can process events and can send failed asynchronous invocation records to a destination such as SQS, but it does not use a durable work queue that drives scaling of a processing fleet based on queue backlog or event volume. The requirement specifically calls for scaling in and out based on the number of events received, and the SQS-plus-Auto Scaling worker pattern is the more direct fit.

- **C. DynamoDB table with DynamoDB Streams and Lambda:** DynamoDB Streams can invoke Lambda for changes to a table, but this option does not configure a dead-letter queue or any separate queue for failed events. Therefore, it does not meet the failure-review requirement.

- **D. EventBridge event bus with an Application Load Balancer target:** This design is not valid as written because an Application Load Balancer is not listed as an EventBridge event bus target. EventBridge supports targets such as API destinations, API Gateway, Lambda, SNS, SQS, ECS tasks, Kinesis streams, Step Functions, and other AWS service targets, but not an ALB directly ([Event bus targets in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-targets.html)).

Therefore, **B** is the solution that best meets both requirements: scalable queue-based processing and failed-message isolation in a dead-letter queue.

zh.question: 一名解决方案架构师正在设计一个用于处理事件的解决方案。该解决方案必须能够根据接收到的事件数量进行扩展和缩减。如果发生处理错误，事件必须移入一个单独的队列以供审查。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 将事件详细信息发送到 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 主题。将一个 AWS Lambda 函数配置为该 SNS 主题的订阅者以处理事件。为该函数添加一个失败时目标。将一个 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列设置为目标。
options.B: 将事件发布到 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列。创建一个 Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling 组。将 Auto Scaling 组配置为根据队列的 ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage 指标进行扩展和缩减。将应用程序配置为把失败消息写入死信队列。
options.C: 将事件写入 Amazon DynamoDB 表。为该表配置 DynamoDB stream。配置该 stream 以调用 AWS Lambda 函数。配置 Lambda 函数来处理这些事件。
options.D: 将事件发布到 Amazon EventBndge 事件总线。在位于 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面的 Amazon EC2 实例上使用 Auto Scaling 组创建并运行应用程序。将 ALB 设置为事件总线目标。配置事件总线重试事件。如果应用程序无法处理消息，则将消息写入死信队列。

zh.explanation:
该解决方案需要一个持久的事件处理队列、一个能够随着队列负载变化而扩展和缩减的处理层，以及一个用于存放无法成功处理的消息的单独队列。

**正确答案：B。将事件发布到 Amazon SQS 队列，使用 EC2 Auto Scaling 组处理事件，基于队列指标进行扩缩容，并将失败消息发送到死信队列。**

Amazon SQS 是用于缓冲事件的正确服务。然后，Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling 可以运行一组工作实例来轮询队列并处理消息。AWS 文档说明了这种确切模式：你可以根据 Amazon SQS 队列中系统负载的变化来扩缩 Auto Scaling 组，由 EC2 实例处理来自该队列的消息。AWS 还描述了如何根据 SQS 消息数量和 Auto Scaling 组容量计算每个实例的队列积压量，以便进行扩缩容决策（[Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html)）。

对于错误处理，Amazon SQS 支持死信队列。源队列可以将未成功处理的消息发送到 DLQ，而 DLQ 让你可以隔离并审查未消费的消息，以确定处理失败的原因（[Using dead-letter queues in Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-dead-letter-queues.html)）。这直接满足了将失败事件移动到单独队列以供审查的要求。

**其他选项不正确的原因：**

- **A. SNS 主题配合 Lambda 订阅者以及 Lambda 失败时目标：** 这可以处理事件，并且可以将失败的异步调用记录发送到诸如 SQS 之类的目标，但它没有使用一个持久的工作队列来根据队列积压或事件量驱动处理实例队列的扩缩容。该要求明确要求根据接收到的事件数量进行扩展和缩减，而 SQS 加 Auto Scaling 工作节点模式更直接匹配。

- **C. DynamoDB 表配合 DynamoDB Streams 和 Lambda：** DynamoDB Streams 可以针对表的更改调用 Lambda，但此选项没有配置死信队列或任何用于失败事件的单独队列。因此，它不满足失败审查要求。

- **D. EventBridge 事件总线配合 Application Load Balancer 目标：** 该设计按描述并不有效，因为 Application Load Balancer 未被列为 EventBridge 事件总线目标。EventBridge 支持 API destinations、API Gateway、Lambda、SNS、SQS、ECS tasks、Kinesis streams、Step Functions 以及其他 AWS 服务目标等目标，但不直接支持 ALB（[Event bus targets in Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-targets.html)）。

因此，**B** 是最能满足这两项要求的解决方案：可扩展的基于队列的处理，以及通过死信队列隔离失败消息。

en.question: A company runs a processing engine in the AWS Cloud. The engine processes environmental data from logistics centers to calculate a sustainability index. The company has millions of devices in logistics centers that are spread across Europe. The devices send information to the processing engine through a RESTful API. The API experiences unpredictable bursts of traffic. The company must implement a solution to process all data that the devices send to the processing engine. Data loss is unacceptable. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the RESTful API. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create a listener and a target group for the ALB Add the SQS queue as the target. Use a container that runs in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Fargate launch type to process messages in the queue.
options.B: Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API that implements the RESTful API. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create an API Gateway service integration with the SQS queue. Create an AWS Lambda function to process messages in the SQS queue.
options.C: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API that implements the RESTful API. Create a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Create an API Gateway Auto Scaling group proxy integration. Use the EC2 instances to process incoming data.
options.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the RESTful API. Create a data stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Set the data stream as the origin for the distribution. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume and process data in the data stream.

en.explanation:
The scenario asks for an ingestion architecture for a RESTful API that receives unpredictable bursts from millions of devices, while ensuring that accepted data is not lost and can be processed reliably. The key design need is a durable, scalable buffer between the API ingestion layer and the processing engine.

**Correct answer: B.**

API Gateway HTTP APIs are appropriate for implementing RESTful APIs: AWS states that **REST APIs and HTTP APIs are both RESTful API products** ([API Gateway: choose between REST APIs and HTTP APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-vs-rest.html)). HTTP APIs also support AWS service integrations. The documentation specifically says that a first-class integration can connect an HTTP API route to an AWS service API and gives **Amazon SQS `SQS-SendMessage`** as an example integration to send a message to an SQS queue ([Create AWS service integrations for HTTP APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-develop-integrations-aws-services.html)).

Placing SQS behind the API provides a durable buffer that decouples ingestion from processing and absorbs traffic bursts. SQS stores copies of messages on multiple servers for redundancy and high availability, and provides at-least-once delivery semantics ([Amazon SQS at-least-once delivery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues-at-least-once-delivery.html)). Lambda is also a native consumer for SQS: Lambda can process messages in SQS queues, polls the queue, invokes the function with message batches, and deletes messages after successful processing ([Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)). This combination directly addresses burst absorption, decoupling, and reliable processing.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. Incorrect.** An Application Load Balancer target group cannot directly target an SQS queue. ALB target groups support target types such as `instance`, `ip`, and `lambda`, not SQS ([ALB target groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-target-groups.html)). Although ECS/Fargate could process SQS messages, the proposed ALB-to-SQS target configuration is invalid.

- **C. Incorrect.** There is no such thing as an “API Gateway Auto Scaling group proxy integration” as described. More importantly, sending requests directly to EC2 instances, even in an Auto Scaling group, does not provide a durable ingestion buffer. During unpredictable bursts, requests can be throttled, fail, or overwhelm the compute layer unless the clients retry successfully. It does not meet the “data loss is unacceptable” requirement as well as SQS-backed ingestion.

- **D. Incorrect.** CloudFront is not used by setting a Kinesis Data Stream as an origin. CloudFront origins are resources such as S3 buckets, MediaStore/MediaPackage endpoints, EC2 instances, Elastic Load Balancing load balancers, or custom HTTP servers; the origin must be a DNS-accessible resource from which CloudFront retrieves objects ([CloudFront origin domain settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistValuesOrigin.html)). Kinesis Data Streams is not a CloudFront origin. Also, Kinesis capacity planning/sharding considerations make this option less directly suited than API Gateway to SQS for unpredictable bursts in this answer set.

Therefore, **B** is the best solution: API Gateway HTTP API → SQS queue → Lambda processor.

zh.question: 一家公司在 AWS Cloud 中运行一个处理引擎。该引擎处理来自物流中心的环境数据，以计算可持续发展指数。该公司在遍布欧洲的物流中心拥有数百万台设备。这些设备通过 RESTful API 将信息发送到处理引擎。该 API 会遇到不可预测的突发流量。公司必须实施一种解决方案来处理设备发送到处理引擎的所有数据。数据丢失是不可接受的。哪种解决方案能满足这些要求？

options.A: 为 RESTful API 创建一个 Application Load Balancer (ALB)。创建一个 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列。为 ALB 创建一个侦听器和目标组。将 SQS 队列添加为目标。使用在 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 中以 Fargate 启动类型运行的容器来处理队列中的消息。
options.B: 创建一个实现 RESTful API 的 Amazon API Gateway HTTP API。创建一个 Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) 队列。创建一个与 SQS 队列的 API Gateway 服务集成。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来处理 SQS 队列中的消息。
options.C: 创建一个实现 RESTful API 的 Amazon API Gateway REST API。创建一个位于 Auto Scaling 组中的 Amazon EC2 实例群。创建一个 API Gateway Auto Scaling 组代理集成。使用 EC2 实例处理传入数据。
options.D: 为 RESTful API 创建一个 Amazon CloudFront 分配。创建一个 Amazon Kinesis Data Streams 中的数据流。将该数据流设置为该分配的源站。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来消费并处理数据流中的数据。

zh.explanation:
该场景要求为一个 RESTful API 设计摄取架构。该 API 接收来自数百万台设备的不可预测突发流量，同时确保已接受的数据不会丢失，并且可以被可靠处理。关键设计需求是在 API 摄取层和处理引擎之间建立一个持久、可扩展的缓冲区。

**正确答案：B。**

API Gateway HTTP APIs 适合用于实现 RESTful APIs：AWS 表示 **REST APIs 和 HTTP APIs 都是 RESTful API 产品**（[API Gateway：在 REST APIs 和 HTTP APIs 之间选择](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-vs-rest.html)）。HTTP APIs 还支持 AWS 服务集成。文档明确说明，一等集成可以将 HTTP API 路由连接到 AWS 服务 API，并给出 **Amazon SQS `SQS-SendMessage`** 作为向 SQS 队列发送消息的示例集成（[为 HTTP APIs 创建 AWS 服务集成](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api-develop-integrations-aws-services.html)）。

将 SQS 放在 API 后面提供了一个持久缓冲区，可将摄取与处理解耦，并吸收突发流量。SQS 会在多台服务器上存储消息副本，以实现冗余和高可用性，并提供至少一次交付语义（[Amazon SQS 至少一次交付](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues-at-least-once-delivery.html)）。Lambda 也是 SQS 的原生消费者：Lambda 可以处理 SQS 队列中的消息，轮询队列，使用消息批次调用函数，并在成功处理后删除消息（[将 Lambda 与 Amazon SQS 结合使用](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)）。这种组合直接解决了突发吸收、解耦和可靠处理的问题。

**其他选项为什么不正确：**

- **A. 不正确。** Application Load Balancer 目标组不能直接将 SQS 队列作为目标。ALB 目标组支持 `instance`、`ip` 和 `lambda` 等目标类型，而不支持 SQS（[ALB 目标组](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-target-groups.html)）。虽然 ECS/Fargate 可以处理 SQS 消息，但所提出的 ALB 到 SQS 目标配置无效。

- **C. 不正确。** 并不存在所描述的“API Gateway Auto Scaling 组代理集成”。更重要的是，将请求直接发送到 EC2 实例，即使这些实例位于 Auto Scaling 组中，也不能提供持久的摄取缓冲区。在不可预测的突发流量期间，请求可能会被限流、失败或压垮计算层，除非客户端能够成功重试。它不像基于 SQS 的摄取那样能满足“数据丢失不可接受”的要求。

- **D. 不正确。** CloudFront 不能通过将 Kinesis Data Stream 设置为源站来使用。CloudFront 源站是 S3 桶、MediaStore/MediaPackage 端点、EC2 实例、Elastic Load Balancing 负载均衡器或自定义 HTTP 服务器等资源；源站必须是 CloudFront 可从中检索对象的 DNS 可访问资源（[CloudFront 源站域设置](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistValuesOrigin.html)）。Kinesis Data Streams 不是 CloudFront 源站。此外，Kinesis 的容量规划/分片考虑因素使该选项在本答案集中不如 API Gateway 到 SQS 更直接适合不可预测的突发流量。

因此，**B** 是最佳解决方案：API Gateway HTTP API → SQS queue → Lambda processor。

en.question: A company is designing its network configuration in the AWS Cloud. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage a multi-account setup. The company has three OUs. Each OU contains more than 100 AWS accounts. Each account has a single VPC, and all the VPCs in each OU are in the same AWS Region. The CIDR ranges for all the AWS accounts do not overlap. The company needs to implement a solution in which VPCs in the same OU can communicate with each other but cannot communicate with VPCs in other OUs. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create an AWS CloudFormation stack set that establishes VPC peering between accounts in each OU. Provision the stack set in each OU.
options.B: In each OU, create a dedicated networking account that has a single VPC. Share this VPC with all the other accounts in the OU by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Create a VPC peering connection between the networking account and each account in the OU.
options.C: Provision a transit gateway in an account in each OU. Share the transit gateway across the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Create transit gateway VPC attachments for each VPC.
options.D: In each OU, create a dedicated networking account that has a single VPC. Establish a VPN connection between the networking account and the other accounts in the OU. Use third-party routing software to route transitive traffic between the VPCs.

en.explanation:
The company has three large OUs, each with more than 100 accounts and one non-overlapping VPC per account in the same Region. The requirement is to allow communication among VPCs within the same OU while keeping VPCs in different OUs isolated, with the least operational overhead.

**Correct answer: C. Provision a transit gateway in an account in each OU. Share the transit gateway across the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Create transit gateway VPC attachments for each VPC.**

AWS Transit Gateway is designed for this type of scalable hub-and-spoke network. A transit gateway is a network transit hub used to interconnect VPCs and other networks, and it supports attachments for one or more VPCs ([AWS Transit Gateway overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/what-is-transit-gateway.html)). AWS documentation also states that a transit gateway can attach VPCs and route traffic between them, works across AWS accounts, and can be shared with other accounts by using AWS RAM ([Transit gateways in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-transit-gateways.html)).

For this scenario, the low-overhead design is to deploy a separate transit gateway for each OU and attach the VPCs from that OU to that OU's transit gateway. This provides intra-OU connectivity through a managed central hub. Because each OU has its own transit gateway, VPCs in one OU do not have a network path to VPCs in another OU unless additional interconnection and routing are explicitly configured.

AWS RAM further reduces administrative effort in a multi-account AWS Organizations environment. When resource sharing with AWS Organizations is enabled, AWS RAM can share resources with individual accounts, the entire organization, or an OU without enumerating each account ([Sharing your AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/getting-started-sharing.html)). Sharing each OU's transit gateway with the intended OU accounts allows those accounts to create the required transit gateway VPC attachments without manually managing hundreds of individual account-level shares.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. Create VPC peering by using CloudFormation StackSets.** VPC peering is a direct connection between two VPCs ([Connect VPCs using VPC peering](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-peering.html)). With more than 100 VPCs per OU, full intra-OU communication would require a large mesh of pairwise peering connections and route table entries. Even if StackSets automate creation, the resulting topology has high ongoing operational overhead. AWS Well-Architected guidance recommends a hub-and-spoke model such as AWS Transit Gateway when more than two network address spaces are connected, because mesh connectivity becomes difficult to maintain as the number of networks grows ([REL02-BP04 Prefer hub-and-spoke topologies over many-to-many mesh](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/2023-10-03/framework/rel_planning_network_topology_prefer_hub_and_spoke.html)).

- **B. Share a dedicated networking VPC and create VPC peering connections.** Sharing a VPC does not provide managed transitive routing among all of the existing account VPCs. This option still depends on VPC peering between the networking VPC and each account VPC, which creates a peering-based hub-and-spoke design rather than using the native managed hub provided by Transit Gateway. It is more complex and less scalable than attaching each VPC to a transit gateway.

- **D. Use VPN connections and third-party routing software.** This introduces VPN infrastructure and self-managed routing components that must be deployed, monitored, patched, and troubleshot. AWS Transit Gateway natively provides managed VPC attachments and routing between attached VPCs, so using VPNs and third-party routing software adds unnecessary operational overhead.

Therefore, **option C** is the best solution because a transit gateway per OU, shared through AWS RAM and connected with VPC attachments, provides scalable intra-OU connectivity while preserving isolation between OUs with the least operational overhead.

zh.question: 一家公司正在 AWS 云中设计其网络配置。该公司使用 AWS Organizations 管理多账户设置。该公司有三个 OU。每个 OU 包含 100 多个 AWS 账户。每个账户都有一个 VPC，并且每个 OU 中的所有 VPC 都位于同一个 AWS 区域。所有 AWS 账户的 CIDR 范围都不重叠。公司需要实施一种解决方案，使同一 OU 中的 VPC 可以相互通信，但不能与其他 OU 中的 VPC 通信。哪种解决方案能够以最少的运营开销满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 AWS CloudFormation 堆栈集，在每个 OU 的账户之间建立 VPC 对等连接。在每个 OU 中预置该堆栈集。
options.B: 在每个 OU 中，创建一个具有单个 VPC 的专用网络账户。使用 AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) 将此 VPC 共享给该 OU 中的所有其他账户。在网络账户和该 OU 中的每个账户之间创建 VPC 对等连接。
options.C: 在每个 OU 的一个账户中预置一个 transit gateway。使用 AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) 在整个组织中共享该 transit gateway。为每个 VPC 创建 transit gateway VPC attachment。
options.D: 在每个 OU 中，创建一个具有单个 VPC 的专用网络账户。在网络账户与该 OU 中的其他账户之间建立 VPN 连接。使用第三方路由软件在 VPC 之间路由传递流量。

zh.explanation:
该公司有三个大型 OU，每个 OU 有 100 多个账户，并且每个账户在同一区域中有一个不重叠的 VPC。要求是在同一 OU 内的 VPC 之间允许通信，同时保持不同 OU 中的 VPC 彼此隔离，并且运营开销最少。

**正确答案：C. 在每个 OU 的一个账户中预置一个 transit gateway。使用 AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) 在整个组织中共享该 transit gateway。为每个 VPC 创建 transit gateway VPC attachment。**

AWS Transit Gateway 专为这种可扩展的中心辐射型网络而设计。transit gateway 是用于互连 VPC 和其他网络的网络传输中心，并支持一个或多个 VPC 的 attachment（[AWS Transit Gateway overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/what-is-transit-gateway.html)）。AWS 文档还说明，transit gateway 可以连接 VPC 并在它们之间路由流量，可以跨 AWS 账户工作，并且可以使用 AWS RAM 与其他账户共享（[Transit gateways in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-transit-gateways.html)）。

对于此场景，低开销设计是在每个 OU 部署一个单独的 transit gateway，并将该 OU 中的 VPC 附加到该 OU 的 transit gateway。这通过托管的中心枢纽提供 OU 内连接。由于每个 OU 都有自己的 transit gateway，除非显式配置额外的互连和路由，否则一个 OU 中的 VPC 不会有通往另一个 OU 中 VPC 的网络路径。

在多账户 AWS Organizations 环境中，AWS RAM 进一步降低了管理工作量。启用与 AWS Organizations 的资源共享后，AWS RAM 可以将资源共享给单个账户、整个组织或某个 OU，而无需逐一枚举每个账户（[Sharing your AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/getting-started-sharing.html)）。将每个 OU 的 transit gateway 共享给目标 OU 账户，可以让这些账户创建所需的 transit gateway VPC attachment，而无需手动管理数百个单独的账户级共享。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

- **A. 使用 CloudFormation StackSets 创建 VPC peering。** VPC peering 是两个 VPC 之间的直接连接（[Connect VPCs using VPC peering](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-peering.html)）。每个 OU 中有 100 多个 VPC 时，要实现 OU 内全互通，就需要大量成对的 peering connection 和路由表条目。即使 StackSets 能自动化创建，最终拓扑的持续运营开销仍然很高。AWS Well-Architected 指南建议，当连接两个以上的网络地址空间时，优先使用 AWS Transit Gateway 这类中心辐射型模型，因为随着网络数量增加，网状连接会变得难以维护（[REL02-BP04 Prefer hub-and-spoke topologies over many-to-many mesh](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/2023-10-03/framework/rel_planning_network_topology_prefer_hub_and_spoke.html)）。

- **B. 共享一个专用网络 VPC 并创建 VPC peering connection。** 共享 VPC 并不能在所有现有账户 VPC 之间提供托管的传递路由。该选项仍依赖于网络 VPC 与每个账户 VPC 之间的 VPC peering，这会创建基于 peering 的中心辐射型设计，而不是使用 Transit Gateway 提供的原生托管中心。与将每个 VPC 附加到 transit gateway 相比，它更复杂且可扩展性更差。

- **D. 使用 VPN 连接和第三方路由软件。** 这会引入 VPN 基础设施和自管理路由组件，需要部署、监控、修补和排障。AWS Transit Gateway 原生提供托管 VPC attachment，以及附加 VPC 之间的路由，因此使用 VPN 和第三方路由软件会增加不必要的运营开销。

因此，**选项 C** 是最佳解决方案，因为每个 OU 一个 transit gateway，通过 AWS RAM 共享并使用 VPC attachment 连接，可以在保持 OU 之间隔离的同时，提供可扩展的 OU 内连接，并且运营开销最少。

en.question: A company is migrating an application to AWS. It wants to use fully managed services as much as possible during the migration. The company needs to store large important documents within the application with the following requirements: 1. The data must be highly durable and available 2. The data must always be encrypted at rest and in transit 3. The encryption key must be managed by the company and rotated periodically Which of the following solutions should the solutions architect recommend?

options.A: Deploy the storage gateway to AWS in file gateway mode. Use Amazon EBS volume encryption using an AWS KMS key to encrypt the storage gateway volumes.
options.B: Use Amazon S3 with a bucket policy to enforce HTTPS for connections to the bucket and to enforce server-side encryption and AWS KMS for object encryption.
options.C: Use Amazon DynamoDB with SSL to connect to DynamoDB. Use an AWS KMS key to encrypt DynamoDB objects at rest.
options.D: Deploy instances with Amazon EBS volumes attached to store this data. Use EBS volume encryption using an AWS KMS key to encrypt the data.

en.explanation:
The company needs a fully managed storage service for large important documents, with high durability/availability, encryption in transit, encryption at rest, and company-managed keys that rotate periodically.

**Correct answer: B. Use Amazon S3 with a bucket policy to enforce HTTPS and SSE-KMS.**

Amazon S3 is the best fit for large documents because it is a fully managed object storage service. S3 Standard is designed for **99.999999999% durability** and **99.99% availability**, with data stored across at least three Availability Zones according to the S3 storage class comparison table in the official documentation ([Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)).

For encryption at rest with company-managed keys, S3 supports server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys. The S3 default encryption documentation states that if you need more control over keys, including key rotation and access policy grants, you can use **SSE-KMS** ([Setting default server-side encryption behavior for Amazon S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)). AWS KMS customer managed keys can be configured for automatic rotation; by default, AWS KMS rotates key material every year, and custom rotation periods can also be specified ([Enable automatic key rotation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/rotating-keys-enable.html)).

For enforcement, S3 bucket policies can deny uploads that are not encrypted with SSE-KMS, including requiring a specific KMS key. The S3 bucket policy examples also show how to deny HTTP requests by using the `aws:SecureTransport` condition key, thereby requiring HTTPS/TLS for access ([Examples of Amazon S3 bucket policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies.html)). Therefore, option B satisfies all requirements: fully managed storage, high durability/availability, encryption in transit, encryption at rest, and company-managed periodically rotated keys.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **A. Storage Gateway in file gateway mode with EBS volume encryption** — This is unnecessarily complex for an application being migrated to AWS and is not the most fully managed/native option for storing large documents in the application. It also focuses on encrypting Storage Gateway volumes rather than enforcing object-level encryption and HTTPS access policies for application document storage.

- **C. DynamoDB with SSL and KMS encryption** — DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL database, not an object/document storage service for large files. DynamoDB has a maximum item size of **400 KB**, which makes it unsuitable for storing large documents directly ([DynamoDB constraints: Items](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Constraints.html)). A common pattern is to store large objects in S3 and store metadata in DynamoDB, but the option says to store the documents in DynamoDB.

- **D. EC2 instances with EBS volumes** — This uses self-managed compute instances and block storage, so it does not meet the requirement to use fully managed services as much as possible. It also lacks the native object durability/availability characteristics and policy-based enforcement capabilities of S3 for document storage.

Thus, **B** is the correct recommendation.

zh.question: 一家公司正在将一个应用程序迁移到 AWS。该公司希望在迁移过程中尽可能多地使用完全托管服务。公司需要在应用程序中存储大型重要文档，并满足以下要求：1. 数据必须具有高持久性和高可用性 2. 数据在静态和传输过程中必须始终加密 3. 加密密钥必须由公司管理并定期轮换。解决方案架构师应推荐以下哪种解决方案？

options.A: 以 file gateway 模式将 Storage Gateway 部署到 AWS。使用采用 AWS KMS key 的 Amazon EBS 卷加密来加密 Storage Gateway 卷。
options.B: 使用 Amazon S3，并通过 bucket policy 强制对存储桶连接使用 HTTPS，同时强制使用 server-side encryption 和 AWS KMS 进行对象加密。
options.C: 使用 Amazon DynamoDB，并通过 SSL 连接到 DynamoDB。使用 AWS KMS key 对静态 DynamoDB 对象进行加密。
options.D: 部署附加了 Amazon EBS 卷的实例来存储这些数据。使用采用 AWS KMS key 的 EBS 卷加密来加密数据。

zh.explanation:
公司需要一种用于大型重要文档的完全托管存储服务，并要求高持久性/可用性、传输中加密、静态加密，以及由公司管理并定期轮换的密钥。

**正确答案：B. 使用 Amazon S3，并通过 bucket policy 强制使用 HTTPS 和 SSE-KMS。**

Amazon S3 最适合大型文档，因为它是一项完全托管的对象存储服务。根据官方文档中的 S3 存储类别比较表，S3 Standard 设计为提供 **99.999999999% 持久性** 和 **99.99% 可用性**，数据存储在至少三个可用区中（[Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)）。

对于使用公司管理的密钥进行静态加密，S3 支持使用 AWS KMS keys 的 server-side encryption。S3 默认加密文档说明，如果你需要对密钥进行更多控制（包括密钥轮换和访问策略授权），可以使用 **SSE-KMS**（[Setting default server-side encryption behavior for Amazon S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-encryption.html)）。AWS KMS customer managed keys 可以配置为自动轮换；默认情况下，AWS KMS 每年轮换 key material，也可以指定自定义轮换周期（[Enable automatic key rotation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/rotating-keys-enable.html)）。

对于强制执行，S3 bucket policies 可以拒绝未使用 SSE-KMS 加密的上传，包括要求使用特定的 KMS key。S3 bucket policy 示例还展示了如何使用 `aws:SecureTransport` 条件键拒绝 HTTP 请求，从而要求通过 HTTPS/TLS 访问（[Examples of Amazon S3 bucket policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/example-bucket-policies.html)）。因此，选项 B 满足所有要求：完全托管存储、高持久性/可用性、传输中加密、静态加密，以及由公司管理并定期轮换的密钥。

**其他选项不正确的原因：**

- **A. Storage Gateway in file gateway mode with EBS volume encryption** — 对于正在迁移到 AWS 的应用程序来说，这过于复杂，也不是在应用程序中存储大型文档时最完全托管/原生的选项。它还侧重于加密 Storage Gateway 卷，而不是针对应用程序文档存储强制执行对象级加密和 HTTPS 访问策略。

- **C. DynamoDB with SSL and KMS encryption** — DynamoDB 是托管 NoSQL 数据库，不是用于大型文件的对象/文档存储服务。DynamoDB 的最大项目大小为 **400 KB**，因此不适合直接存储大型文档（[DynamoDB constraints: Items](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Constraints.html)）。常见模式是将大型对象存储在 S3 中，并将元数据存储在 DynamoDB 中，但该选项说的是将文档存储在 DynamoDB 中。

- **D. EC2 instances with EBS volumes** — 这使用自管理计算实例和块存储，因此不满足尽可能使用完全托管服务的要求。它也缺少 S3 用于文档存储的原生对象持久性/可用性特征以及基于策略的强制执行能力。

因此，**B** 是正确建议。

en.question: A company’s public API runs as tasks on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The tasks run on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and are configured with Service Auto Scaling for the tasks based on CPU utilization. This service has been running well for several months. Recently, API performance slowed down and made the application unusable. The company discovered that a significant number of SQL injection attacks had occurred against the API and that the API service had scaled to its maximum amount. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that prevents SQL injection attacks from reaching the ECS API service. The solution must allow legitimate traffic through and must maximize operational efficiency. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Create a new AWS WAF web ACL to monitor the HTTP requests and HTTPS requests that are forwarded to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.
options.B: Create a new AWS WAF Bot Control implementation. Add a rule in the AWS WAF Bot Control managed rule group to monitor traffic and allow only legitimate traffic to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.
options.C: Create a new AWS WAF web ACL. Add a new rule that blocks requests that match the SQL database rule group. Set the web ACL to allow all other traffic that does not match those rules. Attach the web ACL to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.
options.D: Create a new AWS WAF web ACL. Create a new empty IP set in AWS WAF. Add a new rule to the web ACL to block requests that originate from IP addresses in the new IP set. Create an AWS Lambda function that scrapes the API logs for IP addresses that send SQL injection attacks, and add those IP addresses to the IP set. Attach the web ACL to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The API is served by Amazon ECS tasks on Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer. The immediate problem is that malicious SQL injection requests are reaching the API, consuming capacity and causing ECS Service Auto Scaling to scale to the maximum. The requirement is to stop SQL injection traffic before it reaches the ECS service, allow legitimate requests, and minimize operational overhead.

## Correct answer: C

**C. Create a new AWS WAF web ACL. Add a new rule that blocks requests that match the SQL database rule group. Set the web ACL to allow all other traffic that does not match those rules. Attach the web ACL to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.**

This is the best fit because AWS WAF web ACLs can inspect HTTP(S) requests and apply allow/block decisions based on request criteria, including **detection of malicious SQL code**. AWS documentation states that a web ACL provides fine-grained control over HTTP(S) requests and can use criteria such as malicious SQL code detection to allow or block requests ([AWS WAF web ACL protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl.html)).

AWS also provides an AWS Managed Rules **SQL database managed rule group** named `AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet`. The documentation states that this rule group contains rules to block request patterns associated with SQL database exploitation, including SQL injection attacks, and the individual SQLi rules have **Rule action: Block** ([SQL database managed rule group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/aws-managed-rule-groups-use-case.html)).

Finally, AWS WAF web ACLs can be associated with regional resources, including **Application Load Balancers**, so attaching the web ACL to the ALB protects the ECS/Fargate service before traffic reaches the tasks ([Resources that you can protect with AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/how-aws-waf-works-resources.html)). This uses an AWS-managed rule group rather than custom log scraping or manual IP maintenance, so it maximizes operational efficiency.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Create a WAF web ACL to monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests forwarded to the ALB

This does not meet the requirement because it only says to **monitor** requests. Monitoring/counting can help with visibility and tuning, but the question requires preventing SQL injection attacks from reaching the ECS API service. A web ACL must include blocking rules for SQL injection patterns to meet the requirement.

### B. Use AWS WAF Bot Control and allow only legitimate traffic

Bot Control is aimed at identifying and managing bot traffic. AWS documentation describes Bot Control protection levels for detecting self-identifying bots, scraping frameworks, automated browsers, sophisticated bots, and anomalous bot activity ([AWS WAF Bot Control rule group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/aws-managed-rule-groups-bot.html)). The problem is specifically SQL injection payloads, not merely bot traffic. SQL injection can be attempted by non-bot clients or by clients that Bot Control might not classify as bots. The purpose-built SQL database managed rule group is the operationally efficient control for this requirement.

### D. Use an IP set and Lambda to scrape logs and block attacking IPs

This is reactive and operationally inefficient. It allows initial attacks from new IP addresses to reach the API until logs are processed and IPs are added to the IP set. It also requires custom Lambda logic, log parsing, and ongoing IP list maintenance. SQL injection is better blocked by inspecting request content with the AWS Managed Rules SQL database rule group, independent of attacker IP address.

## Conclusion

Option **C** is correct because it uses AWS WAF at the ALB layer with the managed SQL injection rule group to block SQL injection requests while allowing other traffic, providing the most targeted and operationally efficient protection.

zh.question: 一家公司的公共 API 以任务形式运行在 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 上。这些任务在 Application Load Balancer (ALB) 后面的 AWS Fargate 上运行，并且配置了基于 CPU 利用率的任务 Service Auto Scaling。该服务已经稳定运行了数月。最近，API 性能变慢，导致应用程序无法使用。公司发现针对该 API 发生了大量 SQL 注入攻击，并且该 API 服务已经扩展到了最大数量。解决方案架构师需要实施一种解决方案，防止 SQL 注入攻击到达 ECS API 服务。该解决方案必须允许合法流量通过，并且必须最大限度提高运营效率。哪种解决方案满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个新的 AWS WAF web ACL，用于监控转发到 ECS 任务前端 ALB 的 HTTP 请求和 HTTPS 请求。
options.B: 创建一个新的 AWS WAF Bot Control 实施。在 AWS WAF Bot Control 托管规则组中添加一条规则，用于监控流量，并仅允许合法流量到达 ECS 任务前端的 ALB。
options.C: 创建一个新的 AWS WAF web ACL。添加一条新规则，用于阻止与 SQL 数据库规则组匹配的请求。将 web ACL 设置为允许所有其他不匹配这些规则的流量。将该 web ACL 附加到 ECS 任务前端的 ALB。
options.D: 创建一个新的 AWS WAF web ACL。在 AWS WAF 中创建一个新的空 IP set。向 web ACL 添加一条新规则，用于阻止来自新 IP set 中 IP 地址的请求。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，从 API 日志中抓取发送 SQL 注入攻击的 IP 地址，并将这些 IP 地址添加到 IP set。将该 web ACL 附加到 ECS 任务前端的 ALB。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该 API 由位于 Application Load Balancer 后面的 Fargate 上的 Amazon ECS 任务提供服务。当前问题是恶意 SQL 注入请求正在到达 API，消耗容量，并导致 ECS Service Auto Scaling 扩展到最大值。要求是在流量到达 ECS 服务之前阻止 SQL 注入流量，允许合法请求，并尽量减少运营开销。

## 正确答案：C

**C. 创建一个新的 AWS WAF web ACL。添加一条新规则，用于阻止与 SQL 数据库规则组匹配的请求。将 web ACL 设置为允许所有其他不匹配这些规则的流量。将该 web ACL 附加到 ECS 任务前端的 ALB。**

这是最合适的选择，因为 AWS WAF web ACL 可以检查 HTTP(S) 请求，并根据请求条件应用允许/阻止决策，包括**检测恶意 SQL 代码**。AWS 文档说明，web ACL 可对 HTTP(S) 请求提供精细控制，并且可以使用恶意 SQL 代码检测等条件来允许或阻止请求（[AWS WAF web ACL protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/web-acl.html)）。

AWS 还提供名为 `AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet` 的 AWS Managed Rules **SQL 数据库托管规则组**。文档说明，该规则组包含用于阻止与 SQL 数据库利用相关的请求模式的规则，包括 SQL 注入攻击，并且各个 SQLi 规则具有 **Rule action: Block**（[SQL database managed rule group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/aws-managed-rule-groups-use-case.html)）。

最后，AWS WAF web ACL 可以与区域资源关联，包括 **Application Load Balancers**，因此将 web ACL 附加到 ALB 可以在流量到达任务之前保护 ECS/Fargate 服务（[Resources that you can protect with AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/how-aws-waf-works-resources.html)）。这使用 AWS 托管规则组，而不是自定义日志抓取或手动 IP 维护，因此可以最大限度提高运营效率。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. 创建 WAF web ACL 来监控转发到 ALB 的 HTTP/HTTPS 请求

这不满足要求，因为它只说**监控**请求。监控/计数可以帮助提升可见性和调优，但题目要求防止 SQL 注入攻击到达 ECS API 服务。web ACL 必须包含针对 SQL 注入模式的阻止规则，才能满足要求。

### B. 使用 AWS WAF Bot Control 并仅允许合法流量

Bot Control 旨在识别和管理机器人流量。AWS 文档描述了 Bot Control 的保护级别，用于检测自我识别的机器人、抓取框架、自动化浏览器、复杂机器人和异常机器人活动（[AWS WAF Bot Control rule group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/aws-managed-rule-groups-bot.html)）。该问题具体是 SQL 注入载荷，而不仅仅是机器人流量。SQL 注入可能由非机器人客户端尝试，也可能由 Bot Control 未分类为机器人的客户端尝试。专门用于 SQL 数据库的托管规则组是满足此要求且运营效率高的控制措施。

### D. 使用 IP set 和 Lambda 抓取日志并阻止攻击 IP

这是被动的，并且运营效率低。它会允许来自新 IP 地址的初始攻击到达 API，直到日志被处理且 IP 被添加到 IP set。它还需要自定义 Lambda 逻辑、日志解析和持续的 IP 列表维护。更好的做法是使用 AWS Managed Rules SQL 数据库规则组检查请求内容来阻止 SQL 注入，而不依赖攻击者的 IP 地址。

## 结论

选项 **C** 正确，因为它在 ALB 层使用 AWS WAF 和托管 SQL 注入规则组来阻止 SQL 注入请求，同时允许其他流量，从而提供最有针对性且运营效率最高的保护。

en.question: An environmental company is deploying sensors in major cities throughout a country to measure air quality. The sensors connect to AWS IoT Core to ingest timeseries data readings. The company stores the data in Amazon DynamoDB. For business continuity, the company must have the ability to ingest and store data in two AWS Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon Route 53 alias failover routing policy with values for AWS IoT Core data endpoints in both Regions Migrate data to Amazon Aurora global tables.
options.B: Create a domain configuration for AWS IoT Core in each Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing policy. Use AWS IoT Core data endpoints in both Regions as values. Migrate the data to Amazon MemoryDB for Redis and configure cross-Region replication.
options.C: Create a domain configuration for AWS IoT Core in each Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 health check that evaluates domain configuration health. Create a failover routing policy with values for the domain name from the AWS IoT Core domain configurations. Update the DynamoDB table to a global table.
options.D: Create an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing policy. Use AWS IoT Core data endpoints in both Regions as values. Configure DynamoDB streams and cross-Region data replication.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The company has IoT sensors publishing time-series readings to AWS IoT Core and stores the data in DynamoDB. The requirement is business continuity with the ability to ingest and store the data in two AWS Regions. The solution therefore needs two parts:

1. **Regional AWS IoT Core ingestion endpoints** with DNS failover so devices can connect to another Region if the primary Region is unhealthy.
2. **Multi-Region DynamoDB storage** so data remains available and writable across Regions.

## Correct answer: C

**C. Create a domain configuration for AWS IoT Core in each Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 health check that evaluates domain configuration health. Create a failover routing policy with values for the domain name from the AWS IoT Core domain configurations. Update the DynamoDB table to a global table.**

This is the best fit.

AWS IoT Core supports **domain configurations**, which are the setup and configuration of a domain for AWS IoT Core endpoints. The documentation explains that a customer managed domain lets devices connect by using a custom domain data endpoint, which is useful for maintaining a stable endpoint name while changing or migrating infrastructure ([AWS IoT Core domain configurations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-domain-configuration-what-is.html)). Creating a domain configuration in each Region gives the company regional IoT ingestion endpoints behind DNS names.

Route 53 supports DNS failover by checking resource health and responding to DNS queries using only healthy resources ([Configuring DNS failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-configuring.html)). In an active-passive failover configuration, Route 53 returns the primary resource when healthy and returns the secondary resource when the primary is unhealthy ([Active-passive failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html)). This satisfies the business continuity requirement for IoT ingestion.

For the storage layer, DynamoDB **global tables** are explicitly designed for this use case. They are a fully managed, multi-Region, multi-active feature that automatically replicates table data across AWS Regions. The documentation states that global tables are ideal for applications requiring business continuity and high availability through multi-Region deployment, and that any replica can serve reads and writes ([DynamoDB global tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html)).

Therefore, option C correctly combines **AWS IoT Core regional domain configurations + Route 53 failover + DynamoDB global tables**.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Incorrect

This option incorrectly says to migrate data to **Amazon Aurora global tables**. The existing data store is DynamoDB, and the correct DynamoDB multi-Region feature is **DynamoDB global tables**, not Aurora. Aurora has global database capabilities, but replacing DynamoDB with Aurora is unnecessary and does not match the stated architecture.

Also, the option refers directly to AWS IoT Core data endpoints with a Route 53 alias failover policy, but the stronger and intended pattern is to use AWS IoT Core **domain configurations** and Route 53 failover for those domain names.

### B. Incorrect

This option unnecessarily migrates the data from DynamoDB to **Amazon MemoryDB for Redis**. MemoryDB is not the correct persistent time-series storage replacement in this scenario, and the question already states that the company stores data in DynamoDB. The correct multi-Region DynamoDB feature is DynamoDB global tables.

Latency-based routing also does not specifically provide the active-passive business continuity pattern described by the answer choices. Route 53 failover routing is the more direct fit for a regional failover design.

### D. Incorrect

This option uses Route 53 latency-based routing with AWS IoT Core data endpoints and then suggests DynamoDB Streams with custom cross-Region replication. DynamoDB global tables already provide managed multi-Region replication and allow replicas to serve reads and writes. Building custom replication with DynamoDB Streams would add operational complexity and is not the recommended solution when DynamoDB global tables are available.

## Conclusion

Option **C** is correct because it provides regional IoT ingestion continuity through AWS IoT Core domain configurations and Route 53 failover, and it provides managed multi-Region DynamoDB storage through DynamoDB global tables.

zh.question: 一家环保公司正在一个国家的主要城市部署传感器，以测量空气质量。这些传感器连接到 AWS IoT Core 以摄取时间序列数据读数。该公司将数据存储在 Amazon DynamoDB 中。为了实现业务连续性，该公司必须能够在两个 AWS 区域中摄取和存储数据。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 创建一个 Amazon Route 53 别名故障转移路由策略，其值为两个区域中的 AWS IoT Core 数据终端节点。将数据迁移到 Amazon Aurora global tables。
options.B: 在每个区域中为 AWS IoT Core 创建域配置。创建一个 Amazon Route 53 基于延迟的路由策略。使用两个区域中的 AWS IoT Core 数据终端节点作为值。将数据迁移到 Amazon MemoryDB for Redis 并配置跨区域复制。
options.C: 在每个区域中为 AWS IoT Core 创建域配置。创建一个 Amazon Route 53 运行状况检查，用于评估域配置运行状况。创建一个故障转移路由策略，其值为来自 AWS IoT Core 域配置的域名。将 DynamoDB 表更新为全局表。
options.D: 创建一个 Amazon Route 53 基于延迟的路由策略。使用两个区域中的 AWS IoT Core 数据终端节点作为值。配置 DynamoDB streams 和跨区域数据复制。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

该公司有 IoT 传感器向 AWS IoT Core 发布时间序列读数，并将数据存储在 DynamoDB 中。要求是实现业务连续性，并具备在两个 AWS 区域中摄取和存储数据的能力。因此，解决方案需要两部分：

1. **区域性 AWS IoT Core 摄取终端节点**，并配合 DNS 故障转移，以便在主区域不健康时设备可以连接到另一个区域。
2. **多区域 DynamoDB 存储**，以便数据在多个区域中保持可用并可写入。

## 正确答案：C

**C. 在每个区域中为 AWS IoT Core 创建域配置。创建一个 Amazon Route 53 运行状况检查，用于评估域配置运行状况。创建一个故障转移路由策略，其值为来自 AWS IoT Core 域配置的域名。将 DynamoDB 表更新为全局表。**

这是最合适的选择。

AWS IoT Core 支持 **domain configurations**，即 AWS IoT Core 终端节点的域设置和配置。文档说明，客户托管域允许设备使用自定义域数据终端节点进行连接，这对于在更改或迁移基础设施时保持稳定的终端节点名称很有用（[AWS IoT Core domain configurations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-domain-configuration-what-is.html)）。在每个区域中创建一个域配置，可以为公司提供位于 DNS 名称背后的区域性 IoT 摄取终端节点。

Route 53 通过检查资源运行状况并仅使用健康资源响应 DNS 查询来支持 DNS 故障转移（[Configuring DNS failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-configuring.html)）。在主动-被动故障转移配置中，当主资源健康时，Route 53 返回主资源；当主资源不健康时，返回辅助资源（[Active-passive failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-types.html)）。这满足了 IoT 摄取的业务连续性要求。

对于存储层，DynamoDB **global tables** 明确是为此用例设计的。它们是一项完全托管的多区域、多活功能，可自动在 AWS 区域之间复制表数据。文档指出，全局表非常适合需要通过多区域部署实现业务连续性和高可用性的应用程序，并且任何副本都可以提供读取和写入服务（[DynamoDB global tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html)）。

因此，选项 C 正确地结合了 **AWS IoT Core 区域性域配置 + Route 53 故障转移 + DynamoDB global tables**。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. 不正确

此选项错误地说要将数据迁移到 **Amazon Aurora global tables**。现有数据存储是 DynamoDB，而正确的 DynamoDB 多区域功能是 **DynamoDB global tables**，不是 Aurora。Aurora 具有全局数据库功能，但用 Aurora 替换 DynamoDB 没有必要，也不符合题目所述架构。

此外，该选项直接提到将 AWS IoT Core 数据终端节点与 Route 53 别名故障转移策略结合使用，但更可靠且预期的模式是使用 AWS IoT Core **domain configurations** 以及针对这些域名的 Route 53 故障转移。

### B. 不正确

此选项不必要地将数据从 DynamoDB 迁移到 **Amazon MemoryDB for Redis**。MemoryDB 不是此场景中正确的持久化时间序列存储替代方案，而且题目已经说明公司将数据存储在 DynamoDB 中。正确的多区域 DynamoDB 功能是 DynamoDB global tables。

基于延迟的路由也并不专门提供答案选项所描述的主动-被动业务连续性模式。Route 53 故障转移路由更直接地适用于区域故障转移设计。

### D. 不正确

此选项使用 Route 53 基于延迟的路由配合 AWS IoT Core 数据终端节点，然后建议使用 DynamoDB Streams 进行自定义跨区域复制。DynamoDB global tables 已经提供托管式多区域复制，并允许副本提供读取和写入服务。当 DynamoDB global tables 可用时，使用 DynamoDB Streams 构建自定义复制会增加运维复杂性，并不是推荐的解决方案。

## 结论

选项 **C** 正确，因为它通过 AWS IoT Core 域配置和 Route 53 故障转移提供区域性 IoT 摄取连续性，并通过 DynamoDB global tables 提供托管式多区域 DynamoDB 存储。

en.question: A company uses AWS Organizations for a multi-account setup in the AWS Cloud. The company's finance team has a data processing application that uses AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB. The company's marketing team wants to access the data that is stored in the DynamoDB table. The DynamoDB table contains confidential data. The marketing team can have access to only specific attributes of data in the DynamoDB table. The finance team and the marketing team have separate AWS accounts. What should a solutions architect do to provide the marketing team with the appropriate access to the DynamoDB table?

options.A: Create an SCP to grant the marketing team's AWS account access to the specific attributes of the DynamoDB table. Attach the SCP to the OU of the finance team.
options.B: Create an IAM role in the finance team's account by using IAM policy conditions for specific DynamoDB attributes (fine-grained access control). Establish trust with the marketing team's account. In the marketing team's account, create an IAM role that has permissions to assume the IAM role in the finance team's account.
options.C: Create a resource-based IAM policy that includes conditions for specific DynamoDB attributes (fine-grained access control). Attach the policy to the DynamoDB table. In the marketing team's account, create an IAM role that has permissions to access the DynamoDB table in the finance team's account.
options.D: Create an IAM role in the finance team's account to access the DynamoDB table. Use an IAM permissions boundary to limit the access to the specific attributes. In the marketing team's account, create an IAM role that has permissions to assume the IAM role in the finance team's account.

en.explanation:
The company needs to give a principal in the marketing AWS account access to a DynamoDB table that is owned by the finance AWS account, while limiting access to only approved attributes in the table. The correct answer is **B**.

**B. Create an IAM role in the finance team's account by using IAM policy conditions for specific DynamoDB attributes, establish trust with the marketing account, and allow a role in the marketing account to assume it.**

This design satisfies both requirements:

- **Cross-account access:** IAM roles are the standard mechanism for delegating access across AWS accounts. AWS documents that a role can be created in one account with a trust policy that names another account as a trusted principal, and users or roles in the trusted account can be granted permission to call `sts:AssumeRole`. While using the role, the principal can perform only the actions and access only the resources permitted by that role. See [IAM cross-account role access](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_aws-accounts.html).
- **Attribute-level DynamoDB restrictions:** DynamoDB supports fine-grained access control through IAM policy conditions. AWS documentation states that IAM policies can restrict access to individual items and attributes in DynamoDB tables, and identifies DynamoDB condition keys such as `dynamodb:Attributes` and `dynamodb:Select` for controlling which attributes can be accessed. See [Using IAM policy conditions for fine-grained access control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/specifying-conditions.html).

Therefore, the finance account should own the role that has permissions to the DynamoDB table and contains the DynamoDB attribute restrictions. The role trust policy should allow the marketing account to assume the role, and the marketing account should grant its appropriate role or users permission to assume that finance-account role.

**Why the other options are incorrect**

- **A. Create an SCP to grant access.** This is incorrect because service control policies do not grant permissions. SCPs define the maximum available permissions for IAM users and roles in accounts in an organization; they are guardrails. AWS explicitly states that no permissions are granted by an SCP. See [Service control policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html).

- **C. Attach a resource-based IAM policy to the DynamoDB table and create a role in the marketing account.** This does not match the best cross-account role-delegation approach described in the answer. The access should be granted by a role in the resource-owning finance account, with a trust relationship to the marketing account and a permissions policy that applies the DynamoDB fine-grained attribute conditions. The marketing account role then receives permission to assume that finance-account role.

- **D. Use a permissions boundary to limit access to specific attributes.** This is incorrect because a permissions boundary is not the mechanism for granting DynamoDB access or implementing DynamoDB attribute-level filtering. A permissions boundary only sets the maximum permissions that an identity-based policy can grant to a user or role; it does not provide permissions by itself. See [Permissions boundaries for IAM entities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html). Attribute restrictions for DynamoDB should be implemented with DynamoDB IAM condition keys such as `dynamodb:Attributes` and `dynamodb:Select`.

The correct solution is **B**: create a cross-account assumable IAM role in the finance account, apply DynamoDB fine-grained access control conditions to that role, and allow the marketing account to assume it.

zh.question: 一家公司在 AWS Cloud 中使用 AWS Organizations 进行多账户设置。该公司的财务团队有一个使用 AWS Lambda 和 Amazon DynamoDB 的数据处理应用程序。公司的市场团队希望访问存储在 DynamoDB 表中的数据。该 DynamoDB 表包含机密数据。市场团队只能访问 DynamoDB 表中数据的特定属性。财务团队和市场团队拥有不同的 AWS 账户。解决方案架构师应如何为市场团队提供对 DynamoDB 表的适当访问权限？

options.A: 创建一个 SCP，以授予市场团队的 AWS 账户访问 DynamoDB 表中特定属性的权限。将该 SCP 附加到财务团队的 OU。
options.B: 在财务团队的账户中创建一个 IAM 角色，并使用针对特定 DynamoDB 属性的 IAM policy conditions（细粒度访问控制）。与市场团队的账户建立信任关系。在市场团队的账户中，创建一个有权限代入财务团队账户中该 IAM 角色的 IAM 角色。
options.C: 创建一个 resource-based IAM policy，其中包含针对特定 DynamoDB 属性的条件（细粒度访问控制）。将该策略附加到 DynamoDB 表。在市场团队的账户中，创建一个有权限访问财务团队账户中 DynamoDB 表的 IAM 角色。
options.D: 在财务团队的账户中创建一个 IAM 角色以访问 DynamoDB 表。使用 IAM permissions boundary 将访问限制为特定属性。在市场团队的账户中，创建一个有权限代入财务团队账户中该 IAM 角色的 IAM 角色。

zh.explanation:
该公司需要让市场 AWS 账户中的某个主体访问由财务 AWS 账户拥有的 DynamoDB 表，同时将访问限制为表中仅经过批准的属性。正确答案是 **B**。

**B. 在财务团队的账户中创建一个 IAM 角色，使用针对特定 DynamoDB 属性的 IAM policy conditions，与市场账户建立信任关系，并允许市场账户中的某个角色代入该角色。**

此设计同时满足两个要求：

- **跨账户访问：** IAM 角色是跨 AWS 账户委派访问权限的标准机制。AWS 文档说明，可以在一个账户中创建一个角色，其 trust policy 将另一个账户命名为受信任主体，并且可以授予受信任账户中的用户或角色调用 `sts:AssumeRole` 的权限。使用该角色时，主体只能执行该角色允许的操作，并且只能访问该角色允许的资源。请参阅 [IAM cross-account role access](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_aws-accounts.html)。
- **DynamoDB 属性级限制：** DynamoDB 支持通过 IAM policy conditions 实现细粒度访问控制。AWS 文档说明，IAM 策略可以限制对 DynamoDB 表中单个项目和属性的访问，并标识了 DynamoDB 条件键（例如 `dynamodb:Attributes` 和 `dynamodb:Select`），用于控制可访问哪些属性。请参阅 [Using IAM policy conditions for fine-grained access control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/specifying-conditions.html)。

因此，财务账户应拥有该角色，该角色具有对 DynamoDB 表的权限，并包含 DynamoDB 属性限制。该角色的 trust policy 应允许市场账户代入该角色，并且市场账户应授予其相应角色或用户代入该财务账户角色的权限。

**为什么其他选项不正确**

- **A. 创建 SCP 以授予访问权限。** 这是错误的，因为 service control policies 不会授予权限。SCP 定义组织中账户内 IAM 用户和角色可用权限的上限；它们是防护栏。AWS 明确说明，SCP 不授予任何权限。请参阅 [Service control policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)。

- **C. 将 resource-based IAM policy 附加到 DynamoDB 表，并在市场账户中创建角色。** 这与答案中描述的最佳跨账户角色委派方法不符。访问权限应由资源拥有者财务账户中的角色授予，该角色与市场账户建立信任关系，并具有应用 DynamoDB 细粒度属性条件的权限策略。然后，市场账户角色获得代入该财务账户角色的权限。

- **D. 使用 permissions boundary 将访问限制为特定属性。** 这是错误的，因为 permissions boundary 不是授予 DynamoDB 访问权限或实现 DynamoDB 属性级筛选的机制。permissions boundary 仅设置 identity-based policy 可以授予用户或角色的最大权限；它本身不提供权限。请参阅 [Permissions boundaries for IAM entities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html)。DynamoDB 的属性限制应使用 DynamoDB IAM 条件键（例如 `dynamodb:Attributes` 和 `dynamodb:Select`）来实现。

正确解决方案是 **B**：在财务账户中创建一个可跨账户代入的 IAM 角色，对该角色应用 DynamoDB 细粒度访问控制条件，并允许市场账户代入该角色。

en.question: A solutions architect is creating an application that stores objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The solutions architect must deploy the application in two AWS Regions that will be used simultaneously. The objects in the two S3 buckets must remain synchronized with each other. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose three.)

options.A: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point Change the application to refer to the Multi-Region Access Point
options.B: Configure two-way S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) between the two S3 buckets
options.C: Modify the application to store objects in each S3 bucket
options.D: Create an S3 Lifecycle rule for each S3 bucket to copy objects from one S3 bucket to the other S3 bucket
options.E: Enable S3 Versioning for each S3 bucket
options.F: Configure an event notification for each S3 bucket to invoke an AWS Lambda function to copy objects from one S3 bucket to the other S3 bucket

en.explanation:
The application will run in two AWS Regions at the same time and use an S3 bucket in each Region. The requirement is to keep the objects synchronized between the two buckets with the least operational overhead.

**Correct answers: A, B, E**

- **A. Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point. Change the application to refer to the Multi-Region Access Point** — Correct. An S3 Multi-Region Access Point gives the application a single access point across buckets in multiple Regions. AWS documentation states that in an **active-active** Multi-Region Access Point configuration, requests are automatically sent to the closest AWS Region, and all Regions can receive traffic. This fits an application deployed in two Regions simultaneously with low operational complexity. See [Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Points routing states](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/FailoverConfiguration.html).

- **B. Configure two-way S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) between the two S3 buckets** — Correct. The buckets must remain synchronized regardless of which Region receives writes. AWS documents that two-way, or bidirectional, replication creates a rule from bucket 1 to bucket 2 and a second rule from bucket 2 to bucket 1, ensuring that data is synchronized between buckets in different AWS Regions. See [Create two-way replication rules for your Multi-Region Access Point](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mrap-create-two-way-replication-rules.html).

- **E. Enable S3 Versioning for each S3 bucket** — Correct. S3 replication requires versioning. AWS states that both source and destination buckets must have versioning enabled for replication, and the two-way replication documentation also says all buckets selected for replication must have S3 Versioning enabled. See [Requirements and considerations for replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-requirements.html) and [Create two-way replication rules for your Multi-Region Access Point](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mrap-create-two-way-replication-rules.html).

**Why the other options are incorrect**

- **C. Modify the application to store objects in each S3 bucket** — Incorrect. This pushes synchronization logic into the application. It increases operational overhead, creates additional failure-handling complexity, and is less reliable than using managed S3 replication.

- **D. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule for each S3 bucket to copy objects from one S3 bucket to the other S3 bucket** — Incorrect. S3 Lifecycle rules are used for lifecycle management actions such as transitions and expiration, not for bidirectional object synchronization between buckets. S3 replication is the managed feature for this use case.

- **F. Configure an event notification for each S3 bucket to invoke an AWS Lambda function to copy objects from one S3 bucket to the other S3 bucket** — Incorrect. This could be custom-built, but it has more operational overhead than native S3 two-way replication. It would require Lambda code, error handling, retries, idempotency handling, monitoring, and loop prevention.

Therefore, the least-operational-overhead solution is to use an **S3 Multi-Region Access Point**, configure **two-way Cross-Region Replication**, and **enable S3 Versioning** on both buckets.

zh.question: 一名解决方案架构师正在创建一个应用程序，该应用程序将对象存储在 Amazon S3 存储桶中。解决方案架构师必须将该应用程序部署在两个将同时使用的 AWS 区域中。两个 S3 存储桶中的对象必须彼此保持同步。哪一组步骤能够以最少的运维开销满足这些要求？（选择三项。）

options.A: 创建一个 S3 Multi-Region Access Point。更改应用程序以引用该 Multi-Region Access Point
options.B: 在两个 S3 存储桶之间配置双向 S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR)
options.C: 修改应用程序以将对象存储在每个 S3 存储桶中
options.D: 为每个 S3 存储桶创建一个 S3 Lifecycle 规则，以将对象从一个 S3 存储桶复制到另一个 S3 存储桶
options.E: 为每个 S3 存储桶启用 S3 Versioning
options.F: 为每个 S3 存储桶配置事件通知，以调用 AWS Lambda 函数将对象从一个 S3 存储桶复制到另一个 S3 存储桶

zh.explanation:
该应用程序将同时在两个 AWS 区域中运行，并在每个区域中使用一个 S3 存储桶。要求是在两个存储桶之间保持对象同步，并且运维开销最小。

**正确答案：A、B、E**

- **A. 创建一个 S3 Multi-Region Access Point。更改应用程序以引用该 Multi-Region Access Point** — 正确。S3 Multi-Region Access Point 为应用程序提供一个跨多个区域中存储桶的单一访问点。AWS 文档说明，在 **active-active** Multi-Region Access Point 配置中，请求会自动发送到最近的 AWS 区域，并且所有区域都可以接收流量。这适合同时部署在两个区域中且需要低运维复杂度的应用程序。请参阅 [Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Points routing states](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/FailoverConfiguration.html)。

- **B. 在两个 S3 存储桶之间配置双向 S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR)** — 正确。无论哪个区域接收写入，存储桶都必须保持同步。AWS 文档说明，双向复制（或称 bidirectional replication）会创建一条从存储桶 1 到存储桶 2 的规则，以及第二条从存储桶 2 到存储桶 1 的规则，从而确保不同 AWS 区域中的存储桶之间的数据保持同步。请参阅 [Create two-way replication rules for your Multi-Region Access Point](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mrap-create-two-way-replication-rules.html)。

- **E. 为每个 S3 存储桶启用 S3 Versioning** — 正确。S3 replication 需要版本控制。AWS 声明，源存储桶和目标存储桶都必须启用版本控制才能进行复制，双向复制文档也说明，所有选择用于复制的存储桶都必须启用 S3 Versioning。请参阅 [Requirements and considerations for replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-requirements.html) 和 [Create two-way replication rules for your Multi-Region Access Point](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mrap-create-two-way-replication-rules.html)。

**其他选项为什么不正确**

- **C. 修改应用程序以将对象存储在每个 S3 存储桶中** — 不正确。这会将同步逻辑推入应用程序。它会增加运维开销，带来额外的故障处理复杂性，并且可靠性不如使用托管的 S3 replication。

- **D. 为每个 S3 存储桶创建一个 S3 Lifecycle 规则，以将对象从一个 S3 存储桶复制到另一个 S3 存储桶** — 不正确。S3 Lifecycle 规则用于生命周期管理操作，例如转换和过期，而不是用于存储桶之间的双向对象同步。S3 replication 是适用于此用例的托管功能。

- **F. 为每个 S3 存储桶配置事件通知，以调用 AWS Lambda 函数将对象从一个 S3 存储桶复制到另一个 S3 存储桶** — 不正确。这可以自定义构建，但与原生 S3 双向复制相比，运维开销更高。它需要 Lambda 代码、错误处理、重试、幂等性处理、监控和循环防护。

因此，运维开销最小的解决方案是使用 **S3 Multi-Region Access Point**，配置 **two-way Cross-Region Replication**，并在两个存储桶上**启用 S3 Versioning**。

en.question: A company has an IoT platform that runs in an on-premises environment. The platform consists of a server that connects to IoT devices by using the MQTT protocol. The platform collects telemetry data from the devices at least once every 5 minutes. The platform also stores device metadata in a MongoDB cluster. An application that is installed on an on-premises machine runs periodic jobs to aggregate and transform the telemetry and device metadata. The application creates reports that users view by using another web application that runs on the same on-premises machine. The periodic jobs take 120-600 seconds to run. However, the web application is always running. The company is moving the platform to AWS and must reduce the operational overhead of the stack. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose three.)

options.A: Use AWS Lambda functions to connect to the IoT devices
options.B: Configure the IoT devices to publish to AWS IoT Core
options.C: Write the metadata to a self-managed MongoDB database on an Amazon EC2 instance
options.D: Write the metadata to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
options.E: Use AWS Step Functions state machines with AWS Lambda tasks to prepare the reports and to write the reports to Amazon S3. Use Amazon CloudFront with an S3 origin to serve the reports
options.F: Use an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster with Amazon EC2 instances to prepare the reports. Use an ingress controller in the EKS cluster to serve the reports

en.explanation:
The company is migrating an on-premises IoT/MQTT ingestion platform, MongoDB-compatible metadata store, periodic report-generation jobs, and always-on report web serving to AWS. The key requirement is **least operational overhead**, so the best choices are managed/serverless services rather than self-managed servers or Kubernetes.

**Correct answers: B, D, and E.**

- **B. Configure the IoT devices to publish to AWS IoT Core** — Correct. AWS IoT Core is the managed AWS service designed for device connectivity and messaging. The AWS IoT documentation states that devices can use AWS IoT Device SDKs to send messages to and receive messages from AWS IoT, and AWS IoT Core supports MQTT connectivity. This replaces the on-premises MQTT server with a managed IoT ingestion layer. See [What is AWS IoT?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-iot.html) and [MQTT - AWS IoT Core](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/mqtt.html).

- **D. Write the metadata to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)** — Correct. The existing metadata store is MongoDB. Amazon DocumentDB is a **fully managed** MongoDB-compatible database service; AWS states that it makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale MongoDB-compatible databases and lets applications use the same MongoDB drivers and tools.
