- **C 错误。** 在 VPC 外部托管 Lambda 不会提供到 Neptune DB 集群的私有连接。Neptune 集群端点可在 VPC 内访问，除非显式配置了公有端点功能，而此选项并未这样做。此外，依赖“Lambda 函数的 IP 范围”并不是默认 Lambda 互联网出口的有效且稳定的访问控制模式。

- **D 错误。** Neptune 接口 VPC 端点用于 **Amazon Neptune API 操作**，而不是用于从 VPC 外部的 Lambda 函数连接到 Neptune 数据库集群端点。Neptune 文档说明，可以使用 PrivateLink 创建到 **Amazon Neptune API 端点** 的私有连接；这并不会使在 VPC 外部运行的 Lambda 函数能够访问 Neptune 数据库端点。请参阅 [Amazon Neptune and interface VPC endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/vpc-interface-endpoints.html)。

因此，**B** 和 **E** 是两个可行的独立解决方案：要么使用带 NAT 的私有子网来访问 DynamoDB，要么使用私有/隔离子网并配合 DynamoDB VPC 端点。

en.question: A company wants to design a disaster recovery (DR) solution for an application that runs in the company’s data center. The application writes to an SMB file share and creates a copy on a second file share. Both file shares are in the data center. The application uses two types of files: metadata files and image files. The company wants to store the copy on AWS. The company needs the ability to use SMB to access the data from either the data center or AWS if a disaster occurs. The copy of the data is rarely accessed but must be available within 5 minutes.

options.A: Deploy AWS Outposts with Amazon S3 storage. Configure a Windows Amazon EC2 instance on Outposts as a file server.
options.B: Deploy an Amazon FSx File Gateway. Configure an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ file system that uses SSD storage.
options.C: Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Configure the S3 File Gateway to use Amazon S3 Standard- Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) for the metadata files and to use S3 Glacier Deep Archive for the image files.
options.D: Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Configure the S3 File Gateway to use Amazon S3 Standard- Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) for the metadata files and image files.

en.explanation:
## Scenario and requirement

The application currently writes a copy of files to a second SMB share in the data center. The company wants that copy stored in AWS for DR. The copy is rarely accessed, but if a disaster occurs, the data must be accessible within 5 minutes and must be accessible by SMB from the data center or from AWS.

## Correct answer: D

**D. Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Configure the S3 File Gateway to use Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) for the metadata files and image files.**

Amazon S3 File Gateway is designed for exactly this kind of pattern: it presents file shares by using standard file protocols while storing the backing data as objects in Amazon S3. AWS states that S3 File Gateway lets you store and retrieve objects in Amazon S3 by using file protocols such as **NFS and SMB**, and that it can be deployed on premises or as an AMI in Amazon EC2. It also provides access to S3 objects as files or file share mount points, and supports SMB 2 and 3 access. See [What is Amazon S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html).

The storage class also fits. S3 Standard-IA is intended for long-lived, infrequently accessed data and provides **millisecond access**, which easily satisfies the “available within 5 minutes” requirement. AWS also recommends S3 Standard-IA for the primary or only copy of data that cannot be re-created, and it is stored across multiple Availability Zones. See [Storage classes for infrequently accessed objects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html).

The “SMB from either the data center or AWS” requirement is not a blocker for S3 File Gateway because AWS documents that S3 File Gateway can be deployed as an AMI in Amazon EC2, in addition to on-premises deployment. See [Deploy a customized Amazon EC2 host for S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/ec2-gateway-file.html). Therefore, the solution can provide SMB access to the S3-backed copy from the on-premises environment and, during DR, from AWS-hosted clients through an EC2-hosted S3 File Gateway.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Deploy AWS Outposts with Amazon S3 storage and a Windows EC2 file server

This is unnecessarily complex and expensive for a DR copy that is rarely accessed. Outposts is for running AWS infrastructure on premises and does not match the requirement to store the copy in AWS in a cost-effective, cloud-backed DR model. It also introduces a Windows file server that the question does not require.

### B. Deploy Amazon FSx File Gateway with an FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ SSD file system

FSx for Windows File Server provides native SMB file storage, so this option could technically provide SMB access. However, the workload is a rarely accessed DR copy. A Multi-AZ SSD FSx file system is a higher-performance, higher-cost file system choice than needed for infrequently accessed DR data. The question’s access pattern points to S3 Standard-IA with S3 File Gateway rather than continuously running high-performance Windows file storage.

Additionally, current AWS documentation notes that **Amazon FSx File Gateway is no longer available to new customers**. See [What is Amazon FSx File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/filefsxw/what-is-file-fsxw.html). Even aside from that current-service caveat, option B is not the best fit for rarely accessed DR storage.

### C. Use S3 File Gateway with S3 Standard-IA for metadata files and S3 Glacier Deep Archive for image files

The S3 File Gateway portion is appropriate, and S3 Standard-IA for metadata is appropriate. The problem is **S3 Glacier Deep Archive** for image files. The requirement says the copy of the data must be available within 5 minutes. AWS documents that S3 Glacier Deep Archive is archival storage, is not available for real-time access, and standard retrieval typically restores objects within 12 hours, while bulk retrieval typically restores within 48 hours. See [S3 Glacier Deep Archive](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html). This does not meet the 5-minute availability requirement.

## Conclusion

Option **D** is the best answer because S3 File Gateway provides SMB file access backed by Amazon S3, can be deployed on premises or in Amazon EC2 for DR access, and S3 Standard-IA provides cost-optimized storage for infrequently accessed data with millisecond access.

zh.question: 一家公司希望为在公司数据中心运行的应用程序设计灾难恢复（DR）解决方案。该应用程序写入一个 SMB 文件共享，并在第二个文件共享上创建副本。两个文件共享都位于数据中心。该应用程序使用两种类型的文件：元数据文件和映像文件。公司希望将该副本存储在 AWS 上。公司需要在发生灾难时，能够从数据中心或 AWS 使用 SMB 访问数据。该数据副本很少被访问，但必须在 5 分钟内可用。

options.A: 部署带有 Amazon S3 存储的 AWS Outposts。将 Outposts 上的一个 Windows Amazon EC2 实例配置为文件服务器。
options.B: 部署 Amazon FSx File Gateway。配置一个使用 SSD 存储的 Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ 文件系统。
options.C: 部署 Amazon S3 File Gateway。配置 S3 File Gateway，对元数据文件使用 Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)，对映像文件使用 S3 Glacier Deep Archive。
options.D: 部署 Amazon S3 File Gateway。配置 S3 File Gateway，对元数据文件和映像文件使用 Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)。

zh.explanation:
## 场景和要求

该应用程序目前将文件副本写入数据中心中的第二个 SMB 共享。公司希望将该副本存储在 AWS 中用于 DR。该副本很少被访问，但如果发生灾难，数据必须在 5 分钟内可访问，并且必须能够从数据中心或 AWS 通过 SMB 访问。

## 正确答案：D

**D. 部署 Amazon S3 File Gateway。配置 S3 File Gateway，对元数据文件和映像文件使用 Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)。**

Amazon S3 File Gateway 正是为这种模式而设计的：它使用标准文件协议呈现文件共享，同时将后端数据作为对象存储在 Amazon S3 中。AWS 表示，S3 File Gateway 允许您使用 **NFS 和 SMB** 等文件协议在 Amazon S3 中存储和检索对象，并且它可以部署在本地，也可以作为 AMI 部署在 Amazon EC2 中。它还提供以文件或文件共享挂载点形式访问 S3 对象的能力，并支持 SMB 2 和 3 访问。请参阅 [What is Amazon S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html)。

存储类也符合要求。S3 Standard-IA 适用于长期保存、访问频率较低的数据，并提供**毫秒级访问**，这很容易满足“在 5 分钟内可用”的要求。AWS 还建议将 S3 Standard-IA 用于无法重新创建的数据的主副本或唯一副本，并且它跨多个 Availability Zones 存储。请参阅 [Storage classes for infrequently accessed objects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)。

“从数据中心或 AWS 通过 SMB”这一要求并不是 S3 File Gateway 的阻碍，因为 AWS 文档说明，除了本地部署之外，S3 File Gateway 还可以作为 AMI 部署在 Amazon EC2 中。请参阅 [Deploy a customized Amazon EC2 host for S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/ec2-gateway-file.html)。因此，该解决方案可以从本地环境提供对 S3 后端副本的 SMB 访问，并且在 DR 期间，通过 EC2 托管的 S3 File Gateway 从 AWS 托管的客户端提供访问。

## 其他选项为何不正确

### A. 部署带有 Amazon S3 存储的 AWS Outposts 和 Windows EC2 文件服务器

对于很少访问的 DR 副本来说，这过于复杂且昂贵。Outposts 用于在本地运行 AWS 基础设施，不符合以经济高效、云后端 DR 模型将副本存储在 AWS 中的要求。它还引入了题目并不需要的 Windows 文件服务器。

### B. 部署 Amazon FSx File Gateway，并使用 FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ SSD 文件系统

FSx for Windows File Server 提供原生 SMB 文件存储，因此该选项从技术上可以提供 SMB 访问。但是，该工作负载是很少访问的 DR 副本。Multi-AZ SSD FSx 文件系统是比很少访问的 DR 数据所需更高性能、更高成本的文件系统选择。题目的访问模式指向 S3 Standard-IA 与 S3 File Gateway，而不是持续运行的高性能 Windows 文件存储。

此外，当前 AWS 文档指出 **Amazon FSx File Gateway 不再对新客户开放**。请参阅 [What is Amazon FSx File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/filefsxw/what-is-file-fsxw.html)。即使撇开这个当前服务方面的注意事项，选项 B 也不是很少访问的 DR 存储的最佳选择。

### C. 将 S3 File Gateway 与 S3 Standard-IA 用于元数据文件，并将 S3 Glacier Deep Archive 用于映像文件

S3 File Gateway 部分是合适的，S3 Standard-IA 用于元数据也是合适的。问题在于将 **S3 Glacier Deep Archive** 用于映像文件。要求说明该数据副本必须在 5 分钟内可用。AWS 文档说明，S3 Glacier Deep Archive 是归档存储，不适用于实时访问，标准检索通常会在 12 小时内还原对象，而批量检索通常会在 48 小时内还原。请参阅 [S3 Glacier Deep Archive](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/glacier-storage-classes.html)。这不满足 5 分钟可用性要求。

## 结论

选项 **D** 是最佳答案，因为 S3 File Gateway 提供由 Amazon S3 支撑的 SMB 文件访问，可以部署在本地或 Amazon EC2 中以便 DR 访问，并且 S3 Standard-IA 为很少访问的数据提供成本优化的存储和毫秒级访问。

en.question: A company is creating a solution that can move 400 employees into a remote working environment in the event of an unexpected disaster. The user desktops have a mix of Windows and Linux operating systems. Multiple types of software, such as web browsers and mail clients, are installed on each desktop. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that can be integrated with the company’s on- premises Active Directory to allow employees to use their existing identity credentials. The solution must provide multifactor authentication (MFA) and must replicate the user experience from the existing desktops. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use Amazon WorkSpaces for the cloud desktop service. Set up a VPN connection to the on- premises network. Create an AD Connector, and connect to the on-premises Active Directory. Activate MFA for Amazon WorkSpaces by using the AWS Management Console.
options.B: Use Amazon AppStream 2.0 as an application streaming service. Configure Desktop View for the employees. Set up a VPN connection to the on-premises network. Set up Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) on premises. Connect the VPC network to AD FS through the VPN connection.
options.C: Use Amazon WorkSpaces for the cloud desktop service. Set up a VPN connection to the on- premises network. Create an AD Connector, and connect to the on-premises Active Directory. Configure a RADIUS server for MFA.
options.D: Use Amazon AppStream 2.0 as an application streaming service. Set up Active Directory Federation Services on premises. Configure MFA to grant users access on AppStream 2.0.

en.explanation:
The company needs a remote-work/DR desktop solution for 400 users that can reproduce users' existing desktop experience across Windows and Linux, integrate with on-premises Active Directory credentials, and enforce MFA.

**Correct answer: C. Use Amazon WorkSpaces with AD Connector and configure a RADIUS server for MFA.**

Amazon WorkSpaces is the best fit because it provides full virtual cloud desktops, not just streamed applications. AWS states that WorkSpaces lets you provision virtual cloud-based desktops for users and that those desktops can run Microsoft Windows, Ubuntu Linux, Rocky Linux, or Red Hat Enterprise Linux. The same documentation also says WorkSpaces can be connected to on-premises Active Directory so users can use existing credentials, and can use MFA for additional security ([Amazon WorkSpaces: What is Amazon WorkSpaces?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/amazon-workspaces.html)). AWS also documents Linux WorkSpaces support and Active Directory integration for Linux WorkSpaces ([Manage your Linux WorkSpaces in WorkSpaces Personal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/manage-linux-workspaces.html)).

AD Connector is appropriate for the identity requirement because it is a directory gateway that redirects directory requests to an on-premises Microsoft Active Directory without caching information in the cloud. AWS notes that AD Connector allows end users to use existing corporate credentials for AWS applications such as WorkSpaces, and that it can enable MFA by integrating with RADIUS-based MFA infrastructure ([AD Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/directory_ad_connector.html)).

For WorkSpaces with AD Connector, MFA is specifically implemented through RADIUS configuration. AWS documentation for WorkSpaces MFA says that the RADIUS server can be hosted in AWS or on premises, and the MFA setup requires entering RADIUS server IP addresses, port, shared secret, protocol, timeout, and retries ([Multi-factor authentication (AD Connector) for WorkSpaces Personal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/connect-mfa.html)). Therefore, option C matches all major requirements: full desktop service, Windows/Linux support, on-premises AD integration through AD Connector, and MFA through RADIUS.

### Why the other options are incorrect

**A. Incorrect.** WorkSpaces plus AD Connector is the right direction, but the MFA detail is wrong. MFA is not simply “activated for Amazon WorkSpaces by using the AWS Management Console” as a standalone mechanism. For AD Connector-backed WorkSpaces, MFA is enabled by configuring RADIUS server settings, including the RADIUS server endpoint, port, and shared secret ([WorkSpaces MFA with AD Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/connect-mfa.html)).

**B. Incorrect.** Amazon AppStream 2.0 / WorkSpaces Applications is an application streaming service, not primarily a persistent full-cloud-desktop replacement. AWS describes it as a fully managed application streaming service that gives users access to desktop applications from anywhere ([What Is Amazon WorkSpaces Applications?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appstream2/latest/developerguide/what-is-appstream.html)). Even with a desktop-style view, it is better suited to streaming curated applications than replicating each employee's full existing desktop environment with installed browsers, mail clients, and OS-specific desktop experience. This option also does not provide the WorkSpaces AD Connector + RADIUS MFA pattern required for the stated identity/MFA requirements.

**D. Incorrect.** This uses AppStream 2.0 rather than WorkSpaces. AppStream/WorkSpaces Applications can stream applications, but the question asks for a solution that replicates the user desktop experience across Windows and Linux desktops. WorkSpaces is the AWS service designed to provision full virtual desktops, while AppStream/WorkSpaces Applications is documented as an application streaming service ([What Is Amazon WorkSpaces Applications?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appstream2/latest/developerguide/what-is-appstream.html)). Also, the option does not specify AD Connector or RADIUS-based MFA for WorkSpaces-style authentication.

Thus, **C** is the most complete and AWS-aligned solution.

zh.question: 一家公司正在创建一个解决方案，以便在发生意外灾难时将 400 名员工转移到远程工作环境中。用户桌面混合使用 Windows 和 Linux 操作系统。每台桌面上都安装了多种类型的软件，例如 Web 浏览器和邮件客户端。解决方案架构师需要实施一个可与公司本地 Active Directory 集成的解决方案，以允许员工使用其现有身份凭证。该解决方案必须提供多重身份验证（MFA），并且必须复制现有桌面的用户体验。哪种解决方案能满足这些要求？

options.A: 使用 Amazon WorkSpaces 作为云桌面服务。设置到本地网络的 VPN 连接。创建 AD Connector，并连接到本地 Active Directory。使用 AWS Management Console 为 Amazon WorkSpaces 激活 MFA。
options.B: 使用 Amazon AppStream 2.0 作为应用程序流式传输服务。为员工配置 Desktop View。设置到本地网络的 VPN 连接。在本地设置 Active Directory Federation Services（AD FS）。通过 VPN 连接将 VPC 网络连接到 AD FS。
options.C: 使用 Amazon WorkSpaces 作为云桌面服务。设置到本地网络的 VPN 连接。创建 AD Connector，并连接到本地 Active Directory。为 MFA 配置 RADIUS 服务器。
options.D: 使用 Amazon AppStream 2.0 作为应用程序流式传输服务。在本地设置 Active Directory Federation Services。配置 MFA 以授予用户对 AppStream 2.0 的访问权限。

zh.explanation:
公司需要为 400 名用户提供远程工作/灾难恢复桌面解决方案，该方案能够在 Windows 和 Linux 上复现用户现有的桌面体验，与本地 Active Directory 凭证集成，并强制执行 MFA。

**正确答案：C. 使用 Amazon WorkSpaces，并结合 AD Connector，同时为 MFA 配置 RADIUS 服务器。**

Amazon WorkSpaces 最适合此场景，因为它提供完整的虚拟云桌面，而不仅仅是流式传输的应用程序。AWS 表示，WorkSpaces 允许你为用户预置基于云的虚拟桌面，并且这些桌面可以运行 Microsoft Windows、Ubuntu Linux、Rocky Linux 或 Red Hat Enterprise Linux。同一文档还说明，WorkSpaces 可以连接到本地 Active Directory，使用户能够使用现有凭证，并且可以使用 MFA 来增强安全性（[Amazon WorkSpaces: What is Amazon WorkSpaces?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/amazon-workspaces.html)）。AWS 还记录了 Linux WorkSpaces 支持以及 Linux WorkSpaces 的 Active Directory 集成（[Manage your Linux WorkSpaces in WorkSpaces Personal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/manage-linux-workspaces.html)）。

AD Connector 适用于该身份要求，因为它是一个目录网关，可将目录请求重定向到本地 Microsoft Active Directory，而不会在云中缓存信息。AWS 指出，AD Connector 允许最终用户对 WorkSpaces 等 AWS 应用程序使用现有企业凭证，并且它可以通过与基于 RADIUS 的 MFA 基础设施集成来启用 MFA（[AD Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/directory_ad_connector.html)）。

对于使用 AD Connector 的 WorkSpaces，MFA 具体是通过 RADIUS 配置来实现的。AWS 关于 WorkSpaces MFA 的文档说明，RADIUS 服务器可以托管在 AWS 中或本地，并且 MFA 设置需要输入 RADIUS 服务器 IP 地址、端口、共享密钥、协议、超时和重试次数（[Multi-factor authentication (AD Connector) for WorkSpaces Personal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/connect-mfa.html)）。因此，选项 C 符合所有主要要求：完整桌面服务、Windows/Linux 支持、通过 AD Connector 集成本地 AD，以及通过 RADIUS 实现 MFA。

### 为什么其他选项不正确

**A. 不正确。** WorkSpaces 加 AD Connector 的方向是正确的，但 MFA 细节错误。MFA 并不是作为一种独立机制，通过使用 AWS Management Console 就能简单地“为 Amazon WorkSpaces 激活”。对于由 AD Connector 支持的 WorkSpaces，MFA 是通过配置 RADIUS 服务器设置来启用的，包括 RADIUS 服务器终端节点、端口和共享密钥（[WorkSpaces MFA with AD Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/connect-mfa.html)）。

**B. 不正确。** Amazon AppStream 2.0 / WorkSpaces Applications 是应用程序流式传输服务，而不是主要用于替代持久完整云桌面的服务。AWS 将其描述为一种完全托管的应用程序流式传输服务，使用户能够从任何位置访问桌面应用程序（[What Is Amazon WorkSpaces Applications?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appstream2/latest/developerguide/what-is-appstream.html)）。即使具有桌面风格的视图，它也更适合流式传输经过精选的应用程序，而不是复制每位员工包含已安装浏览器、邮件客户端和特定操作系统桌面体验的完整现有桌面环境。该选项也没有提供满足所述身份/MFA 要求所需的 WorkSpaces AD Connector + RADIUS MFA 模式。

**D. 不正确。** 该选项使用 AppStream 2.0 而不是 WorkSpaces。AppStream/WorkSpaces Applications 可以流式传输应用程序，但题目要求的是一种能够在 Windows 和 Linux 桌面上复制用户桌面体验的解决方案。WorkSpaces 是 AWS 中专为预置完整虚拟桌面而设计的服务，而 AppStream/WorkSpaces Applications 在文档中被定义为应用程序流式传输服务（[What Is Amazon WorkSpaces Applications?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appstream2/latest/developerguide/what-is-appstream.html)）。此外，该选项没有指定用于 WorkSpaces 风格身份验证的 AD Connector 或基于 RADIUS 的 MFA。

因此，**C** 是最完整且最符合 AWS 的解决方案。

en.question: A company has deployed an Amazon Connect contact center. Contact center agents are reporting large numbers of computer-generated calls. The company is concerned about the cost and productivity effects of these calls. The company wants a solution that will allow agents to flag the call as spam and automatically block the numbers from going to an agent in the future. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution to meet these requirements?

options.A: Customize the Contact Control Panel (CCP) by adding a flag call button that will invoke an AWS Lambda function that calls the UpdateContactAttributes API. Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the spam numbers. Modify the contact flows to look for the updated attribute and to use a Lambda function to read and write to the DynamoDB table.
options.B: Use a Contact Lens for Amazon Connect rule that will look for spam calls. Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the spam numbers. Modify the contact flows to look for the rule and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to read and write to the DynamoDB table.
options.C: Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the spam numbers. Create a quick connect that the agents can transfer the spam call to from the Contact Control Panel (CCP). Modify the quick connect contact flow to invoke an AWS Lambda function to write to the DynamoDB table.
options.D: Modify the initial contact flow to ask for caller input. If the agent does not receive input, the agent should mark the caller as spam. Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the spam numbers. Use an AWS Lambda function to read and write to the DynamoDB table.

en.explanation:
The contact center needs an agent-driven way to mark an active call as spam and then prevent future calls from that caller from reaching an agent. The most efficient design is to capture the agent’s flag in the agent UI, persist the caller number in a deny/block list, and have the inbound contact flow check that list before routing to an agent.

**Correct answer: A**

Amazon Connect supports updating user-defined contact attributes for ongoing or completed contacts with `UpdateContactAttributes`; AWS states that these attributes are available in flows and can be used to “flag calls for additional analysis” or identify abusive callers ([UpdateContactAttributes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateContactAttributes.html)). Amazon Connect flows can also invoke Lambda functions, and the Lambda event includes contact data such as `CustomerEndpoint.Address`, which is the caller’s phone number ([Grant Connect access to your AWS Lambda functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/connect-lambda-functions.html); [contact attributes list](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/connect-attrib-list.html)). Therefore, a customized CCP button can invoke Lambda to flag the contact/update attributes and write the number to DynamoDB, while the initial/inbound flow invokes Lambda to check DynamoDB and route/block before sending future calls to agents. This directly meets both requirements with minimal agent effort: agents click a flag button rather than transferring or performing manual call handling.

**Why the other options are incorrect**

- **B**: Contact Lens rules analyze conversations and are applied when Contact Lens analyzes contacts, but this option does not provide the required agent-controlled “flag call” action. It also describes contact flows “looking for the rule,” which is not the right mechanism for pre-routing future inbound calls against a custom deny list. Contact Lens rules are not the most operationally efficient way to let an agent mark a number and immediately maintain a DynamoDB-based block list.
- **C**: A quick connect transfer could be made to a special flow that writes the number to DynamoDB, but it is less operationally efficient than a CCP flag button. Agents would need to transfer the spam call, which adds handling steps and may affect metrics/agent workflow. The question asks for the most operationally efficient solution, and a direct CCP button is more streamlined.
- **D**: Asking every caller for input adds friction to all legitimate callers and still requires the agent to mark calls manually if no input is received. It also does not reliably identify computer-generated calls because some automated calls can provide DTMF or speech, and some valid callers might not respond. This is less efficient and less targeted than checking a maintained deny list before routing.

zh.question: 一家公司已部署 Amazon Connect 联络中心。联络中心座席报告称接到了大量计算机生成的呼叫。公司担心这些呼叫带来的成本和生产力影响。公司希望有一种解决方案，允许座席将呼叫标记为垃圾呼叫，并自动阻止这些号码将来转接到座席。哪种解决方案在运营上最有效地满足这些要求？

options.A: 通过添加“标记呼叫”按钮来自定义 Contact Control Panel (CCP)，该按钮将调用一个 AWS Lambda 函数，而该函数调用 UpdateContactAttributes API。使用 Amazon DynamoDB 表存储垃圾号码。修改联系流以查找更新后的属性，并使用 Lambda 函数读写 DynamoDB 表。
options.B: 使用 Contact Lens for Amazon Connect 规则来查找垃圾呼叫。使用 Amazon DynamoDB 表存储垃圾号码。修改联系流以查找该规则，并调用 AWS Lambda 函数读写 DynamoDB 表。
options.C: 使用 Amazon DynamoDB 表存储垃圾号码。创建一个 quick connect，使座席可以从 Contact Control Panel (CCP) 将垃圾呼叫转接过去。修改 quick connect 联系流以调用 AWS Lambda 函数写入 DynamoDB 表。
options.D: 修改初始联系流以请求呼叫者输入。如果座席未收到输入，座席应将呼叫者标记为垃圾呼叫者。使用 Amazon DynamoDB 表存储垃圾号码。使用 AWS Lambda 函数读写 DynamoDB 表。

zh.explanation:
联络中心需要一种由座席驱动的方式，将正在进行的呼叫标记为垃圾呼叫，然后防止该呼叫者未来的呼叫转接到座席。最高效的设计是在座席 UI 中捕获座席的标记，将呼叫者号码持久化到拒绝/阻止列表中，并让入站联系流在路由到座席之前检查该列表。

**正确答案：A**

Amazon Connect 支持使用 `UpdateContactAttributes` 为正在进行或已完成的联系更新用户定义的联系属性；AWS 表示这些属性可在流中使用，并可用于“标记呼叫以进行进一步分析”或识别滥用呼叫者（[UpdateContactAttributes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateContactAttributes.html)）。Amazon Connect 流还可以调用 Lambda 函数，并且 Lambda 事件包含联系数据，例如 `CustomerEndpoint.Address`，即呼叫者的电话号码（[Grant Connect access to your AWS Lambda functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/connect-lambda-functions.html)；[contact attributes list](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/connect-attrib-list.html)）。因此，自定义 CCP 按钮可以调用 Lambda 来标记联系/更新属性并将号码写入 DynamoDB，而初始/入站流调用 Lambda 来检查 DynamoDB，并在将未来呼叫发送给座席之前进行路由/阻止。这以最少的座席工作量直接满足两项要求：座席只需点击标记按钮，而不是转接或执行手动呼叫处理。

**为什么其他选项不正确**

- **B**：Contact Lens 规则会分析对话，并在 Contact Lens 分析联系时应用，但此选项没有提供所需的由座席控制的“标记呼叫”操作。它还描述了联系流“查找该规则”，这并不是在预路由未来入站呼叫时针对自定义拒绝列表进行检查的正确机制。Contact Lens 规则并不是让座席标记号码并立即维护基于 DynamoDB 的阻止列表的最具运营效率的方式。
- **C**：可以创建一个 quick connect 转接到写入号码到 DynamoDB 的特殊流，但它的运营效率低于 CCP 标记按钮。座席需要转接垃圾呼叫，这会增加处理步骤，并可能影响指标/座席工作流。题目要求的是运营效率最高的解决方案，而直接的 CCP 按钮更加简化。
- **D**：要求每位呼叫者输入会给所有合法呼叫者增加阻力，并且如果未收到输入，仍需要座席手动标记呼叫。它也无法可靠识别计算机生成的呼叫，因为有些自动呼叫可以提供 DTMF 或语音，而有些有效呼叫者可能不会响应。与在路由前检查已维护的拒绝列表相比，这种方式效率更低，也不够有针对性。

en.question: A company has mounted sensors to collect information about environmental parameters such as humidity and light throughout all the company's factories. The company needs to stream and analyze the data in the AWS Cloud in real time. If any of the parameters fall out of acceptable ranges, the factory operations team must receive a notification immediately. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Stream the data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Use AWS Step Functions to consume and analyze the data in the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the operations team.
options.B: Stream the data to an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) cluster. Set up a trigger in Amazon MSK to invoke an AWS Fargate task to analyze the data. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to notify the operations team.
options.C: Stream the data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume the Kinesis data stream and to analyze the data. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the operations team.
options.D: Stream the data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application. Use an automatically scaled and containerized service in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to consume and analyze the data. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to notify the operations team.

en.explanation:
The requirement is to ingest sensor telemetry continuously, analyze it in near-immediate/real time, and notify the operations team immediately when a reading is outside acceptable thresholds.

**Correct answer: C. Stream the data to Kinesis Data Streams, process it with Lambda, and notify with SNS.**

Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is designed for rapid, continuous data intake and real-time processing. AWS documentation states that Kinesis Data Streams supports real-time metrics, reporting, and analytics, and that the delay between putting a record into a stream and being able to retrieve it is typically less than 1 second, so consumers can start processing almost immediately after data is added ([Kinesis Data Streams introduction](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/introduction.html)). AWS Lambda is a valid consumer for Kinesis Data Streams: Lambda reads records from the stream, invokes the function with batches of stream records, and by default invokes the function as soon as records are available ([Using Lambda with Kinesis](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-kinesis.html)). The Lambda function can evaluate each record against threshold ranges and publish alerts to Amazon SNS. SNS is appropriate for immediate operations notifications because SNS topics deliver messages to subscribers such as email, SMS, mobile push, HTTP/S, Lambda, and other endpoints, and the documentation specifically describes application alerts and user notifications through SNS ([Amazon SNS concepts and scenarios](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

* **A. Kinesis Data Firehose + Step Functions + SNS** — Firehose is primarily a delivery service to destinations and buffers incoming data before delivery. For S3 backup/delivery, AWS documents configurable buffering intervals of 60–900 seconds and buffer sizes before delivery ([Firehose buffering settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/create-configure-backup.html)). That is not the best fit for immediate per-event analysis. Also, Step Functions is not a native consumer of a Firehose delivery stream for continuous stream processing.
* **B. Amazon MSK + Fargate task + SES** — MSK can support streaming workloads, but the option describes an “MSK trigger” to invoke a Fargate task, which is not the typical managed integration pattern for immediate threshold evaluation. It also uses Amazon SES, which is for email sending, whereas SNS is the AWS service designed for pub/sub notifications and application-to-person alerts across email, SMS, push, and other endpoints.
* **D. Kinesis Data Analytics + ECS + SES** — Kinesis Data Analytics/Managed Service for Apache Flink can analyze streaming data, but this option then adds an automatically scaled ECS service to consume and analyze the data, making the architecture unnecessarily complex and internally inconsistent. It also uses SES instead of SNS for immediate operations notifications. SNS is the better fit for operational alerts.

Therefore, **C** is the solution that most directly satisfies real-time streaming analysis and immediate notification requirements using managed AWS integrations.

zh.question: 一家公司在其所有工厂中安装了传感器，用于收集有关湿度和光照等环境参数的信息。该公司需要在 AWS Cloud 中实时流式传输并分析这些数据。如果任何参数超出可接受范围，工厂运营团队必须立即收到通知。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 将数据流式传输到 Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose 传输流。使用 AWS Step Functions 使用并分析 Kinesis Data Firehose 传输流中的数据。使用 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 通知运营团队。
options.B: 将数据流式传输到 Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) 集群。在 Amazon MSK 中设置触发器以调用 AWS Fargate 任务来分析数据。使用 Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) 通知运营团队。
options.C: 将数据流式传输到 Amazon Kinesis data stream。创建 AWS Lambda 函数来使用 Kinesis data stream 并分析数据。使用 Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) 通知运营团队。
options.D: 将数据流式传输到 Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics 应用程序。使用 Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) 中自动扩展且容器化的服务来使用并分析数据。使用 Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) 通知运营团队。

zh.explanation:
要求是持续摄取传感器遥测数据，进行近乎即时/实时分析，并在读数超出可接受阈值时立即通知运营团队。

**正确答案：C。将数据流式传输到 Kinesis Data Streams，使用 Lambda 处理，并使用 SNS 通知。**

Amazon Kinesis Data Streams 旨在实现快速、连续的数据摄取和实时处理。AWS 文档说明，Kinesis Data Streams 支持实时指标、报告和分析，并且从将记录放入流到能够检索该记录之间的延迟通常小于 1 秒，因此消费者可以在数据添加后几乎立即开始处理（[Kinesis Data Streams introduction](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/introduction.html)）。AWS Lambda 是 Kinesis Data Streams 的有效消费者：Lambda 从流中读取记录，使用成批的流记录调用函数，并且默认情况下会在记录可用时立即调用函数（[Using Lambda with Kinesis](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-kinesis.html)）。Lambda 函数可以根据阈值范围评估每条记录，并将警报发布到 Amazon SNS。SNS 适用于即时运营通知，因为 SNS 主题可将消息传递给订阅者，例如电子邮件、SMS、移动推送、HTTP/S、Lambda 和其他端点，文档也明确描述了通过 SNS 实现应用程序警报和用户通知（[Amazon SNS concepts and scenarios](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html)）。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

* **A. Kinesis Data Firehose + Step Functions + SNS** — Firehose 主要是向目标位置传输数据的服务，并会在传输前缓冲传入数据。对于 S3 备份/传输，AWS 文档记录了可配置的缓冲间隔为 60–900 秒，并在传输前使用缓冲区大小（[Firehose buffering settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/create-configure-backup.html)）。这并不是即时逐事件分析的最佳选择。此外，Step Functions 并不是 Firehose delivery stream 的原生消费者，无法用于连续流处理。
* **B. Amazon MSK + Fargate task + SES** — MSK 可以支持流式处理工作负载，但该选项描述了使用“MSK 触发器”来调用 Fargate 任务，这不是用于即时阈值评估的典型托管集成模式。它还使用 Amazon SES，后者用于发送电子邮件，而 SNS 才是 AWS 中为发布/订阅通知以及通过电子邮件、SMS、推送和其他端点进行应用到个人警报而设计的服务。
* **D. Kinesis Data Analytics + ECS + SES** — Kinesis Data Analytics/Managed Service for Apache Flink 可以分析流式数据，但该选项随后又添加了一个自动扩展的 ECS 服务来使用并分析数据，使架构不必要地复杂且内部不一致。它还使用 SES 而不是 SNS 来实现即时运营通知。SNS 更适合运营警报。

因此，**C** 是最直接满足实时流式分析和即时通知要求的解决方案，并使用了托管的 AWS 集成。

en.question: A company is preparing to deploy an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for a workload. The company expects the cluster to support an unpredictable number of stateless pods. Many of the pods will be created during a short time period as the workload automatically scales the number of replicas that the workload uses. Which solution will MAXIMIZE node resilience?

options.A: Use a separate launch template to deploy the EKS control plane into a second cluster that is separate from the workload node groups.
options.B: Update the workload node groups. Use a smaller number of node groups and larger instances in the node groups.
options.C: Configure the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to ensure that the compute capacity of the workload node groups stays underprovisioned.
options.D: Configure the workload to use topology spread constraints that are based on Availability Zone.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The workload is expected to create many **stateless pod replicas in a short period**. The question asks which approach will **maximize resilience** for the EKS worker-node/data-plane environment during this scaling behavior.

The correct answer is **D. Configure the workload to use topology spread constraints that are based on Availability Zone.**

AWS EKS best-practice guidance says that a resilient data plane should be highly available and able to scale and heal automatically. It specifically recommends spreading worker nodes and workloads across multiple Availability Zones to protect workloads from an individual AZ failure. The same guidance states that the recommended method for spreading pods across AZs is to use **Topology Spread Constraints for Pods**, and shows `topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone` as the relevant configuration. It also notes that autoscaling capabilities can be aware of topology spread constraints and launch nodes in the correct AZs to meet the constraints where supported ([EKS Data Plane best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-plane.html)).

AWS Prescriptive Guidance similarly states that distributing workloads across failure domains such as **Availability Zones and nodes** improves component availability and decreases the chance of failure for horizontally scalable applications. It explains that Kubernetes pod topology spread constraints instruct the scheduler to distribute pods across failure domains such as Availability Zones and nodes, and identifies horizontally scalable/stateless-style applications as an appropriate use case ([Spread workloads across nodes and Availability Zones](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/ha-resiliency-amazon-eks-apps/spread-workloads.html)).

Therefore, for many stateless replicas created quickly by autoscaling, using topology spread constraints based on AZ reduces concentration of pods in a single failure domain and improves resilience during node or AZ failures.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Use a separate launch template to deploy the EKS control plane into a second cluster

This is incorrect. Customers do not deploy the EKS control plane into a launch template or worker-node group; the EKS control plane is managed by AWS. Also, creating a separate cluster for the control plane does not solve the stated problem of resilient placement of rapidly scaling workload pods across worker nodes and AZs.

### B. Use fewer node groups and larger instances

This is not the best resilience choice. Larger instances and fewer node groups can increase the blast radius of a single node failure because more pods can be concentrated on fewer nodes. The AWS guidance emphasizes distributing workloads across nodes and Availability Zones to improve availability, not consolidating them onto fewer, larger nodes ([Spread workloads across nodes and Availability Zones](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/ha-resiliency-amazon-eks-apps/spread-workloads.html)).

### C. Configure Cluster Autoscaler to keep workload node groups underprovisioned

This is incorrect and counterproductive. The EKS Cluster Autoscaler is described as ensuring that the cluster has **enough nodes to schedule pods without wasting resources**; it watches for unschedulable pods and underutilized nodes and adjusts Auto Scaling groups accordingly ([Cluster Autoscaler - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/cas.html)). Intentionally keeping node groups underprovisioned would make rapid pod creation more likely to result in pending pods and reduced availability, not greater resilience.

### D. Configure topology spread constraints based on Availability Zone

This is correct. AZ-based topology spread constraints direct the Kubernetes scheduler to spread replicas across AZs, reducing failure-domain concentration and improving availability for horizontally scalable/stateless workloads. AWS explicitly recommends this method for spreading pods across AZs in EKS ([EKS Data Plane best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-plane.html)).

zh.question: 一家公司正准备为某个工作负载部署 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) 集群。该公司预计该集群需要支持数量不可预测的无状态 pod。由于该工作负载会自动扩展其使用的副本数量，许多 pod 会在短时间内被创建。哪种解决方案将最大限度地提高节点弹性？

options.A: 使用单独的启动模板将 EKS 控制平面部署到第二个集群中，该集群与工作负载节点组分离。
options.B: 更新工作负载节点组。在节点组中使用更少数量的节点组和更大的实例。
options.C: 配置 Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler，以确保工作负载节点组的计算容量保持供应不足。
options.D: 配置工作负载使用基于可用区的拓扑分布约束。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

该工作负载预计会在短时间内创建许多**无状态 pod 副本**。题目询问哪种方法将使 EKS 工作节点/数据平面环境在这种扩展行为期间**最大限度地提高弹性**。

正确答案是 **D. 配置工作负载使用基于可用区的拓扑分布约束。**

AWS EKS 最佳实践指南指出，具有弹性的数据平面应当具备高可用性，并能够自动扩展和自我修复。它特别建议将工作节点和工作负载分布到多个可用区，以保护工作负载免受单个 AZ 故障的影响。同一指南还说明，在多个 AZ 之间分布 pod 的推荐方法是使用 **Topology Spread Constraints for Pods**，并展示了 `topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone` 作为相关配置。它还指出，在受支持的情况下，自动扩展能力可以感知拓扑分布约束，并在正确的 AZ 中启动节点以满足这些约束（[EKS Data Plane best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-plane.html)）。

AWS Prescriptive Guidance 同样指出，将工作负载分布到诸如**可用区和节点**之类的故障域，可以提高组件可用性，并降低水平可扩展应用程序发生故障的概率。它解释说，Kubernetes pod topology spread constraints 会指示调度器将 pod 分布到诸如可用区和节点之类的故障域中，并将水平可扩展/无状态风格的应用程序确定为合适的使用场景（[Spread workloads across nodes and Availability Zones](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/ha-resiliency-amazon-eks-apps/spread-workloads.html)）。

因此，对于由自动扩展快速创建的许多无状态副本，使用基于 AZ 的拓扑分布约束可以减少 pod 在单个故障域中的集中，并在节点或 AZ 故障期间提高弹性。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. 使用单独的启动模板将 EKS 控制平面部署到第二个集群

这是不正确的。客户不会将 EKS 控制平面部署到启动模板或工作节点组中；EKS 控制平面由 AWS 管理。此外，为控制平面创建单独的集群并不能解决快速扩展的工作负载 pod 在工作节点和 AZ 之间进行弹性放置这一既定问题。

### B. 使用更少的节点组和更大的实例

这不是最佳的弹性选择。更大的实例和更少的节点组会增加单个节点故障的爆炸半径，因为更多 pod 可能集中在更少的节点上。AWS 指南强调将工作负载分布到节点和可用区以提高可用性，而不是将它们整合到更少、更大的节点上（[Spread workloads across nodes and Availability Zones](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/ha-resiliency-amazon-eks-apps/spread-workloads.html)）。

### C. 配置 Cluster Autoscaler 使工作负载节点组保持供应不足

这是不正确且适得其反的。EKS Cluster Autoscaler 被描述为确保集群有**足够的节点来调度 pod，同时不浪费资源**；它会监视不可调度的 pod 和利用率不足的节点，并相应地调整 Auto Scaling 组（[Cluster Autoscaler - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/cas.html)）。故意使节点组保持供应不足，会使快速创建 pod 更有可能导致 pod 处于 pending 状态并降低可用性，而不是提高弹性。

### D. 配置基于可用区的拓扑分布约束

这是正确的。基于 AZ 的拓扑分布约束会指示 Kubernetes 调度器将副本分布到多个 AZ 中，从而减少故障域集中并提高水平可扩展/无状态工作负载的可用性。AWS 明确推荐这种方法用于在 EKS 中跨 AZ 分布 pod（[EKS Data Plane best practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/data-plane.html)）。

en.question: A company needs to implement a disaster recovery (DR) plan for a web application. The application runs in a single AWS Region. The application uses microservices that run in containers. The containers are hosted on AWS Fargate in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The application has an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance as its data layer and uses Amazon Route 53 for DNS resolution. An Amazon CloudWatch alarm invokes an Amazon EventBridge rule if the application experiences a failure. A solutions architect must design a DR solution to provide application recovery to a separate Region. The solution must minimize the time that is necessary to recover from a failure. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Setup a second ECS cluster and ECS service on Fargate in the separate Region. Create an AWS Lambda function to perform the following actions: take a snapshot of the RDS DB instance, copy the snapshot to the separate Region, create a new RDS DB instance from the snapshot, and update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.
options.B: Create an AWS Lambda function that creates a second ECS cluster and ECS service in the separate Region. Configure the Lambda function to perform the following actions: take a snapshot of the RDS DB instance, copy the snapshot to the separate Region, create a new RDS DB instance from the snapshot, and update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.
options.C: Setup a second ECS cluster and ECS service on Fargate in the separate Region. Create a cross- Region read replica of the RDS DB instance in the separate Region. Create an AWS Lambda function to promote the read replica to the primary database. Configure the Lambda function to update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.
options.D: Setup a second ECS cluster and ECS service on Fargate in the separate Region. Take a snapshot of the RDS DB instance. Convert the snapshot to an Amazon DynamoDB global table. Create an AWS Lambda function to update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.

en.explanation:
The application currently runs in one Region. The requirement is a cross-Region DR design that **minimizes recovery time** after a failure. Therefore, the best pattern among the options is to keep the recovery application stack already provisioned in the secondary Region and keep the database data continuously replicated there, then automate promotion and DNS cutover during failover.

**Correct answer: C**

Option C is the best solution because it combines:

- A pre-created ECS cluster and ECS service on Fargate in the recovery Region, avoiding the delay of creating container infrastructure after the disaster.
- A cross-Region Amazon RDS for MySQL read replica, so database changes are asynchronously replicated to the secondary Region before a failure.
- Automated promotion of the read replica to a standalone writable DB instance during failover.
- Route 53 DNS update to direct users to the recovery Region.

Amazon RDS documentation explicitly lists read replicas as a DR mechanism: RDS read replicas can be used for **implementing disaster recovery**, and a read replica can be promoted to a standalone instance if the primary DB instance fails ([Amazon RDS read replicas overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)). The documentation also states that cross-Region read replicas can reside in a different AWS Region from the primary DB instance, with RDS establishing secure replication between Regions ([Amazon RDS read replicas overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)). For promotion, AWS documents the failure recovery process as: promote the read replica, direct database traffic to the promoted DB instance, and create a replacement read replica afterward; promotion stops replication and makes the replica available as a new standalone DB instance after a short process ([Promoting an RDS read replica](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Promote.html)).

Route 53 is also an appropriate part of the failover design because Route 53 supports DNS failover and can route traffic to healthy resources in active-passive failover patterns ([Route 53 DNS failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-configuring.html)).

### Why the other options are incorrect

**A. Incorrect** — This option pre-creates the ECS recovery environment, which is good, but it relies on taking an RDS snapshot, copying the snapshot to another Region, and restoring a new DB instance only after failure. RDS snapshot restore is a valid DR mechanism, but it has a longer recovery time than maintaining an already-running cross-Region read replica. AWS describes restoring from a DB snapshot as a DR solution, but replication/read replicas are specifically suited to lower recovery time because data is already being asynchronously copied before the failure ([RDS resilience: backup/restore and replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html)).

**B. Incorrect** — This is even slower than option A because the Lambda function creates the ECS cluster and ECS service only after the failure occurs. Creating the recovery compute environment during the outage increases RTO. It also uses the same slow snapshot-copy-restore database recovery process as option A.

**D. Incorrect** — This is not a valid migration or DR mechanism. An Amazon RDS for MySQL snapshot cannot simply be “converted” into an Amazon DynamoDB global table. DynamoDB global tables are for DynamoDB data replication, not automatic conversion of relational MySQL snapshots. This option also changes the application’s data layer from relational MySQL to DynamoDB, which would require application and schema redesign.

Therefore, **C** best minimizes recovery time by keeping both the application tier and database replica ready in the secondary Region and automating read replica promotion plus DNS cutover.

zh.question: 一家公司需要为一个 Web 应用程序实施灾难恢复（DR）计划。该应用程序运行在单个 AWS 区域中。该应用程序使用运行在容器中的微服务。这些容器托管在 Amazon Elastic Container Service（Amazon ECS）中的 AWS Fargate 上。该应用程序使用一个 Amazon RDS for MySQL 数据库实例作为其数据层，并使用 Amazon Route 53 进行 DNS 解析。如果应用程序发生故障，一个 Amazon CloudWatch 警报会调用一条 Amazon EventBridge 规则。解决方案架构师必须设计一个 DR 解决方案，以便将应用程序恢复到另一个区域。该解决方案必须最大限度地缩短从故障中恢复所需的时间。哪种解决方案能够满足这些要求？

options.A: 在另一个区域中的 Fargate 上设置第二个 ECS 集群和 ECS 服务。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来执行以下操作：为 RDS 数据库实例创建快照，将快照复制到另一个区域，从该快照创建新的 RDS 数据库实例，并更新 Route 53 以将流量路由到第二个 ECS 集群。更新 EventBridge 规则，添加一个将调用该 Lambda 函数的目标。
options.B: 创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，在另一个区域中创建第二个 ECS 集群和 ECS 服务。配置该 Lambda 函数执行以下操作：为 RDS 数据库实例创建快照，将快照复制到另一个区域，从该快照创建新的 RDS 数据库实例，并更新 Route 53 以将流量路由到第二个 ECS 集群。更新 EventBridge 规则，添加一个将调用该 Lambda 函数的目标。
options.C: 在另一个区域中的 Fargate 上设置第二个 ECS 集群和 ECS 服务。在另一个区域中为 RDS 数据库实例创建跨区域只读副本。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数，将该只读副本提升为主数据库。配置该 Lambda 函数更新 Route 53，以将流量路由到第二个 ECS 集群。更新 EventBridge 规则，添加一个将调用该 Lambda 函数的目标。
options.D: 在另一个区域中的 Fargate 上设置第二个 ECS 集群和 ECS 服务。为 RDS 数据库实例创建快照。将该快照转换为 Amazon DynamoDB 全局表。创建一个 AWS Lambda 函数来更新 Route 53，以将流量路由到第二个 ECS 集群。更新 EventBridge 规则，添加一个将调用该 Lambda 函数的目标。

zh.explanation:
该应用程序当前运行在一个区域中。要求是设计一个跨区域 DR 方案，在故障后**最大限度地缩短恢复时间**。因此，在这些选项中，最佳模式是在辅助区域中预先配置恢复应用程序堆栈，并将数据库数据持续复制到那里，然后在故障转移期间自动执行提升和 DNS 切换。

**正确答案：C**

选项 C 是最佳解决方案，因为它结合了：

- 在恢复区域中的 Fargate 上预先创建的 ECS 集群和 ECS 服务，避免在灾难发生后创建容器基础设施所带来的延迟。
- 跨区域 Amazon RDS for MySQL 只读副本，因此数据库更改会在故障发生前异步复制到辅助区域。
- 在故障转移期间自动将只读副本提升为独立可写的数据库实例。
- Route 53 DNS 更新，将用户定向到恢复区域。

Amazon RDS 文档明确将只读副本列为一种 DR 机制：RDS 只读副本可用于**实施灾难恢复**，并且如果主数据库实例发生故障，可以将只读副本提升为独立实例（[Amazon RDS read replicas overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)）。文档还指出，跨区域只读副本可以位于与主数据库实例不同的 AWS 区域中，RDS 会在区域之间建立安全复制（[Amazon RDS read replicas overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.html)）。关于提升，AWS 记录的故障恢复流程为：提升只读副本，将数据库流量定向到已提升的数据库实例，并在之后创建替代只读副本；提升会停止复制，并在一个短暂过程后使副本作为新的独立数据库实例可用（[Promoting an RDS read replica](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Promote.html)）。

Route 53 也是故障转移设计中的适当组成部分，因为 Route 53 支持 DNS 故障转移，并且可以在主动-被动故障转移模式中将流量路由到正常运行的资源（[Route 53 DNS failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-configuring.html)）。

### 为什么其他选项不正确

**A. 不正确** — 此选项预先创建了 ECS 恢复环境，这是好的，但它依赖于在故障发生后才创建 RDS 快照、将快照复制到另一个区域并还原新的数据库实例。RDS 快照还原是一种有效的 DR 机制，但与维护一个已运行的跨区域只读副本相比，它的恢复时间更长。AWS 将从数据库快照还原描述为一种 DR 解决方案，但复制/只读副本尤其适合较短的恢复时间，因为数据在故障发生前就已经在异步复制（[RDS resilience: backup/restore and replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html)）。

**B. 不正确** — 这比选项 A 更慢，因为 Lambda 函数仅在故障发生后才创建 ECS 集群和 ECS 服务。在中断期间创建恢复计算环境会增加 RTO。它还使用与选项 A 相同的缓慢的快照复制还原数据库恢复流程。

**D. 不正确** — 这不是有效的迁移或 DR 机制。Amazon RDS for MySQL 快照不能简单地“转换”为 Amazon DynamoDB 全局表。DynamoDB 全局表用于 DynamoDB 数据复制，而不是自动转换关系型 MySQL 快照。此选项还将应用程序的数据层从关系型 MySQL 更改为 DynamoDB，这需要重新设计应用程序和架构。

因此，**C** 通过在辅助区域中准备好应用程序层和数据库副本，并自动执行只读副本提升和 DNS 切换，最能最大限度地缩短恢复时间。

en.question: A company has AWS accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company wants to track Amazon EC2 usage as a metric. The company’s architecture team must receive a daily alert if the EC2 usage is more than 10% higher the average EC2 usage from the last 30 days. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure AWS Budgets in the organization's management account. Specify a usage type of EC2 running hours. Specify a daily period. Set the budget amount to be 10% more than the reported average usage for the last 30 days from AWS Cost Explorer. Configure an alert to notify the architecture team if the usage threshold is met
options.B: Configure AWS Cost Anomaly Detection in the organization's management account. Configure a monitor type of AWS Service. Apply a filter of Amazon EC2. Configure an alert subscription to notify the architecture team if the usage is 10% more than the average usage for the last 30 days.
options.C: Enable AWS Trusted Advisor in the organization's management account. Configure a cost optimization advisory alert to notify the architecture team if the EC2 usage is 10% more than the reported average usage for the last 30 days.
options.D: Configure Amazon Detective in the organization's management account. Configure an EC2 usage anomaly alert to notify the architecture team if Detective identifies a usage anomaly of more than 10%.

en.explanation:
The company needs an organization-level mechanism to track an **EC2 usage metric** (for example, EC2 running hours), compare the current daily usage against a historical 30-day average, and notify the architecture team when usage exceeds that baseline by more than 10%.

**Correct answer: A**

AWS Budgets is the best fit because it supports **usage budgets**, including budgets based on usage type groups or usage types. The AWS documentation states that AWS Budgets can be used to track costs and usage, and that **usage budgets** establish usage limits for services and notify when usage approaches or exceeds the threshold ([Managing your costs with AWS Budgets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-managing-costs.html)). When creating a usage budget, you can choose a usage type group or usage type, set the budget period to **Daily**, and configure alert thresholds as either an absolute value or a percentage of the budgeted amount ([Creating a usage budget](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/create-usage-budget.html)).

AWS Budgets also supports an **auto-adjusting** budgeting method. AWS states that an auto-adjusting budget dynamically sets the budget amount based on cost or usage over a specified time range, and that at the beginning of each new period AWS Budgets calculates the budget amount from the cost or usage data in that baseline range ([Budget methods](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budget-methods.html)). Therefore, a daily usage budget for EC2 running hours can use a 30-day historical baseline and an alert threshold of 110% of the budgeted amount, or equivalently set the budget amount to 10% above the average usage baseline and alert when met.

Cost Explorer is also relevant because AWS Budgets provides a Cost Explorer graph during budget creation, and Cost Explorer is designed to view and analyze AWS costs and usage, including historical usage data ([Creating a budget](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-create.html), [Analyzing your costs and usage with AWS Cost Explorer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-what-is.html)).

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

- **B. AWS Cost Anomaly Detection** – Cost Anomaly Detection is focused on anomalous **spend**, not a specific EC2 usage metric such as running hours. AWS describes it as a feature that uses machine learning to detect and alert on anomalous **spend patterns** in AWS services, and it monitors anomalies in net unblended cost data ([Detecting unusual spend with AWS Cost Anomaly Detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/manage-ad.html)). Its alert thresholds are based on cost impact or percentage difference between expected and actual **spend**, not directly on EC2 running-hour usage ([Getting started with AWS Cost Anomaly Detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/getting-started-ad.html)).

- **C. AWS Trusted Advisor** – Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks provide recommendations, but they do not provide a configurable daily alert comparing EC2 usage against a rolling 30-day average usage metric. This option does not meet the custom metric and threshold requirement.

- **D. Amazon Detective** – Amazon Detective is a security investigation service, not a cost or usage budgeting/alerting service. It does not provide EC2 usage anomaly alerts based on a 30-day usage average.

Therefore, **AWS Budgets with a daily EC2 usage budget and alert threshold** is the solution that meets the requirement.

zh.question: 一家公司拥有属于 AWS Organizations 中某个组织的 AWS 账户。该公司希望将 Amazon EC2 使用量作为指标进行跟踪。如果 EC2 使用量比过去 30 天的平均 EC2 使用量高出 10% 以上，该公司的架构团队必须每天收到提醒。哪种解决方案能满足这些要求？

options.A: 在组织的管理账户中配置 AWS Budgets。指定 EC2 running hours 的使用类型。指定每日周期。将预算金额设置为比 AWS Cost Explorer 中报告的过去 30 天平均使用量高 10%。配置提醒，以便在达到使用量阈值时通知架构团队。
options.B: 在组织的管理账户中配置 AWS Cost Anomaly Detection。配置 AWS Service 的监控类型。应用 Amazon EC2 筛选条件。配置提醒订阅，以便在使用量比过去 30 天平均使用量高 10% 时通知架构团队。
options.C: 在组织的管理账户中启用 AWS Trusted Advisor。配置成本优化建议提醒，以便在 EC2 使用量比过去 30 天报告的平均使用量高 10% 时通知架构团队。
options.D: 在组织的管理账户中配置 Amazon Detective。配置 EC2 使用量异常提醒，以便在 Detective 发现超过 10% 的使用量异常时通知架构团队。

zh.explanation:
公司需要一种组织级机制来跟踪 **EC2 使用量指标**（例如 EC2 running hours），将当前每日使用量与历史 30 天平均值进行比较，并在使用量超过该基线 10% 以上时通知架构团队。

**正确答案：A**

AWS Budgets 最适合，因为它支持 **usage budgets**，包括基于 usage type groups 或 usage types 的预算。AWS 文档指出，AWS Budgets 可用于跟踪成本和使用量，并且 **usage budgets** 会为服务建立使用量限制，并在使用量接近或超过阈值时发出通知（[使用 AWS Budgets 管理成本](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-managing-costs.html)）。创建 usage budget 时，你可以选择 usage type group 或 usage type，将预算周期设置为 **Daily**，并将提醒阈值配置为绝对值或预算金额的百分比（[创建使用量预算](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/create-usage-budget.html)）。

AWS Budgets 还支持 **auto-adjusting** 预算方法。AWS 表示，auto-adjusting budget 会根据指定时间范围内的成本或使用量动态设置预算金额，并且在每个新周期开始时，AWS Budgets 会根据该基线范围内的成本或使用量数据计算预算金额（[预算方法](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budget-methods.html)）。因此，针对 EC2 running hours 的每日使用量预算可以使用 30 天历史基线，并设置预算金额 110% 的提醒阈值，或者等效地将预算金额设置为比平均使用量基线高 10%，并在达到时发出提醒。

Cost Explorer 也相关，因为 AWS Budgets 在创建预算时会提供 Cost Explorer 图表，而 Cost Explorer 旨在查看和分析 AWS 成本和使用量，包括历史使用量数据（[创建预算](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-create.html)，[使用 AWS Cost Explorer 分析成本和使用量](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-what-is.html)）。

**其他选项为何不正确：**

- **B. AWS Cost Anomaly Detection** – Cost Anomaly Detection 侧重于异常 **spend**，而不是特定 EC2 使用量指标，例如 running hours。AWS 将其描述为一项使用机器学习检测 AWS 服务中异常 **spend patterns** 并发出提醒的功能，并且它监控 net unblended cost data 中的异常（[使用 AWS Cost Anomaly Detection 检测异常支出](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/manage-ad.html)）。其提醒阈值基于成本影响或预期 **spend** 与实际 **spend** 之间的百分比差异，而不是直接基于 EC2 running-hour 使用量（[AWS Cost Anomaly Detection 入门](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/getting-started-ad.html)）。

- **C. AWS Trusted Advisor** – Trusted Advisor 成本优化检查会提供建议，但它不会提供可配置的每日提醒来将 EC2 使用量与滚动 30 天平均使用量指标进行比较。此选项不满足自定义指标和阈值要求。

- **D. Amazon Detective** – Amazon Detective 是一项安全调查服务，而不是成本或使用量预算/提醒服务。它不提供基于 30 天使用量平均值的 EC2 使用量异常提醒。

因此，**使用 AWS Budgets 配置每日 EC2 使用量预算和提醒阈值** 是满足要求的解决方案。

en.question: An e-commerce company is revamping its IT infrastructure and is planning to use AWS services. The company’s CIO has asked a solutions architect to design a simple, highly available, and loosely coupled order processing application. The application is responsible for receiving and processing orders before storing them in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The application has a sporadic traffic pattern and should be able to scale during marketing campaigns to process the orders with minimal delays. Which of the following is the MOST reliable approach to meet the requirements?

options.A: Receive the orders in an Amazon EC2-hosted database and use EC2 instances to process them.
options.B: Receive the orders in an Amazon SQS queue and invoke an AWS Lambda function to process them.
options.C: Receive the orders using the AWS Step Functions program and launch an Amazon ECS container to process them.
options.D: Receive the orders in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and use Amazon EC2 instances to process them.

en.explanation:
The question asks for the **most reliable** design for a **simple, highly available, loosely coupled order-processing application** with **sporadic traffic** and the ability to scale during campaigns with minimal delay before writing to DynamoDB.

**Correct answer: B. Receive the orders in an Amazon SQS queue and invoke an AWS Lambda function to process them.**

This architecture best matches all stated requirements:

* **Loose coupling and reliability:** SQS buffers orders between the order-ingestion layer and processing layer. AWS documentation states that SQS standard queues are suitable for use cases such as **decoupling live user requests from intensive background work**, **allocating tasks to multiple worker nodes**, and **batching messages for future processing**. SQS also redundantly stores messages in **multiple Availability Zones** before acknowledging them, protecting messages from a single host, network, or AZ failure ([Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html)).
* **Simple serverless processing:** Lambda natively integrates with SQS. AWS documentation states that Lambda can process messages in an SQS queue, polls the queue through an event source mapping, invokes the function with message batches, and deletes messages after successful processing ([Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)).
* **Scales for sporadic and campaign-driven traffic:** Lambda SQS event source mappings automatically scale based on queue message volume. AWS documentation states that Lambda automatically manages scaling, starts processing batches concurrently, and increases concurrent processing when messages remain available ([Configuring scaling behavior for SQS event source mappings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-scaling.html)). This is well suited for bursty order traffic without maintaining always-on compute capacity.

Why the other options are incorrect:

* **A. EC2-hosted database and EC2 instances:** This is not the simplest or most loosely coupled approach. It requires managing EC2 capacity, availability, patching, and scaling. An EC2-hosted database is also less aligned with the requirement to store processed orders in DynamoDB and does not provide the durable managed queue buffering that SQS provides.
* **C. Step Functions and ECS container:** Step Functions is useful for orchestrating multi-step workflows, and ECS is useful for containerized processing. However, the question asks for a **simple** loosely coupled order processor, not a complex workflow orchestration system. This option also does not directly provide the durable queue-based decoupling called for by the scenario.
* **D. Kinesis Data Streams and EC2 instances:** Kinesis is primarily for streaming data ingestion and real-time stream processing. It is more complex than required for a simple order queue and still requires managing EC2 consumers in this option. SQS plus Lambda is a simpler and more directly appropriate pattern for asynchronous order processing.

Therefore, **SQS + Lambda** is the most reliable and appropriate solution for this simple, highly available, loosely coupled, burst-scalable order processing workload.

zh.question: 一家电子商务公司正在改造其 IT 基础设施，并计划使用 AWS 服务。该公司的 CIO 要求解决方案架构师设计一个简单、高可用且松耦合的订单处理应用程序。该应用程序负责接收和处理订单，然后将订单存储到 Amazon DynamoDB 表中。该应用程序的流量模式不稳定，并且应能够在营销活动期间扩展，以便以最小延迟处理订单。以下哪种方法最可靠地满足这些要求？

options.A: 在 Amazon EC2 托管的数据库中接收订单，并使用 EC2 实例处理这些订单。
options.B: 在 Amazon SQS 队列中接收订单，并调用 AWS Lambda 函数处理这些订单。
options.C: 使用 AWS Step Functions 程序接收订单，并启动 Amazon ECS 容器处理这些订单。
options.D: 在 Amazon Kinesis Data Streams 中接收订单，并使用 Amazon EC2 实例处理这些订单。

zh.explanation:
该题要求为一个**简单、高可用、松耦合的订单处理应用程序**选择**最可靠**的设计，该应用具有**不稳定流量**，并且能够在营销活动期间扩展，以便在写入 DynamoDB 之前以最小延迟处理订单。

**正确答案：B. 在 Amazon SQS 队列中接收订单，并调用 AWS Lambda 函数处理这些订单。**

该架构最符合所有给定要求：

* **松耦合和可靠性：** SQS 在订单摄取层和处理层之间缓冲订单。AWS 文档指出，SQS 标准队列适用于诸如**将实时用户请求与密集型后台工作解耦**、**将任务分配给多个工作节点**以及**批量处理消息以供将来处理**等用例。SQS 还会在确认消息之前，将消息冗余存储在**多个可用区**中，从而保护消息免受单个主机、网络或 AZ 故障的影响（[Amazon SQS standard queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html)）。
* **简单的无服务器处理：** Lambda 原生集成 SQS。AWS 文档指出，Lambda 可以处理 SQS 队列中的消息，通过事件源映射轮询队列，使用消息批次调用函数，并在成功处理后删除消息（[Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html)）。
* **针对不稳定和营销活动驱动的流量进行扩展：** Lambda SQS 事件源映射会根据队列消息量自动扩展。AWS 文档指出，Lambda 会自动管理扩展，并发开始处理批次，并在消息仍然可用时增加并发处理能力（[Configuring scaling behavior for SQS event source mappings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-scaling.html)）。这非常适合突发性订单流量，而无需维护始终在线的计算容量。

其他选项不正确的原因：

* **A. EC2 托管的数据库和 EC2 实例：** 这不是最简单或最松耦合的方法。它需要管理 EC2 容量、可用性、补丁和扩展。EC2 托管的数据库也不太符合将已处理订单存储到 DynamoDB 的要求，并且不提供 SQS 所提供的持久托管队列缓冲。
* **C. Step Functions 和 ECS 容器：** Step Functions 适用于编排多步骤工作流，ECS 适用于容器化处理。但是，该题要求的是一个**简单**的松耦合订单处理器，而不是复杂的工作流编排系统。此选项也没有直接提供该场景所需的基于持久队列的解耦。
* **D. Kinesis Data Streams 和 EC2 实例：** Kinesis 主要用于流数据摄取和实时流处理。对于简单的订单队列来说，它比所需方案更复杂，并且在此选项中仍需要管理 EC2 消费者。SQS 加 Lambda 是用于异步订单处理的更简单且更直接合适的模式。

因此，**SQS + Lambda** 是针对此简单、高可用、松耦合、可应对突发扩展的订单处理工作负载的最可靠且最合适的解决方案。

en.question: A company is deploying AWS Lambda functions that access an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. The company needs to launch the Lambda functions in a QA environment and in a production environment. The company must not expose credentials within application code and must rotate passwords automatically. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Store the database credentials for both environments in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Encrypt the credentials by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Within the application code of the Lambda functions, pull the credentials from the Parameter Store parameter by using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3). Add a role to the Lambda functions to provide access to the Parameter Store parameter.
options.B: Store the database credentials for both environments in AWS Secrets Manager with distinct key entry for the QA environment and the production environment. Turn on rotation. Provide a reference to the Secrets Manager key as an environment variable for the Lambda functions.
options.C: Store the database credentials for both environments in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Turn on rotation. Provide a reference to the credentials that are stored in AWS KMS as an environment variable for the Lambda functions.
options.D: Create separate S3 buckets for the QA environment and the production environment. Turn on server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for the S3 buckets. Use an object naming pattern that gives each Lambda function’s application code the ability to pull the correct credentials for the function's corresponding environment. Grant each Lambda function's execution role access to Amazon S3.

en.explanation:
## Analysis

The requirement is to support Lambda functions in separate QA and production environments that connect to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, while ensuring that database credentials are not embedded in application code and that passwords rotate automatically.

## Correct answer: B

**B is the best solution.** AWS Secrets Manager is designed to store, retrieve, and rotate database credentials and other secrets. The AWS documentation states that Secrets Manager helps you manage, retrieve, and rotate database credentials, and that it avoids hard-coded credentials by replacing them with runtime calls to Secrets Manager. It also supports configuring an automatic rotation schedule for secrets ([What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)).

Secrets Manager rotation updates credentials in both the secret and the database or service, and Secrets Manager can set up automatic rotation for secrets ([Rotate AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)). For Lambda specifically, AWS documents Secrets Manager as a common solution for storing database credentials used to connect to Amazon RDS and for rotating credentials automatically without updating function code ([Use Secrets Manager secrets in Lambda functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-secrets-manager.html)).

Using separate Secrets Manager secrets, or distinct secret entries, for QA and production is appropriate because each environment should have isolated credentials and access permissions. Supplying the secret name or ARN as a Lambda environment variable is acceptable because the environment variable contains only a reference to the secret, not the database password itself. The function still needs IAM permissions to retrieve the appropriate secret.

## Why the other options are incorrect

### A. Systems Manager Parameter Store with KMS encryption

Parameter Store can store secure parameters, but this option does not meet the automatic password rotation requirement as directly as Secrets Manager. The AWS Secrets Manager documentation specifically identifies Secrets Manager as the service for managing and automatically rotating database credentials, and for replacing hard-coded secrets in application code ([What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)). Parameter Store would require additional custom automation to rotate database passwords and update the database, which is not described in the option.

### C. Store credentials in AWS KMS

AWS KMS is for managing cryptographic keys, not for storing and rotating database passwords. The Secrets Manager documentation explicitly distinguishes use cases: for encryption keys AWS recommends KMS, while Secrets Manager is for database credentials and other secrets ([What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)). KMS key rotation rotates KMS keys, not RDS PostgreSQL user passwords.

### D. Store credentials in encrypted S3 buckets

Although S3 with SSE-KMS can encrypt objects, S3 is not a purpose-built secrets-management service and does not provide native automatic rotation of database credentials. This approach would also require application code to implement object lookup and custom rotation workflows. It does not satisfy the requirement as cleanly or securely as Secrets Manager.

## Conclusion

The solution that satisfies both key requirements—no credentials exposed in application code and automatic password rotation—is **B: store the QA and production database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager, enable rotation, and provide Lambda functions with a reference to the appropriate secret.**

zh.question: 一家公司正在部署访问 Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 数据库的 AWS Lambda 函数。公司需要在 QA 环境和生产环境中启动这些 Lambda 函数。公司不得在应用程序代码中暴露凭证，并且必须自动轮换密码。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 将两个环境的数据库凭证存储在 AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store 中。使用 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 密钥对凭证进行加密。在 Lambda 函数的应用程序代码中，使用 AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) 从 Parameter Store 参数中拉取凭证。为 Lambda 函数添加一个角色，以提供对 Parameter Store 参数的访问权限。
options.B: 将两个环境的数据库凭证存储在 AWS Secrets Manager 中，并为 QA 环境和生产环境使用不同的密钥条目。开启轮换。将对 Secrets Manager 密钥的引用作为 Lambda 函数的环境变量提供。
options.C: 将两个环境的数据库凭证存储在 AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) 中。开启轮换。将对存储在 AWS KMS 中的凭证的引用作为 Lambda 函数的环境变量提供。
options.D: 为 QA 环境和生产环境创建单独的 S3 存储桶。为这些 S3 存储桶开启使用 AWS KMS 密钥的服务器端加密 (SSE-KMS)。使用一种对象命名模式，使每个 Lambda 函数的应用程序代码能够拉取该函数对应环境的正确凭证。授予每个 Lambda 函数的执行角色访问 Amazon S3 的权限。

zh.explanation:
## 分析

要求是支持在单独的 QA 和生产环境中的 Lambda 函数连接到 Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL，同时确保数据库凭证不会嵌入应用程序代码，并且密码会自动轮换。

## 正确答案：B

**B 是最佳解决方案。** AWS Secrets Manager 旨在存储、检索和轮换数据库凭证以及其他机密。AWS 文档说明，Secrets Manager 可帮助你管理、检索和轮换数据库凭证，并通过用运行时对 Secrets Manager 的调用替代硬编码凭证来避免硬编码凭证。它还支持为机密配置自动轮换计划（[What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)）。

Secrets Manager 轮换会同时更新机密以及数据库或服务中的凭证，并且 Secrets Manager 可以为机密设置自动轮换（[Rotate AWS Secrets Manager secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html)）。对于 Lambda，AWS 专门将 Secrets Manager 记录为一种常见解决方案，用于存储连接到 Amazon RDS 所需的数据库凭证，并在不更新函数代码的情况下自动轮换凭证（[Use Secrets Manager secrets in Lambda functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-secrets-manager.html)）。

为 QA 和生产使用单独的 Secrets Manager 机密或不同的机密条目是合适的，因为每个环境都应具有隔离的凭证和访问权限。将机密名称或 ARN 作为 Lambda 环境变量提供是可以接受的，因为该环境变量只包含对机密的引用，而不是数据库密码本身。该函数仍然需要 IAM 权限来检索相应的机密。

## 为什么其他选项不正确

### A. 使用 KMS 加密的 Systems Manager Parameter Store

Parameter Store 可以存储安全参数，但该选项不像 Secrets Manager 那样直接满足自动密码轮换要求。AWS Secrets Manager 文档明确将 Secrets Manager 认定为用于管理并自动轮换数据库凭证、以及替代应用程序代码中硬编码机密的服务（[What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)）。Parameter Store 需要额外的自定义自动化来轮换数据库密码并更新数据库，而该选项中并未描述这一点。

### C. 将凭证存储在 AWS KMS 中

AWS KMS 用于管理加密密钥，而不是存储和轮换数据库密码。Secrets Manager 文档明确区分了使用场景：对于加密密钥，AWS 推荐使用 KMS；而 Secrets Manager 用于数据库凭证和其他机密（[What is AWS Secrets Manager?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html)）。KMS 密钥轮换轮换的是 KMS 密钥，而不是 RDS PostgreSQL 用户密码。

### D. 将凭证存储在加密的 S3 存储桶中

虽然带有 SSE-KMS 的 S3 可以加密对象，但 S3 不是专门构建的机密管理服务，也不提供数据库凭证的原生自动轮换。此方法还需要应用程序代码实现对象查找和自定义轮换工作流。它无法像 Secrets Manager 那样简洁或安全地满足要求。

## 结论

同时满足两个关键要求（应用程序代码中不暴露凭证，并且自动轮换密码）的解决方案是 **B：将 QA 和生产数据库凭证存储在 AWS Secrets Manager 中，启用轮换，并向 Lambda 函数提供对相应机密的引用。**

en.question: A company is using AWS Control Tower to manage AWS accounts in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company has an OU that contains accounts. The company must prevent any new or existing Amazon EC2 instances in the OU's accounts from gaining a public IP address. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure all instances in each account in the OU to use AWS Systems Manager. Use a Systems Manager Automation runbook to prevent public IP addresses from being attached to the instances.
options.B: Implement the AWS Control Tower proactive control to check whether instances in the OU's accounts have a public IP address. Set the AssociatePublicIpAddress property to False. Attach the proactive control to the OU.
options.C: Create an SCP that prevents the launch of instances that have a public IP address. Additionally, configure the SCP to prevent the attachment of a public IP address to existing instances. Attach the SCP to the OU.
options.D: Create an AWS Config custom rule that detects instances that have a public IP address. Configure a remediation action that uses an AWS Lambda function to detach the public IP addresses from the instances.

en.explanation:
The company needs an OU-level guardrail that **prevents** EC2 instances in all accounts in the OU from obtaining public IP addresses, whether the instance is newly launched or an existing instance is later modified/associated with a public address.

**Correct answer: C. Create and attach an SCP to the OU.**

AWS Organizations service control policies (SCPs) provide centralized permission guardrails for member accounts. The Organizations documentation states that SCPs provide “central control over the maximum available permissions” for IAM users and roles in the organization and restrict what principals in member accounts can do, even if account administrators grant broader IAM permissions ([AWS Organizations SCPs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)). An SCP attached to the OU can explicitly deny EC2 actions that would create or associate public IP addresses, such as launching instances with a public IP configuration and associating Elastic IP addresses or modifying network-interface attributes as applicable.

This is also compatible with AWS Control Tower if done correctly. AWS Control Tower guidance says not to update existing SCPs that AWS Control Tower created, but explicitly says you can use AWS Organizations to **create new SCPs and attach those to OUs** rather than editing AWS Control Tower-created SCPs ([AWS Control Tower Organizations guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/orgs-guidance.html)). Therefore, option C is the best preventive, OU-wide solution.

Relevant EC2 authorization support exists for this type of control. The EC2 service authorization reference includes the `ec2:AssociatePublicIpAddress` condition key, which “filters access by whether the user wants to associate a public IP address with the instance,” and also includes public-IP-related condition keys such as `ec2:PublicIpAddress` ([EC2 condition keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/service-authorization/latest/reference/list_amazonec2.html)). These can be used in deny-based guardrails along with denying relevant EC2 actions.

**Why the other options are incorrect:**

* **A. Systems Manager Automation runbook** – This is not an organization-wide preventive guardrail. It would depend on every instance being managed by Systems Manager and on automation/remediation after the fact. The requirement is to prevent instances from gaining public IP addresses, not to run per-account or per-instance remediation.

* **B. AWS Control Tower proactive control** – AWS Control Tower proactive controls are not broad API-level preventive controls. AWS Control Tower documentation says proactive controls check resources before provisioning and monitor resources deployed by means of CloudFormation templates; they are implemented as CloudFormation hooks ([How controls work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/how-controls-work.html)). The proactive controls reference further states that they run on CloudFormation stack create/update operations and “may not affect requests” made directly through the AWS console, APIs, SDKs, or other IaC tools ([Proactive controls behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/proactive-controls.html)). Also, the EC2 proactive public-IP controls are scoped to CloudFormation resources such as `AWS::EC2::Instance`, launch templates, and subnets, not all possible ways to associate public IP addresses with existing instances ([EC2 controls](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/ec2-rules.html)). Therefore, B does not meet the broad prevention requirement.

* **D. AWS Config custom rule with Lambda remediation** – AWS Config is detective/remediative. It can detect noncompliance and attempt to fix it after a public IP has already been assigned. That does not satisfy the requirement to prevent new or existing instances from gaining a public IP address in the first place.

Therefore, the best answer is **C**.

zh.question: 一家公司正在使用 AWS Control Tower 管理 AWS Organizations 中某个组织内的 AWS 账户。该公司有一个包含多个账户的 OU。公司必须阻止该 OU 账户中的任何新的或现有的 Amazon EC2 实例获得公有 IP 地址。哪种解决方案可以满足这些要求？

options.A: 将该 OU 中每个账户的所有实例配置为使用 AWS Systems Manager。使用 Systems Manager Automation runbook 阻止将公有 IP 地址附加到这些实例。
options.B: 实施 AWS Control Tower 主动控制，以检查该 OU 账户中的实例是否具有公有 IP 地址。将 AssociatePublicIpAddress 属性设置为 False。将该主动控制附加到该 OU。
options.C: 创建一个 SCP，阻止启动具有公有 IP 地址的实例。此外，配置该 SCP 以阻止将公有 IP 地址附加到现有实例。将该 SCP 附加到该 OU。
options.D: 创建一个 AWS Config 自定义规则，用于检测具有公有 IP 地址的实例。配置一个修复操作，使用 AWS Lambda 函数从实例上分离公有 IP 地址。

zh.explanation:
公司需要一个 OU 级别的防护栏，用于**阻止**该 OU 中所有账户的 EC2 实例获得公有 IP 地址，无论该实例是新启动的，还是现有实例后来被修改/关联到公有地址。

**正确答案：C。创建 SCP 并将其附加到 OU。**

AWS Organizations 服务控制策略（SCP）为成员账户提供集中式权限防护栏。Organizations 文档指出，SCP 为组织中的 IAM 用户和角色提供“对最大可用权限的集中控制”，并限制成员账户中的主体可以执行的操作，即使账户管理员授予了更广泛的 IAM 权限也是如此（[AWS Organizations SCPs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)）。附加到 OU 的 SCP 可以显式拒绝会创建或关联公有 IP 地址的 EC2 操作，例如使用公有 IP 配置启动实例，以及关联 Elastic IP 地址或在适用时修改网络接口属性。

如果操作正确，这也与 AWS Control Tower 兼容。AWS Control Tower 指南说明，不要更新 AWS Control Tower 创建的现有 SCP，但明确表示你可以使用 AWS Organizations **创建新的 SCP 并将其附加到 OU**，而不是编辑 AWS Control Tower 创建的 SCP（[AWS Control Tower Organizations guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/orgs-guidance.html)）。因此，选项 C 是最佳的预防性、OU 范围解决方案。

EC2 授权支持中存在与这类控制相关的功能。EC2 服务授权参考包含 `ec2:AssociatePublicIpAddress` 条件键，该条件键“根据用户是否希望将公有 IP 地址与实例关联来筛选访问”，并且还包含与公有 IP 相关的条件键，例如 `ec2:PublicIpAddress`（[EC2 condition keys](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/service-authorization/latest/reference/list_amazonec2.html)）。这些条件键可以与拒绝相关 EC2 操作一起用于基于拒绝的防护栏。

**为什么其他选项不正确：**

* **A. Systems Manager Automation runbook** – 这不是组织范围的预防性防护栏。它依赖每个实例都由 Systems Manager 管理，并且依赖事后自动化/修复。要求是阻止实例获得公有 IP 地址，而不是运行按账户或按实例的修复。

* **B. AWS Control Tower 主动控制** – AWS Control Tower 主动控制不是广泛的 API 级预防性控制。AWS Control Tower 文档说明，主动控制会在预置之前检查资源，并监控通过 CloudFormation 模板部署的资源；它们实现为 CloudFormation hooks（[How controls work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/how-controls-work.html)）。主动控制参考进一步说明，它们在 CloudFormation 堆栈创建/更新操作上运行，并且“可能不会影响”通过 AWS 控制台、API、SDK 或其他 IaC 工具直接发出的请求（[Proactive controls behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/proactive-controls.html)）。此外，EC2 主动公有 IP 控制的范围限定在 CloudFormation 资源上，例如 `AWS::EC2::Instance`、启动模板和子网，而不是所有可能将公有 IP 地址与现有实例关联的方式（[EC2 controls](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/ec2-rules.html)）。因此，B 不满足广泛预防的要求。

* **D. AWS Config 自定义规则与 Lambda 修复** – AWS Config 是检测性/修复性的。它可以检测不合规情况，并在公有 IP 已经分配之后尝试修复。这不满足从一开始就阻止新的或现有实例获得公有 IP 地址的要求。

因此，最佳答案是 **C**。

en.question: A company is deploying a third-party web application on AWS. The application is packaged as a Docker image. The company has deployed the Docker image as an AWS Fargate service in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). An Application Load Balancer (ALB) directs traffic to the application.
